situation: I saw an article about pets being abandoned in Dubai, and it made me cry. The article mentioned that due to the Iran US War, the bombs made a lot of people escape their homes, leaving pets behind. There was nothing I could do about it. I couldn't understand how people with so much money just left their pets; it made me very sad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was in the last few days, world war three has started in the Middle East. It makes me sad because war is terrible, but abandoning animals makes me even more sad because they cannot fend for themselves.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I wish I could rescue the animals.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well if there wasn't a war then this wouldn't be happening so the world leaders are to blame first of all. Then the pet owners, it's their responsibility to look after their pets as they would their own children!
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I did not feel in control at all. I live in the UK which is too far away to be able to help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I don't know what the outcome is yet, I haven't seen any articles about anyone rescuing the animals or anything but hopefully someone will.

situation: I was watching Britain's unusually successful showing at the Winter Olympics, particularly the freestyle skiing events. I wanted to see some good competitive sport, and it was quite exciting, especially the freestyle skiing events.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a little as I enjoy sport when it's exciting.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It entertained me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The sportspeople competing.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Passive observer.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Best sport is always unexpected especially when people are pushing themselves to their limits.

situation: I was on annual leave when I received a message from one of my staff members about an incident at work between two colleagues. I had to reply, but I really wanted the person I left in charge to handle it so I could enjoy my time off. I felt stressed and annoyed that they messaged me during my leave. It was frustrating because it was something that could have been dealt with within the team on the day if they acted like adults and weren't rude to each other.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened while I was at a spa day relaxing with my mum. It mattered to me because it annoyed me and disrupted my relaxation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by disrupting my time at the spa. I tried to ignore it and deal with it later once I was home.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that the two colleagues who spoke to each other disrespectfully were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control as I wasn't there to deal with the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. I had to reply and deal with it later.

situation: I had a conflict with my work supervisor while discussing a data system that was built long before any of us were in our current roles. I was pointing out something missing with a rhetorical question, not expecting an answer, just wanting my concern about the missing information to be heard. This situation left me feeling annoyed and frustrated because it's a pattern that's been happening over the past several months. I'm frustrated that someone keeps asking me to stop asking questions they can't answer, even though I'm not looking for an answer. I also feel like I'm treated differently than others in the group. She often states rhetorical questions to me, and I just acknowledge them as they should be.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday. It matters to me a lot because my workload and frustration with my current job has really caused me a lot of stress this week.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It makes me less motivated to continue working hard to help out the group. I produce more output than anyone else in the group and when things like this occur, it's hard for me to continue on the current trajectory.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think both I and my supervisor can both work on how to better communicate.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I was not aware that normal conversational techniques that I have used for forty something years would cause such an issue, especially when I have not had one instance of this ever.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Expected, as in this is a recent pattern that has been occurring over the past few months. Unexpected because it's not something that anyone would expect in a normal conversation scenario.

situation: I had a health scare and had to wait a couple of weeks to have a scan at the hospital, which was emotionally stressful. During that time, I just wanted to think positively and be distracted, rather than overthink it. Waiting made me feel a mix of nervousness and anxiety, but there was also a bit of excitement—I was excited for the wait to be over. After the scan last week, when I got the results that same day, I felt relieved and very happy and joyful. Having support from my partner was really important to me, and thankfully, I did have that support.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened recently, as I mentioned the scan was last week. It mattered a lot to me because health is so important.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I now have less health anxiety, having confirmation I am healthy. Being exposed to hospital and medical settings also helped because I now feel less scared if anything medical was to happen again in the future. At the time, the situation hurt me as I was experiencing anxiety, but I don't think that's had any lasting effects.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: At first, I did not feel in control before I booked the appointment. After I had it booked, I felt like I was in control because I was making progress with my health.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. I had a gut feel everything would be okay, but I was still worried despite this, and it was.

situation: My mum went to the hospital because she was feeling awful, with a banging headache and lots of pain. They couldn't figure out what was wrong with her, which made me emotional. I was trying to help her by offering tablets she usually has to try and make it better. I just wanted her to be better. The situation left me feeling really stressed and worried. I didn't want it to happen again and was really anxious. The situation was resolved, but it still worries me that it could happen again. Support from other family members to help was really important.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot, the most important thing that was happening at that time. I was really worried and all of my mental power was just focusing on this. I couldn't focus on anything else.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me; I don't like seeing people I care about in pain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible, no one was to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't think I was in control at all. There was nothing I could do; I felt helpless.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I suppose when we went to the hospital, the situation unfolded in ways you would expect in a hospital environment. Like say the issue, wait, doctor/nurse comes out, talk to them, tests, try to resolve.

situation: Someone I had been close with and talking to often just stopped responding to me. I really wanted them to reply or at least have someone around to keep me company and help me feel like I'm not inferior. I started to accept the situation, even though it still doesn't feel good. I realized that if someone doesn't want to talk to me anymore, there's no point in pursuing it. This person had been someone I talked to for a long time and had helped me through some stressful situations, so it was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me quite a bit because they are probably the person that I have spoken most with in the last few years. Also they are someone that I like as more than a friend, so it made that much worse.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it made me feel like I'm not good enough. Also it made me feel a sense of loneliness since they are someone I talk to regularly.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well I was probably the person most responsible for this, maybe I acted in a way that made the person want to stop talking.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I didn't feel in control, they basically had all the control. I'm sure they aren't thinking about the situation any more, while I am.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected because it came out of nowhere and there was nothing to suggest it was going to happen.

situation: Recently, I was working on a project at work that was almost completed when the requirements suddenly changed. These new requirements meant I had to significantly rework what I had already done. I was trying to complete the project and deliver a high-quality piece of code as requested. This situation left me feeling mad, annoyed, and betrayed. I think what bothers me the most is the thought that the stakeholders of the project, the ones I'm building the code for, didn't put enough thought into their original request and are now making changes. It's disrespectful of my time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened last Thursday. It mattered a lot because I had worked on the project for about 4 weeks at that point.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The new requirements meant that I needed to redesign and rebuild much of the project that I had previously built. I think my annoyance was visible. I did not push back nor criticize anyone so I think I did not suffer anything professionally.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The stakeholders are entirely at fault for this. They submitted the project request with their exact specifications. They did not account for the additional requirements that would come later.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control. My job is to implement the ideas of others to their specifications. I am handed orders that I then commit.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They did not go as expected. Traditionally, I am given goals and requirements and then I build software to accomplish them.

situation: We had a leak on our water supply pipe, and it was very stressful. I was trying to figure out where the leak was and get it repaired. The whole situation left me feeling really stressed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because the leaking water was costing us a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me financially and in terms of stress.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The leak was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn't in control because I was at the mercy of my water supplier and my insurer.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Eventually things went as I expected, but it took ages.

situation: The US and Israel have declared war on Iran, and they're killing innocents. I feel like I can't do anything about it, and it's leaving me feeling hopeless and helpless. It's really sad, and I feel small and puny, like the world is dying right in front of my eyes. I think this situation will affect America soon, and we'll see the effects here in the upcoming months.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered quite a lot. I don't like seeing innocent people die. This will affect America in the upcoming months. This makes me sad and nervous.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel immoral and sad. It also made me very upset and mad that our leaders could do this. It makes me feel like we live in a dystopia.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: President Trump and everyone in government.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. The government doesn't care about people like me. They never will.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not at all. I'm a pacifist. I don't want people to die. War was somewhat unexpected.

situation: I finally managed to afford a new, actually good car after going a while without one and really struggling because of that. It was emotional because all the cars I've had in the past have been what you would call 'bangers' and have been close to their last legs when I've bought them, so having a good car finally is just an amazing feeling! I had been struggling financially due to health problems last year and the year before and couldn't afford a car then. I wanted a bit more freedom for myself and my family, and a car provides that, especially living somewhere where public transport links are lacking to say the least. I felt excitement for sure, pride to finally be able to finally get some freedom for my family. Happiness! Price was obviously a factor, but being able to afford it made me feel proud of how far I've come despite my health issues.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was very important to me because we'd lacked reliable transport for so long and with my health issues it is even more important for us to have a reliable form of transport.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped give me and my family freedom, a sense of pride and a feeling of achievement to have finally made happen something we've wanted for a long time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt personally responsible, with the help of my partner and son for helping me stay strong and achieve this goal with their unlimited support.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I definitely felt like I was in control; I made the decision to buy the car, worked out all the logistics and the like so I definitely controlled the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went completely smoothly and as expected!

situation: I was listening to someone I've supported and encouraged over the years talk about people my age as being old, and he expressed a preference for much younger people to watch or listen to his content. He's made similar comments before, and I thought it was just a one-off, but now it seems more deep-rooted than I first imagined. I wanted to feel respected for myself regardless of my age, and I was being a supportive listener. The situation left me feeling like, even though inside I feel much younger than I am and enjoy popular culture, some people will only see my age and dismiss me or my opinion because of that. I felt that it could work anyway—he may dismiss young people for not having life experience, but some young people could have more life experience than myself at a much older age. He dismissed me because he obviously thought I couldn't understand youth culture. I hope he is not typical of the youth of today.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered because previously I had had a lot of respect for this person and felt they were such a great human being who was not judgemental. It mattered a lot to me because I wondered if he was typical of the youth of today and yet maybe it didn't matter at all as he was ill-informed and short-sighted and worked in an industry where youth pays the wages.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not hurt me; it disappointed me. I would like to feel the world is moving in a less judgemental way.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt he had come from a very privileged background and mixed nearly solely with people of a similar wealth and education background in the same wealthy area, and this opinion may be specific to this group of people.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I am in control. I can choose to support him in the future or not support him, so the control is all on my side. In the moment, I felt disappointed.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I made my feelings known, and another member of the team told him to stop saying such stuff and that all age groups are relevant.

situation: My daughter just landed her first proper job, and I'm so proud of her because she did incredibly well in her first interview. I didn't really want or need anything from this situation; I just wanted her to be happy and settled. I'm feeling so happy for her, but it's also bittersweet because she's leaving home and moving into her own flat. It's important to me that she got somewhere nice to live and that she found a job she enjoys and finds interesting.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last Friday at 2ish, it mattered so much as she has done a degree, worked abroad and this is her first proper job for a career.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped her having me to support her which I have done all along but I know she’s flying the nest and leaving her family home.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Her getting her life together after a bit of a bad period, being happy in herself and my support for her.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I do I am a big support to her and I know she appreciates me a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes they did, finding her a flat was a bit of stress but we have got her a lovely place with an ideal location for her work.

situation: My daughter sent me something emotional that she had seen on Instagram. It was a trend where you lift up your oldest child, which will be the last time you ever do that. Watching it made me feel sad and nostalgic for when my adult children were of an age where I could pick them up. I had very strong memories of my children when they were this age and I could reflect on how it felt to pick them up like that. It left me feeling sad and nostalgic for a lost time. This was my favorite time of life and it reminded me of how much I enjoyed being a mum to youngsters.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered because it reminded me of a time when I could do this and now I can't.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help or hurt me; it was just poignant and nostalgic.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The content creator in the video as she explained to her son that she was going to pick him up for the very last time.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was a teary mess.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I knew it would be a weepy moment.

situation: My partner, who is a full-time carer for a parent, is going to have a well-earned break next month, and we're both looking forward to it immensely. I want to provide a break for her from the constant attention of care she has to provide. This should be good for her physical and mental health. I'm feeling happy and relieved about this. Spending quality time together is important to us, and we rarely get that at present, so this break is really special.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because I could see my partner was struggling after so long as a 24/7 carer.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me purely in the sense that I know it helped my partner.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The dirge of dementia sadly, which is what her mother has, was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control to some degree. However, you can never be certain of any plans as they can change in an instant to react to the caring situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Thankfully, yes things went as best as they could.

situation: My husband started an argument and said some extremely cruel and hurtful things. One of them took my breath away, and I was quite emotional for more than a day because of it, even though he apologized pretty much straight away. I wasn't trying to do anything; he didn't like something I said but was deliberately looking for a fight, literally putting words in my mouth so he could respond. A close friend is currently dying, and it was the anniversary of another friend's death, so I know he was ready to explode as that's how he deals—anger, not tears. But what he said crossed a line. I just wanted him to stop and go away to gather his thoughts. I felt very upset. He is an exploder because he doesn't handle emotion well, but there was something really horrible about what he said this time, like he hated me. It was hard to shake off, and still is. I actually felt a little bit afraid because of the level of venom and anger directed at me just for being there. I've never been afraid before. I have been unwell and was in quite a lot of pain, so I might have been more sensitive than usual, but it's something new and I didn't like it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 nights ago. It mattered because of the particular things he chose to say this time, which stunned me to the point I could barely speak. We don't have a great relationship these days, but this was something else altogether.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It felt like a line was crossed, but only I know it. Some of my feelings for him died there and then.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: His personality and the events of the day built up to a pressure cooker in his head, then a trigger from me, really just by being there as I had hardly spoken. It's a common occurrence for him, but he usually picks something inconsequential to shout and rant about. This time he wanted to tell me how well he would do if I was dead.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control. I would normally let him vent for a minute or two and then leave the room, but he wanted to carry on and was extremely angry.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, he eventually went for a lie down, came down after half an hour to apologize, and then went out. Ever since, he acts like nothing happened.

situation: Earlier in the week was the anniversary of my grandfather's death. I got really emotional talking to my partner about him, and for the rest of that day, I was thinking about him and how much I missed him. I wanted my grandad back. I wanted to be transported back to being a little boy and spending Saturdays with my grandad where he would spoil me and tell me amazing stories. I felt really emotional, nostalgic, but also grateful that I have these wonderful memories. I realized the influence he had on me and that his advice and help have made me into the person I am today.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The anniversary of my grandfather's death happened earlier in the week. It matters a lot to me because I do not want to forget my grandad. Remembering him and thinking about him helps me achieve the goal of telling my grandchildren about him one day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because an important person in my life is not here anymore. I could go to him for advice, and his support was always unconditional. I do not have many people like that in my life these days.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The anniversary of his death triggered all this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: For the most part, I was in control. I did get emotional for a minute or two, but on the whole, I coped well.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I felt that sense of loss greatly, and all the memories came back, some of which I had not thought about in a long time, so that was unexpected.

situation: A family member started treatment for a disease they have, and I was really worried about how they will feel on the treatment. I felt concerned and apprehensive about the whole situation. What was most important to me was that the treatment works.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot as I care about this person.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me in that I was reassured that treatment had started. However, it hurt me due to the fear of the unknown and the possibility that something bad may happen.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No-one. It is out of everyone's control.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really, no, as no one can tell if treatment will work.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it did.

situation: I accompanied my husband to a hospital appointment to discuss treatment for suspected bowel cancer. We needed to know the options for exploratory investigations and treatment. The whole experience left me feeling dismissed and dissatisfied. Life expectancy was important to me in this situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened this week following a positive FIT test. This mattered greatly to me because it threatened our future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it threatened our future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Disease was a factor.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We were not directed to challenge the advice of wait and see, which made me feel a lack of control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as expected. We expected a colonoscopy investigation, which did not happen.

situation: It all started the day before the actual reaction. People in the house were arguing over something so stupid, which also makes no sense. It's a common occurrence at this point, so I just try my best to tune it out with headphones. However, one of the said persons has a habit of arguing with that person, then carrying on shouting and screaming for the next hour or so, and somehow bringing other people into it. The next morning, they woke up and started complaining again about everyone, even though nobody said anything. At this point, it gets irritating and telling them to be quiet never works. At the same time, tensions are flaring and I don't want to hurt this person, hence I throw an object at the wall to get the anger out. It works and they leave, however, I feel irritated and unsure if that's a correct reaction to get anger out. Physically, I wasn't trying to do anything. Mentally, I wanted peace and quiet. I wanted to be left alone for a bit in silence without having to hear complaining, especially not the first thing when waking up. During, I remember thinking to myself, you can keep it in, they'll leave in a bit, but they just wouldn't. Eventually, it got too much that I had to get it out somehow, and that being throwing an object at a wall. After, I felt irritated at myself for not being able to hold it in for a little longer, but at the same time, at them, for complaining for absolutely no reason. It's a constant thing, so I'm used to it at this point. I used to manage it way worse and now, throwing an object at a wall is the worse it gets, although, even that is pushing my limits, especially as I spent an awful lot of time trying to tune it out and tell myself they'd just leave.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a couple days ago. As I said, it's quite common, so it has less and less of an effect as each one happens. It just lets me know every time that I need to save up money and leave as soon as I can, which I'm in the process of currently.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt because I feel like all the arguments and conversations from similar past situations didn't matter. It's like going over the same process again and again. It helped me in seeing clearly that if I truly want what I want in life, then moving out is the best option.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: For the argument itself, I attribute most of it to the other person, for stirring up fights like this, where I wasn't involved at all at the beginning. They have a common theme in terms of picking fights like this with others too, with whom I've talked to about. At the same time, the reaction and how I handled it in terms of trying to keep it in, not being able to, and having to throw something to the wall to get my emotions out was all me and something I could improve on.
appraisal_reasoning.control: At the time, I probably thought no, since they were the one who'd come up to me and started talking about stupid things. I felt like it was their cue, they should be the one leaving, not me. Thinking back now, I probably could've just left to another room like the bathroom for a little while and came back, which would've been a better reaction. However, I felt like I wanted them to know how I felt, that I was irritated and angry, since that's the only way they'd stop, and going to another room would just make them think everything was normal.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Like I said before, it's a common theme with this person, so minute details might be different, but it always goes like this: They start talking to themselves about me or someone else in front of them, complaining about them. The person tries to keep it in for a bit. They carry on for 10 mins to an hour. The other person, me in this case, gets annoyed and says something. They start saying more stupid things. I get more irritated, throw something or swear. They carry on for a minute and then leave.

situation: Last week, I was trying to do laundry when an item in my home that was recently repaired suddenly broke again. Specifically, a valve to the water supply broke while I was attempting to do laundry. The valve had just been replaced last year at a cost of 600 dollars, so I felt angry and helpless because it happened in the evening and couldn't be repaired for 16 hours. I needed the laundry for the next day, so I had to take the items to be cleaned at night.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a great deal, because it was not only inconvenient, but also could be dangerous, and is an expensive repair.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt my finances and created stress.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The faulty craftsmanship of the previous part and repair.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control, since the water could not be used, and a repair was needed.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The entire situation was unexpected, since the fault had been recently repaired and the part replaced.

situation: I met my friend's baby for the first time. I was trying to enjoy time with my friend and her baby. It was mostly a happy experience, but I also felt a bit sad because I wanted the same.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a couple of days ago. It mattered quite a bit to me because the friend is important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did neither of those things.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were equally responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, for the most part. I felt in control of my emotions even though I was worried I might not be.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Went better than expected.

situation: We got the results of my daughter's applications to secondary school. We wanted her to get into an academic secondary school, and she had worked hard towards the entrance exams. In the run-up to the email confirming the results, I was very stressed, but then I felt very relieved and delighted when we received a successful acceptance into our first-choice school. We had had some difficulties confirming with my parents that they would pay the fees for this school, as they do for my older daughter, so it was a relief when they confirmed that they would.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This was important as the choice of secondary school is very important to us as it will have a significant effect on my daughter's potential outcomes.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: We were collectively rather on edge and then relieved when the results came through.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was a joint effort, but mainly from my daughter's hard work.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control as much as I was able to do as much as I could in preparation, but ultimately the exam was my daughter's effort.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing unexpected.

situation: It was my mum's birthday last week, and I went out for lunch with her and my sisters. We were just celebrating my mum's birthday, and it left me feeling happy. I haven't seen them in a long time, so I got to catch up with my family, which was nice.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week. It wasn't a huge deal, but it mattered to me that my mum had a nice time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me feel more connected to my family.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were all responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt like I was in control during this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had a better time than I thought.

situation: I got to experience a genuine Valentine's Day date for the first time in my life with my new boyfriend. I just wanted to spend time with someone who I like a lot and who likes me too. I felt really happy. He thanked me for keeping Valentine's Day from being depressing for him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened last weekend. It meant a lot because it was a new experience for me that I had always been curious about.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because it made me feel cherished.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My boyfriend.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did because if anything happened that made me feel uncomfortable, I know my boyfriend would do whatever it took to make me feel comfortable. I wasn't forced to be there, I could leave at any time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did.

situation: I finished my most recent university assignment, proofread it, and handed it in early. I'm doing a BSc in Public Health and Wellbeing with the Open University, and I was trying to achieve handing in a completed assignment. To do this, I needed peace and quiet. Once I had handed in my assignment early, I felt very good and treated myself to a new TV since my current one has been broken for a bit. I felt good that I managed to hand it in, rather than go over it every day for days. One thing that has stuck with me is something a lecturer said: you get 80% of the mark in 20% of the time, and 20% of the mark in the other 80%, so I try to remember that. I felt I relied on myself well. On a previous degree, we were encouraged to get friends to proofread it for you, but my current university discourages this.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It is very important to me that I succeed with this course. 16 years ago I started a DPhil at Oxford, but had to drop out because of my health. Because of this, I am lacking in confidence about studying, but doing my BSc is helping me become more confident.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Handing the assignment in early was a significant step in rebuilding my confidence in my academic abilities, as was handing in one that I was 99% happy with.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I was most responsible for how things turned out. I was proactive in contacting my tutor to ask for some advice, which I have found difficult in the past. I made sure I did 30 mins to an hour each day, no matter how I felt, and encouraged myself to just write if I was struggling.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control throughout. This is because the assignment was totally reliant on me rather than with peers, and I got to choose a peer-reviewed journal article to comment on in the assignment, so I could pick something that interested me. And I was in control of when and how I studied.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It mostly went as expected. I had some difficulty restraining myself and staying on track when it came to reducing my word count, as I always find that difficult.

situation: My mum called me, sounding upset because she was abroad and had been quite ill. I expressed concern and asked if she had access to medical help and if she needed assistance in contacting a doctor. I reassured her that I was there for her and offered to help in any way I could. After talking to her, I felt relieved that she was okay now. I also wanted to know if she was having a nice time on holiday and what the weather was like, so I asked her about her experiences and encouraged her to focus on enjoying the rest of her trip.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was important to me as I care about my mum and her health.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Talking to her gave me reassurance. As she was in a different country, the phone connection was not that stable.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, the connection was not in my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they did.

situation: I developed Bell's palsy, and the right side of my face drooped. I was prescribed steroids, which helped improve the situation, but I felt mortified and embarrassed. It was especially hard for me because my husband didn't see me at my best, and that added to my feelings of embarrassment.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened suddenly, and an ambulance had to come because they thought it was a stroke. It mattered to me because I take care of my appearance.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I thought I would stay with my face drooped. There were no positives apart from it did get better, but it made me realize that life can get you.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt out of control because I could not control how I looked.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was not sure, but after I had the steroids, thankfully they worked.

situation: I was feeling joyful because I had dedicated a lot of effort to my writing, which made me feel competent. It boosted my mood and increased my confidence, reassuring me that I possess skills I can further develop.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened sometime when I was accepted for publishing, which seemed unreal. It mattered to me because of the significance of being published.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped open the door for more access in the writing world.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this due to my dedication to writing, which has definitely paid off.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt some control over the writing. Most of my emotions in the process weren't always happy; there were sadness and anger depending on the situation. But overall, I am pleased.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had to rewrite sentences and had a writer's block that eventually resolved, which was unexpected.

situation: I ran on the treadmill for an hour and managed to reach 9 miles in 59 minutes, which I've never done before. I just wanted to get my time under an hour. I've been trying for a few months, but I kept feeling like I was going to get injured. After achieving this, I felt great and very accomplished, especially since I've only been running for a year. Plus, I wasn't all that sore the next day, which made me feel like I'm getting better at running.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened after trying for a few months to hit 9 miles, and it mattered to me because I had been failing to reach this milestone before, only managing 8 miles. Achieving this was a significant accomplishment in my fitness journey.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Running 9 miles in an hour helped me in my efforts to lose weight and get fit, marking a good accomplishment for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this because I'm the only one that can make me lose weight.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt that the process was 80% under my control and 20% the pace of the treadmill.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had been inching towards that time for a while, so I guess it was expected.

situation: I've been thinking a lot more about my dad who died recently, especially over the past week. I find myself thinking about him when I have some time to fill or during moments when I would have normally reached out to him for an update. These thoughts make me feel sad and really make me realize how much I miss him. I've also been contemplating visiting his grave and wondering how I'll feel knowing he's there, under the ground.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I was watching a TV program where one of the characters visited her husband's grave. It made me think I have to do it soon.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It just made me realize he is under the ground, which made me sad.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am not sure.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I am in control, but I am not sure how in control I will be if I visit the grave.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected as I did what I do well and pushed the thought out of my head.

situation: I came to realize that a former best friend doesn't care about me in the way I want to be cared about. After months of waiting to see if she'd remember me, I realized that a friendship would only ever be on her terms. We spent the first time in months seeing each other, catching up, but it was 2 and a half hours of her only talking about herself. I wanted, and needed, to feel like I was an equal partner within our relationship, that she cared about me as much as I cared about her. I was hoping we could spend time seeing each other and catching up. It left me feeling used and empty, like I did not matter all that much to her and that, in fact, she just wanted the status of being liked to continue to feel important in the world. I just felt deflated as I had relied on her a lot. It helped to show me who actually cared about me and who was just paying lip service. It also finalized that the kind of friendship I had with her would forever remain face only. I was no longer going to put effort in when effort wasn't given back.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot because I had been invited into her safe space for the first time, and it was the first time we'd seen each other in months. I thought this would be the chance to bond and get back to how we were again, but I believe she had other plans.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Emotionally, it hurt because I feel a lot, love a lot, and have different social needs from others. She was one of the few people I could be myself around in a way I'm not with others. It also helped as it really allowed me to see that she wasn't a great friend, as a great friend wouldn't treat you that way.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I believe she was, and will remain, responsible. I have always checked in and tried to keep the connection current with her despite going through some heavy emotional and mental health issues this past year. I tried my hardest and talked about it a lot with several people, but if she is unable to make the effort but can for other superficial friendships, she will always be at fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control at all. We were in her home, with her stuff. I could not get a word in edgeways about myself, and every effort was met with her turning the conversation back to herself.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected. I was expecting a mutual discussion talking about our lives, but instead it was incredibly one-sided and only involved herself and not anyone else. It was about her struggles and growth with no mention or question of my own.

situation: My friend was talking about the anniversary of the death of her husband, who was also my friend. It was nice to recall good memories rather than dwelling on their actual death. There was a slight feeling of sadness that they were no longer here, but it was also uplifting to reminisce and share our feelings. It was important to me that my friend felt comfortable talking about it with me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened within the last week when I visited my friend at their home. It mattered a great deal as I feel that it comforted both of us.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt reassured that we could describe the death of a loved one without it badly affecting my friend's emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were discussing a holiday that we have booked for this summer and my friend recalled memories of when she visited this destination with her husband.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt that we were both in control as we both participated.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was surprised at how comfortable my friend was discussing her memories without getting upset.

situation: I attended my daughter's parents evening and listened to the teachers' comments. I wanted to hear how well my daughter is doing. As I listened, I felt positively emotional and very, very proud. It was important to me to hear the teachers praise my daughter's personality as well.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened on Tuesday 1st March 2026 at my daughter's secondary school. She is in her first year at the school and is really liking it. I attended her parents evening at 3pm that day to see 6 different teachers. It was important to me because all the teachers gave my daughter great feedback in all of her lessons.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation was very positive for me because all the teachers gave my daughter great feedback in all of her lessons.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The teachers said that as parents we've done a good job, but also my daughter is the one with her own personality and learning techniques along with how the teachers teach, so we are all responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, it was a very comfortable setting and we could sit where we wanted and ask what we wanted anytime.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected because of the high levels of praise she got in all subjects.

situation: I met with a friend I haven't seen in years because I wanted to reconnect with her. I really enjoyed it; it was lovely to see her. It felt like we had never been out of touch, and we still have lots in common.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered because it was someone who used to be a really good friend and I was sad that we'd lost touch.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was helpful, it helped me remember how much I enjoyed her company.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were both equally responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't trying to be in control. I just wanted it to unfold naturally. Control isn't a big motivation for me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't have a lot of expectations. I just wanted to reconnect.

situation: I realized that my cat, whom I thought was ill, is actually not, and it was a great relief. I was trying to achieve peace of mind in the face of duress, and finding out my cat was okay left me feeling quite happy, in fact.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I have come to expect loss in my life. I have learned about grief firsthand. So, I did not expect this grace.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It showed me that there is a chance at redemption if you do not give up.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Fate, or chance. I thought a condition was malignant and it turned out to be non-threatening.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I have no control over others' health outcomes.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, what I expected was that my cat would die.

situation: My son's expensive laptop stopped working, and we were faced with the possibility of either paying to get it fixed or replacing it entirely. I wanted to either get his laptop fixed without it costing too much or replace it with the same caliber laptop without spending more than we wanted. I spent three days doing research and bought different components to try and fix it myself. The thought of having to replace it was extremely stressful because it could cost over $600, maybe even $700-800, to get a new one. Plus, he would have lost a good chunk of his files, and I had files on his laptop too. I worried for a day and looked at different replacement options in the meantime. I really went straight to worst-case scenarios instead of being optimistic that things would work out and be okay. I was relieved when the local laptop repair shop called the next day and told me it was a fraction of the cost I thought it would be.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot because my son is really attached to his laptop. He uses it every day for gaming, creating digital art and music, and talking with friends. Without it, he felt off, and seeing him distressed was tough for me. The financial aspect was also worrying, as replacing it could be very expensive.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation made me realize I tend to think in worst-case scenarios. If I had gone straight to buying a new laptop, I would have lost a lot of money and my son would have lost his work. It caused unexpected stress, but it also highlighted the need for a backup drive, which could be a bonding experience with my son.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt mostly responsible, with some responsibility on my husband, though he's not good with tech maintenance. I should have been more mindful about backing up my son's work, and my pessimism made the issue seem bigger than it was.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt sort of in control. I couldn't know the final outcome, but I made choices to alleviate the worst-case scenario by trying to fix the laptop instead of buying a new one, which would have wasted money and made my child unhappy.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I anticipated having to pay hundreds of dollars, but it ended up costing only around $200, saving much more money than I thought. The repair was quick, and we picked it up the next day.

situation: I had to use a chat messaging service to contact a telecommunications company because I wanted to fix an internet issue. I was on the service for over an hour, but I still didn't resolve the problem. I felt very angry and frustrated, like my time had been wasted. It left me feeling despairing, ignored, and let down. I just wanted to get the issue fixed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened earlier today, it mattered because there was a fault and the internet kept going off, and it mattered because I was unable to work or access the internet.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help in any way, it wasted my time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The company itself and its employees.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I was waiting for them to respond and I could not speed things up.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I maybe should have known better than to contact them, but I thought at least I would get some sort of resolution, but no, I just wasted an hour of my day.

situation: My daughter is starting her final exams in school soon, and I've been asking her more and more to revise, especially over one subject that I know she's been struggling with. Last week, I offered to help her, but we ended up arguing. She refused my help, saying it always gets heated, and that's why she didn't want my help. I kept asking her what she's going to do, but after some time, I realized this was achieving nothing and walked away from the situation. I wanted her to be more accepting of help and for me to see that she was putting effort into revising, especially since it seemed like she hadn't been doing much at all. The whole thing left me feeling a mix of negative emotions: anger, frustration, hurt, and regret that I had allowed us to argue like that and hadn't kept better control of the situation during what is a stressful time for her. It was important for me not to argue with my daughter and to be more understanding of the stresses of the exams.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 4 days ago, and it mattered enough that it is still on my mind now. It matters to this extent as me and my daughter do argue often and generally get on very well.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did help as it reminded me to try and be more understanding. It hurt me most of all because I did not deal with it in the best way possible.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We both had our part to play, but I was in a better position to diffuse the situation more, so the fault would lay more firmly with me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did lose control, hence walking away.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, they did not go as I expected. I had assumed more openness on my daughter's part, and the quick escalation of the situation was surprising.

situation: I accompanied my wife to the doctor to deal with a pain she's had since giving birth to our son six years ago. We had to go over the experience of that difficult birth with the doctor, and it made both of us relive it and break down in tears. We were trying to get a diagnosis for my wife's continued pain by giving as clear a description of the cause as possible. We felt emotionally drained but also pleased because we finally got a promising diagnosis after years of trying. It was important to me to ensure my wife had some clarity and hope.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened earlier today. It mattered a great deal to me as I wanted my wife to get the best help possible in managing and curing her pain.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped us because our descriptions helped the doctor to diagnose the problem. It hurt us because reliving a trauma is emotionally and mentally hard.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were responsible for the choice to discuss in such detail as we wanted the doctor to have as much detail as possible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control of what information to share with the doctor but I didn’t feel totally in control of my emotions as I was unable to keep them fully in check.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went pretty much as expected. After 6 years of trying I suppose it was quite surprising to get a diagnosis but I was optimistic.

situation: I was relaxing in the evening and decided to watch The Green Mile to wind down. As I watched, I felt a little sad, especially during the parts involving the guy with the mouse. Despite the sadness during the film, I ended up feeling quite happy afterwards because I really enjoyed the movie. It left me feeling fulfilled, and I thought it was time well spent.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 4 days ago. It didn't matter a great deal to me because watching films is something I do quite regularly. If a film isn't very good, I'm not too bothered.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me to relax and put the day behind me. It also helped me to get to sleep easier.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I guess the producers, directors, and actors were most responsible for all of this. It was a very good film and well made.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control. I could turn off and do something else at any time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it all went as planned.

situation: Scenario: My stepson disobeyed instructions and was avoiding cutting the lawn. I wanted him to follow through with the task, but under duress, he did cut the lawn with minimal effort and poor results. I was infuriated because he is deliberately disobedient. If he moved out of the family home, it would make it better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event concerns me greatly because he is out of work and has a bad attitude.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because he frustrates me deliberately, causing anger and arguments.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel his narcissistic personality and laziness are most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of my anger.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I gave him some bags to poo-pick the lawn before cutting it, but he simply ran over the cat poo with the lawnmower instead.

situation: My children were playing nicely together, which is quite rare. Watching them interact like that made me feel love, warmth, and a bit of pride. It was one of those warm and fuzzy moments that I wish could happen more often. Seeing them be nice to each other in a meaningful way was just the confirmation I needed that they can actually get along.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because it made up for the times when they fight in a small way.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me feel hope for the future of my children.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just the kids really, maybe my influence as a mother was finally paying off.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was just observing the behavior.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Unexpected because usually they avoid each other or bicker and complain.

situation: I found out that a neighbor I was fond of had unexpectedly died. She was very unwell and elderly, and it's a blessing in a way, so I feel more relieved than sad now. I needed someone to offload to. A few days ago, I felt sad and a bit guilty that I hadn't checked on her for a couple of days as I had been very busy. The neighbor had been struggling with her mental and physical health for a while and was due to go into a care home, which she was unhappy about.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Thursday. The neighbor was a good friend of my mum's who passed away 3 years ago.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It felt like another link to my mum had broken which further upset me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The fact that I can no longer see this neighbor and chat about my mum.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't feel I had any control of the situation or my feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect to feel so sad.

situation: I was standing with a can of Pepsi, ready to drink it, when it suddenly dropped. I managed to catch it, but it fizzed up and went everywhere, including all over my laptop. I needed to drink the Pepsi, but instead, I was left feeling very upset and angry. I was so annoyed and upset that I nearly burst into tears at the thought that I might have broken the laptop. To make things worse, I had to spend a long time cleaning up afterward, which just added to my frustration.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened earlier this afternoon. It really mattered at the time as I thought I'd broken my laptop.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it went everywhere and was a big surprise that it could happen.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the Pepsi can was the most responsible, but I feel partly responsible for catching it instead of letting it drop.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I don't feel like I was in control as it all happened in a millisecond, so I had no time to think about it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was all unexpected, so it did not go as I thought it would, as never in my wildest dreams did I expect that to happen.

situation: I was bouldering indoors, working on a particular route problem that I'd been trying to solve for a long time. Honestly, I never thought I would ever get it, but I was determined to persevere. Completing it was such a positive emotional experience, especially with my friends egging me on and congratulating me afterwards. I was just trying to complete this route for personal gratification, and all I needed was patience, determination, and a bit of bravery and skill. After finishing the route, I felt happy, elated, and on a high from the adrenaline rush.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me purely from a personal satisfaction point of view and proving to myself that I could do something hard that I thought I would never be able to do.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped my confidence in my climbing and helps in being able to forget any other troubles or issues I have going on in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Only myself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control because I was the only one climbing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: In terms of I never thought I would complete the problem, that means things did not go as expected. But in a good way.

situation: I was watching Bridgerton, a modern period drama on Netflix, and it made me really emotional. The story was about a maid who attended a Masquerade ball and fell for a gentleman. This gentleman was highly sought after by many young ladies and gents, but he was insistent on remaining a bachelor. When he caught sight of the maid, he was hooked line and sinker, but in true Cinderella style, she ran away at the stroke of midnight, leaving him with only a glove. He became obsessed with finding her, and it was all he thought about. He met her several times without realizing who she was, but she was a maid and he a gentleman; their relationship was not allowed. He ended up falling for her as the maid, giving up on his masked lady. It was gut-wrenching to see them so in love but society not willing to accept them. When they finally admitted their feelings and the relationship became more, he spoiled it by asking her to be his mistress. This tore at my heartstrings and made me cry for her. It's unusual for a fictitious story or drama to make me so emotional, but this one really got me. She made me cry, he made me angry. I wanted him to tell her they could be together, that he would run away with her, but no, he wanted to marry a lady and have her be his mistress away from everything like a dirty secret. It made me feel hopeless, that love wasn't enough and that society hierarchy was the reason. He went after her but didn't; he left it and sent a message via a note to ask of her answer, which was clearly a no.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event made me feel bad for the character, who was sweet and kind and deserved more. It resonated with me emotionally, making me feel hopeless about love and societal hierarchy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me personally by making me feel bad and upset at the situation. However, later in the show, the gentleman told his mother he loved the maid, and she gave him her blessing despite the societal differences.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The laws of the time were responsible for the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Most of the time, I felt in control of my emotions, but other stories in the show also made me cry. For example, the gentleman's sister's husband died from a brain aneurysm, which was very emotional.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The show ended unexpectedly with the maid discovering her father was a gentleman of high status who left her lots of money in his will. The Queen decided to let them be together, which made me very happy in the end.

situation: I bent over to collect something and suddenly got a very intense headache. This was the second day in a row that this happened, and I became incredibly dizzy and light-headed. I got really emotional because I was scared I would die. I just needed reassurance that I wasn't ill. The whole situation left me feeling incredibly sad and concerned for my health.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me as it was in relation to my health and life. I was concerned that I would die and not see my partner again.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation made me very scared and concerned, meaning I then researched what the issue could be. It also affected me positively because it made me realise how much I love life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was likely myself and my poor care for my health.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control, as I had no idea what was going on and needed information.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It has gone as expected, as the pain has somewhat disappeared.

situation: My husband and I were trying to buy a house using only his credit and income because I have a lot of credit card debt. We initially got pre-approved for a $314,000 mortgage and spent weeks searching for a place. We found a condo for less than half that amount, but then the loan officer insulted my husband, accusing him of lying about his income, and refused to give him the loan. It was really frightening to think we wouldn't be able to buy it, and frustrating to have spent so much time searching for no reason. Thankfully, our realtor forwarded my husband's application to a different loan officer, who got him approved for the mortgage. The most important thing for us is to get out of the rental rat race after 13 years of steadily increasing monthly payments, so we can save money without the fear of being priced out of the town we've lived in for 20 years.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a tremendous amount because my family have been renting since we lost our home 13 years ago after the financial crisis of 2006.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Losing our home was devastating because we spent all of our money trying to save it, and then ruined our credit when we lost it. Since then, we've spent 13 years paying ever-increasing rents, just waiting for the housing market to soften just a bit so that we don't find ourselves in the same situation again.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like the original loan officer was at fault because he took my husband's information and immediately told him he could get him into a home very easily. Then after we'd spent weeks and weeks searching for the perfect situation, he took the same information and said not only could he not work with it, but that he felt my husband had been untruthful.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We felt out of control because it was out of our hands.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Ultimately things did go as we expected, but we had to go with a different mortgage company with a slightly less favorable deal.

situation: I have a neurodivergent child who had a massive meltdown earlier in the week. The experience was draining both physically and mentally, and emotionally too, as I wondered if I should’ve spotted the triggers earlier, which might have stopped the meltdown from occurring. I was just trying to aid my child in calming down and preventing them from injuring themselves. The whole situation left me feeling overwhelmed and drained. Ensuring the safety of others in the house, mainly my younger child, was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered because my child was emotionally overwhelmed and couldn’t 'function' effectively.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation did neither help nor hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There was no one factor responsible; I believe a myriad of lots of things had built up over time.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control as I was able to manage my own emotions, ensuring that I remained calm.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected; the child calmed as quickly as I thought they would, maybe even a bit quicker, and we were then able to discuss what were the possible causes.

situation: I was packing for a holiday and was retrieving items from my bedside cabinet for traveling. Out of the corner of my eye, I noticed a photograph of my deceased parents on holiday, both looking at me. It made me quite emotional. Despite the emotions, I felt grateful and recognized the importance of human kindness in that moment.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened three hours ago just after work. It mattered a great deal to me because I had forgotten to fully value how lucky I was to have the parents I did have.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by reminding me to value friends and family; it didn’t hurt me at all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was obviously me who was responsible as I chose to respond in that way to the trigger of the photo.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I could choose how to steer my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had no expectations to be fair but enjoyed the emotional ride.

situation: I attended a course validation meeting at my university as a stakeholder. I wasn't expecting to have to say anything, but when a question came up, I answered it. Apparently, I answered it very well because I received praise from a manager at work who holds a very senior position. This left me feeling confident that I know what I am doing. I did it because I am invested in my job and where I work, but it was wonderful to have my efforts recognized.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This was yesterday and it did matter. The outcome of the meeting affects my institution, my job, and my colleagues. This is important.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It clearly did not hurt as my contribution - minimal though it was in the broader context - was praised and appreciated.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My direct manager who had discussed the forthcoming meeting and made it clear what the validation event was for. He provided all the information I needed to be well-informed.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had a feeling I would have to say something, but I was not in control of that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went how I expected - although having to say something was unexpected.

situation: I had a voicemail left from my doctor's office and a missed call, but they didn't tell me why they called. This made me quite anxious. I really wanted to know why they needed me to call back and book an appointment. I felt very anxious, annoyed, and frustrated because every time I called, I couldn't get through. When I did manage to get through, the answering machine said they were understaffed and only taking emergency phone calls in the morning, so I had to call back later. I was worried because I would run out of medication before I could get an appointment, and I was concerned about the withdrawals and pain I would experience from not being able to get a renewal prescription and an appointment early enough. I was annoyed that I was not told I needed an appointment earlier and therefore would run out because of their poor planning .

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event started about 2 weeks ago and mattered a lot to me because I need access to medication to be able to function every day. I don't have control over this situation and fear that it could happen again.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by causing anxiety, annoyance, and difficulty focusing every day. It was always at the back of my mind as I tried to phone every day to get through, not knowing if I would eventually be able to get an appointment and how long it would take.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the staff's poor planning was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all. There was nothing I could do to get through on the phone or to get an appointment any earlier.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. It takes 2 weeks for an appointment, and due to the one offered being booked just as the receptionist offered it, it delayed things by two extra days.

situation: We had a new baby arrival in the family, and I went to the hospital to visit. I was surprised by how emotional and overwhelmed I got when holding the little one for the first time. It was the connection and closeness of family that really hit me. I was trying to hold myself together because it was really moving to see my genetics in the next generation. I didn't need anything but to feel what I felt. The experience left me feeling happy and hopeful. This baby is much wanted and has taken us all by surprise by arriving a little earlier than expected. The family was together and bonded; it felt positive and comfortable but amazingly emotional.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened four days ago so is very recent and vivid. It mattered a great deal as this is my family and the fact that the baby arrived early heightens the moment as we just wanted all to be well but it did make me worried until I saw the little bundle myself.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me as we lost a close family member recently and to have a new addition has both helped and given us a focus.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The baby arriving early changed everything, we were all taken by surprise and all that came with this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of the situation or my emotions as worry creeps in with the unexpected arrival. But seeing the little one safe and here made all the difference.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: We were lucky as things could have been very different including the outcome. It’s hard not to overthink about what could have happened but the baby is here, a little premature but safe and the parents are doing well so it’s impossible to take the positives.

situation: My Dad had an important hospital appointment regarding his cancer diagnosis. He was found to be responding really well to his medication, and the medics are very pleased with him. We wanted the confirmation that his medication is working, and this is the best possible outcome. I'm feeling happy and grateful because we know there's no cure, but this should stabilize him. I'm also happy that the NHS are looking after him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered an awful lot. My Dad is a very important part of my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was helpful, it was good to get confirmation that his medication is helping to prolong his life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The NHS.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I'm not in control, the illness is the controller however the NHS are trying to steer it in a positive direction.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't know what to expect but this was the best outcome I could hope for.

situation: On Wednesday of last week, my son and his partner had to have their beloved cat put to sleep. It was so upsetting for us all. I wanted to help as much as possible, especially with handling their understandable grief. I felt somewhat at a distance, just talking on the phone. But I hope I used my past experience with loss to help them both. Actually, anything that is said in this situation does not really resonate with those experiencing the loss. All I can do is be there when needed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Wednesday of last week. It mattered greatly to me because my son and his partner are childless, so this cat was 'their baby'. I fully understood this and although I was crying and upset, I needed them both to know they had support.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was hurt for their loss. But oddly, there was an upside. My son had to undergo a medical procedure just 2 days later, and the loss of his pet took his mind off the prospect completely.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No-one was responsible. It is just how life goes, I feel. The cat had rapid kidney failure, so there was no hope.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control, not even of my own emotions. Living apart from my son and his partner made this more difficult.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Both myself and my husband knew what the likely option would be, having lost so many loved pets throughout our life. I did expect my son's level of grief and despair, and this is what worried me so much.

situation: I was in the park on one of the first sunny days of the year with my children. I watched them play and have fun, and I enjoyed the view and nature around me. I wanted my children to have fun and I wanted to be outside in nature. I wanted us all to have fresh air and exercise and live a nice life. The situation left me feeling happy and content. I thought about my life choices up to now, like my husband being the main earner so I can work part-time and have these times with my children. We have no money worries and we are all healthy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me as my children are my life and I sometimes struggle with mental health, so I try and really enjoy the good times.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped me be happy with what I have and appreciate it. It helped me live in the moment and enjoy it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me and my husband were most responsible for creating that positive experience.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I chose to take them to the park and stay so they had a good time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went even better than I expected as my children played with others in the park.

situation: My partner passed away five years ago, and this April would have been his 60th birthday. His sister has arranged a party for the occasion, but she didn't even consult with me about it, which really upset me. As his fiance, it would have been nice to be spoken to about the date and the venue. This whole situation has left me feeling upset, and I don't want to attend the party because I don't feel like I'm part of the family. I felt like the party was arranged vindictively.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a week ago when it was announced on the family group without my involvement in the discussion. It mattered to me because he was my partner, and I had arranged his 50th birthday, so I would have been arranging this one too.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt excluded from the arrangements.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt his sister was most responsible for all of this because she likes to take over everything. We've not been getting on much recently as she's done a few things to upset me, so I feel this was deliberate by her.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt she was in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I felt normally she would have involved me, so I don't know why I wouldn't be involved in something so important.

situation: I have to go for blood tests every 8 weeks to make sure my cancer hasn't come back. Before heading to the hospital, I get extremely anxious, and once I'm there, my heart rate is through the roof. I go through the blood tests and then meet with my consultant right away to get the results. For the past 5 years, the results have been fine, and when I hear that everything is okay, I feel on top of the world for another 6 weeks until the cycle starts again. I really don't want to be there; I don't want to be someone who's had cancer twice in 10 years. I just need the reassurance that there's no cancer present. Once I get the results, I'm super happy and buoyant, and life feels normal for a few weeks. But as the next 8-week test approaches, the anxiety kicks in again. The most important thing to me is that the cancer hasn't returned. It's also comforting that once I'm in the hospital, the nursing staff are very kind, and the place is full of people like me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I was told that I had cancer the first time 10 years ago, I had to have a major operation and then 6 horrible rounds of chemotherapy every 4 weeks. It was a very upsetting time for myself and my family. It matters to me because I have a rogue gene and my cancer is 50% sure to come back for a third time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation has helped me live my life and be extremely grateful for that albeit I am very frightened. It has hurt me in ways I could never explain fully, my body has had two major operations and doesn’t work that well any more but in the great scheme of things life is good most days.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I have a gene which one of my parents must have passed onto me, which makes me 80% chance of getting cancer, which I did twice. No one is responsible obviously it is just one of those extremely sad things in life, but I am better off than most.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No control over this at all, it is completely out of my control - I am unable to change this.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What was unexpected was the huge two 8 hour operations I had to have, the chemotherapy side effects which were Gaston - the whole thing was very unexpected obviously.
