situation: My cat became critically unwell, and it led to him being hospitalized for a few days. He was unable to pass urine, so he needed to be catheterized and admitted to the hospital to help him. I just wanted him to be better and was looking for guidance on how we could prevent this from happening again. The whole situation left me feeling anxious, scared, and upset. The most important thing to me was my boy surviving.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week, it was really important to me as my cat is essentially my child, I even took time off work.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I was helpless, I couldn’t physically help him. I left him in a strange place although the hospital was the best place for him to be he is a sensitive boy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible, it’s just an unfortunate health issue.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Absolutely not, I felt like I was partly to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes they did, he was helped at the hospital and came home.

situation: A friend of mine killed themself after being depressed for a long time by jumping off a cliff. I spoke to them just two hours before, and there was no warning at all. I didn't find out until the next day. I couldn't understand why they didn't talk to me or come round, especially since they promised never to do anything like that because they had cats they adored at home that kept them going. I was totally shocked and upset, and it left me feeling like I could have done more, almost a sense of guilt. I keep thinking about the fact that I maybe missed signs that could have prevented this from happening.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot as they were my friend. I was upset to have lost them as they were only 31, and also I had to sort the cats being rehomed, which was awful. They were just looking for him all the time in the flat, and being in the flat felt scary not knowing why, knowing what he had done.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me seeing the cats so distressed and taking them to a cat rescue as they were so scared. Also, I had arranged to meet them 2 days later, so that kept going through my head—why? But what helped me was knowing the struggle they had gone through for many years was gone, but still a waste of life. I felt I should have bothered with them more and did not notice severe signs.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: To be honest, his mother, as she never cared about him, had other children, and he was in a flat alone. She did not even have him over for Christmas, which I thought was awful when photos were posted online, and she lived in the same town. I think he thought nobody cared, to be honest.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt I was not in control as I could have had him at mine over Christmas, and at times when he wanted to call, I said I was busy when I was not. So I feel all this built up, and I should have thought more about what my actions did.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I never expected him to jump off a high cliff! Yes, he had self-harmed before, but this was too much. Two hours before, we talked briefly on Facebook, and there was nothing odd about the way he seemed. But then I did not say a lot really. Looking back, maybe he was reaching out, and I missed the signal.

situation: My best friend at work got a new job in another organization. Though I'm happy for her, I'm actually upset because work won't be the same without her. The selfish part of me wanted her not to get it so we could continue to work together, but as a friend, I also want what's best for her. This job will play to all her strengths, so it's a very conflicted time for me. I'm upset for myself because I've loved working with her. We work together a lot, so she's my closest colleague as well as a friend. I don't think I will ever enjoy work as much again. She just makes work more enjoyable, and it won't be the same. I understand that she was being limited in her current role and progression was unlikely.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This only happened this week, though she still has to work her month's notice. It matters a lot to me because she has been a massive part of my working life as a full-time employee and my closest colleague and friend.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurts me because she will be a loss, and I don't think I will ever enjoy work as much again. She makes work more enjoyable, and it won't be the same without her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel our current employer is most responsible because they never gave her the opportunity to progress, despite her doing plenty of extra training in attempts to do so.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I have no agency here and can only wish her the best and continue to stay friends outside of work.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was aware of her interview and knew she was a good fit for the job, so I wasn't surprised when she got it.

situation: Somebody I was very close and attached to has died. I'm not trying to do anything right now, and I don't need or want anything except food, liquids, and warmth. When someone dies, I always feel relieved because they will no longer suffer, but I'm sad for those who are left behind. I don't really include myself in that group, although I am sad, but such is life. Life equals death. Talking to a computer about it isn't something I would normally do—not because of sadness, but because I prefer my thoughts to remain thoughts rather than being turned into words. It's too abstract to attach importance to the situation. I would rather feel things and think things compared to notions of importance.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered obviously, but I am not into explaining things with something that does not exist.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think there is a general consensus on what occurs to people when someone dies, including different ways of coping, avoiding, or grieving.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Death seems to be a natural thing and that is that.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I cannot control death and do not see what control has to do with any of this.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The death was unexpected but expected as well. It comes at different times for everyone and everything.

situation: A family member got caught up in the conflict happening in the Middle East. They were ultimately safe, but they saw the rocket fire and had to take shelter. It was a pretty intense few days with a lot of calls and just as much waiting. Thankfully, they've now been flown out and are safely in the UK. During this time, I was trying to manage the rest of my family to prevent them from freaking out and losing track of the situation. It took all of my people skills because not all of the emotions expressed were easy to handle or hear, ranging from deep anger to panic. My approach was to actively listen and not push back too much, waiting until there was a lull or I sensed that people had kind of talked themselves out before suggesting things or taking some sort of action, like calling someone or looking up information. By the end of it, I felt drained. Heavily drained. But it was important to me that I kept calm and was a reference point of calm for others.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on a Saturday when I received a text from my mum about the situation. It mattered a lot to me because it was shocking and unexpected, with the US going to war with Iran.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was mentally taxing and emotionally draining. It cemented in my mind that handling stressful situations with many competing demands and voices is best done by actively listening and managing emotions systematically.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: A mix of factors and variables were responsible. With people, there are various individual emotional responses that I can only respond to but not control. Ultimately, the hysterical response my family tends to lend to events was responsible, but something like this is outside of everyone's control.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It felt like a battle to gain control as everyone tends to compete for having the biggest emotion, and those who lose out either spin out of control or go a bit quiet and unconstructive. Dealing with each thing one at a time, systematically, counteracted that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went pretty much as expected and as I have outlined.

situation: I went to see Peter Capaldi play a gig in Leeds. I've admired him for a long time, and he's amazing both as an artist and as a person. I absolutely had a great time at the gig, but I ended up missing my train because I wanted to chat with him and get his autograph afterwards. So, I was stuck in Leeds for six hours in cold weather. On top of that, I had very unsettled feelings because my abusive sister lives in Leeds. Knowing she was only a mile or so away from me was unsettling, even though she didn't know I was there. It made me anxious thinking she could come and attack me at any point. Despite all this, I believe you have to celebrate the good in life.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last Sunday and it matters a lot. I had wanted to go and see him when he performed in Glasgow last year, but I didn’t have the ability to take the time off. So when I found out that he was playing quite close by to where I am staying at the moment, I jumped at the chance to book it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me realise that I am my own person, and I should do the things that bring me happiness and not trying to conform just to make people happy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was definitely me! I planned it, booked it and paid for it. And got myself there and back with my own intuition.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I definitely was in control. I went there by myself and nobody made any decisions on any aspect apart from me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They’re pretty much did go as I expected, the only thing that didn’t go perfectly was of course missing the train. But even that was as expected. Because I made the conscientious decision to not try and catch it. Despite what the circumstances would be.

situation: Two days ago, I heard that my Aunt had died. She was 80, but it was still unexpected. It's still early, but I know the funeral is on the 18th, and I'll be meeting up with the family to pay our respects. I'm feeling a bit isolated because I don't live close to the rest of my family, and they are a lot closer to each other. Sandra was the last of my mum's generation to pass, and it's raised a lot of memories for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened two days ago. I felt slightly distant from the news, a bit like I should be more upset than I was. It mattered to me because Sandra was the last of my mum's generation to pass, which raised a lot of memories for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation has saddened me. It feels like the end of an era, which has upset me more than the news itself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible; it was simply old age.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, not at all. I was upset but there was no one there to support me, my sisters were not there.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I'm not sure how things will go. The funeral is on the 18th of March. I have no other thoughts really at the moment, perhaps a bit of anticipation.

situation: I suffered severe childhood abuse, both physical and emotional, starting from before I was even born. My mother had a lot of mental and physical health issues, and my father died a month before I was born. People kept telling my mom to abort me, and I'm amazed I was born. Growing up, I lived with a few different family members after my mom was hospitalized when I was 8, and my stepdad couldn't take care of my brother and me. These family members were also abusive and controlling. Until I was 8, I didn't always have food at home, and then my food was controlled for the next four years. I lived with my mom again for a bit over a year, but my stepdad and brother were also physically and emotionally abusive to me. Again, I didn't always have food to eat, and people weren't kind to me. From ages 13 to 20, I lived with an aunt and uncle who didn't have room and put me in what was almost a closet. I had a twin-size bed, a small dresser, and a TV. No AC. I passed out in my room from the heat. I was often yelled at and bullied in high school for being chubby, and then people had crushes on me when I turned skinny from puberty and walking around all the time. Again, I didn't have enough food to eat at home and often didn't get to have lunch. I've struggled with jobs due to having fibromyalgia and feeling dizzy and overwhelmed from my CPTSD. Nowhere that I've worked has been understanding that I pour myself out in my jobs and work as hard as I can, but when I feel ill, I don't feel like being overly empathetic and just want to focus on my work or I need to call out sick. This has made it so hard for me to have a job. I want to try to find somewhere I belong. College is beyond expensive, and I worked in the medical field for a few years, but I got burnt out and treated terribly. I don't have a college degree, and I also just had spinal surgery. My partner wants to leave me because I am not independent, and I haven't had a proper job in about 7 years. It leaves me feeling hopeless and terrified about my future. I've moved 17 times in my life and have zero support from my family. My husband gets so much support from his family, and his mom messages him every single day. I feel like I constantly meet people way better off than me, and I don't know how to get out of this situation. I don't deserve any of what happened to me or how people dumped their trauma on me. My whole life, I have acted like a therapist or almost motherly to other people. They feel better and move on, leaving me feeling hurt and alone.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters to me because it shaped my life and the person I am. I had a lot of issues with emotional regularity because I have a trauma brain. Scientists have proven that people who suffered severe childhood abuse do not have healthy brains. I would snap and yell at others because I was hurt and that's what people did to me. I hurt people emotionally that I never meant to. But I also learned to be observant and caring, and I am proud of that. My older brother is very angry and resentful and kept taking things out on me, so I cut him out of my life. No one in my family ever confronted him for his physical and emotional abuse, and part of me hates them for that.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I am an empathetic and loving person. I listen, I try to provide solutions, and I give support to others to help them grow. I like making ripples that make waves in the world. I want to find my place. However, I do get sicker easily, I am not healthy, my chronic health issues, moving around a lot, terrible friends, and medication turned me from skinny to obese. I was also assaulted in public in 2016 in NYC in front of hundreds of people, and no one stepped in. I almost was killed. I don't fully feel like I can be myself anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My family was responsible. The Aunt I lived with through high school and till I was 20 knew how horribly physically and emotionally abused my brother and I were being, and me by my brother as well. There were always people doing drugs in my apartment, and my aunt didn't do anything till another aunt saw my stepdad punch me and choke my mom against the wall when I was 12, and the cops arrested him. How could someone stand by and let that abuse happen to people?
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control because I was a child and I had no power or money to leave.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I lost my home in 9th grade and almost had to go to a shelter, but my mom's friend took me and her in for a week, and then my aunt took me in.

situation: I needed help with the garden after a rainy winter had left it in a bit of a mess. My ex-husband, who is still living in the house, refused to engage in supporting me to get the garden sorted. I was trying to persuade him to help me with just about everything, including mowing the lawn. His refusal left me feeling extremely distressed and overworked because it meant I had to do all the physical work myself. It was important to me that he engaged in this so that the children could see that he was helpful.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday morning. It was extremely important to me and was time-bound as rain was due again. I am getting the house ready to sell and need support.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me emotionally and physically. I had to then undertake the work myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He was completely responsible. I had nothing but good will in this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I lacked any control. He continued to lie on the sofa for an entire day.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected this as this was typical of his behaviour.

situation: I watched a video of my grandsons playing in the garden, and it made me feel warm and emotional. I was seeking connection, and seeing them so happy was really important to me. It left me feeling happy to see them, but also sad that they are far away.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened this morning and mattered a lot to me because I am so proud of them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was reassured of their wellbeing.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my son and daughter-in-law were responsible for the kids being so happy.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control due to the distance, but I was in control of rewatching the video.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was as I expected.

situation: Last week, I had an important project due at work, and as the deadline got closer, I started to worry a lot. I kept thinking about whether I had finished everything and if I was missing anything. I was trying to make sure all the financial papers were correct and ready for the audit. I needed my team of six people to finish their work quickly and accurately so we could finish on time. The pressure made me nervous and anxious because I was afraid we might fall behind or make mistakes. It was also really important for me to keep my team motivated and calm.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it mattered a lot to me because the success of the audit was important for the company’s reputation and for meeting our deadlines. I cared because I wanted everything to be accurate and to do a good job as a leader.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me become more focused and determined to finish the work. It made me try harder to stay organised and support my team. I also learned how to stay calm and manage stress when things get hard, which will help me in the future. But it also hurt me because the stress made me feel anxious and tired, and I was worried about making mistakes or not finishing on time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was mostly responsible for the situation. As the leader, it was my job to make sure everything was on track and that my team was working well. I felt responsible for managing the deadlines, keeping everyone motivated and making sure the work was accurate.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn’t always feel in control. The pressure made me worried I might not finish on time or miss something important. I felt overwhelmed and unsure at times.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Looking back, things did go as I hoped because we finished the work and met the deadline. But what was unexpected was how stressful it felt at times and how much I doubted myself along the way.

situation: I got a call from my nephew, and he shared the exciting news that his partner is pregnant and they're having a little girl. It made me so happy that they took the time to tell me personally. As the one who received the call, I really wanted to glow in the moment and savor this positive news, especially with all the negative news that's been around lately. I felt amazing, not just for myself but for them, because having a child is such a blessing. It was important to me that they appreciated me enough to call and share this wonderful news.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because I care about my family and their happiness. Knowing they will be happy reassures me that there are good things in the world to be excited about.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation reassured me that there are good things in the world to be excited about, but it did not help or hurt me directly.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that the universe has blessed them with this, so it is a blessing to have this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control over the situation, as I was able to celebrate with them but had no control here.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was not expecting the call and the news, but I was elated for them.

situation: My husband was leaving for a month to travel for business, and I was really upset and sad about not being able to see him for that long. I wanted comfort during this time, but the thought of being apart for a whole month left me feeling very sad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because he is my husband and I live with him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as it made me feel sad. I was sad because I would be in the house by myself, feeling sad and lonely.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The situation was most responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control because I didn't have the option to make him stay.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as I expected. I was able to get over it and be happy again.

situation: I learned quite by chance that a close friend had died. My son discovered the fact through a Facebook post. I had been trying to get hold of her by phone and letter since the beginning of the year, without success; it turns out she had been in a hospice. I was very frustrated by the fact I couldn't make contact, little realizing the reason for this; when I found out, I was very much saddened.I really wanted to discover details of any arrangements regarding the funeral, but didn't have the contact details of her two sons.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered very much; she and I originally met over 30 years ago when we job-shared. During that time we became great friends and subsequently she became godmother to my youngest son.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was sorry that I hadn't been able to speak with her during her latter days and frustrated by the fact we live at opposite ends of the country, so were not able to meet in recent years.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No-one was responsible, it was just a fact of life; sad things happen and we have no control over them.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was obviously not in control of her illness and couldn't have predicted the outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I have managed to ascertain that the funeral will be held in a week's time and have made plans to travel the distance to support her sons. Hopefully there will be no obstacles to our journey.

situation: I completed a group project at work that encountered several delays. It was finally able to be done after dragging on for awhile. I wanted to complete the project and have it as perfect as possible while following company guidelines and client requests. I felt a range of emotions during the project. When I encountered something new that was a learning experience, I felt happy as it better helped me develop myself. When I encountered roadblocks or something that came up which put the project to a halt, I felt annoyed and even aggravated. But when I finally finished it all, my group and I were relieved and happy to move on. It was a group project so it did help me bond and learn a little more about my coworkers.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The project stood out because of how it panned out. All projects we do are important as it's part of what we do at work, and putting our best efforts lets management know how much we care and what we're capable of.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation may have hurt a little due to the delays, and on the surface level, it might look like we were inexperienced to the organization. However, it was a learning experience that helped develop further skills and facilitated team bonding.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The team, as a whole, was responsible for it. Every team member played a critical role and was equally as important throughout.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control of the work I was assigned but not for anyone else. I wasn't going to go about and tell people how to do their work. If they came to me for advice, I'd give my input but I wasn't going to have them do it my way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things were unexpected due to issues coming up that delayed the project as a whole. There wasn't anything else that particularly caught me by surprise.

situation: My good friend Suz decided to drive drunk on her birthday instead of taking the ride I offered. She lied to me, saying she was going to take an Uber. I was really upset and spent a lot of time thinking about this issue. In the end, I confronted her and told her that I knew she drove drunk. Between the risk she took and the lie she told, I realized I was no longer comfortable being close to her. I wanted to end the friendship. I felt a little sad about it, but also a bit proud of standing up for what I believe in. There were so many ways she could have hurt people, but listing them all wasn't worth my time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal, she was a good friend. The lie and the fact so many could have been injured got me indignant.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Well I lost a friend, but they come and go. It helped me by sticking to my convictions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I guess I am. I saw something I did not like and took action, others ignored it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of my friend's decisions but was in control of my reaction.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected, she made an excuse and said she had a drinking problem. She asked if she could call me, I said of course, no call came.

situation: A close friend of mine has been receiving treatment for cancer, and now he's been declared clear of the disease. It's been a very emotional time, not just for me but for his family as well. I've been truly inspired by his strength of character and his fight through this tough period. To celebrate this incredible milestone, I'm planning a special occasion for him. Throughout his treatment, I tried to provide as much support as I could, helping with shopping and other domestic chores, and being there as a shoulder to lean on whenever needed. As a lifelong friend, this has meant a lot to me personally. While I feel inspired by his resilience, I also have this underlying fear that he might deteriorate again, given the severity of the treatment he underwent. This experience has taught me a lot about my own character, taking me on an emotional roller coaster with many ups and downs. I feel more emotionally connected to my friend and his family than ever before.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I felt such a weight being lifted from my shoulders when my friend was declared clear of cancer. I felt energized and so happy at this news and looked forward to spending some really good times together in the future. The whole episode has helped me so much. I have developed a more positive outlook on life and take each day as it comes.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: When I wake up each morning, I feel more energized and able to face up to challenges in a positive way. Life can be very tough at times, but I really feel that this event has been a turning point not only for my friend but also for myself. The whole story is a case of triumph over adversity.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Taking each day as it comes was very important for us both throughout the course of treatment. I wanted to be there at all times for my friend and his family and am extremely proud of myself that my help and support made a real difference to everyone. I also found it helpful to remain as positive as possible despite facing some really difficult, challenging, and often stressful times.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I think it was important for me to remain strong despite this being severely tested at certain times. There were times throughout the past few months when the outlook was a little bleak, but I am sure that my support and positive outlook really helped my friend during what was the most difficult period of his life.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Some months ago, the outlook for my friend's long-term survival looked bleak. I think that standing by my friend throughout his course of treatment and supporting his family contributed to his eventual recovery. I wanted to relieve as much of the pressure on him so that he could focus entirely on dealing with his treatment in the hospital without the worry of how his family was coping. I think I learned a lot about myself through this very challenging time. I surprised myself with how I managed to deal with my own day-to-day challenges whilst also supporting my friend and his family. The whole story has left me with a spring in my step where I look forward to each day and never take anything for granted. I also feel very humble at the way that my friend handled such a life-changing event.

situation: We had a blizzard, and it caused me to become anxious. I was trying to make sure I had enough food and didn't lose power. The whole situation left me feeling unprepared and uneasy. On top of that, I also didn't have enough money on hand, which added to my stress.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened the weekend of February 21, 2026. It mattered very much because two feet of snow was expected.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It impacted me by making me feel uneasy because I didn't have enough time to prepare.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was the most responsible because I should have had more food on hand and better resources.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control because mother nature was.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It didn't go as expected because the roads were bad and most of my food didn't arrive.

situation: My nephew proposed to his girlfriend, and she said yes. I wasn't trying to do anything and I didn't need anything; I was just happy to know that he was happy. The situation left me feeling happy for him and proud of him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: A few days ago, it mattered a lot because I love and care for him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help or hurt; I was just happy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My Nephew.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't have any control and I didn't need any.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't have any expectations.

situation: I was in the middle of deciding whether to take voluntary redundancy or not. I was trying to achieve a balance in my career, wanting to stay in a secure role while also considering the opportunity for a potentially large payout. This whole situation left me feeling perplexed. Another important factor for me was how my wife feels about all of this.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I am deciding whether to leave my organisation whilst it's very uncertain to take voluntary redundancy and leave. This decision matters to me because I feel it's time to leave, but I also feel loyal to the organisation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I am not sure how I feel about it. I have very mixed feelings. It's put me in a challenging situation and I don't know what to do. I feel it's time to leave but I also feel loyal to the organisation. I am bitter towards this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Politics.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I'm not in control at all. Nothing is happening as expected. I am constantly reacting to changes that I have not influenced.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing is happening as expected. I am constantly reacting to changes that I have not influenced.

situation: When I heard about the school in Iran getting bombed, with over 100 school children losing their lives in the attack, it made me feel extremely sad. I was just an observer in this sad and tragic situation, but it affected me emotionally, seeing such a great loss of life. I felt sad and quite upset. Masses of children being killed and thinking how their parents must be feeling really got me close to tears. I also felt that there was going to be more tragic stories like this coming out in the following days and weeks.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about six days ago. It mattered because I do not want to see a needless loss of life, especially when it comes to children who still have so much of their lives still to live. It mattered because I do not want other children to grow up in a world where they fear they could be killed for no reason, being caught up in conflicts that they have nothing to do with.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because this is not what should be happening. Children should be happily going to school and doing the things that children should be doing. They have so much to live for and accomplish in life. I absolutely empathize with their parents and feel immense sadness that so many beautiful souls were taken away that day.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The American administration, who brought about a war without any clear objectives, strategy or timeline. Also potentially having used AI in their targeting system and hitting the wrong target.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control at all, as all I could do was observe. I had no power to influence and make any decisions that could lead to a situation like this, nor could I have any control in what could happen moving forwards.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The situation itself was unexpected and the aftermath was deeply tragic and sad.

situation: My dad had to have a hospital procedure, and I was trying to stay calm and keep him calm too. The whole situation left me feeling very stressed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Monday. It mattered a lot to me because he is family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me stressed. Nothing helped me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control as there was nothing I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected.

situation: I recently received a letter from the hospital, and I was shocked because it used words like 'urgent.' I only read the letter online and didn't get my physical copy, which made me panic. I needed an explanation because it was quite scary. The whole situation left me feeling disregarded and unimportant. It was important for me to express my emotions and upset, so I found the right person to speak to. They conducted investigations for me and then explained everything in a phone call.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me as this is my health, and I've had bad health in the past, so it's important that I feel looked after.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me due to the emotion it caused, but it helped me stand up for myself and complain about the treatment I received.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was my consultant who was responsible, and he admitted this to me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: At first, I didn't feel in control, and I still don't feel totally in control as these sorts of things leave you feeling vulnerable. I felt in control when trying to sort it out, but I should never have been put into this position in the first place.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think they went as expected. I would have liked a better response from my hospital in terms of their contact with me, but as I was in that situation, however not nice it was, I guess it met my expectations.

situation: I went to get my eyes tested because I needed a new prescription for glasses. I thought it was going to be a simple procedure, and then I'd be able to get new glasses. But instead, I learned that I have cataracts. It left me feeling set behind, like it's just another thing I have to add to my list of things to deal with. Getting old sucks, and it feels like it's another setback.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot because I'm trying to get my health together and it's taking longer than expected.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: In the short run it doesn't help me because it adds to my growing list of things that need to get done. However, I guess it was better to find out now than later.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Age and time. It's just a natural part of aging.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Nope, I didn't feel like I was in control because I can't control the aging process.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nope, I didn't expect to deal with cataracts. I thought I was finally going to get a new pair of glasses. Done and over.

situation: I met up with my relatives after not seeing them for just over a year. I was really anxious before the meeting because in the past, they've been extremely critical of me, and I was anticipating more of the same. Even though they didn't say anything negative this time, all those past experiences came rushing back to my mind and affected me even after the meeting. I only went because I didn't want to let my partner down and didn't want things to be any more awkward. I just didn't want to be criticized, but because of those past experiences, I was so on my guard that I couldn't relax. Initially, I thought it went okay, but over the next couple of days, I started to process it, and it brought up a lot of past emotions. It's made me feel like things will always be awkward, and it's got me wondering whether I should move further afield.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event matters a lot to me because I do not want things to be awkward for my partner, but I cannot be myself around these people. It makes me question a lot, as past experiences come up every time I meet them, leading me to wonder whether I should not see them again.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: There were no positives. I felt anxious before and after the meeting, and even almost a week later, I am still going over it and wondering if living so close is a bad idea.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that because of how they have spoken to me in the past, I am struggling to get over this. They have intentionally left me out of things over the most recent years, which weighs on my mind.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I struggle to feel in control when we meet up, which is part of the problem. They ask me about things I have a hard time talking about and speak to me like they haven't known me for 20 years. Sometimes they are kind, which lures me into a false sense of feeling like they are safe people to confide in, which is very confusing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Mostly things went as I expected, but I was worked up prior because I wondered whether they would be rude, so I had my guard up. I did not come across as my authentic self, which bothers me.

situation: I recently found out my mom has cancer, and it's been affecting my daily life. I'm trying to support her because she's really scared, and I need her to feel supported, and myself too. It's left me feeling very upset because it's going to be a long battle, and she can either get better or worse. What's important to me is making sure we do everything we can to help her recover and beat the cancer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened 1 week ago and matters the world to me. I want to make sure my mom beats this.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I found out my mom is sick and suffering.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She smoked for many years and we think that is what caused it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I have no control over the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as good as they could go considering the circumstances.

situation: I needed to tell my mother something that might upset her. I was trying to think of the best way to tell her to cause the least amount of distress. The whole situation left me feeling nervous.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened today. It mattered a lot as I didn't want to upset my mother and I wanted the best possible outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel stressed and it made other stressors feel worse.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt fully responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did because I made a bad decision which would impact her. I could have made another decision where it wouldn't have impacted her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected where she wasn't distressed.

situation: I've been talking to this guy from another town for about four months now, and since the beginning, he's been saying he wants to meet me. He even mentioned possibly coming to see me this weekend, but I haven't heard from him at all this week, which is unusual. I used to see his band many years ago, so he's not a complete stranger, and I thought he was keen to meet up. It would have been nice to finally talk in person; I guess I thought he liked me. But now, I feel like it's the same old thing that always happens in my life, where guys keep me waiting. Honestly, I'm considering blocking his Facebook. What's frustrating is that he's been the one wanting to initiate the meet-up, but weeks go by, and he doesn't arrange anything. I know he's busy with work since he's a gardener, and the weather has been awful this winter. Still, the fact he keeps saying 'this month' or 'in the next couple of weeks' is really annoying. I'd rather he just didn't say anything about meeting up. I can't stand people who mess me about.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was last weekend he mentioned maybe coming this weekend or next. The thing is, not letting me know messes up my day, as I didn't want to plan something else, in case he was driving up.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurts, because he says one thing and doesn't follow through. When we have spoken on the phone, we chat for hours, so it just seems odd to me, like he's afraid to actually meet up.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We both are responsible for the talking, but he is responsible for not letting me know if he still is coming to see me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't now no, I thought we had a mutual understanding, but clearly he is the one controlling this situation, until I just block him and be done with it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What is unexpected, is that he usually messages me most days, and I have not heard from him since last Sunday, which seems to correlate with the time he said about coming to see me, he's running scared.

situation: My wife and I got into a huge argument, and I ended up leaving to stay in a hotel. I was sick and just trying to eat breakfast, but I was on a bit of a different schedule than she was. She got annoyed because I was in her way, and I was annoyed by her too. Things blew up pretty quickly. I felt pretty terrible afterward. I had taken sleeping medication the night before but still didn't sleep well. In the heat of the moment, I threw my food across the kitchen, and I was really disappointed in myself for doing that. Things got very heated, and she said some terrible things to me, which always hurt, but that's about it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot. We've been together for 26 years and haven't had that type of fight in a long time. It felt like a regression. We almost split up.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It wasn't any help in any sort of way. It hurt our relationship and it's taking a while to fully get over it. There's still a little tension in the house.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like I should be in control of my emotions because when I'm not that's when things escalate. So with my being sick and very tired, I lacked control.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control at all. I don't throw things or get that upset. I could see myself doing these things but I couldn't control them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: She asked me to leave in a not very nice way and I was happy to leave in the moment. This was sort of expected. Later that evening after we calmed down we at least spoke about it. I also expected this outcome.

situation: I met with some old friends for a drink, hoping we would share some memories and have a good day. It was important to me that I was there for them and listened to how they have been recently. The whole experience left me feeling warm and happy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I met with some old friends for a drink and a catch-up. It mattered to me because it helped me reconnect and share some recent life events.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by allowing me to reconnect and share some recent life events.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The loving friendship we have is responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control because I could say or do as I please.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected.

situation: My horse suddenly developed lameness, and I was really worried about what he had done. I needed to know what was wrong with him and how to make it better. The situation left me feeling sad and scared. I just needed him to get better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Tuesday, and it mattered a lot to me as my horse is important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as I didn't know what was wrong with him or how to help him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There was no one responsible for it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I didn't have the resources to know how to help him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, the vet arrived to see him and made a plan.

situation: My mum got taken to the hospital and admitted to ICU. She had been sick for about a week and wasn't eating or drinking, which made her very weak. My brother had to arrange for her to go to the hospital to be put on a drip for her fluids and to have her potassium and sodium levels raised. I wanted her to get better. I felt scared because I didn't know she was as ill as she turned out to be and didn't know if she was going to get better or not. I also had to deal with my brother, who is someone I don't get on with and don't like being around. That, too, made me anxious.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot because it's my mum and I care about her. It felt like it was all happening very suddenly so it was shocking.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I was very anxious for a few days and I imagined several horrible scenarios that might be the outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt kind of responsible because I didn't take my mum that seriously when she told me how ill she was. I also think my mum herself was kind of responsible for not seeking help sooner. And I feel like my brother was partly responsible because he talks about watching out for our mum and monitoring how well she is taking care of herself but he doesn't really do that.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt completely out of control. This felt like a situation which just erupted out of nowhere and I had no say over it. I didn't even feel I had a say over what I should do in response because my mind was bogged down with what was the 'right' thing to do. For example, on the night my mum was taken to hospital, I went home rather than waiting there with her. I felt like maybe I was a bad person for doing that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I thought she might be put on an IV drip to improve her hydration and maybe some antibiotics, so I imagined maybe she would stay in overnight. I never expected that she would get admitted to ICU.

situation: I found myself quite emotional when I learned that a relative had taken unwell and had to be admitted to the hospital. He had gone outdoors, became unwell, and it turned out he had a serious medical condition that needed urgent treatment; otherwise, he would die. It was urgent that he was visited and we got him the right support. The situation left me feeling overwhelmed, concerned, and worried. Nothing else was important—just getting the help needed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it was very concerning and family is important.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it was scary, the thought of a family member being seriously unwell or passing away.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nothing was particularly responsible for this. It was a situation that could not have been predicted.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt slightly in control of getting help, etc., but other than that, everything else felt outwith my control because emotional support is all that could be provided.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected because treatment was received and recovery was a thing.

situation: My four-month-old puppy suddenly became very sick after eating something he shouldn't have. I wanted to make him feel better as soon as possible, which meant we needed to go to the vet for x-rays and medication. At first, I was anxious and afraid, but as we went through the treatments, I started to feel grateful and relieved. It was also important to me to consider my partner's feelings during the whole episode.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The health of my pup meant the world to me. He has become a member of our little family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: We were afraid for the puppy's life and health but now we are reassured that we can respond to an emergency situation regarding our puppy capably.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My partner and I were primarily responsible for not properly training our puppy to eat certain things.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I felt like I was primarily an observer due to not knowing how to respond to the situation before visiting the vet.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I always imagine the worst in the beginnings of such situations, but after we got some insight as to what was happening most things went as expected.

situation: I had some time alone and decided to watch a film for entertainment. As I was watching, some music came on that made me well up with emotions. It was based upon sadness and loss, and I cried and cried. The music unexpectedly brought up deep emotions related to loss within my family, making me feel incredibly sad. However, I felt that the release through crying made me feel slightly better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Saturday evening when I was alone at home. It mattered a lot because it's important to deal with feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was a release in some ways but in others brought up sad feelings. The emotional release was uplifting but the memories were sad to relive.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I'm uncertain whether there's a correct answer to this. I had a parent who died of older age.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I suppose I could have turned off the film and its music. But I had time alone and was free to explore my feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was as much as I could have expected.

situation: I met up with some old friends from my past at a beerex and spent the evening chatting about the past and what we are doing today. We all got something positive from the evening and decided we would like to repeat it the following year. I felt rather good because not only did we all enjoy ourselves, I felt particularly good knowing I contributed in the past to their being friends today. I also had my brother there and my best friend who also knew these people, and they also enjoyed the evening.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered as I hardly ever see these people and it is always good to catch up.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It reminded me that I helped contribute to other peoples development when I was very much younger. This was a positive contribution to making our community better.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was all down to me who suggested the gathering.
appraisal_reasoning.control: The fact that they all turned up was a tribute to me and although I had no control over their arrival I was always there to meet them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Originally we had to sit at a table near the live music but this was not conducive to conversation so we eventually moved to the quiet room and after that we converse with no loud music in the background.

situation: I was awarded a promotion that I had put a lot of effort into achieving. I had been unsure whether I would get the promotion, so I was trying to secure it by impressing my boss and senior management. When I finally got the promotion, it left me feeling shocked, surprised, proud, and grateful. It reassured me that I was capable of achieving something which I previously had doubts about.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened two weeks ago. It mattered a great deal to me because securing the promotion would allow me to take the next step up in my career, along with extra responsibilities and a pay increase. It allowed me to earn the respect of my peers.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The promotion helped me by opening doors in my career, to take the next step up in my job and field of work. It also helped me by securing extra income, which will be helpful in my financial future. It did not hurt me in any way.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was mostly responsible for the success in achieving the promotion. I was successfully able to demonstrate my skills and suitability for the role in a way that convinced senior management in my company. My line manager was also responsible in helping to convince management that I was the right choice for the promotion.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was totally in control. I tried my best to control what I could, but I also felt that much of the decision and timeframe was out of my control. I had to wait and see what would happen.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went mostly as expected. I felt I was a strong choice for the promotion and that I would ultimately be successful. However some elements of the process were unexpected, such as the time it took and points where not all information was communicated to me.

situation: This week, a friend's husband was taken to the hospital urgently, and it made me very emotional. I was trying to offer support to my friend and be there for them emotionally. I also wanted to ensure that my friend's children were taken care of while they were in the hospital. The situation left me feeling apprehensive and very nervous as it was a 'touch and go' situation that was so nerve-wracking and intense.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because my friend has always been very supportive to me, and I wanted to repay the kindness and be there for her and her family too.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was emotionally hurtful for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: A traffic accident was the cause of all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control of the situation, but I could offer emotional support to my friend.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, he was taken to surgery at the hospital and thankfully he survived.

situation: My baby got a cough for the first time, and he's only 7 months old. When he coughs, he cries because it sounds very painful and rough. I wanted my baby to get well, so I took him to the doctor to get checked. After the doctor's assessment and advice, I felt reassured. The doctor said it's most likely a viral issue, and his ears and throat looked okay, even though he has a temperature. The doctor prescribed antibiotics just in case he doesn't improve. I'm glad my baby is getting better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me as this is about my baby's health and he cannot help himself, it is down to me to help him as much as possible.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because my baby is hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was most responsible, as his mother.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel fully in control as my baby cannot communicate with me about what is happening to him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected, my baby is now getting better.

situation: One of my special educational needs students won an award during the school assembly, and seeing his face light up brought tears to my eyes. I had put his name forward to recognize the positive changes I had noticed in him recently. I felt immensely proud of him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me, not just to recognize his efforts, but also the efforts of myself in being able to get him to a place where he is hitting achievements.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by reminding me that I am good at my job and always have my student's best interests at heart.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The student made the positive changes to his behavior and effort, however, it was myself that had to show up each day and instill the school values.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because without my consistency, it wouldn't have paid off.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected, but what was unexpected was how happy the student was. He had the biggest smile on his face for the rest of the assembly.

situation: I work with children who have Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), and this week was particularly draining because I was very tired due to lack of sleep. I was trying to get the kids to focus, but I was struggling myself because of how exhausted I felt. The whole situation was stressful, and I really wanted to leave work, but I knew they would be short-staffed if I did.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday of last week. It mattered to me because I felt incapable and like I was letting the kids and the team down.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt incapable and like I was letting the kids and the team down.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because of lack of sleep.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected.

situation: I just lost an old friend about two weeks ago, and it was a complete shock because he was fit and healthy. We were very close as we grew up together, and he was younger than me, which makes it even harder for me to get over. I've been trying to piece together the memories we had and made together, and what I really needed was emotional support from my friends and especially my own family. I felt shocked and surprised, with a deep sense of loss and finality, knowing I won't be able to speak to my friend again. His family were not the friendliest to me for a long time, and I don't think they ever will be. I would have liked to mend some fences during this time, but it never happened.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened almost 2 weeks ago. It was the death of a very close, almost family friend, so it was a very important and particularly sad time for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did hurt very much as we were very close. Meeting some of the family who saw I was hurting helped me as they almost gave me their condolences.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was all both mine and my friend's doing as we never made much of an attempt to mend the hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt totally out of the loop as I had not spoken to any of the family for a long time and it was awkward.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went very well although there were some rumblings of bad feelings from some of the family members, so I was pleasantly surprised at the outcome.

situation: I tried a new yoga class and really enjoyed it. I wanted to do some exercise and also have some time to myself to deeply relax. The class itself was great, and after the relaxation session at the end, I felt completely and utterly relaxed and positive. I felt at peace and more positive overall. Another important part of the experience was enjoying the social connections I have made in the class.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event actually happened this morning. It mattered a great deal to me as I have had a particularly stressful week.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The session provided some physical activity which is good for my body. It also provided some calming activity for my mind and some relaxation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I was lucky to have an excellent instructor and I was also responsible as it was my decision to attend the class.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel in control to a certain extent as I could choose my own level of participation. The instructor also had control as she designed the session and delivered it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think things did go as I expected. I did not expect to feel quite so calm and deeply relaxed by the end of the class.

situation: My manager had a lot of negative feedback about my performance, and it seriously made me cry. I wanted to run away and just quit my job because I could not stand listening to the negative words my manager had to say about me. I felt very betrayed, almost like disappointed in the organization that my worth was not seen, that nobody had ever any positive words about me, that everything I got from people was negative. It made me feel unappreciated and incompetent. After the feedback, I felt numb and confused; it made no sense to me. It upset me that my manager seemed to hold no respect for me as a human, and every word was rather yelled at me than said normally.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because my job is important to me. I rely on it to have finances to survive, and I constantly evolved and tried my best in everything. Despite my effort, I was seen as a stupid person with no strengths, so I felt defeated. It mattered a lot because it is a job I enjoy doing, but I do not like dealing with my manager. I have to because my manager may get me fired in some way, possibly by speaking ill about me. I am a perfectionist, so I strive to do well in everything I take on.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me; it made me think I should look for another job, and that is a time waste. It also makes me feel unstable both financially and mentally because I don't have a consistent job. Every job I do within my job is different, so it's always a question of whether I can do it fully.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was my manager; nobody else in my job treats me like my manager does. But maybe partially me if I was that awful at my job?
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control. Everything I said my manager twisted or implied I lied about, or that whatever I did I had to do faster, better. I should know better, and that I had no motivation to get better. So I felt zero control in the conversation and in my job during that time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it did not go as expected. I tried my hardest to complete a job to hundred percent, but my manager always finds something to complain about, so of course during our interaction it was the same.

situation: This week has been really tough for me. A close family member suddenly became seriously ill and was taken into the hospital, even though they were okay just a few days before. I was trying to get to them as quickly as I could, but I was working away from home, which made it difficult. Not being able to reach them as fast as I wanted left me feeling really upset. On top of that, it was important for me to get back to help their children during this time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened this week and it mattered greatly to me because a close family member collapsed in front of their children, which was incredibly distressing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me more because I was unable to get back quickly, which left me feeling really upset. I had to get other people involved to cover my work meetings, adding to the stress.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Illness is something that happens, and I feel there is nobody to blame here.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control initially, but it took others getting involved for me to regain a sense of control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things worked out okay in the end as I was able to get back.

situation: I passed my final probation at work, which means I'm now an early career teacher and can move up the pay scale. This whole experience has left me feeling proud and relieved. It was really important to me to maintain my high standards throughout the probation period, and the pay rise is also a significant factor for me. Teaching is my passion, and I find immense joy in inspiring and educating my students. Being able to continue doing what I love while advancing in my career is incredibly fulfilling.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was today. I was in my classroom. It mattered a great deal to me because it was a moment that was long awaited.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me in my career, I am now an established teacher. If anything could hurt me from it is the fact I won’t be as cheap to employ anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like my hard work and commitment was the most responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did, however external observations made me doubt the outcome occasionally.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected. I expected to pass my ECT course.

situation: My granny passed away two weeks ago, and I've been feeling really sad. I just want to feel better and remember the good times we had together. I miss her a lot, but I'm also happy she's out of pain now. I need comfort and support to help me hold onto those happy memories and find solace in them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 weeks ago. It mattered a huge deal to me as I won't see her again.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me to know she was out of pain, but it hurt to not see her again.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nature.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No - it's nature.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes.

situation: Scenario: My best friend's mum passed away, and it was incredibly sad. There wasn't anything I could do, but I wished she could have stayed alive longer and hopefully recovered. I felt really bad for my friend, and it brought back memories of my own mum's death. It was a stark reminder that life is short, and we need to make the most of it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because I felt bad for my friend, although I didn't know her mum that well personally.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as it reminded me of my mum's death.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The illness that she had is what is responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, as I had no control over events.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect her to die as quickly as she did.

situation: My friend decided that he could no longer be my friend because he has feelings for me. I wanted to be his friend, but he couldn’t just be friends. This situation left me feeling sad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because he’s been my friend for over 17 years.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was sad because I felt like it was a waste. Nothing else.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both of us.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because I couldn’t do anything about his feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I didn’t expect him to end our friendship.

situation: A friend called me distressed because she had broken up with her husband. I wanted to listen, comfort, and support my friend. It left me feeling upset for her, drained, and a little emotional. It was important to me to be there for my friend.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Monday. It mattered somewhat to me because it had a negative and distressing impact on my friend.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Emotionally hurt me. It made me feel sad for my friend being left in this way and this upset me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Her other half.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not as it was my friend's feelings and I could not control those.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it did.

situation: I had extensive back surgery two days ago, and the nursing care was totally absent. There was no understanding or compassion, and the procedures were poor. I was in tears and ended up leaving earlier than I should have because I felt I could care better for myself at home. I needed to be in control of my pain and wanted someone to ask me how severe it was. Instead, one nurse decided that two paracetamol would be just fine, which left me frustrated beyond belief. I even hoped he would end up in my situation one day. As a retired nurse, I'm ashamed of what passes for care in hospitals now. A used bed pan was left in the toilet as if it was beneath someone to remove it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened two days ago. It mattered greatly to me because without adequate pain relief, I could not sleep or relax to help the recovery process.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This experience hurt me by making me afraid and unwilling to ever go to a hospital again. There were other instances of poor care too, like raising my bed to remove a dressing and moving the side trolley out of the way, then just going, leaving me unable to reach the floor to get out of bed and reach my water. I could have fallen and also succumbed to dehydration.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The nursing staff were most responsible for all of this. It's shocking to say as I am a nurse, but we were not trained to these poor standards.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was weak, immobile, and helpless. I was unable to advocate for myself as I did not want to point out failings and make a bad situation worse.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. I was expecting to have patient-controlled analgesia, not have an inexperienced youth decide what I needed without even asking me.

situation: My wife went to the hospital because we thought she had a chest infection, but it turned out to be stage 4b lung cancer. We were both distressed and cried, feeling as though the bottom had fallen out of our world. I needed some answers, specifically whether there is a treatment that can control the cancer. Miraculously, there is a treatment called a TKI inhibitor, and I'm hoping to get my wife on a trial. It was devastating. I felt as though I was grieving for the loss of my wife even though she is still alive. The important thing is knowing how long she has and what her quality of life is going to be.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened this week. It really mattered. I've known my wife for over 30 years. I will be lost without her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It certainly has not helped. In terms of hurt, I've had to change the way I work so that I can give my wife maximum support. I fear I will become mentally and physically exhausted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible. Life is a lottery and everyone has a 1 in 2 chance of getting cancer. Unfortunately my wife lost on life's toss of the coin.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control then but I am going to get in control by finding the right care and medication for my wife.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Clearly, it's new and raw so we could have never have expected that one day everything is ok and another it is a complete disaster. But we have to hold onto hope, positivity and grim determination.

situation: Me and my partner had an argument and almost broke up. I got so frustrated with how he is and his lack of support that I just snapped. The whole situation left me feeling just drained and fed up. I feel trapped into staying with him because we have a 1-year-old.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered because it is our lives.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It makes me feel like I am mental and unreasonable because he makes me doubt myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We completely differ on our views which means we clash.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, as my partner wants to stay together. It is me that does not.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well eventually he just wears me down so much that I agree to staying together.

situation: I was talking to someone I hadn't spoken to in years because of a fallout. During our conversation, they brought up the past event where they had spoken to me badly, which was really disrespectful. They apologized, and although it upset me to be reminded of the original event, I was glad because it had been playing on my mind. I wanted an apology without having to ask for it, and they did apologize. I wanted them to recognize that their behavior was wrong. I wanted to move on from it, acknowledge it, forgive, and move forward. It was important to me that there was no anger in the conversation from either side. I wanted understanding and empathy on both sides, which was more or less what happened, as I never thought I would bring it up to them again. In the end, I felt sad, but also relieved that it wasn't brushed under the carpet and was resolved.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The initial fallout happened about 4 years ago, and me speaking to them about it this week. It did matter quite a lot as the previous event was on my mind and I feel it had to be spoken about to move on, because it might lead to resentment if I keep speaking to them and not resolve the issue or elephant in the room.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me, because of the words that occurred and hurt from the fallout. It helped a lot to speak; I felt a relief and happy to speak about with forgiveness on both sides.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was the other person apologizing and saying sorry for their part of what happened, and both of us for discussing it and putting the past behind us.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did as they allowed me to express how I felt without defense or interruption. I said what I wanted to say and did not hide how I felt.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did go as I expected, the issue was talked about and I wanted to move forward and regain perspective on the current events and be mindful that in order to move on I need to forget the hurt and realize that I can't hold onto past issues.

situation: My father has pretty advanced dementia and generally can't communicate or remember past events. I was just trying to have a conversation with him, even though I knew going in that he wasn't likely going to be able to communicate back to me. However, the last time I talked with him, he very clearly asked me if I remembered when we went ice skating together when I was a kid. When I told him I did, he said 'good, I loved it.' It was a really special and emotional moment for me because it felt like I had him back for a fleeting moment. I felt a mix of emotions. I felt really happy at first because I did get a glimpse of the father that I know and love. However, I also felt sadness because I didn't want the moment to go so fast - I wanted to keep talking with him like that.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened two days ago and it was a very impactful moment because I don't get to have clear communication with my father like that anymore. So when it does happen, and it is a special memory on top of it, it is really important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I don't think it hurt me at all. It did help because it gave me another chance to connect with my father even though it was so short.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My father was the one responsible even though I don't think he had any control over it. His clear communication of the memory is what made the moment special.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I definitely was not in control. I couldn't make my father remember or communicate in that moment. I also couldn't control how long the moment lasted.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I definitely did not expect my father to communicate such a clear memory to me because he hasn't been able to for over a year.

situation: My daughter was accepted back into high school this week after being homeschooled for approximately six months. We tried to get her into the school of her choice because she was missing the social aspect of friends and sports, and we finally received our offer this week. I was elated and nervous for her, with my emotions being up and down. It was definitely what she wants.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened on Tuesday last week and it really matters as she was bullied at her previous school so I understand going back will be a challenge.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped because it's exactly what she is after.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both equally I had to think about what was best for her in this situation and also take into consideration what she wanted.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because ultimately the decision lies with the council.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: So far yes.

situation: I went overdrawn and didn't have enough money to fix the issue. I wasn't really trying to do anything specific, but I definitely wanted or needed more money in my bank account. The whole situation left me feeling stressed. On top of that, I felt guilty because I hadn't been responsible enough.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me somewhat because I knew I would be charged overdraft fees if I couldn't put money into my bank account. It wasn't a huge deal though.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me slightly because it means I will probably be charged a late fee for a payment I wasn't able to make.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible for it because I wasn't more careful with my money.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control because I didn't have a way of resolving the situation when it happened.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: A charge that had taken my account into overdraft was reversed which I wasn't expecting.

situation: I had a medical appointment because I was in pain, and I wanted to find out what was causing it. During the appointment, I found out that I'm too overweight for any kind of treatment. They tried to do an ultrasound, but it couldn’t get a sufficient picture, and I can't access an MRI because of my weight. This whole situation left me feeling upset, anxious, and let down. I had sought help 4 years ago, and it feels like people started listening only when it was too late to help.
