appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about 6 days ago. It was important to seek the diagnosis; however, the fact I cannot access one has left me feeling despondent, like nobody cares and the system isn’t for people like me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was meant to help but instead it hurt. It removed my sense of hope of resolve.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It’s me isn’t it. I let myself be ignored by the medical help, I didn’t push hard enough for treatment and diagnostics, and I let myself put on an exorbitant amount of weight.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I was at the mercy of medical help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I got an appointment which was good. The fact that a diagnosis or treatment aren’t on the cards was unexpected.

situation: Me and my family had booked a trip to Disneyland Paris, flying from Edinburgh to Paris with Air France. We were all set for a fun family holiday, with only two days planned at the theme park. When we got to the airport, we boarded the plane and were just about to take off when the flight was cancelled, completely ruining our trip. I felt very, very angry and heartbroken at the same time. It was especially upsetting for our kids because we had surprised them with the trip that morning, and they were so excited, only to be told they couldn't go.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last weekend. It was our first trip there so it mattered a lot! Creating memories with our kids that we couldn’t then do.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: We were upset for the hopes and dreams of our kids.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Air France. They cancelled the flight.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We had no control and felt we had no control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: We couldn’t go! It was unexpected that the flight would get cancelled!

situation: I arranged for a friend to be assessed by his local council at home because he's struggling with his health and mobility. The council set up for someone to go out and assess his mobility and general well-being at home. The person who was going to his home called me to let me know when she'd be going, so I told my friend, and he was okay with the appointment. When the lady went to my friend's home, he didn't answer the door, so she called me and asked me to ring him. I did, and he said he was still in bed. I told him the lady was outside and asked if he would answer the door; he said he would. This was an important assessment. Five minutes later, she called me back to say he hadn't answered the door, so I rang him, and he ignored my calls. I had to call the woman and apologize for him. I know my friend needs help in the home with mobility aids, like a shower chair, handrails, perching stools, things like that. The lady would assess him and tell him what was needed and get the aids delivered to him. If he needed a carer, she would have discussed this too. I felt angry because he asked me to do this. I know he needs the help, and he couldn't be bothered to get out of bed. His well-being is important. I know he is an alcoholic, and he takes tablets for vertigo which affect his balance. He has already had falls. I was trying to support him to the best of my ability.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because the man lives on his own, and he has two sons who hardly see him. I have spoken to one son, but he hasn't done what I asked him to do, which was to check up on his father a few times a week by phone because of his falls. I tried to help him as much as I could; he needs a carer, and he also has accidents with incontinence and soiling himself.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because he wanted the help, but when it came, he refused it. I am disabled myself, and I became friends with this man by accident really, but I have tried to help as much as I can.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Alcohol is responsible for this. I know my friend was probably hung over from the day before and just couldn't be bothered to answer the door.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was not in control of the situation because I was at home. The assessor who attended rang me, so she thought I could help, but it was out of my hands.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it did not go as expected. I did not expect my friend to not answer the door; he had previously assured me he would, that's why I didn't attend.

situation: My mother decided to have a breakdown because I didn’t want to do what she wanted me to do for my birthday. Instead, I chose something that would have less pressure for everyone. She wanted me and my partner to go to hers for a buffet on or around our birthdays. Knowing how she can be, I decided I’d rather not do that and do something that is less pressure for her and me and will less likely cause an argument. She came at me with arguments saying I’ve changed and that she doesn’t feel emotionally safe around me. It left me feeling exhausted and depressed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was last Monday a week ago, it didn’t matter to me at all in truth, because I’m so sick of her making arguments like this.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Because it’s emotionally draining she always does this. It drained my energy emotionally and socially at the beginning of the day and ruined the rest of my day.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My mother.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because it’s impossible to control the emotions of others.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was exactly as expected.

situation: In the middle of the night, my daughter jumped out of her cot, and I had to rush her to A&E because I wasn't sure how she landed. This was really distressing at the time. I just wanted to make sure she was okay and didn't have a concussion. The whole situation left me feeling very stressed and traumatized. On top of that, I felt guilty because the cot was obviously too high and should have been lowered beforehand.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal that she was not hurt. It happened in the middle of the night in the dark.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt guilty that I should have lowered the cot previously. I was stressed that she had really hurt herself and could potentially have a head injury.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was the person most responsible for this happening.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control when it happened, but I immediately took control of the situation and took her to A&E.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't have any expectations initially.

situation: This past week turned out to be good. I've been feeling nervous about my financial situation because I haven't had enough work from my regular clients lately. The freelance job market has changed quite a bit and become way more competitive, which added to my worries. Out of the blue, an old client contacted me and asked if I was available for new projects in the next few months. This work came at a good time, and I'm very thankful for it. Even though I'm grateful, I still have the problem of getting new clients and need to devise a strategy for landing them, which is not something I'm good at. It's important for me to remember that my work is exceptional, and that's why I'm still in business. But I have to move out of my comfort zone of passive acquisition and develop a diversified game plan for landing more work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal as it helped me not to spiral into more worry about my future. I think it grounded me in thinking that I've got this, I just need to persevere.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me gain confidence in myself and my work, despite the challenging circumstances of the economic landscape.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well, it was good fortune that the client contacted me when they did, but I felt like I'm responsible for having a good body of work that at least some people find valuable.
appraisal_reasoning.control: At first I didn't, because the employment situation and overall economy doesn't feel stable. It's greater than me and my efforts, so that makes me not feel totally in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did seem to fall into place, but the scope of the work to be done has not been defined, so I don't know if this will be enough. My main goal still remains to develop stronger client acquisition skills.

situation: My son was deployed to Washington DC with the National Guard, and I was scared for him. I felt uncertain about him going to DC, worried for his safety, especially since two guards have been killed working there. I needed reassurance that everything was going to be okay, someone to tell me to calm down and let him go. The situation left me feeling scared, lost, and terrified. It's important to me that my son is safe and happy, and I just want him to be okay.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened about a week ago. My son is my pride and joy so I care deeply for him. I wanted to make sure he was going to be ok being deployed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Knowing that he was going somewhere that is unrest worried me. The situation hurt me. I had the biggest amount of anxiety.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The terrorist in our country is who is responsible for this. My son wouldn't have to be deployed if people would act right. It's irritating that people protest and act a fool.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not even close to being in control. The Governor of Florida was the one that ordered him to go to DC. I had no say so in the matter. He has a contract with the National Guard that he must honor.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected. Everything has turned out fine and he is having the best time working in DC. He is a deputy there now and he likes it. He said most people have been nice. There are a few that harass him while he works but most are kind.

situation: I was in a therapy session when my therapist informed me that next week would be our last session. I felt so emotional at the thought of saying goodbye to her. I was trying not to cry and trying to cope with my overwhelming feelings about not speaking to her every week anymore. This news left me dreading the next session because of it. I've gotten a lot out of therapy and really thrown myself into it, and it's been amazing. It's bittersweet that it's ending.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Friday and mattered to me because I have gotten a lot out of therapy, as I was feeling very mentally unwell before.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me gain confidence in myself again.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both me and my therapist were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I reached out, but we both have gotten us to this point, indicating a sense of shared control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole thing was way better than I expected.

situation: One of my close friends, who has a partner and a child, has just separated from her partner. I've known them both as a couple for a long time. I was trying to provide support and help for my friend, but I find it difficult. I felt like I couldn't quite help like I wanted. I didn't know what to advise or how to console them properly. I was also feeling conflicted, as I know both members of the relationship well.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I was incredibly shocked. It matters as it will fundamentally change how I interact with these people.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't really hurt me, it was more empathy for them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There is no one to blame really, relationships end. It is just very sad.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I was not in control. It is not my situation to be in control of though, I am just an observer.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think things are going as expected, but it is still very sad.

situation: I received an offer to study medicine this September, and it's something I'm really happy about, especially after facing quite a few difficulties over the last 10 years. I was trying to get an offer to study medicine, and it was a big goal for me. The whole process left me feeling ambivalent. On one hand, I was determined to secure a place, but on the other, I sometimes felt stressed and withdrawn trying to focus on this. It was important for me to be confident in myself throughout the application process.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a great deal as I had always wanted to study medicine as a teenager but circumstances in life got in the way.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did make me feel somewhat depressed as I thought life was pitted against me as things never seemed to go my way. In some ways it did allow me to question my motives for studying medicine.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well my mother became ill and needed caring for.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt somewhat in control but there are only so many hours in a day so I couldn't really focus on anything else.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as expected with regard to having little time to spare, but I never truly expected I would end up being able to study medicine after all of these years.

situation: I was asked to commit to overtime at work on a day that I really didn't want to work. I wanted to refuse and say I couldn't commit to the overtime because I prioritize my kids, and they had clubs scheduled at the same time. I felt very under pressure and obliged to do the overtime, and it made me really upset that I was being steamrolled into it. I wanted to be clear with my boss that I would be willing to help out with future overtime if I was free to do so.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This mattered to me a lot as I felt under pressure to agree to doing the overtime when I really didn't want to let my children down by not being there for them at their activities.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me realize that I would always put my children first and even though I found it difficult to say NO, I did what was best for me and my family.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think my work had assumed that I would agree to working this particular shift even though it is outwith my regular hours and that I would be obliged due to my contract.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I was in control enough to say No but only because I had agreed to work a date later in the year.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think the outcome was as best as it could be for me.

situation: I went to the doctor with my daughter because she's struggling to eat a variety of food. I was hoping the doctor would give us some advice or refer us to a specialist for eating disorders, so we could get some expert help. Instead, the doctor told her she needed to try harder and said if she didn't, she wouldn't have a partner, have kids, or a job. Even after I expressed my concern that she might have an eating disorder, he dismissed it. I was very angry and felt hopeless. I also worried about my daughter and how it might have affected her listening to what the doctor said. I hoped that after going to the doctor, my daughter would feel as though she had been listened to and that there was hope for her to improve, but she was left feeling deflated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot as I wanted to help my daughter to feel better about what she was going through and that she felt listened to and supported.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because she wasn't listened to and it made her feel worse. She already struggles with her mental health and I don't want her to think that she hasn't got a future if she doesn't eat as she doesn't need the extra pressure. It's made me worried how this is going to affect her in the long term.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The doctor was most responsible as he was the professional that we had put our faith and trust in and he sat there and lectured her for 20 minutes and made her feel worthless and that she didn't have a future. He could have been more supportive and listened to us more and directed us more efficiently.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control as whenever I tried to interject he just disregarded what I had to say or he would just turn his attention to my daughter and not listen to me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected. I was hoping that he would refer me to someone that would be able to help but he just asked us to go back to him in a few weeks time and hoped in that time that she would have started to eat more as he had requested. I thought at the very least he would have given us some suggestions on help that was out there but he just thought that she was being picky with her food and not that she has an eating disorder.

situation: My partner and I had a chat about our future plans, and it made me really happy to know she thinks that way about us. I'm not always confident in relationships, even though we've been together for 4 years and are very happy. So, for her to talk about next year and beyond feels like a vote of confidence. It left me feeling very happy and wanted. It's just good to know she feels that way.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened at her house while we were talking about visiting family and friends next year. It mattered to me because I'm not so good at feeling settled about the future, and this conversation provided reassurance.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I am not so good at feeling settled about the future, and this conversation provided reassurance.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She was the driver of this conversation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not need to be in control; we were speaking in a collaborative way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was a surprise to hear this, but in a very good way.

situation: I look after some elderly patients, and recently I found out that one of them had died. It was surprising to me because, even though he was old, his death wasn't expected. I felt surprised and slightly sad about the news. I decided to call the family to offer my condolences.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened recently, and it mattered to me because I visit the care home weekly to review the patients and had lots of dealings with him. I thought he was a lovely man.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation made me think about life, but also that he wasn’t suffering anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It all went as expected.

situation: I was petting my cat and feeling very emotional because she is so cute and furry. I felt really happy while petting her. I wanted a little emotional support, and petting the cat gave it to me. Afterward, I felt satisfied and relieved. Everything was perfect, and I felt great afterward.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week and it made me feel good.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt loved and supported by my cat. It made me feel calm.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like the cat was most responsible for me feeling good.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control since I could stop petting her at any time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I got the love I wanted and she was happy as well.

situation: I was planning to attend a job interview, but I decided not to go ahead with it because I felt it was unscrupulous. I wanted to give myself some hope and a safety net of sorts for the future, but the whole situation left me feeling incredibly overwhelmed, to be honest. It's important to mention that I generally feel a little overwhelmed with life at the minute, so that context is important as well.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Wednesday morning, although concern over the validity of the offer emerged the previous evening (Tuesday evening). It mattered to me because I generally feel a little overwhelmed with life at the minute, and this situation added to that feeling.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by delivering yet another blow to my confidence.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I blame myself and the situation I am in, although I do feel the job market is very fake in general at the moment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was losing control, metaphorically drowning.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: As it stands now, the situation isn't totally resolved, but that particular aspect of it is over.

situation: I hung out with a new friend and had a great sit-down. I really wanted to get to know them more one-on-one and just hang out. It made me feel happy and like we were on the same wavelength. Getting to unwind after a long work week and venting while we can also relate was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I'm a social person and finding someone to get along with can be rare these days as you get older.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me see I can make and maintain having friends, I can put myself out there.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I would say both of us, me and my friend.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did because it felt easy to talk with them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected, it was positive overall.

situation: I was having a conversation with someone, and they mentioned that someone else had said something negative about having two boys instead of girls, which is what I have. I didn't really want anything from the situation; I never had any hang-ups about having boys until that moment. But hearing that left me feeling sad and hurt, realizing that some people think having boys is less than having girls. It was especially important to me because the person who said it is supposed to be close to me, and now I feel sad about it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The conversation made me feel really sad, and it was important because it affected me emotionally. I don't know why it was so important, just that it made me feel that way.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt my children were considered less than having girls.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The person who said it was most responsible for these feelings arising from the conversation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control of my emotions or the situation itself because it was said about having boys generally and not mine specifically.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected that it would have been said, particularly by the person who said it as they’re so close to me.

situation: I failed a driving test that I had been preparing for a long time. I was very nervous and unfortunately failed during an important moment in the test. I still don't have my full driving license, and I feel disappointed and felt very low when it happened. It was important for me to pass my driving test because I wanted to drive a car to my place of work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week, last Tuesday. It mattered a lot to me because I had been working hard on my driving lessons.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt I had let myself down. However, I felt relieved when the test was finished, and the positive is that I won't feel as nervous next time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that only I was responsible for this. I was responsible for the result of that driving test.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt that I was in control but let my nerves get the best of me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected to pass my test so the result was a surprise. But ultimately I am responsible for that result.

situation: A colleague at work had been suffering from depression and tried to take her life two weeks ago. Our whole office is devastated because we didn't realize the extent and depth of her pain. I reached out to her family but didn't get a reply, and I understand that she is still in the hospital. I wanted to see if there was anything I could do to help. Initially, I was in shock because I couldn't believe what had happened. Now, I feel guilt because I feel like I should have been a better friend and work colleague. It's important to me that she knows I'm thinking about her and wishing her a full recovery. As a team, we are all hoping she can return to work when she is feeling better, and we are committed to supporting her in any way we can.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened about a fortnight ago, on a weekend. I heard about it from a friend and I was really sad to hear the news.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help at all; in fact, I was upset for days trying to make sense of it all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was to blame. She had suffered from poor mental health for a decade and I think she was just spiraling down.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control at all. I was like an insider looking in. There was nothing I could do without intruding.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole situation was unexpected. I did not foresee this happening at all.

situation: I went to a football match where my team played against a huge team that's in the top division. It was a once-in-a-lifetime event, and I felt extremely positive and proud of the team. I was trying to watch the match and really wanted to see us win. Unfortunately, we didn't win, but we gave it a very good go. Throughout the match, I felt nervous and apprehensive, worried that we were going to be battered. It was important for us to put our place on the map and give a good account of ourselves.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened this weekend, and it mattered a lot to me as the club is my number one passion in life. It was highly unlikely we would ever play them again.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me see the world in a light of joy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the team and manager were the ones most responsible, as they were the ones directly playing in the match.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I think we could offer a slight edge of control, being able to make noise and make it uncomfortable for the other team.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected; we lost but we gave it a good go and we didn't get battered.

situation: It was the birthday of a close family member who had passed away. I spent the day talking to those who cared about him, and we celebrated his life by sharing funny stories and reminiscing about things he did that made us laugh. Doing this made me feel better and less sad. However, I couldn't help but notice how sad it made his living siblings.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: His birthday was on Valentine's day. It mattered because it was the first birthday he had where he wasn't here to celebrate it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped to think back on his memory and the affect he had on his family, the good times we shared.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think he was. He had such a big personality that I couldn't help but think about his life as opposed to his death.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because, as a family, we chose whether or not grieve the day of his passing or to honor it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did go as expected. There were moments of sadness, but they didn't last. His memory was more important than his death.

situation: I watched a YouTube video of last year's finale of the Malta International Fireworks Festival and got emotional at the words spoken during intervals between rounds of fireworks. I was trying to remember how incredible it was to be there in person since it is a very happy memory. The situation left me feeling joy at the shared experience of the thousands of spectators in the crowd as well as the beautiful words that tied us together as one people.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event of watching the video was this morning as I lay in bed in a coffee thinking ahead to this year's fireworks festival in April 2026. I am beginning to plan for the event and invite friends and family to witness the spectacle I have come to really enjoy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The video helped me remember last year's competition, stood for 2 hours watching the most incredible firework display I had ever seen, interspersed with a very impressive drone show where fireworks launched from the drones themselves. The drones made shapes important symbols of Maltese culture such as the flag, a map of the islands, a knight and a Maltese cross. It made me very happy to remember how connected I felt to the strangers around me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well, a friend can take some credit for bringing up the festival and asking about dates. It spurred me to search for a high quality video of last year's finale to share with them to impress upon them the scale of the event.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I felt completely in control, I was alone with only myself making the decision to watch the video and set the goal I wished to achieve.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect to tear up at the voice over's words but otherwise, I found the video I was looking for, remembered what I wanted to remember and shared the video URL with my friend as planned.

situation: My elderly father-in-law is currently in respite care, but he's attempted to harm himself twice, so the home has told us they can't meet his needs anymore. After trying 18 different care homes, we finally found one that said they could meet his needs. Their manager assured us the cost would be less than what he's currently paying. But then we got the official quote, and it was nearly £7,000 a week—over 50% more than what he's paying now and way outside his budget. We're feeling very frustrated and tearing our hair out because we have nowhere else to go. We were trying to find a care home that could look after him with his various health issues until he dies, and at a fee he could meet with his savings and pension. We're angry and frustrated. We've wasted two weeks with the one care home that's quoting such a high figure, and the breakdown of their quote is just ridiculous. We just need to get him somewhere. The care home he's currently in seemed great and he was happy there, but he stupidly decided to try to kill himself twice, though he has neither the strength nor means to achieve his aim.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: He went into hospital just before Christmas, then respite care in the middle of January. His two attempts at self-harm were in early February, so we have been trying to find another home since then. It matters a lot because we have got to find somewhere to live his final days. He doesn't have any accommodation of his own, and our house is not suitable to care for him. But the current care home wants him out because they can't care for his mental health needs, so we are really struggling.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has meant that my wife has been left trying to ring around care homes without any luck as well as dealing with my father-in-law's demands while I try to keep our own family going. We have an autistic 21-year-old son who needs a fair bit of support. My wife is emotionally exhausted, which isn't fun to witness.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My father-in-law is most responsible for the situation. He wants to die and therefore has tried his best to injure himself, but he hasn't thought about the knock-on effects for the staff at the care home, who are lovely, or my wife.
appraisal_reasoning.control: The only control we have is ringing the other care homes in the area, but they also say no. And we obviously can't control what my father-in-law does or doesn't do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: His attempted suicides weren't expected, and the high quote wasn't expected.

situation: My granddaughter flung her arms around my neck and said, 'I love you, Nana.' In that moment, I didn't need anything else; I just wanted to enjoy what she said. It left me feeling happy and pleased that she'd expressed her love like that. It's important to me that I know I'm doing all I can to make her happy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I love her very much too. It's important to me that I know I'm doing all I can to make her happy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me realize that I'm doing the right things to be a good nana to her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that her mum was responsible for teaching her to be a loving little girl.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel I was in control because the words had come from her and I had no input in that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected and I gave her a huge hug and kiss.

situation: I found out my son is getting medically discharged from the Marines. I really want to know how soon he will be home. I'm feeling sad for him, but at the same time, I'm happy for me that he may be coming home.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened this week. It matters to me because I really want to know how soon he will be home. I'm feeling sad for him, but at the same time, I'm happy for me that he may be coming home.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helps me because I will be able to see my son more. However, I'm sad my son has to leave the Marines.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was an accident; he was injured during PT.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, it was an accident.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes.

situation: My friend insisted that I go visit her, so I agreed and started walking to her place. It's quite far, about an hour's walk. When I was almost there, she texted me saying she was going to sleep and suggested we meet next time. I was very upset and walked back home. I didn't text her back because I was upset that she just changed her mind, knowing that I had been walking a long distance already. It left me feeling like she doesn't appreciate me or respect me. Now, I've got trust issues about my friend.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened before yesterday and mattered a lot to me because I can't trust her anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by opening my eyes about how inconsiderate she can be, maybe even selfish. It hurt because I thought less selfishness of her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I was in control. I did not say anything bad to her back; I just went home.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because she hasn't contacted me since.

situation: Scenario: I recently had to attend a disciplinary meeting with a member of the team and issue a warning letter due to poor performance. The staff member had broken the company's rules, and I had no choice but to issue a warning to this employee. I felt sorry for the guy; he had made a mistake. Now, he's got a warning on his file. During the meeting, I tried to personalize the conversation by acknowledging his previous contributions to the team and discussing specific ways he could improve his performance moving forward. I wanted to ensure the discussion was constructive and relevant to his situation, rather than just following a generic protocol.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Wednesday. It mattered to me because I had the guy's livelihood in my hands.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me emotionally as I felt guilty having to issue this guy a warning. I felt sorry for the employee who made the mistake, but I'm mainly over it now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The employee was most responsible for all of this because he had made the mistake.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt fully in control. It was my meeting and I needed to decide what to do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went pretty much as I expected. I had the choice of either issuing a warning or dismissing the guy, and I chose the warning.

situation: My mum's funeral comes to mind. We had the usual funeral activities and a tea gathering for her friends afterwards. I was focused on honoring my mum's memory and providing a space for her friends to gather and remember her. I felt exhausted and like I was putting on a face. Giving myself time to grieve was important to me during this difficult time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 5 days ago. It mattered to me because I wanted to give her a good send-off.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was and still am numb. I think it will hit me when things have quietened down.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was as in control as I could be. I had to get arrangements made.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected. Nothing was really unexpected.

situation: I left my son's dad in December because he was struggling with addiction and became abusive. I'm safe now, but it's been really hard and difficult to deal with the trauma bonded feelings. I knew I needed to leave, but the whole situation left me heartbroken. Throughout it all, my son's safety and my own were the most important things to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in December and it mattered a lot to me because this was my son's father, not just anyone.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by being trauma bonded, leaving me alienated with other people who think I am wrong if I stay, wrong if I leave.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't know who feels responsible. Everyone.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control. People made a lot of decisions for me and have for years.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as expected. He did ask us to go back, but I didn't want that because I felt unsafe.

situation: My daughter had a new baby, and I found out through someone else. I really wanted to know when she gave birth, but I felt left out of the whole situation. It's important to me to be involved, and I don't even know the baby's name.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago, and it mattered a great deal to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I'm the grandparent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of this situation because my daughter won't speak to me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as expected.

situation: My cat had just come home after having major surgery, and he became really unwell, bleeding from his back end. I was anxious, fearful, and concerned, wanting some clarification that he was going to be okay. Ensuring that my cat got the help he needed was really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a week ago, and my cat is an important part of my life, so it mattered a lot to me that he got the help he needed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The thought of losing him caused me a lot of hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible for it; it was an unfortunate illness.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was definitely not in control; my anxiety took over.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I was sure there was something seriously wrong with him. On arrival at the vets, they weren't too concerned and felt that the blood was coming from his bladder due to it being inflamed. They were very calm and sure that he was fine.

situation: I was pleasantly surprised during my end-of-year review when my boss told me he had rated me a grade higher than he originally mentioned, which meant my bonus amount would be bigger. I had been trying to achieve the grade I received, but I was told it wasn't possible at this stage. So, when I heard the news, I was really surprised and happy, almost in shock. It was important to me that multiple people were involved in the decision and all rated me highly.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I was considering other options in terms of work, as I had been feeling undervalued.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me see that I am valued and that perhaps I am too hard on myself, and that I don't see the bigger picture.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like my boss was responsible for it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control as I did not know it was happening.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was unexpectedly happy.

situation: I've been struggling with homeschooling my son. He doesn't like to write, and we think it's because it hurts his hands. To make the homeschooling experience more comfortable for him, I've been trying to give him more breaks between classes and sometimes doing the writing for him. Despite my efforts, I feel like I've failed him. He's very smart, but he gets upset when he has to write more than a few words and starts crying, and that hurts my heart.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Friday, and it mattered a lot to me because I know he's smart, but when he has to prove that with writing, it overwhelms him and he gets very anxious and upset.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I know how he feels; writing hurts my hands too.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I can't make it better for him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I thought it was getting better, but even cushioned pencils don't seem to help.

situation: Last week, my husband got a promotion at work that he was aiming for. I was really supportive of him, making sure he wasn't too stressed out when he worked late on projects. I felt happy, content, and satisfied knowing that he trusts me and comes to me for emotional support.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday morning, early, just after I finished making coffee for us. It mattered a lot to me because I remember screaming and jumping for joy, even though I was still half asleep.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because some stress of late nights is now gone. Plus, we get more income and benefits now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My husband for sure. He worked so hard to get this promotion. I was just his anchor during the process.
appraisal_reasoning.control: For the most part, I was in control of my husband's emotional state.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected. We just found out sooner than initially planned.

situation: I got the 8th rank, which made me really happy. I was aiming to get into the best college, and achieving this rank felt like a big step towards that goal. My teachers played a crucial role in helping me reach this milestone, and I'm really grateful for their support.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was important as it was my future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It improved my life. I got a good job.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My teachers.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control because I studied hard.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No surprise.

situation: I got a very large tax refund, and it was such a relief. I've been living paycheck to paycheck, and I really wanted a break from that constant stress. This refund lifted a lot of pressure off my chest, and now I can breathe a little easier. Plus, it means I can finally expedite some home improvement projects I've been putting off.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When I saw the amount on TurboTax, I was elated. It was more than I expected.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me financially and in turn relieved stress.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Donald Trump. He helped pass the OBBBA which provided many tax breaks for me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not, this is taxes.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went better than expected, I got more back than anticipated.

situation: It was an amazing moment when my 6-month-old daughter rolled over for the first time. She's been trying to do it for weeks, and then she finally managed it. I wasn't trying to do anything at that moment; it just felt like another milestone in her short journey so far. I was emotional and happy, watching her achieve this new skill.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a great deal as it’s my baby daughter and she’s growing up so fast, learning to do new things all the time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me knowing she’s growing up and all perfect.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don’t feel anyone was responsible for it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No was not in control it was all her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yeah she did it perfectly.

situation: My oldest son accused me of not caring about him because I took away his computer privileges. I needed him to understand that he was losing these privileges because he hasn't been doing what he's expected to do around the house. This situation left me feeling sad and angry. I'm not usually the one who has to take privileges away from the kids when they don't do what they're supposed to do, so it was hard for me. My wife normally handles the punishing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Friday. It matters because I don't like being the bad guy but I also don't like my son lashing out the way he does when I do actually punish him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I don't like it when my son acts like I don't care about him. It's like he wants me to be his friend not his parent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I start out in control and then he says things like I don't care about him and I feel like I lose control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I always expect him to say something along those lines but it's normally to his mother and not me. I see why my wife wants me to be the bad guy sometimes.

situation: My sister-in-law is going through a divorce, and we found out this week that she has left her ex-husband for her best friend. They've been keeping it a secret for the last 4 months. We knew about it, but she was forced to tell her ex-husband about him, as they were all best friends. It's horrible seeing the situation develop and feeling so powerless. I wanted to help her, but also to tell her to grow up and be an adult, as it's been affecting my mother-in-law and father-in-law. I needed to tell her what I really thought of the situation, but I couldn't in order to keep the peace. I'm feeling frustrated, I guess, but also powerless as there's nothing we can do apart from be there to pick up the pieces when things fall apart. I believe she has told him now, but we are yet to find out how things went, nor how things will turn out. It was important to maintain my relationship with my husband and not to disclose my feelings too much, as I don't want to risk influencing his own thoughts toward his sister. We want to keep the peace, but also feel caught in the middle between their silly childish behaviors and feeling like we want to tell them what we really think. It's been hard.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last weekend, and it mattered because it is my sister-in-law and I care about her feelings (and my husband's feelings) during this event and stressful time, as it affects everyone in the family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurts me indirectly through the feelings and frustrations of others, and me feeling like I cannot act on my conscience by telling her what I really think about the situation, and how it will affect not only her ex-husband, but also their small children who will be affected by the fallout.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My sister-in-law is primarily responsible for this, unfortunately (and her new partner), which makes things all the much harder.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really - nothing much we or anybody can do but watch it play out and hope for the best. She keeps us in the loop when significant things happen (or will happen), but all we can do is be there to pick up the pieces.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, tears and frustrations on behalf of my sister-in-law, as expected. Things have only developed today, so we haven't received any recent updates. But I guess I can see it play out how we expected it to.

situation: I went to the pub with my son to watch a football match. My team beat our biggest rivals, and we both celebrated and felt great. We went on to get drunk. I wanted my team to win and to spend quality time with my son and make memories. Luckily, the next day I was off work as I had a hangover and did not feel very good. I stayed in bed for a long time. Although I did not feel very well, I still had a smile on my face as I had had a good time with my son, and that is really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The match was on Sunday with a 12 o'clock kick off. Me and my son also met one of my son's friends, and we all got on well with each other and had a good laugh. This is important to me to have fun as life is too short to not take time to enjoy yourself. Also, one of my friends died recently, and it now feels even more important to make the most of your life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It really cheered me up as my team won, and I had a good time with my son, and not everybody can say that. This experience did not hurt me at all except for the hangover that I had the next day, but it was worth it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Mainly my son was responsible as it was his suggestion to do this and to go to a pub that we don't normally go to, but they had big screens to watch the match.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt that me and my son had equal control as we get on really well and consider what each person wants.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went more or less as I expected as I thought that my team would win, but we did stay out drinking longer than I thought that we would.

situation: I was with my friend on Monday evening after a really nice weekend away with them. We had spent a lot of time together, and even though we can be relatively volatile, nothing like that happened over the weekend. As the time approached for us to travel to our respective homes, my friend made a comment about me that I found hurtful. This made me immediately angry, and I walked away. I wasn't sure if I was overreacting, so I needed time to reflect on what had been said and made a short goodbye. As I drove off, I felt so disappointed and confused that I began to cry. We were looking at a child's magazine that included a small gift. My friend explained that he had bought the magazine just to get the gift and threw away the magazine. I asked jokingly if he had read the magazine, and he said he had thrown it away. I asked why he hadn't given it to his young nephew, and he said again that he hadn't, he had thrown it in the bin. The comment he made followed this when I told him his action was annoying; he told me, 'You don't live in the real world.' I wasn't sure why he'd say that or what he meant by it at all. I'm still confused about where this comment came from and whether he meant it or just said the wrong thing. I was angry, I was upset. I made a passive-aggressive comment about it a day or so later and still have no closure, but I've decided I need to move on—he isn't acting strangely or making any other comments, so I think it was a mistake. I have been considering a romantic relationship with him and felt we'd had a lovely weekend; this spoiled it and the thoughts of what could have been.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday evening after a weekend away with my friend. It mattered massively to me because I overthink things and had started thinking about a potential future, which made me question that and my own future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me that he might think I don't live in the real world. It made me question why he'd say this and what I do or how I live that might make him say this about me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I initiated it by telling him his action was annoying—I felt that his action was selfish because he has a child nephew and had a free child's magazine he could have given to him. But I didn't feel that his response was adequate.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control and did not manage it well. I should have turned immediately to respond and say 'What did you mean by that?', resolve the issue in that moment. Instead, I walked away 'in a huff' and now lack any closure.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting anything to happen, so it was all unexpected.

situation: I got through a breakup last month, and yesterday, a couple of friends I've known for around 5-6 years sat me down for tea. They confronted me about partaking in a 'throuple' and said they both loved me and wanted to become more intimate as three. I was very flattered because I love them very much, but I had to turn them down. I didn't want to mess with their relationship since they've been together for 4-5 years. It was a mixed situation; I felt really good afterwards, very affirmed, but also a little confused. I didn't really need too much from it, but I've been seeking affection and affirmation since my breakup. The couple has always been a bit flirty with me, and I just wanted to make sure they didn't take the rejection the wrong way. I'm open to hooking up with them since we trust each other and are very close. The situation left me feeling pretty shaky and very uncertain, but also very happy, if that makes sense. I was a little lucid for a while when I came home, but really happy they opened that door. I gave them each a kiss before I headed out. It made me realize I might be longing or being overtly flirtatious. I hope I'm not sending the wrong signal to other people, but I really enjoyed them confronting me over this.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday morning. I told them about my breakup 3 weeks ago and I've been moping a bit. They keep reaching out multiple times a week to make sure I'm okay, we're really close, and we very much love each other as good friends. It really felt like a lot, I thought about it the rest of the day. They're really precious to me and I appreciate them so much.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Well, it helped me feel confident in myself. It helped me have a happy rest of the day as I daydreamed a bit. I sort of took them up on the offer to hook up with them since I know I can trust them. It sort of hurts in that I feel like I might jeopardize our friendship if things go wrong. So I am just anxious about how I balance it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Probably all three of us equally. I am really happy they asked me all this. I am also very flirtatious with everyone so they probably bounced off that, and that's definitely making me lean towards being responsible. They did bring it up though, but I was happy they did.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Mostly. I knew I wasn't being entirely pressured. Being in a 'throuple' isn't something I'd normally do though. I don't want to disappoint them by any means so maybe I have a hard time saying no. But personally, I do want to step up the affection we trade even if it's temporary.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not sure, it was such an unexpected question. But it also felt, right?

situation: I was informed that a work colleague had passed away suddenly. I had been speaking to him just the other week and he seemed very well. Initially, I was shocked when I found out. It made me think of all the times we’d spent working together, and I felt sad. I felt a mixture of great memories but also a reminder that we shouldn’t take anything for granted; life is precious. I also had thoughts of his family and how they must be affected by this news.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I was told a week past Monday that he’d passed on the suddenly on the Sunday, at first I couldn’t believe what I was hearing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was shock more than anything else but focused on the good times we’d spent together at work and the laughs we had shared.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don’t think anyone was responsible for any of it, unfortunately death is part of living there is no escaping it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes totally in control, I am not normally a very emotional person and tend to hide my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes everything was as expected.

situation: I am a student nurse, and during my recent placement, I encountered an elderly person with advanced dementia. They were very ill, and while I usually cope with these kinds of situations, what broke me was seeing their face light up when we handed them a small cuddly toy—it was just lovely. I wasn't trying to do anything in particular; I was just sticking my head around the doors to check that the patients were OK. I could have done with some additional training to sit with this person and communicate with them properly. The situation left me feeling sad because my grandfather died of dementia a couple of years ago, and this person reminded me of what he and our family went through. I felt quite helpless because I wanted to do something to fix this person, but there's no fixing or curing dementia. It was important to me to support the family as best as I could, which I did—even small things like getting them a cup of tea or coffee can go a long way in making people feel better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me. There are times when I wonder why I chose to go into nursing, but there are other times that reaffirm to me that I picked the right career, and this was one of them. It is a privilege to look after people during the darkest days of their lives and to be able to watch them walk out of hospital, hopefully cured.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't really hurt me at all, but it definitely helped me in the process of learning how to cope with different situations, and especially painful situations like this one. Through shadowing the nurses looking after this patient I have been able to learn more about how to break bad news, have difficult discussions, and so on.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't think anyone was responsible, nor do I think the blame can be pinned on any one thing. It's unfortunate but it's just something that happens, and it does not discriminate.
appraisal_reasoning.control: In some ways I felt like I was in control, and in others I did not. I felt in control in the sense that I had a good grip on my emotions and was able to not get too (visibly) upset, but in other ways I felt completely helpless to do much because of the nature of dementia and how it is incurable and very difficult to deal with/manage.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected - while I am not the best at communicating with people with dementia, I do have a lot of experience with them (both my own grandfather and other patients), and nothing really came out of the blue to shock or unsettle me, as it likely would have in the past.

situation: I got emotional thinking about my daughter starting pre-k. I didn't need anything; I was just sad because she's growing up so fast. I've been a stay-at-home mom for 4 years, and seeing her become a big girl makes me really sad but also happy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me because I realize that she is just growing so fast. These four years have flown by.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help or hurt, just provoked a lot of emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one, it's not a situation like that.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I can't control time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went well; she had a great day.

situation: I went to urgent care because my whole leg had been in pain for days, and I needed to know what was wrong. My doctor suggested I go to them. When I got there, they were very rude and acted like I shouldn't have come. It left me feeling very frustrated and upset that there are people in healthcare who are so rude. Afterward, I looked up reviews online and saw that other people had the same issues at this place.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened the other night. It mattered because I really wanted to get some answers and relief but they instead didn't help in any way.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me nervous to go to another urgent care because they made me feel like I was silly for going.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The nurse who made the rude comments.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I didn't feel in control because they refused to help me even though I needed it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No I expected them to help me. Instead they just sent me home quickly after doing nothing.

situation: I went to a gig, and when a certain song was played, I got emotional because of the personal meaning it has for me. I was thinking of the person the song reminds me of, and this made me upset but also comforted. Overall, I felt very touched by it and always will. I was focused on myself and the singer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened during a gig, and it mattered greatly to me because the song was the highlight of the night. I thought the song would be played and was hoping it would be.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt and healed me at the same time. The lyrics have great meaning, and overall, it was one of the highlights of the night.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The setting, the song, and the artist were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't really in control of my emotions as it made me cry, but I was comforted by it overall.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, however, I was more emotional than I expected to be.

situation: I had a conversation with my friend about how I felt like she had let me down recently. Before confronting her, I needed some time to reflect because I didn't want to say something I didn't really mean. I needed to let her know how she had made me feel. She was clearly in the wrong, which she acknowledged, and we both had a good long chat about our friendship and where we go from here. I needed her to apologize and recognize her mistake, which she did, and we're going to put it behind us and move forward, which is exactly what I wanted. I feel much better after having spoken to her about it all. I think we are both adults and can move forward together now and do better. The main thing was for her to acknowledge and apologize and realize that she had really hurt me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Monday when I messaged her to ask if we could meet in person and have a chat. We went for a walk just the two of us and chatted about things for a good 2-3 hours. It meant a lot to me, and I think she knew she needed to have a chat about it too as she was very happy to meet that day to chat.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt at the time because she did something that upset me a lot, but I felt like a weight was lifted afterwards and we got to have a proper good chat about things.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She was the one to blame entirely. I did exactly what I needed to do to be there for my partner when his mum died and she only thought about herself during this time which really hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt like I had full control, and I think my friend would agree. She knew how I would be feeling and that she was the cause and was anticipating my message.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they went exactly as I expected them to. I know her very well and I think we both needed this chat in order to move forward.

situation: My husband and I had an argument about how we should decorate the bathroom. The reason why it turned into an argument was because I felt like my idea was being dismissed, and he wasn't willing to discuss it, which really frustrated me. I was trying to express my wants, but they weren't being listened to or even discussed. What I needed was to feel heard and not be dismissed. The whole situation left me feeling like my opinion wasn't important and that it was being disregarded. It was really just about not feeling heard and disregarded.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was really important to me because he disregards my opinions quite often.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it made me feel unheard and unseen. It affected my relationship by making me feel frustrated as he wasn't hearing me or willing to engage in conversation. I was just shot down, and even though we spoke about it later, I was already frustrated with him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My husband was most responsible for all of this, as he was the one that wasn't listening to me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control, as I couldn't say what I wanted to say because my husband wasn't willing to have a conversation about it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things didn't go as expected, as I was frustrated with him. I wasn't expecting him to shoot me down like that and not engage in the conversation.

situation: My brother has had a bad reaction to his cancer treatment. This made me a little emotional at the time. I am not happy discussing family problems with third parties.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened last Monday and resulted in him being hospitalised for three days due to serious side effects from the treatment.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This did not help me in any way. This depressed me. The solution is to reduce the dose so improvements in health will also be reduced.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Clearly the treatment drugs are responsible for the side effects being experienced.
appraisal_reasoning.control: How on earth could I be in control of these issues?

situation: I recently went for a walk in the countryside for the first time in a long time. I just wanted to be alone and get back to nature. Being in the middle of nature was important to me, and I realized it made me feel better about myself. I felt really refreshed and also at peace.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was a week ago. It mattered a lot to me because I used to go for this walk often, but this was the first time in many months, and I had forgotten how good it made me feel.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by making me feel calmer. There was nothing challenging or less positive about the experience; I was glad I made the effort.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I had been too busy to spend time with nature.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of the situation but had just been too busy.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as I expected.

situation: I was entering a restaurant in the hotel we were staying at in the Canary Islands when the restaurant manager suddenly grabbed me by the arm, accusing me of queue jumping. I immediately told him to take his hands off me, explaining that I wasn't queue jumping because one of his colleagues had called my partner in. I wasn't trying to do anything wrong; I was just about to be directed to a free table. The whole situation left me extremely angry, and I pointed out that if it had happened in the UK, he could have been charged with common assault. Later, I spoke with the General Manager of the hotel, who was intimidating and threatening. He told me that if I was lying about the situation, I could find myself spending a day in the local jail.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened at breakfast time on the 15 February- two days before we returned home. It mattered a great deal as I’m not used to being grabbed by a man.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I wasn’t hurt just angry and embarrassed as there were lots of people around.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The restaurant manager who failed to consider the situation - too busy being impatient and unable to notice what his colleagues.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control because I walked away, sat down and had my breakfast.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: After speaking to the general manager who as I said previously was intimidating and threatening I excused myself from his office and have since complained about his manner to the travel company.

situation: I had a really successful job interview for a big promotion at work, and I really wanted to get it. During the interview, I felt strong and confident, and afterwards, I received some amazing feedback.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was important that I made a good impression and show my skills.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to climb the ladder and get more opportunities at work.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was me and my willpower and having the courage to take the leap.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, as I spent a lot of time preparing and felt really confident presenting to the panel.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went as I planned!

situation: We took our dog for a walk on a route we know well, aiming to exercise both our dog and ourselves while spending some time in nature. To our dismay, we found that some mature sycamore trees had been felled as part of a flood defense project. I felt devastated, actually experiencing some real grief because these trees were familiar to us, and I can't see any good reason for chopping them down. To honor and remember the trees, we took some of the larger chunks of wood for my husband to carve.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about an hour ago and felt like a stone in my chest. It mattered significantly because I felt really hurt and ashamed of my species.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me deeply, as it highlighted my frustration with humanity's tendency to remove obstacles rather than live in harmony with nature.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the council was most responsible, as it was part of their project. Despite trying to see it as for the greater good, I was frustrated they didn't find an alternative.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control. The decision was made by those in charge of the project without consulting the community, leaving me feeling powerless and angsty.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. It was entirely unexpected.

situation: I have just learned that my only sibling, and last remaining member of our family, has been diagnosed with cancer. She lives 200 miles away from me, and I want to see her, but I'm not able to drive that far, so I feel so helpless. I'm very sad and feeling very useless as there is nothing I can do to help. I don't really know how to deal with the situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered greatly to me because I have felt a strong tie to my sister, especially since both our parents are deceased.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation has hurt me by bringing an urgency to our relationship, as I had hoped we would be able to see each other and support each other for a long time yet. Now, there is fear that she may not be there for much longer.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nothing is responsible; it is just fate whether you get so ill or not.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I feel so out of control as I can do nothing to change it or do anything to help her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was very unexpected. The last time I saw her she was fine and looking forward to the birth of her next grandchild. Now that has all been taken away from her.

situation: My wife got called into the office for additional screening after a mammogram she had taken a week prior. It was a little scary waiting for the second test for both of us. We needed the second test to come out normal, and we were really hoping there was nothing there. Before the test, I felt very nervous, but in the end, everything turned out well, and I felt relief. At that moment, we felt blessed to still be healthy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a whole lot to me because my wife is still relatively young and healthy, and for her to get sick would be very devastating to us.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped us to understand that there is no need to panic, and that you don't have to worry when there is no need to worry just yet.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible; the hospital was just being very careful to make sure they got the diagnosis right.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really, we felt it was all up to fate, and we were just hoping for the best.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything turned out well in the end and there was nothing to worry about.

situation: I just started to eat clean again and feel very positive about it. I've realized that I could never lose fat from just working out, so now I've changed to eating healthy too. I'm feeling great and can't wait to see what my future self looks like. My health will be better because of it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I want to be in shape and have abs and could not achieve that, so I started to eat healthy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped to feel better so I can do my workouts better too.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me, I motivated myself to do this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because I started and have been doing it now.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they will. I'm buying certain foods to stick to.

situation: Earlier in the week, one of my elderly cats, who has been with our family for 19 years, suddenly had her health deteriorate. She became bloated and struggled to move, so we took her to the vet. Unfortunately, there wasn't much they could do apart from giving her pain medication. We brought her home, but she stopped eating and drinking, so we had to keep her hydrated using a syringe of water. It was devastating to think about losing her. I was trying to make sure she was in as little discomfort as possible and wanted her to get better, even though I knew that wasn't possible. I just needed to let her know how loved she was. The situation left me feeling very sad, but I know she had a good life and was very much loved. It was also important to me that my children were supported through this situation, as they have had her with them for most of their lives.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: She has been getting more frail for a few weeks. However, it was really in the last week that she had a lot of difficulty moving and then her stomach bloated. It mattered a lot to me because she has been with my family since she was a kitten.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Seeing your pet in discomfort and knowing that all you can do is make them as comfortable as possible is very hard. I'll miss her. I didn't want her to be in discomfort or confused because she struggled to move.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was just the fact that she was very old. She is 19 which is extremely old for a cat. Nobody was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I accepted that there wasn't a lot we could do apart from make her as comfortable as possible. The only thing that I could control was the care she was given. I could control her deterioration.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected she just slowly deteriorated.

situation: My doctor told me that I cannot work anymore, and it's been really tough. I need a job to make money for my family, but my back is messed up so bad I cannot work at all. This situation has left me severely depressed, and I find myself crying every day. The most important thing to me is keeping a roof over my son's head, but I'm struggling to see how I can do that now.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last year and it matters a lot to me as I cannot work anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me more than it helped me. I lost my income, I lost my friends, and I lost the job that was perfect for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was not anyone's fault. It has to do with my previous jobs and hurting my back.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control at all. My injury was an accident.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, nothing went as expected. I did not expect to be disabled at such a young age.

situation: My friend had a major eye operation, and I was trying to be there for her and help if I could. I felt sad and upset for her because she was really uncomfortable. It was important for me that she knew I was there for her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Thursday. It mattered a lot to me because she is one of my best friends, so I wanted to be there for her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because she was in so much pain and couldn't do much but look down at the floor for days. I empathized with her, and it mostly just upset me that I couldn't ease her pain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible; her eye just deteriorated.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I sent her a get well card and kept in touch, as that was all I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. I managed to feel relaxed that I had done all I could.

situation: I was at work and had some free time, so I started listening to a song. The song was about drugs and how the person I care about chose drugs over me, which made me think about my difficult family dynamic. It got me emotional. I really wished I had someone who knows how I feel to talk to about it. I felt sad, really. My difficult upbringing and toxic family dynamic were important factors in how I was feeling.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I listened to the song yesterday at work, and it mattered to me because family are an important figure.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it made me feel helpless about the situation as I distance myself from them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My parents' controlling behavior and emotional abuse.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Inbetween, the emotions were still affecting me but I have controlled the situation overall by becoming distant from them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected just sad and helpless.

situation: We recently found out that our family from New Zealand is coming over to visit. You'd think this would create a positive emotion, but actually, it was negative. The mum is high maintenance, so even though it should be nice to see the nephews, the baggage that comes with the mum makes it more of a worry than excitement at the prospect of them coming over. It's currently a big deal in my household, and there's a mix of emotions about it. We wanted to be able to receive family into our environment with a positive outlook, but instead, it left us worried. They're due to come in less than two weeks, and we didn't want to feel this way, but it's the nature of the mum that has this effect.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Earlier today, we received a call to confirm they had managed to sort alternative flights out that meant they could still come over for Easter. It mattered to us as we had mixed emotions about seeing the kids.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It disappointed us as we thought they would not be able to come.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We are responsible for how we feel, but the concern is in relation to how difficult the mum will be when she gets here.
