appraisal_reasoning.control: No, we feel we have no control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: We are still anticipating their arrival, but in the short term, we are still concerned and are trying to come up with a plan to put our minds at ease.

situation: I own shares, and this week one of them increased in value, which made me feel very happy. They just increased in value a bit, and I assume it's because of some good financial news. I'm always hoping that my shares will increase in value; that's the whole point of investing. The aim is to make money. As I said, it left me feeling happy and pleased. There's nothing else important to me in this situation—just trying to make money.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it's why I risk money by investing—to try and make some money.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because it made me think that I had made the right decision by investing my money.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There was some financial news that affected the price.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because I have confidence in the company and its ability to make money. I felt it was a case of buying the shares and waiting for them to increase in value.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected. As I said, I have confidence in the company, so I was just waiting for the increase.

situation: I had a panic attack in front of a small group during a meeting, which left me feeling embarrassed and upset. I had been feeling increasingly uncomfortable and just needed to take myself away from the situation. Afterward, I felt a bit wrung out and silly.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened an evening last week. It mattered to me because I don't like being the center of attention or drawing attention to myself, and so I felt silly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation neither helped nor hurt me other than making me feel inadequate.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Who knows? These things sometimes seem to happen for no discernible reason.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt I had lost control, which was why I rushed out.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't really expecting anything. I just wanted to escape and go home where I would feel safe.

situation: My friend, who lives abroad, came back for a visit, and we spent the day catching up together. We did fun activities like playing mini golf and going to our favorite Italian restaurant. I needed to feel close with my friend again after a few years of distance. I wanted time dedicated to us and our friendship. I felt really happy and secure in our friendship. It was a relief to know we still had a strong bond and connection, and we were able to share details of our lives comfortably. It was important to understand the ways in which we were still very similar and also appreciate how we had both grown and changed as people, but still maintained a strong friendship. This made me feel very positive.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot because I hadn't spent time in person with my friend in a few years. The day of socialising was something I was excited and eager for.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me feel reassured that despite the physical distance and how our friendship had changed from seeing each other all the time to more rare visits, the relationship was still valuable and close. It made me feel positive about the future as I'm confident we will always maintain a close bond and find ways to continue connecting.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both me and my friend were equally responsible. We coordinated a good time for both of us to meet to ensure we could make the most of it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I was in control because my friend was happy to listen to my feelings and opinions, so the activities we took part in were ones I felt comfortable doing. We both discussed what we wanted to get from the day and planned an itinerary together that worked well.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Although I was slightly nervous before the day in case we no longer had enough in common, it mostly went as expected. We were able to chat freely and enjoyed each other's presence a lot.

situation: I recently moved to a small town after spending decades living in a city, and I've lost my confidence in driving. I had to drive to the city, and it triggered an anxiety attack. I was trying to navigate around the city I used to live in with the confidence I once had, without self-doubt. Beforehand, I felt severely anxious about the whole situation. While I was driving, I felt relieved that it was okay, but there was still a bit of anxiety lingering.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday and it mattered a great deal to me because I could have ended up having a car accident.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me anxious. I felt relieved that it was okay while driving, but there was still a bit of anxiety lingering.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't know who or what was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control of my anxiety.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected. I actually enjoyed much of the drive.

situation: I was really worried about my husband because he was having blood tests to check his kidney function, which is related to his high blood pressure. I was very anxious for a while, but thankfully, all the tests have come back clear now. During that time, I needed to comfort my husband and also wanted reassurance from the doctor. I felt anxious at the time, but I felt much better once we knew the outcome.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered very much to me because it involved my husband's health.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by causing anxiety, but I felt better once we knew the outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was out of our control because it’s health matters.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn’t feel in control because I can’t control health.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, the events went as I expected, and I was happy with the outcome.

situation: My wife went into the hospital, and we were hoping for a quick recovery. But she's been in there for 5 weeks now, and I feel horrible about it. The problems with the NHS have been really important to me in this situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: She fell but did not get seen by a GP for a week. This situation mattered a lot to me because of the lack of information on how serious her illness was.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me due to the lack of information about my wife's illness and the NHS being a mess.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel the UK government is most responsible for all of this due to waste.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all. The NHS did not tell us the truth, and there were monetary issues.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. Nurses made promises they could not keep, and support was not given.

situation: My sister told me that she will be having a baby boy. I wasn't trying to do anything specific at that moment; all I wanted was to give my sister a hug. Hearing the news made me emotional. I was excited for her and excited for me too, knowing she is having a boy. It also made me a bit sad because it brought up memories of my children being babies. It was important to me that my sister was happy about having a boy too.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because she is my sister.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation neither helped nor hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My sister was responsible because she is the one that is pregnant.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control. It's a factual situation and my sister's business to tell me. I also didn't feel in control of my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected for me. For my sister, not so much; she wanted a girl.

situation: My daughter was having problems with her friends at school, with them making fun of her and just general bullying. I wanted her to be friends with other people, but she didn't want to because she has been friends with them for years. I wanted to say something to her friends, but she wouldn't let me. This whole situation left me feeling sad, angry, and out of control. It's horrible being a parent who is unable to help because it might cause further problems for my daughter.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters to me as it is my daughter and she is the most important person, it was people who she classed as her friends saying things, making fun and low level bullying.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel awful, I wanted to help but if I did it would get worse for her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I did I'm her Mum.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Totally out of control as I was unable to protect her like I wanted.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect friends she has had most of her life to turn on her so badly and not have her back.

situation: I didn't receive a promotion that I was more than qualified to get. I wanted to remain within my company because it's flexible and fits around my lifestyle, but I also wanted to move up the career ladder too. When I found out I didn't get the promotion, I felt really annoyed and taken advantage of. I had received glowing feedback throughout all my performance reviews, and then I was told I didn't get the job because I hadn't done things I wasn't told to do.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a couple of weeks ago and it really mattered to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I decided that I would put less effort into my job going forward as it's just not rewarded in any way. I don't think anyone has noticed really, but it has made me feel more empowered.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My manager.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't because I'd done everything I was told to do and then was stopped from progressing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I expected to get the promotion.

situation: I was out having coffee with one of my friends when she surprised me by telling me she's pregnant. It was such a shock because it wasn't planned, but I felt really emotional and happy about it. As she shared the news, I was hoping I was saying the right things to keep her at ease and make sure she was excited about this new chapter in her life. The whole situation left me feeling very happy and excited for the future, knowing that I get to be a part of this journey with her. I felt grateful that she took the time to see me in person to share such special news.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Friday last week in the evening time. It mattered a lot to me that she told me in person and surprised me with the news as it felt very special as we have been friends for a long time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me in the sense that it made me feel happy after a bit of a stressful week.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My friend was responsible for filling me with happiness for the news.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn't in control of the situation as I knew nothing about it and didn't even have any idea that she would be sharing this type of news with me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it wasn't expected as it was a complete surprise to me when I thought we were just meeting up for a general catch up.

situation: I had an argument with my wife about her sleep and my concerns that she wasn't getting enough sleep. I was hoping to bring my concerns to her attention because I worried about the long-term consequences of bad sleep. I wanted us to use this as an opportunity to discuss better sleep habits. Instead of helping things, I just started an argument, and it left me feeling guilty. The day after, I realized that I should've been offering help, instead of just expressing concern.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Tuesday. It was important because it disrupted things on Tuesday and Wednesday.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think it hurt short term. Long term, it probably helped. It reminded me to be more considerate and think about ways that I could make my wife's life better, instead of just expressing concerns.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was definitely the one most responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control, but as it got more emotional, I was less in control of my feelings and behavior.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not at all how I expected. It was unexpected how inflamed things got.

situation: My granddaughter told me she loved me for the first time, and it was exactly what I needed. I think she sensed that I was feeling a bit down and could use some cheering up. When she hugged me and said 'luv u nannie,' it left me feeling warm and needed for the first time in a while.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me immensely. I do not see my other two granddaughters, so when she said it, I was so happy but a bit sad because I miss the other two.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me mentally because I felt that unconditional love that only a two-year-old can give, but it also upset me because of missing my other granddaughters.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My granddaughter, she just lights up my day whenever I see her.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control to a point. I called her name to come to me, but also I was not in control of my emotions because I did not expect to feel so emotional from being told that she loved me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well, I did not expect her to say she loved me. I see her quite often, so it was out of the blue.

situation: I recently celebrated my birthday, and I went into the day with no expectations and no plans. It turned out to be an amazing day. I was just trying to enjoy my day, and I wanted cake and a nice walk, and I got both of those things. I was very happy and grateful for the people in my life. It left me feeling happy and satisfied. It was important to me to be with my loved ones and not have high expectations to enjoy my day to the fullest.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened a week ago and it mattered because it was my birthday and I just wanted a simple day of happiness.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because it gave me a mental health boost and I just felt loved and grateful for everything I have.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My mom and friends are responsible for it all; they made me feel so loved and had a lot of fun.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control because I was just doing whatever I wanted. I slept in, I took a good walk, I wanted cake and I got cake. I was getting things that I wanted.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went as expected except for the food and the gifts I got surprised with, but they were pleasant surprises so I don’t mind.

situation: My son wanted to ask a girl out to a dance and was really nervous about it. He asked and she said yes, and I was so happy for him. I was trying to support him because this is the first time he's asked out a girl. It left me feeling a little sad that he's growing up, but I was proud of him for taking the chance. More than anything, I wanted him to be happy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot because I wasn't sure how it would turn out for him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It gave me confidence that my son is growing up and maturing.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control over it. He was doing the asking and the girl had to make the decision.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was not sure what to expect since I didn't know the girl. I was happy that she said yes.

situation: I was at work last week when I had to assist my colleague in my office. She had suffered a death in the family and was very upset, so I needed to speak with her and allow her to express her emotions. I wanted to support her and make sure she felt like it was a safe place to discuss what was on her mind. It was really important to me to do all I could to support her in this difficult time. Afterward, it took a toll on me emotionally as well, which I wasn't expecting.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it mattered an awful lot to me. I really didn't like seeing my colleague so upset and really wanted to support them the best I could.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me as it gave me the chance to assist, but it also hurt me because I felt upset afterward. The feelings we shared stayed with me for some time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The depth of emotions discussed and how vulnerable we both had to allow ourselves to be were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It wasn't so much about control. I perceived my role as supportive and voluntary, which in some ways made it more important.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. It worked out well and the person seemed to calm down a lot.

situation: My stepson called me fat, and it was emotionally negative for me, really upsetting me. This incident made me evaluate my whole relationship with him and his dad. I feel like I've put up with a lot from my husband's children, and this is just the latest thing. I wanted my husband to stand up for me, but he just laughed at him instead. I was left feeling very upset and like I cannot cope with much more from this situation. It really upset me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Saturday evening. It really affected me because I am insecure about my weight to begin with and he just confirmed my own insecurities.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It just hurt me, it did not help me at all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My stepson, I am thinking that he is not a very nice person.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control, I just had to accept what he said.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well I did not expect him to call me fat.

situation: I passed an exam that I had been preparing for, and the preparation took me about three months. Then, I had to wait another three months for the result. I'm trying to become a Qualified Investment Manager, and this was another step in the right direction. Now, I only have one exam left until I reach this stage. When I found out I passed, I felt fantastic. I lost a family member in November when I sat the exam, so getting the pass result really felt like they were on my shoulder when I sat it, which made it far more emotional. Just getting the pass was important to me, but I exceeded my expectations by getting a great overall result too. I was shocked because I didn't think the exam had gone well at all.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I sat the exam, and it mattered greatly to me because I felt terrible during the exam, thinking I had failed. However, receiving the result brought a great sense of pride, especially since it was my first time taking the exam and I exceeded my expectations. My work was really happy for me, which was an added bonus.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me overall by advancing my career development. However, during revision, I experienced a sense of FOMO (fear of missing out) as I had to say no to occasions that sounded great. I made up for that over the festive period and subsequent months.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible overall, but since the turn of 2026, I found my faith in God again and feel He had a part to play in my decisions to revise instead of going out, as well as in the exam itself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because I'm a big planner and had daily targets that were met well. I allocated the appropriate amount of time to study and did so in the exam too, ensuring the right amount of time per mark throughout.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I fully expected to fail and even had a bet with a friend that I would, which I had to pay up for. The experience made me stop doubting myself, which has been great for my overall confidence. Now, embarking on the last part of the qualification, I know I am capable if I put the work in, as previous results have proved this over and over again.

situation: My young son fell and cut his head. I immediately wanted to provide first aid to make sure he was okay and check that it wasn't a serious injury. The situation left me feeling guilty and worried.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was extremely important as it was the welfare of my child.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt guilty that I had not been able to stop it from happening. I snapped at my husband while we were dealing with it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me. He fell over while I was playing with him.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No as I did not catch him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: He fell unexpectedly when he was walking.

situation: I finished writing my master's thesis, which has taken years of stress off my life. I felt like a weight had been lifted. It had been going on way too long, longer than expected, and it was taking up so much time and stress in my life. I wanted to get back my time, feel free, and earn a really well-deserved degree. I felt so relieved. It was a bit bittersweet but I was overjoyed overall. It was the last step I had from my past before I felt like I have a clear schedule to follow my dreams and actually commit.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was January 30th, 2023, when I first began. It mattered a lot as it took me a long time to get accepted, and I had this idea in my head that I would accomplish it, but unexpected events made it a bit more difficult.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Finishing my master's thesis helped me a great deal because it had been a financial and mental strain, but now those chains have lifted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me and my supervisors were most responsible for all of this. They were so patient and helpful.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt both in control and not in control. I had other factors driving me, such as time and finance, because I needed to work around an awful job that I needed and took so much free time from me. I lost time, plus when I had weekends, I was exhausted from more work.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. It was only supposed to be a year-long master's degree, but I had unexpected events, such as family issues, financial, mental stress, etc.

situation: My favorite team, Michigan, was ranked number 1 and was playing against Duke, who was ranked number 3, on Saturday. It was a big game, and I was really hoping for Michigan to win. I was watching the game, rooting for them, and I even bet on them. Unfortunately, Michigan's guards didn't have a good game, and they lost. I felt upset and frustrated after the game. Then, the new rankings came out on Monday, and now Duke is number 1 and Michigan is number 3.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Saturday, and it mattered somewhat to me because Michigan is my favorite team, I bet money on the game, and it will have some effect on March Madness brackets.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by losing money on the bet and didn't really help me at all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Michigan's guards had a bad game, but Duke is just a good team too.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel like I was in control because I was just watching the game from home.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things didn't go as I expected. I expected Michigan to win, and it was unexpected that Duke won.

situation: My results came through from my smear test, and they weren't what I was hoping for—bad news. It was just a routine test, but now I'm booked in for surgery to hopefully sort out the problems, and then a biopsy. I'd been so stressed, worried, and tense, and when the results came, I just needed a shoulder to cry on and some reassurance. This whole situation has left me feeling worried and upset. Having support and being able to have my questions answered is really important to me right now.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot because it’s cancer related and I want my health to be the best it can be.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn’t really help me as the results were all in a language that was hard to understand and left me confused. I then had to go to Google, which just made me more worried, and the panic and thinking of worst-case scenarios really hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The hospital itself, my results took much longer than they said it would, and I just feel that they should have clarified in simpler form to make me less worried and more knowledgeable.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn’t feel like I was in control as I had to wait ages for another appointment and I didn’t really have any decisions that I could make for myself.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I can’t really answer that as it was unexpected results in the sense that I had prayed for different.

situation: I had received a bonus at work for my good performance, and it was such a surprise—I didn't expect it at all. My family has been working hard, and there have been a lot of needs for different things, so this extra bump of money was really needed. I was very happy, and those happy thoughts rushed through my mind. It was important because it alleviates some stress in my life.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened a month ago. It mattered to me because my wife and I work very hard to provide a comfortable life. It was important because it alleviates some stress in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because my wife didn't have to stress so much about so many extra hours after work and have more quality time together.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible because I worked harder than everyone else in my full time job.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because the situation wasn't clear and I didn't know if I had won until the end.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't think it went the way I was expecting, but I was happy with the end result.

situation: My son asked me to pick him up from a friend's place at a specific time, so I headed over to get him. But when I arrived, he wasn't there. I was trying to pick him up like we had planned, and at first, I felt worried because he was missing. Then, I got upset because he had asked to be picked up at that time and wasn't even there. His safety was really important to me, and I didn't want him walking home alone. Plus, I had no idea where he could be since we had agreed on him being picked up at that time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last night. It mattered a lot to me at the time because I got worried. I had stopped working to make sure that he was able to get home safely.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I don't think it helped or hurt me. I think it was a portion of time that I was confused and worried and then it was resolved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my son was most responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I did not feel in control. I had a plan to do something and then I felt like it had all fell through and I was left wondering what was going on.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No things did not go expected at first because he was not there when he said he would be. Eventually they did go as expected because he showed up but there was a period of time that I felt in limbo and worried about him.

situation: It was my uncle's funeral on Monday. We attended the service at a church before heading to his local working men's club afterward. I wanted to see family that I hadn't seen for a while, even though it was under such unfortunate circumstances. The whole experience left me feeling grateful for everyone I have around me, but it was also emotional and sad seeing some of my close family struggling. I just wish my family would get together more often in happier circumstances.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday. It mattered to me because, although I wasn't necessarily close to my uncle and his passing didn't make me feel sad, I felt sadness for my cousin and my aunt who had lost their father and husband.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation made me feel like I need to reach out to my family more. We don't see each other as much as we should, and I don't want it to end up that the only time we see each other is during bad times. I felt like I was supposed to be sadder than I was, and while I like to try and find positivity in moments like funerals, it's hard to know how other people feel, so you can't really make too many jokes.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Seeing my cousin for the first time in a long time was most responsible for the circumstances surrounding my uncle's funeral and the emotions I experienced.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control of my emotions and actions throughout this situation. It wasn't an overly emotional experience for me, so I felt grounded during the whole day.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect to feel guilt, but other than that, it was as expected. It was nice to see people, but I just wish it was in a better way.

situation: I was overwhelmed with the workload at work, feeling undervalued and under-resourced. Expectations were high, and there was limited empathy from colleagues outside my department. I felt pressure to deliver when there was no time to complete tasks without feeling rushed and without consideration. I was trying to complete a series of tasks and provide documents to support a business-wide project involving multiple outside companies. It was hard for the project to run smoothly due to varying timescales and demands. My department was the only one without additional resources to support the project. Being part-time and solo, the demands within a three-week window, with no forward planning or sight of timelines, made it difficult to respond with clarity and time to think for each request to help with this and that and share this and that with third parties to help the project progress. I felt overwhelmed, rushed, not listened to, and that there was no consideration from others that what was being asked was too much to deliver in the timeframes they wanted. No one offered to help take some of the tasks or asked how they could help or considered their own demands and if they were reasonable with the time allowed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Last week it all came to a head as three weeks of continuing pressure was too much. It mattered to me as I love my job, I'm good at it and although flattered everyone asked me to help, provide the documents and deliver to help move the project forward, there was no consideration for the reality of how I'd get it all done.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I just got on with it, tackled each task, lived in a crazy fog of responding without absorbing and ensuring that I was fighting fire and tackling everything as I could. Everything else was ignored and I have a lot to catch up on but that's for longer term priorities to pick back up now I have more time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The project leaders - poor management and the project has only just launched so it's hectic and still needs time for everything to embed as three companies trying to work together with an overall fourth external project team and it's got teething problems as they all work in different ways and at different pressure speeds.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Nope, not in control just responding reactively.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I got everything done, but not with the care and attention to detail I usually give.

situation: My wife is an alcoholic, and we got into an argument about her drinking. I broke down crying, begging her to stop. She has stopped...for now at least. I was trying to reason with her because she had fallen and fractured her shoulder a couple of months ago due to her drinking. I caught her this past week drinking when she wasn't expecting me. I needed her to understand the destruction this is causing. I'm left feeling concerned. I'm not sure how this will play out in the long run. I have to give her an opportunity though.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal. She is my wife and best friend and I love her and I want her to let me help her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: At least I caught her drinking and we have been able to address this so that was helpful. I've caught her drinking so many times before and I'm losing hope.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Her but maybe me as well. Well my wife keeps choosing to drink and I can't help but wonder if I'm not doing enough for her.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. I always feel like a pleading fool.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes. We have been down this road several times.

situation: When I found out that I was going to get a new car, I was so excited because we have been looking for a very long time. Our current car was getting older, and with my husband potentially having to travel for work, we wanted something more reliable. The news left me feeling relieved.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened within the last month. It mattered to me because the news left me feeling relieved, and we wanted something more reliable due to my husband potentially having to travel for work.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by getting a newer, safer car.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like it was a joint responsibility between my husband and myself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control because I knew what I wanted.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went as I expected.

situation: I had my son's parents evening, and his teacher was so complimentary about him. The part that made me most emotional was when she said he was so lovely and kind, and because of this, everyone wanted to be his friend and he was always first pick for partner work. It was such a lovely thing to hear. I just wanted to find out how he was doing. It's usually academic and is good to hear, but I think raising kind and caring children is SO important as they are our next generation. For her to tell me such nice things was lovely. I felt really happy and teary, but happy tears. It made me feel warm and so proud. It was important that my son was there to hear this feedback. I think it helps solidify his morals.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me. The most important job I have at the moment is being a mum. Raising children during a time which often feels a little hopeless and full of unkind people, to hear that I am raising the opposite of that and therefore must be doing a good job as a mum is what matters most.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to know to carry on doing what I am doing as it's working.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me and my partner but also my son. He's taking the advice and guidance and clearly running with it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes. We were hearing nothing but praise; there is no way to feel out of control in that situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did expect it as I know the type of person he is, but you just never know when they are surrounded by a lot of other children all day, some of whom can be unkind.

situation: I was at my training session at the gym, feeling quite anxious. I've talked about this with my trainer, who is really supportive and someone I trust. She got me doing deadlifts and bench presses, and during the session, I managed to lift a weight that was a personal best. I needed something to make me feel more confident about myself, and achieving this goal left me feeling really proud. I went out feeling much more positive about myself, and that positivity translates into other areas of my life as well. Having a relationship with my trainer that is supportive and built on trust is important to me, as I know she won't ask me to do anything she knows I'm not capable of.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered significantly to me because achieving a personal best in my training session helped boost my confidence and reduced my anxiety. If I had had a bad training session where I didn't feel I was making progress, I think it would have increased my anxiety even more.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by giving me more confidence in other areas of my life. It makes me more willing to take on other challenges or have difficult conversations with people.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think both myself and my trainer were most responsible for all of this. Having a supportive relationship with my trainer, built on trust, is important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control during the situation. Although my trainer gives me exercises, I can feed back if I don't feel comfortable at any point.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected.

situation: I have recently come off crack cocaine, and in the last week, it will be exactly 3 months since I stopped using. I had been using crack cocaine for 2 years, and it was taking all my money and ruining my life. I've been working with a support group for 6 months, and I needed to stop. At first, I felt very, very ill, and it was the hardest thing I ever had to do. But when I received my 3 months clean badge and a gift from my workers, I felt proud and very happy. Seeing my children again was important to me, and I will never go back to that situation again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was Monday 23rd February and it meant everything to me because only 6 months before that I was at the lowest part of my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: When I was using crack cocaine every day I felt like killing myself. I was with a boyfriend who wasn't very nice to me as well. I think the feeling will never completely go away, but as long as I am never around the people I used to be around, I will be fine. It's hard seeing it on the tele so much as well.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My ex-boyfriend.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, not at all. It's all I thought about from the minute I woke up.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I never expected it to take all my money, over £2000 a week.

situation: I had been on the lookout for my dream job and happened to see an advert for a new Jobs App called JOB TODAY. I downloaded the app, and the very first job I saw was exactly what I was looking for, so I immediately applied. Within 48 hours, I got a response and a request to email my CV directly to the company, which I did immediately. The following day, I was offered an interview, which is going to be in two days' time. I wanted to have a fair shot at the position and wanted any positive outcome, in this case being offered an interview. I was very excited and thrilled, especially because I had previously applied for tens of jobs and hardly got any response. It was important to me because I felt recognized and 'seen'.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered immensely to me because it's the first step in organizing my life to ultimately bring me stability and self-worthiness.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by giving me a great sense of purpose and assuring me that there are still opportunities out there if one does not give up.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was largely responsible for that in that I looked at my situation and that spurred me on to taking action and pursuing what I need to be in the right place I want to be.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because only I can be in control; no one else can do this for me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, so far things have gone as expected.

situation: I was having a conversation on the telephone with a relative, just a general catchup since we speak on the phone each week as a matter of habit. During the call, they raised concerns about another one of our relatives, which left me feeling really concerned. The points they brought up were quite worrying, and it made me wonder if this relative's mental health is all right or if there might be other things happening in their life that we're not aware of. On the positive side, it was good that we were both able to talk openly about our concerns surrounding this relative and share how we both felt.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened on Thursday. It was really important to me as it made me aware of issues with this other relative that we may need to address.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by making me aware of a situation with this other relative that I had not previously been aware of.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't think that there was necessarily a sense of responsibility.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control as I had not initiated the discussion on this other relative.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The telephone did not go as expected as I wasn't expecting concerns to be raised in the conversation about the other relative.

situation: During my annual check-up at my primary care doctor's office, I received the results of my recent blood work. Everything came back normal, and my A1C was 5.5, which is the closest to normal you'll ever get. It was an annual checkup, and I was there to get my blood work results. I felt extremely happy and very proud of myself. The fact that my doctor was also extremely happy with my results made me feel very much cared for.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered very much to me because I'm getting older and I live alone, and my health is very important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because it encouraged me to continue on this journey of mine for good health.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both myself and my doctor were responsible for these results.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt completely in control. When you have diabetes, you need to be in control of not only your eating habits but even exercising and sticking to it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I knew I was going to get good results, but I never imagined how good they were going to be, and I was exhilarated.

situation: I recently visited my grandson, who is just 6 months old. I hadn't seen him since Christmas, and he had changed so much in 2 months, which made me very emotional. I wanted to see how much he has grown. When I arrived at the house, I felt extremely happy. It meant so much to me to see him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Feb 19, 2026, in the afternoon. It mattered a lot to me because seeing my grandson after two months and witnessing how much he had grown was very emotional and meaningful.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me somewhat because I knew I would have to leave in a few days, making the visit bittersweet.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my daughter was most responsible for all of this because she moved away. However, I am also proud of her for accomplishing so much.
appraisal_reasoning.control: During the visit, I felt like I had to get as much quality time in as possible, which was stressful. This indicates that I felt some pressure and lacked control over the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, and I had a wonderful time.

situation: I traveled to England to pick up my daughter and grandson because her husband had cheated on her. I wanted to be there to support my daughter, both emotionally and physically. She needed help with my grandson since he's only 1 1/2 years old, and she also needed emotional support to leave her husband and move back to the States. The whole situation left me feeling drained emotionally and physically, but I did not regret doing it. We are always there when our kids need us. It was important for me to show my daughter that I will always be there for her, and to let my grandson see that I will always be his support too.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I just made this trip at the end of February and we have been back in Florida for about a week. This mattered greatly to me because I wanted to be there for my daughter in HER timing, not mine.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was difficult because it left my husband at home to care for our four animals. I was also away from my job for a week. My son traveled with me and that meant him also not working for a week. But traveling and seeing Windsor and London again with my son created some wonderful memories.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Clearly my son-in-law. I still love him but he has made some terrible choices and was not willing to work on anything. This left no choice but for my daughter to leave England.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of the situation at all. I was there in the background, able to help with whatever they needed. But I let my daughter and son-in-law control the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think things went fairly as I expected. I do think that 'tasks' got done slowly and I would not have put them off until the end. It would have left us more time to sightsee and relax.

situation: I visited a town on holiday that reminded me of the holidays I had with my son when he was young. He sadly died in 2023 at the age of 28. I was visiting with my sister and thought it would be a nice drive over the moors. I hadn't expected to feel so emotional. I was trying to have a nice drive over the moors with my sister, but I felt quite sad, thinking about my son and how lovely he was on the holidays we spent there together. I was only wishing I could turn back time, but I realized that this feeling of longing and sadness is something I will carry with me, and nothing will change it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because it was an important part of my son’s childhood. I love holidays and wanted him to experience some memorable holidays whilst he was young.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience hurt me as it just made me remember that my heart has been torn out by losing my son.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for the emotions I felt during that visit, as my emotions and grief pop up uninvited regularly.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I can’t control my grief and don’t expect to. I am having counselling.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The visit went as expected, except I did not stop to look around the town as it would have been too painful.

situation: My manager was made redundant without any warning, and it left me feeling relieved. I needed my organization to act with honesty, and they finally did. It was important for me to realize that my manager was incompetent and not a good leader.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered because I didn't deserve it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Hurt me because I had no warning. Nothing at all helped me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My manager was most responsible because she gave me no warning and didn't reach out afterwards.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control at all because it was all done behind my back.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was shocked how cold and callous the people involved were. I won't trust people in managerial positions again.

situation: My sister went to the hospital last night, panicking and thinking she was dying because she had pains running through her body. She recently lost her husband, so I was very worried about her and thought she was having some kind of panic attack. I wanted answers as soon as possible and to know that she was okay. The whole situation left me feeling worried and anxious. It was also important to me that everyone looking after her was okay, including my mum and dad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last night, and it mattered a lot to me as she's been through so much. I was concerned about her welfare.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as it's more trauma for us as a family to deal with.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think her mental health was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It definitely felt way beyond my control, because there was nothing I could do to help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, as expected it was something minor causing her to feel the way she did.

situation: My job has been under threat for a year, and this week new structures were announced, but my post isn’t in it. Strangely, I found myself wanting to just talk to people, to ask them what gaps I have in my knowledge and experience. Despite being an introvert, I desperately needed company. Honestly, I feel pretty numb about it all. I do feel lighter, as though the uncertainty has been removed, but I’m experiencing episodes of terror when I think about what’s next. The fact that we still don’t have clear information, like job descriptions and functions to retain or transfer, has left me feeling confused and angry.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered hugely because it’s not just my job, but I’ve been working in the field all my life. It’s also quite an important role and I can see the impact that stopping processes is going to have.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped to actually know what the structures looked like - to know what SMT are thinking about in terms of what to retain. But it hurt enormously to know that my colleagues would be impacted, as will providers, external staff and, ultimately, patients. We are at the point where another Mid Staffs like 'scandal' is going to emerge in the foreseeable future, and it’s incredibly frustrating to know that current actions will only make this worse.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Wes Streeting. He has blood on his hands.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, not at all - I had no influence over the decision. It may be adjusted with feedback, but the proposed system is fundamentally unsafe.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think it went entirely as I had feared, rather than being entirely what I had expected. I wasn’t sure what to expect.

situation: My wife's father was told he has to undergo a very serious operation, and the emotions attached to this news were incredibly high. We were trying to give him emotional support during this difficult time. The situation left us feeling worried because we know the operation will leave him in intensive care for a while. We just wanted to express to him how important this operation is, as it is life-saving.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened last week and it mattered as my wife is very close to her dad.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has given us lots of things to worry about over the coming weeks.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody is responsible; it is just part of the situation and cannot be changed.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We didn't feel in control at all; in fact, we felt quite helpless.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went a little unexpectedly as her dad was quite calm about the situation and was actually reassuring towards us.

situation: My cat was acting strange, not eating or drinking, and it made me worried that he was ill. I was really trying to ensure my cat's well-being because I was concerned about his health. I felt very stressed and worried, especially since I recently lost a cat and was upset that the same might happen again. On top of that, I was worried about a potentially high vet's bill and how I could afford it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 10 days ago, I was at home and realized that his food and water hadn't been touched from the night before. I went to find him and he seemed very sleepy and not his usual energetic little bundle of energy. That was when the panic set in and I became afraid that he was seriously ill and I might lose him. He is my baby and after losing Belle last year, I couldn't face losing Toby too.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It brought up a lot of bad memories of Belle and how ill she was. It made my anxiety much worse, especially because I had to call the vet and I get very anxious when I have to talk on the telephone.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't think anyone was responsible for it. It turned out that he was just a little under the weather and he was fine again within a few hours.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt helpless. I did not know how I could help him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I thought that I was going to lose him, so things did not go that way, which was a massive relief.

situation: I had to go to an urgent care treatment centre because I felt very poorly and was worried about my health. I was having heart palpitations, and my GP was concerned. I felt very emotional because I was worried and felt so unwell, and I didn't know what was wrong with me. I just wanted to feel better. But after seeing the nurse at the treatment centre, I felt distressed and upset because it seemed like my health concerns were dismissed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I was feeling so rubbish and I just wanted to get treatment so I felt better and more like myself again. My health problems were taking over my life as I was having to take time off work.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as I felt physically unwell, I was having time off from work, and was struggling to function in my everyday life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was really responsible, but the nurse was for dismissing my health concerns so easily.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control as my health was literally in their hands and they chose to dismiss me, which I could not control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: My expectations were definitely not met. I did not get the treatment I needed or was asking for.

situation: My son was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes and was rushed to the hospital with ketoacidosis. He was very ill, and we ended up staying in the hospital for five days. During that time, my main focus was on his care and wellbeing, going into survival mode to ensure he got better from the immediate danger. I also wanted to learn how to care for him after we left the hospital. It was important for me to rest when I could and also to make sure I was there for my other children.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened just after the household had a virus, and we weren't aware anything more serious was happening at the time. I was devastated when we found out how ill he really was.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me build resilience and expertise, but it has come at the cost of looking after myself and lack of sleep. I also now cannot work as I am a carer.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It's an autoimmune disease, probably brought on by the virus exposure. No one is to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Sometimes yes, sometimes no. Learning how to treat diabetes and having constantly to adapt dosages and ratios is very hard, but the more you do it the more confidence we have.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, because we had no idea what to expect. Everything is unfolding slowly, and the team does not try to overwhelm us with new information, so things will change and we will have to adapt.

situation: My direct supervisor, who I consider a friend, had to take a leave of absence for stress-related reasons. During that time, I was really just trying to make sure he's okay. I felt better when he came back, but it's frustrating because management hasn't lightened his responsibility at all. Right now, what's most important to me is his well-being.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week. It matters because he's my friend and we need him to run the lab.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped to forge new dynamics within our team. It hurts because he has to approve purchase of raw materials which were running out.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Mainly the lack of coordination in other high level departments that he has to coordinate with.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I don't have the knowledge or authority to help much.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing disastrous happened as far as workflows.

situation: I went on a short family holiday to a really nice place in the country. It was a small village that was pretty, with a castle and nice pubs and restaurants. The trip went well, and it was good family time. We love to travel, so we were looking to achieve a few things: travel somewhere new, see some new places, and cover a new area of the country. We wanted to make some family memories and help our children learn and grow. I was aiming for a nice, good value holiday that was busy but overall relaxing. I felt fine overall after the trip and am keen to do more, go somewhere else, and spend similar time as a family again. It was a positive experience and it contributes to my family's overall life goals. Value is important to me, as I like to remain frugal. Food and drink are also important to us, but mainly, it's crucial that our children are fulfilled, meaning they get time to play, relax, and see something interesting.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters a great deal but I am also aware that it is a luxury. Holidays aren't a given and they do cost money and require effort. Without doing this we would function fine and fill our time and purpose another way. But it still matters a lot to us as a family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't hurt. It was quite affordable but it was stressful in parts. The travel wasn't ideal and it was quite rushed. But overall it helped us achieve our goals.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me and my wife. We work hard to get these things and it's hard work with 3 children. It takes planning, organisation and persistence to make these things work. My wife took the brunt of organising this one.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We're always in control. Even if it feels like we're not. Nothing bad happened here so we were able to control the narrative and the pace somewhat.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did go as expected. It was fairly textbook overall.

situation: I'm getting terribly stressed and panicky, feeling time pressured and having to get things done in an emergency because I've received a terminal diagnosis. I need to get my financial affairs simplified, made legally watertight, and explained to my executor. This situation has left me feeling terrified, angry, helpless, resentful, and grieving. It's really important to me to get it all sorted and easy for my husband to understand, and to make sure my money is protected.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I'm going to die very soon, without any prior warning, possibly unpleasantly, and I can't stop it. It matters hugely. As does making sure my husband has the least problems with sorting out my affairs.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Negative! Existential, loss, grief, upset.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me, smoking 30 years ago maybe? God? Who knows. And me not being able to be very calm sometimes.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I have no control. I wish I did. Time is not there for me to press on calmly, too many other things going on, too many unknowns, too many medical appointments, other people.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole situation was utterly unexpected!

situation: Last week, I lost my very close friend who had been suffering from a lot of diseases. After a few days, he reached the end of his life. I think life is nothing but a journey, and we need to be ready to say bye. This situation left me feeling like nothing is permanent.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The incident happened in the last month. It mattered to me a lot because it left me feeling like nothing is permanent.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me a lot. I lost all of my interest towards the world.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible. The fate is written by the Almighty.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Sometimes I am very conscious about the situation, but sometimes I lost my sense.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The situation did not always go as I expected. Sometimes there is no control over the condition.

situation: My son submitted a piece of art he created to a student art fair and won a prestigious award in his chosen category. I didn't personally need anything from this situation except to know that my son was proud of himself. Seeing him achieve this made me feel that he is capable of anything he sets his mind to. It's important to me that he is aware of his accomplishments and understands the value of his hard work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it mattered to my son.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation did not help or hurt me; it was just a proud moment that showcased how multi-faceted he is.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son was most responsible for all of this; it was his talent that led to the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was more along for the ride.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I knew he would get some type of award, but I didn't know it would be the biggest one available at the event.

situation: It was my birthday, and I was spoiled rotten by my grandsons. I was just enjoying my day, and honestly, I didn't need or want anything except for my family to be around me. The whole situation left me feeling really happy, loved, and appreciated. I also wanted my family to enjoy the lunch party I had prepared.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago, and it mattered a great deal to me as I care for my family all year round. It's a time they can show their appreciation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me to realize how loved I am. It didn't hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My whole family, especially my two little grandsons, were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected them to.

situation: In the last week, I had to go into my new job before my formal employment date for a voluntary orientation and to bring in paperwork they needed for my onboarding. They told us in the email that most people go to these things, so I expected a large number of people to turn up. But when I arrived, only three of us had attended. I found the situation very overwhelming and nervous because the big boss was there giving us questions on a one-to-one basis, which I found hard since this is my first job in the specific field. In an ideal world, more people would be there so there was less attention on me and more of an opportunity to observe the role and learn as I go. The situation left me feeling very overwhelmed and anxious for my new job as I felt like I was in a worse situation than my peers who have more experience. It's my first office job and a real step up for me professionally.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me as this is a new and my first role in a professional office setting instead of working a bar or working in retail. I felt like I am in a new league of professionals and I was worried about how to speak and act.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to see the office and where I will work. But I also found it overwhelming going from a small retail store to a large-scale office with well over a thousand people working there. I have worked very hard to get this position but I also feel immensely stressed to succeed in the role.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that the pressure is a mix of me preparing for a new role and potentially having fear for something in the future I have no control over yet. But also the business sends emails asking for new documents for onboarding which is very overwhelming as I have never had this in my older roles.
appraisal_reasoning.control: This was my first time seeing the office and I was on a tour so I had no control over where I was going and what we were going to do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was expecting more people to be there and was expecting more of a group tour type situation. Instead, there were more staff than new people, making me feel on the back foot and overwhelmed. There were also a lot of questions about myself and my personal life which I was not expecting.

situation: A close family member had come to visit me, but they had to return home after a short stay. They live in another country and needed to go back for work. I wasn't trying to do anything specific during their visit, but I was sad to see them go after only staying for two weeks. It was important to me because I knew it would be unlikely for me to see them for a while, as they live on another continent.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot because they are close to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by allowing me to spend time with them. I wasn't hurt, just sad.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don’t think of it in terms of responsibility.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control because I knew beforehand they would be staying for two weeks.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, although they were jet-lagged when they first arrived.

situation: My mum, who has Alzheimer's, now needs a scan to rule out cancer. The hospital called me to let me know about this, and if she does have it, they probably won't be able to operate or do anything because of her physical condition. I really wanted them to tell me she had something else from her recent scan, something we could medicate. At first, I felt shocked, then quite upset. I felt so bad for her; she's been through a lot. It was important to me that the person telling me the information was empathetic and informative, and she was.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few days ago. The call was unexpected because I thought she'd just get medication to help her. It's now weighing on my mind because further testing will be carried out. I love my mum. I want her to be okay.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has helped because it points to the fact that there might be something underlying which has caused my mum to deteriorate so quickly. It's hurt me because cancer didn't cross my mind.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: When I felt angry I blamed the hospital but right now I'm blaming some higher power. Life isn't fair and I'm angry.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel completely out of control. There is nothing I can do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect to hear that they need to rule out cancer. It hasn't crossed my mind.

situation: I had an argument with my partner, and it was really emotional because I felt like I had really upset him. I hadn't phoned him when I said I would, and he felt upset by that and spiraled. I just wanted to have a nice day, but the situation left me feeling deflated and upset. My partner's feelings were a crucial aspect of the situation for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened while I was driving for work and simply forgot to call him. When I did phone him, I couldn't speak for long, and he likes to fall asleep on the phone to me and couldn't. The situation mattered to me because I felt like I had done wrong and upset him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt like I had done wrong and upset him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the expectations of me were too much; it shouldn't have mattered.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't really feel in control. I just felt like I couldn't do anything right.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yeah, kind of. We always seem to go that way when we argue; it is always intense.

situation: I wrote my wedding vows, and it made me emotional. I was trying to complete my vows before my upcoming wedding, and I needed time alone to reflect and do this properly. As I was writing, I felt overwhelmed at times, happy and excited, nervous and scared.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week and it was very important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me express my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me and my fiance.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I do because I was the one writing the vows.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was harder than I expected.

situation: I have a close personal friend who I've known for over 25 years, and she has a granddaughter with some mental issues. I've known the granddaughter her entire life. Recently, the granddaughter has been living with my friend for a few months while she looks for a job and a place of her own. At first, they were getting along well, but now there's a lot of tension between them, and my friend wants to talk to me about it constantly. No matter what I say or recommend, it doesn't seem to please her. I'm at a point where I really don't want to talk to my friend about this situation anymore, but I don't know how to tell her. I keep suggesting that she seek counseling for her granddaughter and encourage her to move out. I don't want to be disloyal, but my friend insists on leaving things the way they are. It's very important to me that the granddaughter gets help with her mental issues, and I also want my friend to not be constantly stressed out because she has health issues of her own.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The granddaughter moved in about 6 months back and things were going well initially. Since then, she has started and lost about 3 jobs and now does not seem to be trying at all, which frustrates my friend and leads her to want to talk to me about it. Last week, they had a very serious argument, and I told her she should ask her granddaughter to leave. This situation matters to me because I care about both of them and want the granddaughter to get help with her mental issues, while also wanting my friend to not be constantly stressed out due to her own health issues.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurts me to see two people that I care about in this turmoil constantly and nothing is being resolved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think that the granddaughter's mental health issues are having a great deal to do with this situation. Also, I think that my friend's love for her granddaughter is blinding her to the seriousness of what is happening.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I never feel like I am in control of this situation and neither is anyone else.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything finally came to a head last weekend, and my friend had to call the police and have her granddaughter removed from her apartment. I could see this coming for a long time, but my friend refused to listen to me. Now she is truly brokenhearted, and I feel sympathy for her but relieved at the same time.

situation: I was at the park with my 15-month-old, just wanting him to have fun and continue gaining his confidence. We were playing around when he fell over and hit some fencing around a broken bit of play equipment. He got a small chip on his tooth, and I was really upset and worried for him. He's only had teeth for a short time, and I was concerned about how his smile might look now. He's recently become more confident in his walking and running, and I was hoping he wasn't in pain, though initially, he was very upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I was upset and worried about how his tooth might look in the future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me very scared of when he hurts himself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel partly the council is responsible for not repairing the park, but mainly it was just an accident as he walks and runs more.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because it couldn't be helped; he just went down so quick.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. Him falling and hitting his face wasn't planned, so it was completely unexpected.

situation: I re-started work after taking a break due to poor mental health, returning to a department I had worked in before. I was worried people might think negatively of me because of my break, but everyone was very nice and compassionate, which was a pleasant surprise. I felt very grateful for such a nice experience. I needed reassurance that I was making the right decision and that I wouldn't be treated differently because of my break and the reasons behind it. I required a bit of extra support to ease myself back in and wanted to feel like I had a safe space if anything went wrong. Flexibility was important to reduce stress. The situation left me feeling very happy and grateful. I felt supported, cared for, and respected for the work I can do. I felt well-liked and comfortable in the workplace. I wanted to feel competent and confident in my ability to perform my job well, and this all came back to me very quickly, like I never left!

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot after having a negative experience in another department, alongside worsening mental health. Therefore, this helped strengthen me and placed faith back into myself and others.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation helped me feel more confident and competent. It proved to myself that I can do hard things. Also, that people are generally nice and compassionate who just want the best for you.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My manager was helpful in being understanding and compassionate whilst not prying for information, this behaviour was also reflected in my colleagues. My manager also let me take the lead regarding how many shifts I do.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt that I was in control as I decided when I would like to start working again, and how often I would like to work and what hours.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They went better than expected. I was concerned people would negatively judge me for my decisions and would pry and push for information. However, people were quick to accept my decisions and thought processes, without pushing me for my information than I was willing to give. No one treated me any differently.

situation: It was the recent cold wave that was harmful to my plants. I wanted to move them indoors, but it wasn't possible, which left me feeling a bit helpless.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because of the appearance of the garden.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making more work for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the climate was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control during this event because it was out of my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went mostly as I expected.

situation: I was watching Grey's Anatomy and the episode was so emotional that it drove me to tears. I wasn't trying to do anything else, I just needed to cry to get it out. Afterward, I felt worn out. I noticed that I cried very easily, and that concerned me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was within the last week. It didn't matter to me that much, I obviously just needed to cry.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't really do either.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The creators of Grey's Anatomy and the actors.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I definitely was not in control. I cried very easily.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting to cry so easily, that was unexpected.

situation: I was estranged from my daughter, but now we're getting back together. This week, she asked me to help her with her health insurance plan. I felt really emotional that she reached out to me for help. I sell insurance, and while she was growing up, I don't think she realized how important health insurance is and how it helps people, mainly because her mother told her my job wasn't important and that all I do is drive around. Despite the years of being estranged, I feel blessed by the Grace of God for helping me through, along with expert therapists who had gone through this horrible experience themselves. I've learned to be a better listener because of the estrangement and discovered the importance of expressing my feelings rather than assuming my daughter knows how I feel about her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it mattered to me because I felt needed by her. I hope that this is the only reason she called.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I was able to be there to help her. I hope it also showed her how much I know about this topic and how important health insurance is and how it helps people. My job does matter.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I did the research to pick out the best plan for her on the health care marketplace as she is going from full-time employment to part-time and does not qualify for health insurance anymore. The reason she is going to part-time is she is in school and her school schedule conflicts with her job. She is studying to be a sonographer.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control as I have been selling insurance, payroll services, and workers compensation insurance B2B for 23 years.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, she signed up for the plan I suggested through BCBS and paid the premium without having a lapse in coverage, which she understood could not happen.

situation: My son's friend's girlfriend committed suicide, and all I was trying to do was support my son so he could support his friend. Both my son and his friend were abroad together at the time. I felt hollowed out and desperately sad for her family. Despite the tragedy, I was proud of the way my son managed to support his friend during such a difficult time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a fair bit to me. I did not know the girl, but I know my son's friend quite well. It mattered because someone had taken their own life. She was only 19 or so. It's tragic and final and destructive and I hate to think how she must have felt and how her family feel now.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Well, it has helped me to see my son as a responsible person who supports his friends in a meaningful way and who was able to go to his friend and be there for him, even although it was very difficult for my son.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I have no idea. I don't know the background at all.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of myself. I was very removed from the situation. No one was in control of the situation. I felt glad that my son phoned me to talk about it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The entire thing was unexpected.

situation: I was informed by my manager that a co-worker would be taking over some of my responsibilities, which left me feeling upset and hurt. I would have been open to 'sharing' the responsibility, but not having her take it over entirely. It feels as though she believes she knows more than I do, which is frustrating. She's not someone I trust, as she tends to act in her own interest. I feel undervalued and disappointed because my manager supported her instead of me. This feels like a betrayal. I am passionate about my work, and this is just one aspect of my many duties.
