I'm trying to come to terms with this change, even though I've had to adapt to numerous changes in my role, but this one is particularly difficult.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal. It still does. I'm losing sleep over it. I can't get it out of my head. We have a meeting next week to go over the changes and I'm dreading it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has hurt my pride. She 'won' and that really bothers me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My manager is responsible, and her and her manager.
appraisal_reasoning.control: They never included me in the discussions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I would have expected to discuss and allow both of us to answer questions for contractors.

situation: We had a stretch of cold weather that made it just miserable for an unusually long amount of time. When it gets below a certain temperature, our furnace makes a horrendous noise that sounds like a rough running big truck is in the house, and you can feel the vibrations. It can be unnerving. The combination of those things, plus my senior dog having a flare of arthritis and not wanting to eat, plus some old memories that resurfaced, all piled together and I came out of it feeling just really sad for quite a few days. I wanted the outside temperatures to warm up, the furnace to stop making the horrible sound and vibration, and I wanted my dog to feel better and to eat. I also wanted to block out memories from the past and feel happier. I felt just horribly sad and not exactly completely hopeless, but close. It was around Valentine's Day, and my first husband had ended our marriage on Valentine's Day, so part of me sometimes gets nervous that my current husband might do the same, even though I know that's not going to happen.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Valentine's Day 1997, it mattered a lot. It felt like my world was collapsing as my first marriage came to an end. I didn't know then that it was actually a new beginning. The more recent stuff was just a lot of little things that stacked up and felt bigger than they were because they went on for so long.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The divorce hurt me because I felt like a complete failure in life and wasn't quite sure what my purpose was. However, once I got over the initial shock and depression, I was able to gather my thoughts and my strength and start over. I picked up and moved across the country to somewhere I'd never been before. Then I met my current husband, who is truly the love of my life, and I'm now able to see that it was really a gift, that first marriage ending, because my life is so much better now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My faith and my current husband.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was definitely in control when I moved myself across the country.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect that moving out here, I'd find my current husband. There were other unexpected events. My mother died unexpectedly just a few months before my wedding to my current husband.

situation: My grandson broke his leg in a freak accident, and it was really upsetting at first. I wanted to reassure my daughter that these things happen and that she wasn't a bad mother, even though she seemed to believe that. Seeing her more calm the next day helped me feel better about the situation. It was important for me to know that my grandson was as happy as could be given the circumstances, so I sent both him and my daughter a small gift to let them know I was thinking of them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot, because I love my daughter and my grandson very much.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I was upset for them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody, because it was a freak accident.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control because I was far away and unable to help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things have settled down and they seem to be coping okay.

situation: I was trying to get on the bus to head to university, but the bus driver didn't let me on for no reason. Just as I was getting on, the driver shut the doors right in my face and drove away. I was pissed off the whole day because of it. It was important to me that I didn't lose my head completely in public, even though I was really frustrated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened earlier this week and it mattered quite a bit for like 20 minutes, but didn't affect me heavily.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because he did it for no good reason.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Him, because he did it maliciously.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control because I wasn't the one driving the bus.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected because I expected to get let on the bus but wasn't.

situation: My wife got mad at me for leaving my journal out, and I responded by saying I will leave it out wherever I want to. I just want freedom. The whole situation left me feeling pissed, like I want to divorce her. She's such a controller.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday. It mattered to me because it reinforced that she is damaged.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by bringing up a big distance between us.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt most responsible for all of this because I've been taking this shit for so long.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control during the situation. She also is a hoarder.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as they always do; she acts like nothing happens and I don't.

situation: I live in an apartment building, and every morning around 5 am, a young woman who clearly has mental issues starts screaming, slamming her door, and pounding on walls. I just want it to stop because she is very mentally unstable and potentially violent. I can't confront her because I don't know how she might react. The situation leaves my heart pounding and gives me a bad headache.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered quite a bit because I needed my sleep, and I had to deal with it long before I wanted to get up for the morning.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as it affects my whole day, causing me to get sleep-deprived and start the morning in a bad mood.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She is responsible, her and her severe mental problems.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't feel like I have much control over the situation. The building isn't doing anything about evicting her, and I can't confront her to stop because it probably would cause her to act out more.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected. She acted nuts and I knew there wasn't anything I could do about it.

situation: My good friend and neighbor recently had surgery in the hospital to remove a cancer growth from her face and mouth. Although the operation is done, there are complications, and she'll be in the hospital indefinitely until it's sorted out. I visited her yesterday. I'm taking care of her house cat by going into her home two or three times a day to feed it, change the litter tray, and wanted to reassure her that everything is okay with her pet. I also wanted to give her some moral support because she has very few friends, and her close family doesn't seem to visit much. When I left, I felt somewhat shocked because she has lost a good part of her face after the operation and will need a facial reconstruction. However, I was pleased to see her, and she looked better than I had thought before visiting. I showed her some pictures of her cat, and she felt better afterwards, which made me feel pleased. On reflection, it was a roller coaster of mixed emotions but nonetheless progress. It was important that I got to see her, and I now know it'll be easier the next time I go.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot as I've been her neighbor for several years and we've grown very close, especially being on our own and enjoying each other's company. I was devastated to hear her news a few weeks ago and how it all materialized so quickly. It's not an overnight fix, and she may be in hospital for quite a number of weeks.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It's not helped at all but hurt, yes maybe, but only from an emotional point of feeling. We also had several days out planned for the next few months which will now have to be put on hold.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was to blame; it's just mother nature and life situations. Unfortunately, people get cancer, and it's something that you can't see coming and just have to deal with accordingly.
appraisal_reasoning.control: The situation of visiting her, yes, I was in control. I knew the visiting times and planned my route and day of traveling to the hospital.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The conversation went as best it could given the circumstances, especially as I went with an open mind.

situation: One of my best friends told me a week ago that my boyfriend was buying me a rose ring for my birthday. When I told her I didn't want to know about it, she showed me a photo of it on her phone. I was so upset and mad at her because it was my first birthday with my new boyfriend and she ruined the surprise. I cried because it hurt my feelings. I needed to trust that she wouldn't hurt me like that by ruining my birthday. She shouldn't have told me. I would have been happier if she hadn't said anything. The whole situation left me feeling very upset and hurt. I would never do that to anybody. I will never trust her again. Our friendship has become distanced since that happened.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a week before my birthday in February. It mattered a lot to me because I hadn't been with my boyfriend long, and the fact he bought me jewelry was a big deal. It should have been a surprise, and knowing about it took away a very happy moment I would have had with my boyfriend.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by taking away the surprise and an intimate moment with my boyfriend. It broke his trust because he told her about it, and she showed it to me the very day he told her. I can't trust her anymore, and she was one of my best friends for the last six years.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She was most responsible for all of this. My boyfriend has also been friends with her for 10 years, and she broke that trust. She should have kept it a secret, but she chose to ruin the surprise for me, so it is her fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control. I was so hurt and stressed over it. I ended up telling my boyfriend what she did because I couldn't pretend like I didn't know about it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did not go as expected. I told her how bad it hurt us, and she said the only reason she told us was because she was happy for the both of us, which makes no sense to me. She said she was sorry, but you can't take it back or change it.

situation: I felt happy when I saw a photo of my daughter and her new boyfriend. She had a very bad relationship in the past, so when I saw her smiling in this new photo with a new boyfriend, I just felt happy. I want the best for her, and seeing her happy made me feel comfortable that she could be happy in life. I felt like she finally found a happiness that she deserves, someone that doesn't bring her down and make her feel bad about herself.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I saw the photo earlier in the week. She had taken a trip with the man and showed me the photo from the trip. Seeing my daughter happy was quite meaningful to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I guess it helped me feel like she was finally able to be herself and be happy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like she was responsible for this. She took herself out of a bad situation and worked on her own development. In doing this, she was able to meet someone who is kind to her.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I am not in control of my daughter's happiness. I just hope I raised her in a way that she has confidence in herself.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was a nice surprise to see her getting close to someone again.

situation: I was watching a movie with my wife on TV, and it turned out to be very emotional, bringing me to tears. I just wanted to be entertained, but the movie ended up making me feel good and sad at the same time. I knew it was based on true events, but I didn't expect to be so moved by it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal because I could relate to the people involved.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did neither.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The actors did a great job of bringing the story to life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I was in control, I just let it flow.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was familiar with the story and knew what the outcome was to be.

situation: I was watching my great grandson drawing. I just wanted him to continue and not react to me watching him, allowing him to be his natural four-year-old self. The whole situation left me feeling warm, happy, and content. I was appreciating that he won't stay so young, innocent, and natural for long.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because any time with him is very special.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me as I don’t see him enough, and he changes and grows so rapidly.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He was responsible by just being him. The situation was good as several members of the family were there, laughing and talking.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I wasn’t controlling nothing or anyone. That felt great, as I usually have to organise everything.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything was lovely. It was a fabulous and relaxed few hours.

situation: I watched a show called 'When Life Gives You Tangerines' and it made me cry a lot and reflect on my life with my parents and how I want to treat them better. I wanted to relax and watch what I have heard was a really good show. I knew it was going to be emotional but it really hit me a lot harder than I thought it would and really made me reflect on my own relationship with my parents. It made me want to change my relationship with my parents and I want to make a change before it is too late.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It made me want to make a change and I really saw myself in one of the characters and how maybe I haven't been the best child to my parents and don't appreciate all that they do and have done for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me in a sense that it made me realize that maybe I have been a bad child and that I should do more for my parents whilst I still have the time to.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really, I was watching it play out and it felt like a mirror in front of me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I guess it did but I didn't realize it was going to hit me as hard as it did.

situation: I had my first session with a new therapist, and it felt like she was a great fit. I've been doing a lot of the work by myself for a while, but then I decided I shouldn't have to anymore. It's been tough finding a therapist who feels qualified, but she was brilliant the whole time. I didn't feel unsafe once. After the session, I felt happy, relieved, and hopeful. I also didn't abandon myself during the session. I stayed with myself the whole time, checking in, noticing what I was feeling, and tracking all of it. That felt great too, and I honored myself.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I can't heal certain things on my own; attachment harm requires others to really heal. It was nice to find someone I felt safe with.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me feel hopeful and excited, but after the session, I felt a lot of grief. Realizing that I didn't really have safety before and had to hide myself my whole life brought up these feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both my therapist and I were responsible for this experience. She felt like someone very good at her job, and I was finally in a spot to accept that kind of help.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt mostly in control during the session. It felt like she let me lead, but when she felt like I was going too far, she flawlessly guided me back.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think it went better than expected, even though part of me was still waiting for it to go wrong.

situation: My wife's grandfather passed away, and it was very sad. I didn't need or want anything for myself; my focus was on consoling my wife, who was very upset about it. The circumstances of his passing made me feel very sad too. The most important thing for me was making sure she was okay.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 weeks ago. It mattered a lot to me because it was so sudden, and we weren't expecting it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I had become close with him. I miss talking to him all the time about sports and life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He worked a job where he was exposed to elements that gave him cancer, and we didn't even know he was sick.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt totally out of my control. There was nothing I could do to help him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. We figured he would be able to recover but was unable to.

situation: I lost my temper and shouted at my child when he poured a cup of tea over me and the floor while we were having some time watching TV. I was trying to spend some nice time with my child and needed him to realize how dangerous doing that could have been. I felt angry and frustrated but at the same time upset that I reacted how I did. It was important to me to make sure my son realized how serious the situation was.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because my son's safety is always at the forefront of my mind.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Had the tea been any hotter, either my son or myself could have been burned. We were both upset over the situation but quickly calmed down and made sure we were both okay. The whole situation upset me as I’m struggling with my son's behavior and how to manage it anyway.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my son was most responsible because he deliberately grabbed the cup from my hand and poured it out.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn’t feel in control at all of the situation or my actions. I was holding the cup away from my son, so when he grabbed it, there was nothing I could do to have stopped him. While I have the best of intentions in how to manage my emotions when situations like this arise, my immediate reaction was to shout.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I never expected my son to do this as he’d never done it before.

situation: I was watching how appreciative animals are when given help, and I found myself helping an animal free its young. I wasn't trying to do anything specific; I just wanted to help. As I was doing this, I felt sad about how these beautiful creatures are abused by humans. I wasn't expecting any emotional reaction, but the mother made it quite clear how happy she was, which surprised me. It got me thinking about society and how it's become a cesspit. People seem to only care about themselves these days, trapped in their own little, sad lives. It's a vicious circle with no empathy or consideration for others. It's becoming increasingly difficult to find like-minded people who aren't just zombies.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event didn't particularly matter to me. I was just acting in the way I always have done.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation didn't help or hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I'm always in control of the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected.

situation: I had to complete a statistics exam as part of a screening test for the CCCU DClinPsy course. It was quite a big deal since I had been preparing for almost 2 months. I needed to score very highly on this test to get through to the next stage of the process, which is receiving the offer of attending an interview. After finishing the exam, I felt mixed emotions - I was pleased it was over but concerned because I didn't know all the answers and worried I may not have done well enough. I felt the urge to search up some of the questions to check whether I was right on some of the ones I wasn't sure about. I did this exam last year too and really struggled with the timings. This year, I managed the time pressures so much better, so I felt proud of myself for this accomplishment.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered very heavily as I had been preparing for weeks and spending my evenings getting ready for it after work. The applications are very important and only happen once a year so there's a lot of pressure.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped raise my confidence in how I can manage tough situations. It hasn't hurt me much apart from doubting my knowledge and whether I'll ever pass it (but that's a bit of catastrophising and jumping to conclusions as I've not had feedback yet).
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible for my own performance. Other people designed the test but weren't responsible for my performance.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes as I was very much aware of the time I had left and checking that so I felt I had control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: More or less yes. Was hoping to have been more confident with some answers but I also knew it wasn't going to be easy.

situation: A friend from Sweden flew in to spend a few days with me. I was just renewing a friendship and spending some quality time together. It was important to me to renew a friendship that for the most part is lived online and by phone. Despite the weather being wet and cold, I felt very pleasant, relaxed, and cheerful.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the last few days. It was pleasant, but not deeply emotional or romantically important.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by having a friend to stay who is an easy and undemanding guest. It did not hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Initially, it was pure chance; we met online. But we each contributed equally.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It was not a matter of control, just two friends being together, but I never felt out of control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was fine, but the weather was not, so we could not get out as much as we would have hoped.

situation: I went to see my nephew's play. He's only six, and when I saw him get on stage, he was so confident and joyful. It made me feel really emotional in a positive way. I felt like he was growing up so fast, and it filled me with so much emotion and pride. I was just trying to be there to support him, and I wanted him to know that even if he didn't do great, we would still be super proud. During the play, I was beaming with pride but also started thinking about myself and the fact that I don't have children and wish that I did. I ruminated on this on the way home. I just felt a mix of pride and sadness.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I went to see my nephew's play. It mattered to me a lot because seeing him confident and joyful on stage made me feel emotional and proud, but also brought up feelings of regret and sadness about not having children.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me to self-reflect but also hurt me in a sad kind of way because it made me regret not having children or feeling like I never was given the opportunity.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like God was the most responsible for all of this, for making me who I am today, which didn’t include children, something I would have liked to have done or at least had the option to.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control because once I felt these feelings come up while I was watching the play, it was very hard for me to push them away.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected for me to feel sadness because I went there with such a light heart and I didn’t think that seeing him on stage was going to trigger that emotion in me.

situation: I had an issue at work where there was a problem with a complaint. I was trying to sort out this complicated complaint, and it left me feeling stressed and tired. On top of that, I didn't want my colleague to be stressed or upset about the situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When the event happened, I cared very much about it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me get closer to my colleague, but finding the information was hard.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible as they are my staff.
appraisal_reasoning.control: After I had gathered the information, I did feel in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected.

situation: I found out that a relative had a serious accident, and I was hoping to hear news that would give a clear update on their condition. Unfortunately, the information I received was very ambiguous. I needed someone who could help me make arrangements for planning ongoing care needs. The situation left me feeling confused and very conflicted. There was some relief that the immediate danger had passed, but knowing there are likely catastrophic head injuries made me feel guilty, wondering if it would have been better if they hadn't survived. I really needed someone who would listen and not make judgments.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me. It's not a relative I am personally very close to, but I am close to people in the family who are hugely affected.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because my immediate concern is more with their siblings, who I'm very close to, but I feel like I need to focus on the person in the hospital. It also brought back a lot of difficult memories surrounding my dad's death last year.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No-one was responsible; it was just a stupid accident at home. It could have happened to anyone.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control during this time because there was no warning.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Initially, we expected they would die when life support was removed, so everyone had prepared for, and found peace with, that. However, they survived, and now the future looks very uncertain and very bleak for them.

situation: I was at my neighbor's 90th birthday party, and just before I left, her daughter, who plays in a band, performed Harvest Moon by Neil Young. That song always reminds me of my dad, and unexpectedly, I found tears leaking from my eyes as his memory came flooding back to me. I wasn't really trying to do anything specific; I just wanted to be in the moment and enjoy the memories. I actually enjoyed being in that sentimental moment, and I wished I could have stayed longer to hear more music. The experience left me feeling moved and touched. I've recently stopped taking antidepressants after many years, and those medications can really numb you to the world. Being able to cry at that moment made me feel more alive and connected to the world. It was important for me to feel something for the first time after being numb for so long.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened about 10 days ago. The experience mattered a lot to me because it felt like progress in my life to be able to feel my feelings. It wasn't quite earth-shaking, but it mattered.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think this situation helped me and didn't hurt me at all. It helped me to realize that I was feeling more fully human.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: In some ways, it was just serendipity - being in the right place at the right time. It was a number of things coming together at once to create the feeling - being off the medication, the song coming up at a surprising time, maybe that particular day.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control, but I also felt carried away into memories. I felt in control because I allowed myself to experience those feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was a totally unexpected situation, so I can't say that I had planned it at all. It just unfolded.

situation: My daughter and I had a falling out over a stupid disagreement. We ended up having telephone calls well into the night, where she accused me of being a failure as a mother. I was trying to support her, even though she doesn't think I am supporting her. She believes I am not the mother that she is to my grandson. I just needed peace from all the arguing and the constant telephone conversations that go on for hour after hour. The way I was being spoken to was important to me in this situation, and it left me feeling tired, worn out, and very upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was last Sunday and it mattered to me as I had been at their house for a meal. All was well but she must have had words with her husband then it ends up her phoning me and turning on me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help me whatsoever. It hurt me because I feel I am doing all I can for her. She is after financial help from me which I can and do give her but she does not think I do enough in that way.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My daughter because it came out of nowhere.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I wasn't in control at all. After over two hours of phone calls constantly calling me I turned my phone off.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well things never get sorted, it's never addressed. She was a completely different person yesterday we went out for the day to the seaside.

situation: My daughter stood independently for the first time while we were playing in the living room. She did it out of the blue, and I wasn’t expecting it. I wasn't trying to do anything specific; we were just playing together. It made me feel proud of her, and it made me happy in a way I can’t really put into words. It’s just lovely to see her progressing, and it makes me so proud.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me, because every milestone she hits matters a lot to me. I’m so proud of her and she is so advanced! It makes me happy to see her learning to do new things.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It gave me a little morale boost, when she hits a new milestone it makes all the sleepless nights worth it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My daughter was responsible for it I suppose.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I wasn’t, I wasn’t expecting it to happen and I can’t control when she does things, I’m just along for the ride.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it happened pretty much how it does with every baby when they stand up for the first time unassisted.

situation: I became emotional when my oldest granddaughter was accepted to college. She called me and said she had great news. When she said 'I'm in!' I immediately teared up and then started screaming with joy for her. She was thrilled. She has worked hard and also did a sport, so this acceptance validated the past four years. I wanted her to know how happy I was for her and how proud I felt. The whole situation left me feeling warm and happy and thankful. I was glad this would be a great example for her younger siblings.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It just happened, and of course it mattered as everyone wants their first choice school, so knowing how much she had put into this, I wanted it for her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me as I was a little stressed thinking about it, and now it was done and I could relax.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My granddaughter was responsible for all this joy as she earned her spot by working hard in academics and athletics.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I could only make suggestions, but she did the work.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Actually, I was more sure that she would get in than not.

situation: I've been trying to lose weight, last week when I checked the scale, I found out I've lost 5kg so far. I'm doing this to improve my health and appearance. Seeing that progress made me feel very happy and more motivated to lose more weight. I also experienced a sense of achievement.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I have been trying to lose weight for some time now to get back to my weight and appearance from 2-3 years ago.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me as my health has improved, my self-confidence has improved, and I feel more happy in general.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I have been making a conscious effort to exercise more and control my eating.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It has gone slightly better than expected as I have lost more weight than I thought.

situation: We were out for dinner with my grown-up kids, who were treating us to a special meal. It was supposed to be a nice evening, but then my husband snapped at me for no reason. My daughter got angry and upset with him, and I felt upset too. The atmosphere at dinner became really strained after that. I felt bad for my kids because they had brought us out for this special meal, and it was costing them a lot of money. My husband was also really upset and angry with himself for kind of ruining things. I wanted him to know he was wrong, but I didn’t want my kids to feel bad since they were treating us. I needed my husband to own it, apologize, and move on, but he just retreated into himself. I'm still a bit fed up with him, to be honest. He is feeling ill at the moment, and I think that contributed to his behavior, but I still find it frustrating.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because I was with the three people I love most in the world, and the kids and I had spent ages planning things as it was my husband’s birthday celebration weekend.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn’t help me at all. It just made me think that my husband is on the way to being a cranky old man.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My husband. Although he is ill arm so that probably didn’t help his mood.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control of myself but not the situation. I just wanted the kids to be alright.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected as I didn’t expect my husband to act like an idiot.

situation: I had a bad result on my yearly smear test and had to go for further checks at the hospital. I was really anxious and scared because I needed reassurance that I didn't have what they suspected I might have. It was important for me to understand what they were going to do and how they were going to do it. I needed clarity to be able to stop worrying. Once I was cleared for three years, I felt relieved, like a weight had been lifted off my shoulders. I could finally go back to a normal life without the stress of waiting for results.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The original test was a couple of weeks ago, but the hospital check was earlier in the week. It mattered to me a lot as it could potentially change my future for the worst.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The clarity of the result helped me mentally. The examination itself wasn't very pleasant and hurt a little bit and was an uncomfortable situation to be in.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nothing in particular, it is just what happened with my body. There wasn't anything I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I had to just be patient and wait for the news of my health either way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't sure what to expect really. But I did get the results instantly which was good for me mentally.

situation: My husband and I got into an argument about the hammock being on the patio. I was trying to get the hammock off the patio because we were cleaning it, and honestly, I hate the hammock. The whole situation left me feeling frustrated and unheard. To make things worse, my husband was yelling at me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a medium amount to me because I spent a lot of time on the porch and it feels cluttered with the hammock.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt our relationship, but I was able to achieve my goal of removing the hammock.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like my husband was responsible for not listening to me about it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like he wasn't listening to me and answering me. He was throwing boundaries in my face, which made me feel a lack of control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I got him to move the hammock, which might have been unexpected given the initial disagreement.

situation: Yesterday, I received a phone call from my daughter, and she sounded emotional. I asked her if she was okay, and she said yes, then asked me how I was. She proceeded to tell me that about 15 minutes ago, she was offered a promotion at her work. I immediately felt shocked and absolutely delighted for her. She explained everything that happened, and I told her how amazed and proud I felt with her. We both became so emotional and excited; it was such an amazing piece of news. She shared that her work was extremely delighted with her collaboration and progress, and she was so appreciative of all the praise and recognition she received for her hard work and efforts. I tried very hard to listen to how this all came about and had to stop myself from interrupting her, even though I wanted to tell her how much I loved her and how proud I was. I needed to let her finish what she was saying because she was on her lunch break and walking up the steep hill next to her work. I also needed to be concise and let her breathe, finish talking to me, finish her lunch break, and get back to work. The situation left me feeling extremely proud and excited for her and her husband because she will get a wage rise, which will help them enormously. I mentioned that her dad would be over the moon with her and so proud of her. He sadly passed away 4 years ago at the age of 57, and Rhiannon was only 24 years old. They were so close and loved each other to bits; she is her dad's double.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me enormously because it was something very positive happening in my daughter's life. It was important to me because she had suffered so much pain and trauma from the death of her beloved father.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation helped me because I felt the love and support my daughter was receiving, which gave me a sense of appreciation and security for her. However, I felt hurt because I couldn't share this fantastic news with her dad, and I missed the love, support, cuddles, and words of advice and praise he would have given her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The joy came from my daughter's wonderful news, and she was responsible for sharing it with me. I was responsible for my own thoughts and feelings about it all. The trauma was caused by the untimely passing of my beloved partner, my daughter's father.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was only in control of my thoughts, feelings, contributions, and reactions. I was not in control of the wonderful news; my daughter was in control of sharing that with me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, but I didn't have any set expectations. Our conversation went extremely well; she shared her news, thoughts, and emotions, and I gave her the space to do so, and she responded in kind to me. The news was completely unexpected for my daughter first and foremost, then for me too.

situation: I went away for a few days with my family, and it was an emotionally positive experience. I wanted to escape from work and other commitments that have been emotionally draining. For those few days, I felt like there was nothing to worry about, just enjoy the moment. The clean, clear air and the area we were at was quiet and isolated. We were the only people for miles.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered because I needed the break from my normal life, just a few days to recharge.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped me realize that there is more to life and in the right environment I can switch off.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Being with my family in a quiet part of the world was most responsible for making this experience what it was.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt very much in control of what we wanted to do or just do nothing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went well with us not putting any pressure on ourselves to be everywhere, just go with the flow.

situation: I saw a man fighting with his wife, and I really wanted to break up the fight. The whole situation left me feeling upset and worried for the couple.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because I don't like violence.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it made me upset.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the people fighting were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I wasn't in the fight.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because the smaller person won the fight.

situation: My mother has recently passed away, and even though she had dementia, it was still a shock. I wasn't trying to do anything or looking for support; I always prefer to work my way through these types of situations first. I felt strangely happy that she had finally been removed from the misery that dementia must put the sufferer under, but equally, I was saddened by the loss of my dear old mother. It left me feeling both at a loss and bewildered. In a huge way, I was relieved that both myself and my mother have had the opportunity to move on, obviously in different directions.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Over the last couple of weeks, it mattered because my mother had just passed away.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It obviously hurt me emotionally as my mother had just died. I felt a huge sigh of relief that my mother was no longer in a state of either pain or lost in her mind.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Ironically, I had the doctor see her the week before her passing, and he was positive about her situation and gave no indication she was suffering more than her diagnosed condition of dementia.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I always felt in control, but felt the opposite when I found her dead.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was not expecting her to pass away, even though she was obviously ill from dementia.

situation: I woke up the other morning and discovered that Trump had put our nation into a horrible war against Iran—unconstitutionally and illegally. He had no authority as he didn't take the matter to Congress for their permission, and there was 'no immediate danger' to us that he had to make the decision alone. It's against the law. I've been involved with many other Americans who don't want our country to lose its democracy and our rights to live as free people in the land we love. I want all of Trump administration arrested for breaking the laws of our country and impeach Trump and all of his Cabinet. They all have broken laws and stolen taxpayer money. This situation left me extremely stressed to the point of crying, feeling and questioning how many of our military and private citizens will be killed needlessly. It should be apparent to all American citizens that this is our red line wake-up call that Trump is going to move forward, ignore our constitution again and again, and destroy our voting rights so that he can stay in office.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Trump putting us at war without permission matters immensely to me. First, my son and granddaughter are members of the military. I don't want their lives put at risk needlessly because Trump is trying to distract the nation away from all the truth being brought forth from the Epstein files and his pedophilia involvement. Trump is destroying all the U.S. Ally relationships and trying to align with the authoritarian-led countries. They think he's a joke. As much as the U.S. Democrats do as well.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation has hurt me in that I haven't been able to sleep or think of anything else. I feel like crying most of the time and worried about my son and grandchildren and what kind of lives they're going to have if we don't defeat this clown. The only way this situation helped is made it more clear that taking us to war against Iran is a practice exercise for what he wants to do with American citizens in November during mid-term elections. We have to stand up -- all of us -- and rally against him on 'NO KINGS' rally day March 28.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Trump and his Project 2025 committee.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control. My body felt physically stressed. I need to watch the news that I know is truthful and safe and doesn't lie like Fox News and national news centers who are afraid of Trump.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect the Ayatollah to be declared dead. I'm thinking that he died sometime before the strikes the other morning as he hadn't been seen for 6 weeks. He was 86 and everyone knew he was preparing his country's next leadership to be ready when he died.

situation: I had a good experience this week where I helped someone out with their shopping. It was just in the moment, and they were surprised, but in a good way. The whole situation left me feeling positive and happy to help someone. What was important to me was that it made someone happy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened in the last few days, it mattered because I don't see many people helping each other.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me feel good about myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like it's a joint situation. It was a positive interaction for both parties.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not in control, just wanting to support someone.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it was a very positive experience.

situation: The son of a close friend was in a car accident. He was seriously hurt, and his girlfriend did not survive. I wasn't sure what to do, but I texted my friend in the moment to let him know that we were praying for the family. I felt sad and shaken up, especially because I have a son that age of my own. It was important to me that his family felt supported and knew that we were there for him and them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Monday, and he texted me while they were in the hospital. It mattered a great deal because he's a close friend and his son is a great kid.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I'm not sure if it hurt me, but I empathized. It helped me by reminding me of what was most important in life, and to not take the people around me for granted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: They were hit by a drunk driver going way too fast, so him.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control—there was nothing I could do to prevent it or even make it better after the fact.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I don't think I was expecting anything—we were just praying that he would recover physically and wanted to be there for what the family needed.

situation: I was trying to work when I found a large bill in the mail. It was an error, but it really made me angry. I needed to pay for electricity, and this unexpected bill just added to my frustration.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered because it was a very large amount.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt my mental state.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The company that issues the bill was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control because they said I needed to pay it ASAP.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. I fought with them for 2 weeks and eventually got the bill dropped.

situation: I was just sitting and reflecting on my life, feeling sad and angry for a short while. I was thinking about how my career hasn't turned out the way I wanted it to. It felt particularly unfair because some of my work colleagues, who performed worse than me, were chosen for new jobs and promotions ahead of me. I wasn't trying to do anything or achieve anything during this time; I was just logically thinking about how unfair things had been. It was important to me that I was thinking logically and not exaggerating my feelings.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered quite a lot to me because I feel that someone who consistently does a good job with professionalism shouldn't lose out to someone whose work standard is lesser and less professional.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me realize I think clearly and logically, but it also made me sad and angry at the true unfairness in it all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Management in my company was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt pretty much in control as I was thinking with clarity and truth.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected.

situation: I enjoyed watching the Winter Olympics. I was really wanting to be entertained, and the games definitely delivered. I felt overjoyed, especially seeing my country do well in the competitions.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened once every four years, and I wanted to savour it. It was quite significant for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Watching the Winter Olympics made me feel connected to the event, which was a positive experience.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The fact that it was so well presented and I had a lot of choice in what to watch was most responsible for my enjoyment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I got to pick what I watched and when.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went even better than I expected.

situation: My dog was unwell, and since he's very old for a Jack Russell, at 18 years old, I thought he might be in his final days. We visited the vet to double-check and prepared for possible outcomes like dementia, vestibular disease, or stroke. The vet determined it was dementia, so we were advised to look after him. The next day, my dog seemed worse, so my wife contacted the vet to prepare for euthanasia later that day, which was a Friday. The vet took a long time to respond and eventually advised that the earliest day for euthanasia would be the following Thursday or Wednesday. My wife and I agreed, so we could console him over the next few days. Since last Thursday, we've been giving him 'renew me' cognitive powder capsules, CBD oil, and good quality meat in his dinner. Since then, his health and mobility have improved tremendously, and we're now going to cancel the vet as the dog is showing a great response to the treatment. We believe he suffered a stroke, so lots of love, attention, and support to get him better over the next few weeks will be our focus, hopefully returning him to a near full bill of health. We're relieved the vet actually delayed, else the outcome would have been a lot different. I needed confirmation of the dog's behavior to see if something specific was the problem so we could focus on his health in that area. We felt sad, but we were preparing due to him nearing the end of life anyway. Let's hope for a couple of years until then, though. The fact that fate and destiny intertwine and cross paths is important to me. I do believe in the multiverse or multiple outcomes from a singularity, so at least our family unit is still together currently.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Thursday, so a quick vet appointment was a must to ensure we would do the right thing for our dog.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped as it gave us direction and how to further care for him. The cognitive powder was a 'let's see' to try and give mobility back if dementia was the actual issue.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one in particular, I did think that myself and my wife were partly responsible as we need to get the dogs (we have 2) walking more, however they are great house dogs.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I did feel in control because of our choices and preparation mentally.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The dog's health increased very rapidly due to the cognitive powder already (3 days and from walking in circles 'spirographing' around the house and only really turning right, he's now walking straighter and turning left as well as some light jumping onto footstools etc).

situation: I got a new job, an internship offer, which I was really hoping for. I wanted to receive a job offer, and I'm very glad that I did! The most important thing for me in this situation was just actually getting the job.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This was last Thursday when I had my interview, and the Friday when I got the offer. It mattered a lot because it was a fantastic job and I needed one as I was previously unemployed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me financially and emotionally as I did not have to worry about job searching anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me and my experience and interview.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Only to an extent as I had to perform well but the decision was up to them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't have any expectations either way!

situation: A person I know recently finished a big project at work that they had been working on for several weeks. At first, they felt stressed and overwhelmed because there were tight deadlines and unexpected problems. In the end, the project was successful, and their team appreciated their effort. The situation ended on a positive note, and they felt relieved and proud once it was over. Being around them, I felt their stress along the way. I was trying to provide a listening ear and give support when I could. I felt good in the end, seeing others' triumph is beautiful.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Not much but over time the significance grew.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: In none.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: They were.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was just a bystander.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I knew they could do it.

situation: I recently spent an afternoon singing in a large choir, something I usually look forward to and have always enjoyed in the past. But this time, I couldn't get into it and felt very disappointed with myself for not really entering into the experience. I wanted to respond with the enthusiasm and enjoyment I've had before, but instead, I felt very lacklustre and didn't really enjoy myself. This left me feeling disappointed for not making the most of the afternoon. Singing has always been an important part of my personality, of who I am, and it was upsetting to find that this might not be the case any longer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event matters a lot to me because I worry that I might be losing my enthusiasm or things that have previously been important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I could not feel enthusiasm for something I have previously loved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of the situation but not in control of how I felt about it - otherwise I would have tried to 'feel' differently.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What was unexpected was the way I felt about the situation.

situation: I had a vent to my mum and felt very emotional, to the point it made me cry. I just needed to have a vent, and she was the best person to listen. Afterward, I felt a little relieved and like I had got things off my chest, which was good. It was important to me that I felt listened to and safe during the conversation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I needed to vent and have someone listen. It mattered to me because she really understands me, and sometimes you just need to vent and have someone listen.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me release some emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both my mum and I were responsible for how it unfolded. I felt comfortable and safe, and she let me talk.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because she did not interrupt and just let me vent.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. I felt better.

situation: I was trying to be nice to my daughter and connect with her by engaging in a conversation, asking what she wanted for dinner. Instead of responding, she was remote and rude to me, and then I got a page full of error messages. This situation left me feeling frustrated and a bit sad. It's important to me because this keeps happening, although there are other times when she's lovely and excitable.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters as she's my daughter and she doesn't live with me full time. It's important to me that she's happy when she is here.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: She's evasive answering questions which is frustrating. I'm also stuck not knowing what to do for dinner, so not knowing if she'll eat what I make or complain about it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Sometimes I feel it's me as I've let her be this way. Sometimes I feel it's her as she's 13 and can obviously choose not to be.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control. I can't force information out of her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Sadly it did go as expected. I knew what mood she was in.

situation: I had a rough meeting with a client at work who didn't speak very nicely to me during the call. I was trying to show the client some new things we have coming to our software, but they weren't really understanding and took their frustration out on me. This really upset me and ruined the rest of my day. It made me feel bad because I don't like when people treat others like that; they treated me like I was lower than them, when we are both just people. After the meeting, my colleagues were really great with me, which was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened a couple of weeks ago on a Friday. It mattered a lot as it happened right at the beginning of the day so really set the tone for the day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help at all. It hurt me because I have to communicate with these people a lot, so I know I have to speak to them again going forwards and I now harbour bad feelings about them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt they were completely responsible. I did my best to explain our systems to them, and their lack of understanding is not my fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt no control at all. I had the control at the beginning as I was the one running the meeting, but then the client completely took over with their demeaning comments.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They did not at all. The unexpected nature came from how they acted, as this was not the first time I had spoken to them. I had great chats with them so many times prior, and this one completely ruined our relationship.

situation: I leveled up in my game. I was really focused on leveling up, and that's exactly what I wanted to achieve. When I finally did it, I felt happy. There wasn't anything else important about the situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered in that moment. I had been working on it for awhile.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help or hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because I was the one playing the game.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, as expected.

situation: My grandson was too ill to go to school, so I had to look after him. He was sleepy and not his usual self, and I really wanted to help him feel better. It left me feeling sad because he was missing school and his friends there.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: He was off school Monday to Wednesday this week. It mattered to me because I felt sorry for him and concerned about him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as I felt sorry for him and concerned about him. It changed my normal daily routine as I looked after him while his mother was at work, which left me feeling tired.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody it cannot be helped.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt as much in control as I could be, although I could not heal him. I made sure he kept himself hydrated and fed him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected.

situation: I received a message from a woman I didn't know, and we started chatting. The conversation quickly became intimate, and we even exchanged pictures. Then she asked if I could help her out by sending some money. I refused, and that's when she threatened to share my pictures and messages with my wife. I was just looking for some fun and a bit of sexual stimulation, but now I'm worried that my wife might find out. It's important to me that this doesn't get into the newspapers or reach my children.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about 4 days ago. It didn't matter much to me because I didn't see how she would know how to contact my wife, nor did I think the newspapers could identify me, so it wouldn't make a good story.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by teaching me to be more careful in the future. My feelings were hurt, but that's okay.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the woman was most responsible for all of this, though maybe it wasn't a woman, maybe just a scammer.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control. I was fairly careful not to send anything that could identify me, and I didn't send money.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I didn't think I'd be threatened.

situation: I had a really nice day out with my partner. We traveled to a city nearby and bought some furniture. I just wanted to have a good day out since it had been a while since we were out and about. I wanted to come to a decision about buying some chairs that we had seen previously. I felt full of joy at mission accomplished. It was important to me that it be a joint decision, and that's how it turned out. We decided that the chairs were good and chose a fabric that would look good and fit in with what we had.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because we were able to travel without too much hassle, and both of us were fit that day, which was really good. Just being together and walking about was lovely.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped me realize that I like being with my partner very much. We got on really well and came to the same conclusions and decisions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was responsible for setting the scene and making sure that we had a good time. I was ready for compromise, but that wasn't needed.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like my plan to keep things lighthearted set the scene well for the day ahead. I tend to initiate the things that we do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The day went really well, in fact better than expected.

situation: I was approached by a company on TikTok to join them as an affiliate after they had seen my weight loss story. I was flabbergasted and taken aback; it's something I have dreamt of and now it's coming true. It made me feel proud and appreciated and also made me feel like I can now help others. The ability to do something for others and potentially earn some money on the side is important to me as I am unemployed due to poor mental health.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I received an email on my TikTok account from the owner of the company, and initially thought it was a scam. I did some research on the company and the person who emailed me because I was worried it was a 'too good to be true' moment.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: When it became clear that the offer was legitimate, the experience helped me as I felt worthy of doing this as a task.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I was responsible, along with my medication, as without it I don't think I would have managed to lose the weight I have.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt kind of in control because I had the say on whether I was going to accept the offer. However, I also felt there was plenty I had to learn to see if I was the right fit.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected. I am starting a training session on Tuesday and have a contract to sign when I feel the time is right.

situation: I went to see my friend who is in a hospice. She's dying, and I wanted to visit her to be supportive. While I was with her, I felt okay because I was putting my own feelings second. We're both Reiki healers, so I gave her Reiki during the visit. She's being really brave and inspirational. But when I got home, I felt really depressed. The most important thing for me was just being there for her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was obviously important to me because it's not often you go and see a friend that is dying.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I got to see her and support her a bit. It hurt me because I felt sad that she was suffering so much and that I will never see her again.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't think anyone was most responsible; it was a dynamic.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't know if I was in control. I was a bit nervous about how to be, but I tried to take her lead. I think she was the one that needed to be in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect to give Reiki. I haven't been able to do that for several years as I've been ill, but I was happy I was able to do it.

situation: I was with my fiancé's sister over the weekend, and we were having a few drinks while watching TV. Suddenly, her housemate got the news that their mum had passed away unexpectedly. This hit me hard because something similar happened with my own mum a few years ago. It was really difficult to try and distract each other after hearing the news. I felt incredibly sad, and a wave of grief washed over me. I was trying to focus on feeling sympathy for the housemate and not just get lost in my own feelings.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Saturday night. It mattered to me because I felt incredibly sad for a while, even though I've only met the person a few times.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me feel sad and reminding me of my mum's death a few years ago. It helped me realize that I'm not fully over my mum's death and still have grieving to do.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't feel like anyone is responsible; death is a part of life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I could put on a brave face and not fully show my emotions. I am good at suppressing my emotions in public.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything was as expected; everyone behaved and reacted as expected. The only unexpected thing was how much it affected me personally.

situation: I received a call from my mother telling me that my grandmother seemed to be dying. I tried to remain positive, but I was very upset initially. In that moment, I just needed support from my family and friends. It was important for me to go see my grandmother.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal because I have been very close to my grandmother. She did a lot for me and my brothers when we were growing up.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I was worried that she was going to die.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I do not have any control over the situation. I could only control my responses and actions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The call was quite unexpected.

situation: Last week at the gym, I was feeling pretty frustrated with CrossFit. Throughout January and February, I was really questioning my training style and even considered taking a break to rethink things, maybe even going back to the bro split. But then, last Monday, something amazing happened—I finally achieved my goal of holding a handstand for over a minute! I felt incredibly proud of myself, like I finally got over that plateau. The support from my coach and other coaches and members at the gym was really important to me during this time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday last week and it meant so much to me because I felt like I had been failing. Achieving the handstand was significant as I managed to do it after working super hard and giving myself a rest.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by bringing the spark back into my training and boosting my confidence, showing me that I can do it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that both myself and my coach were most responsible for achieving this goal, as we really grafted for it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because I asked my coach to change from handstand push-ups to handstands, and he did that for me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected, which was a wonderful surprise.

situation: I was stressed out at work and felt like I was being ignored and underestimated during meetings. I was really looking for support and needed to feel reassured that I’m performing well in my job. This whole situation left me feeling down on myself.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me quite a bit as I take pride in my work.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me at first but reassurance I received from colleagues helped boost my confidence.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The people speaking down to me in the meeting.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had some control as I could respond but needed to make sure I remained professional.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as I expected.

situation: I was feeling really sad for my father because he has dry gangrene, and it's getting worse. It's been going on for a while, and he's not well. I just wish he could be at peace and not have to suffer anymore. The whole situation leaves me feeling sad and a little despondent.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I received more information about his condition on Monday and it matters to me because I am responsible for his affairs and the care he receives in the nursing home abroad.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me understand the latest with regards to his condition, but I feel sorry for him because it must be unpleasant.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think mostly just chronic illness and old age.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really because he’s being cared for in another country and I obviously have no control over his condition.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think what I found unexpected was the news that it has progressed.

situation: A dear friend of mine died, and it seemed to happen without a lot of warning. I really wanted to understand why it happened so suddenly. I was hoping his family could explain it to me, but the situation left me feeling very annoyed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: He died 3 weeks ago. I had been playing table tennis with him the week before and he seemed ok. His death was not as a result of a heart attack.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I could not understand how this could have happened as he was in his late 50s and quite fit. If my friend was unwell, I was hurt that he had not told me about it. The circumstance also shook my faith.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think it was my friend and his family who kept the details from me. I understand this but it still hurts.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was definitely not in control as something had happened I was unprepared for.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had hoped to get more detail from his family about his illness, if indeed he was ill, but this did not happen.

situation: It was the loss of a loved one. We knew they were about to pass, so I tried to spend as much time as possible with them through those final hours. It left me feeling fearful that our time together could be over at any moment. It was important to me that I get to say my goodbyes properly.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered immensely. It was one of my closest relatives - someone who I had spent a lot of time with, growing up.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me that I was soon going to get to a point where I would never see them again. Just the fact that I knew that I managed to get there to see them in time, before it was too late, helped me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible at all. It was just part of the aging process.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, not at all. No one was in control. We knew it was coming, but not exactly how or when.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything happened exactly as I imagined it would.

situation: After nine months of searching for a job, I finally received the call I had been eagerly anticipating, the one that would reveal the outcome of my recent job application. Having gone through two interviews, I felt optimistic about my chances, yet the stress of waiting for the final decision weighed heavily on me. As I answered the call, I tried to maintain a calm and composed demeanor, despite the whirlwind of emotions swirling inside me. When they offered me the position, an overwhelming sense of relief washed over me, and as soon as the call ended, I couldn't hold back the tears any longer. It was as if a massive weight had been lifted off my shoulders, and I felt validated in my professional abilities and genuinely happy. Needing some time alone to process the incredible news, I took a moment to let it all sink in before sharing it with my husband, which was an important step for me once I had regained my composure.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was the most important thing that was happening in my life at the time - getting a job will make our lives easier and remove money worries.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me mentally because I could stop stressing and worrying about getting a job and about money - which all lead to removing worry and stress about the future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Getting the job offer was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It wasn't really a situation that required me to be in control, it was more remaining calm while on the phone.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I hoped they would rather than as expected, but all positive.

situation: Scenario: I recently received a pay raise at my job. I felt the urge to share the news with someone because it made me happy. The raise brought a sense of relief, especially with the rising costs of living, as it will be a significant help. However, it also made me feel like I need to demonstrate my value even more at work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 months ago and it mattered a lot to me because we were starting to struggle financially.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped us by allowing us to keep afloat with the finances and have a little extra left.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that both me and the company were responsible for this, as I always work hard and now it has been recognised.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't need to feel in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, all went well.

situation: I was driving to visit my grandchildren, navigating through country roads, dual carriageways, and motorways. I'm not really used to driving long distances, but with a break to charge the electric car, it wasn't too bad. I wanted a relaxing break to charge the car and have a cup of coffee on the way. At the end of the journey, I felt tired but safe and ready to enjoy the company of my grandchildren. Having an occasional chat with my wife, who came with me on the journey, was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was very important as we wanted to visit our grandchildren and help with toddler sitting.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The journey was tiring but ultimately well worth it because I got to spend time with my grandchildren. I do have to repeat the journey home, but that was left until later.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Fortunately, the roads were clear and there were no holdups. Such holdups on a journey like this can add stress.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt fully in control as the journey took the targeted time of just over two hours.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected because I checked the road conditions on an app and they were as expected.

situation: My partner lost his job a few days ago, and it's been really upsetting and stressful for both of us. He's been dealing with mental health issues for the last few months and hasn't been able to work for several weeks, which led to his employer deciding to terminate his contract. Personally, I've been trying to support him as he comes to terms with this news. At the same time, I've been gathering information to request advice for potential legal action against his former employer. This whole situation has left me feeling stressed and tired. My main worry is my partner's mental health because he had been gradually getting stronger lately, but this job loss has been a major setback.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot as it has been a blow to my partner emotionally. Financially, him losing his job will have consequences for us, too.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has hurt as my partner is upset and feels guilty about losing his job.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: His employer acting in a way that was not compassionate or understanding towards his condition.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control as the event was out of my hands.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The sudden announcement by the employer came as a shock, so that was an unexpected development.

situation: I had a meltdown because my new towels hadn’t been washed, even though my dad had promised to do it. I decided to have a bath, hoping to feel better and clean, but when I wanted to shampoo and condition my hair under the shower, the water was running cold. So, I had to take a cold shower instead. Then, I found my mail and realized that instead of a telephone appointment with my doctor, I was scheduled for a face-to-face appointment in two weeks' time. It was all too much, and the floodgates opened up. I felt stressed, frustrated, angry, sad, and irritated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot because it was the only thing I had done in a few weeks. I was feeling pretty depressed, so I hadn’t got out of bed for a while. That was me taking a step to be proactive.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Having a cold shower ruined my experience because the bath was lovely and hot, then nobody wants to have a cold shower after that, it wasn’t nice. I was angry with the doctor because I was expecting something that he said he would do and he didn’t deliver.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Perhaps I used all the hot water in the bath so maybe that was on me. But the doctor, that’s all him.
