appraisal_reasoning.control: No, definitely not in control because I actually got the mail at about 01.00 on a Sunday morning, so there was absolutely nothing I could do. I couldn’t ring the doctor's receptionist to find out why they had changed the plan; I’d have to wait until Monday to contact them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The unexpected elements were the cold shower, the dirty towels, and the rescheduled appointment.

situation: I was admitted to A&E for tests after I had a fall at home. It was a tense few hours because there was concern that I might have had a minor stroke or maybe a heart attack. I needed a thorough check over to be 100% certain that it wasn't anything serious and to know it was unlikely to happen again if I made changes to my life. Once I was given the all-clear and allowed to go home, I felt very relieved and reassured. It was important for me to understand what the probable cause was and how I can help ensure it does not happen again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I was very worried after blacking out or fainting for a very short while and didn't have a clue why it happened.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me physically because I had fallen on my side and badly bruised my upper arm and legs. However, it helped me gain insights as I now know I must look after myself more and not push myself so hard.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my family was most responsible for all of this because they were worried about me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because I could have brushed it off and done nothing, but I chose to go to A&E to get checked over.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected. There was a lot of procedure to go through, but the NHS took care of me, and the process was long but important.

situation: I found out that a dog I follow on social media passed away. There wasn't anything I needed in this situation, but it left me feeling sad and made me think about my own dog. I've followed this dog for a long time, and it's the same breed as my own dog.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday, at the beginning of the week. It mattered a lot to me because all dogs are beautiful and deserve to be cherished.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt my heart as I am always scared of losing my baby. I also lost my other dog last year in a devastating way, so I am terrified as they are everything and more to me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible; nature, I guess.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt no control, sadly.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I hoped and wanted it to go one way, and well, it didn't, so it was unexpected indeed.

situation: Scenario: I play mahjong with a group of friends, and for a while, things have been pretty chill. But this past week, one of my friends started getting on my nerves again. She used to always get my goat and raise my blood pressure, and now she's back at it. She interrupts me when I'm telling a story, so I never get to finish it. She argues with me about a point and then refuses to discuss it further. All I can do is ignore this behavior, but it gets me so emotional inside. Honestly, I just want peace, but I ended up feeling really pissed. I decided to talk to an AI to see if it could offer any advice or help me find a way to deal with this situation more effectively.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday, and it mattered more than it should. I should just let it go.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation gives me grey hair and made me dislike her in the moment. It ruins the game for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Probably me, since nobody else cared. I feel she envies me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I take back control by not letting her see that her remarks affect me. I wish that I wasn't so sensitive.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, the other girls saw the water run down my back. Barb's remarks don't bother them.

situation: I'd been working on a model car kit for a few weeks now. It was a complicated and detailed kit, and I was really focused on building it. A couple of days ago, one of the cats knocked it off the table, and it smashed on the floor. I was trying to build the model and needed it to be left alone, but having the cats around can be frustrating. I like them, but in moments like this, I felt frustrated and annoyed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a couple days ago. I'd put quite a bit of time and effort into it. It's a relaxing hobby, and fulfilling when a model is done.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt seeing it in pieces on the floor with the cat batting them around like it was the greatest toy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible in part for leaving it out and thinking they'd leave it alone. The cat was responsible by being a cat.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control. I had it set up on the usual work area. The cats have never bothered or paid attention to it before.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it was certainly not expected. I expected it to still be there the next day.

situation: My relationship with my girlfriend of 10 years ended. We were trying to fix and improve things, but we both started to get complacent. I just wanted us to be more connected and spend more personal time together. Losing the love of my life was important to me in this situation. I felt heartbroken, devastated, emotionally crippled, depressed, and alone.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened back in October of 2025. It mattered immensely to me because we had a great life together, we understood each other fully, and we had our first place together. I lost my partner, my home, my cats, and my self worth.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has not helped me at all, only hurt me. It has emotionally and passionately destroyed me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was the catalyst, but we were both to blame for our actions around that time.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I had no control over the situation and there was nothing I could do to rectify the issues.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn’t expect things to go so badly and result in us ending our relationship. Just thought it was another argument.

situation: I was struggling to find ways to make more money so that I could move out of the area where I live. I was really focused on trying to figure out how I could make an extra £10,000 a month, preferably tax-free. At first, I couldn't find a solution, and it seemed like only gambling or trading were the only workable ideas. This left me feeling stuck or limited in my options. I was also thinking about whether any approach would be profitable in the short term rather than the long term, especially considering my age.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: There was no specific place where the event occurred, it has been an ongoing dilemma. At first it was worrying because I couldn't see a way forward, but it mattered to me because the area where I live is not that safe to be in.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has only impacted me personally, it is something that I want to achieve on a personal level, not a professional one.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am the only person who can resolve the dilemma I am facing and therefore, it is myself who is responsible to get myself out of the dilemma I find myself in.
appraisal_reasoning.control: At first I did not because of two aspects, my age and my husband who will be retiring in a year or so. I only felt like I was in control when I finally saw a solution and will be working on this.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing has gone as expected because the action has just started and therefore nothing has occurred immediately.

situation: Last Friday afternoon, I went to my doctor for my annual exam, and I ended up getting the pneumonia vaccine. I hadn't planned on getting this vaccine, but my doctor mentioned that all older adults should receive it, so I agreed to it. I was hoping it would have less severe side effects than some of the other vaccines I've had, but unfortunately, it didn't. On Saturday and Sunday, I experienced chills and aches, and from Monday to Wednesday, I still felt tired and weak. Today is the first day this week that I feel normal again. I was frustrated and disappointed that I didn't feel well for five days because of the vaccine, but at the same time, I felt relieved that it was taken care of and proud of myself for doing what was necessary. I trust science, and vaccines are based on science, so I trust them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: My annual doctor's exam was much more important for my health and peace of mind. I've been ill with the flu many times in my life, I have never had to go the hospital, and I always get well within a few weeks.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to stay current with my health tests (and not miss a year), and add to the list of important vaccines I have received (including shingles and tetanus).
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: In this instance, my doctor, because they sent me a reminder to schedule my appointment, and once I was at my appointment, they recommended this vaccine, which I had not been considering.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because I was able to choose the date and time of my appointment, and I was able to decide if I would get the vaccine or not.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, the appointment started on time, the doctor and nurses were polite and helpful, and the vaccine shot did not hurt.

situation: I became entangled with a fearful avoidant around 4-5 months ago and was discarded over the last week. I felt very heavily for her and I know she felt very intensely for me too. I just wanted us to get more involved based on that, but it provoked fear in her. This left me feeling very confused because I want to be angry with her for hurting me, but I know that it's not her fault. It's honestly the first time I've 'let my walls down' in the last decade and actually feel for somebody, so I was hoping she'd show me that some people are just honest and can be trusted not to hurt those that care about them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event began around the beginning of November last year, and the discard happened last week. It mattered to me because she was desperate to leave my proximity, even willing to worsen her own situation to do so.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me in the usual way heartbreak does, and although it might have been a trauma bond, it felt very real and intense at the time. It helped me move from being anxiously attached to more securely attached.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that whoever traumatized her to the extent that she became a fearful avoidant is ultimately responsible. However, it is partly her fault as well, since she is aware of her avoidant nature and is married, which she didn't disclose, and she had no right to get me attached.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel more in control because after she made it clear she was leaving, I withdrew my regulation and all access to me and my social media.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I am becoming more detached, but there was always hope that she'd realize the loss and reconsider her current prioritizations of bonds. However, it's likely she'll stay with the unhappy known rather than the risky unknown that is me/us.

situation: I was watching my daughter perform in a choir. The singing was very beautiful and it made me emotional. I didn't want anything other than to sit and listen. The whole experience left me feeling uplifted and proud. It was important to me that I was there for her and the performance.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Wednesday evening. It mattered a great deal to me that I was there.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped me feel close to my daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was partly me who was responsible for attending despite it being a busy day with a number of competing things.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control. I was able to carve out time in my day to attend and enjoy the performance.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting to enjoy it as much as I did. I went in expecting it to feel like a chore.

situation: I was hit with a sickness bug and flu at the same time, and my emotions were all over the place. I don't cope well with being ill, and my health anxiety makes it so much worse. To try to get through it quicker, I was just sleeping my days away. I felt anxious and worried, constantly noticing everything my body was doing and fixating on it, which was exhausting. Thankfully, the feelings went away as soon as I woke up feeling better after days of hell.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I woke up and instantly had that ‘I’m gonna vomit feeling’ ran to the toilet. Then it was just a downward spiral until I felt better.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It caused so much anxiety because my brain just assumes the worst-case scenario every time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one’s to blame for this one. A lot of self-care and rest was needed.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not for the first 2 days because I was uncontrollably being sick and couldn’t keep anything down. I felt more in control in the final couple of days.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I just had to rest for a week. Although I have a toddler so that proved kind of difficult but caffeine and paracetamol helped.

situation: I'm an Airbnb host and today I received a 3-star review. We've been hosting for two years and have gotten well over 100 5-star reviews and a couple of 4-star reviews, so getting 3 stars is really upsetting. The guest's only complaint was that the WiFi wasn’t working. Obviously, I want happy guests. He mentioned that the place was great otherwise but needed the WiFi for work, so he was disappointed it didn’t work. Unfortunately, it was a problem with the network. I'm frustrated because we received a low rating, which is especially low in the eyes of Airbnb, and it affects our overall rating and future bookings. I'm just angry because I can’t do anything to resolve it. The review is public and the rating will be exceptionally difficult to change even with loads more future 5-star reviews.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened when he stayed last week. But the review was posted today. It matters a lot as that is my business and a main source of my income.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because a low review is upsetting but it affects our overall rating which then affects where we are placed in search results and future bookings etc. it also can affect our superheat status if we fall below a certain number.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The issue with the WiFi was the problem but I couldn’t change that as was a problem with the providers. I gave the guest a partial refund and I thought he would be more understanding.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn’t in control as couldn’t change it any more than offering a refund as the WiFi problem was out of my hands.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Completely unexpected. It is the lowest star rating we have received. The issue wasn’t that big of a deal in my eyes so to receive three stars is a massive disappointment.

situation: I didn't do as well in my exams as I thought I would have. I was just trying to achieve a bit of a higher grade to get a 2:1. I think I will get over it; I just need some time. It's not completely over as I have more coursework I can do, but it would have been easier if I did better in these exams.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few weeks ago and did mean a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me realise how I could improve but then it also made me sad as there was nothing I could really do.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think it definitely came down to my ability but I do think that the module convenors could have made the exams clearer.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I definitely was in control a bit which means I have myself to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They were a pass but I still think I could have done better.

situation: The situation arose when my longstanding friend moved away after living nearby for years. I had mixed emotions, feeling happy for his new opportunity and sad about losing our daily connection.His departure left me feeling overwhelmed, knowing I wouldn't see him as often . At the same time, I was happy for him to start a new career he always wanted and desired.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: My friend moved away a couple of days ago. It matters to me a lot because we used to spend time at a nearby cafe every day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: We have been friends since childhood and his moving away has made me emotional. I have mixed emotions, to be honest, happy for him to start a new career he always desired and sad not seeing him quite often.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think nobody is exclusively responsible for this situation. But we can say that his future plans created this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt positive because I wanted to see my friend successful in every sphere of his life, so I made it possible for him to grab this opportunity of starting a new career.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: In my opinion, everything went as planned and we were able to make things happen accordingly.

situation: I was at the auction last week, trying to win my dream home. I had really set my heart on that house, so when I didn't win, I felt deflated. It was a tough moment for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it meant a lot to me because we had been trying to purchase that house since the previous owners passed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it was the perfect family home and ticked every box we had, which we know is rare. Missing out on the house was quite disappointing, and it means we are stuck in this house for a while as we have no plan B for another house at this point.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel the builders who are wanting to knock the house down were most responsible for how things turned out.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt like I had no control. I had offered a lot more for the house prior to auction, but it needed to be cash only, which was not the option I could do if putting down a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing in particular was unexpected about the situation.

situation: I had to go to the dentist and hygienist, which I find very anxiety-provoking due to my phobia. I needed to have a dental checkup and hygiene clean, so I had to attend an appointment. I was trying to attend the dental appointment for a checkup and hygiene clean, which was necessary for my dental health. I felt anxious beforehand, and then slightly embarrassed and ashamed after. It was important to me that I actually attended despite my fear.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday, and it mattered a lot to me because I have a phobia and have ended up not going for years, which has damaged my teeth.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Past experience hurt me as it caused long-term damage and was expensive to fix my teeth. This recent appointment was helpful in that I am proud I went and I do not have many issues with my teeth. But I still hate it and dread the next appointment.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel a dentist when I was 6 years old is responsible, plus my parents for not teaching good oral hygiene care.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control as it hurt when the teeth were being cleaned.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected, maybe a bit worse as I felt pain.

situation: A friend of mine was taken into the hospital, and all I could do was hope for the best and wish they would be OK. The situation left me feeling really upset and worried, especially thinking about her kids and hoping they would be OK too.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Monday when she phoned for an ambulance because she wasn't feeling well. It matters to me because she is a friend of mine.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It's not helped me at all. It's upset me and causing me a lot of worry.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I would say herself because if it wasn't for her drinking then she might not be in the state she is in.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I'm not in control at all. She does her own thing and makes her own decisions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes I expected her to eventually be in hospital because of her lifestyle.

situation: My daughter woke up feeling really unwell. She was coughing and had been sick from the coughing. I was trying to look after her, but I felt upset that someone so young and vulnerable was so unwell. Her temperature was in a fever, and I was concerned about that.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Sunday morning at 6am when she woke me up. It mattered a lot as I care for her so much and I found it difficult to see her unwell.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as she is so young and vulnerable.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible as she was just unwell.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, as I could only give her medication to try and bring the fever down.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I gave her medication and it brought the fever down, but she was still tired from it all.

situation: My husband had to go to the hospital for surgery, and I was very anxious and worried. It was an emotional time for me. I was trying to support him, look after him, and keep him calm. All I wanted was reassurance that the procedure was successful and that he could come home safely and well. Once it was all over, I felt hugely relieved but also exhausted from all the emotional stress. Despite the tension, I was grateful for the support of the hospital staff and the comfort of knowing he was in good hands.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me as it was a possible cancer diagnosis or the discovery of some horrible condition that would change our lives.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The surgery did not discover cancer so this was a huge relief.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible, our health is always in balance and it's good we have the NHS to help us when needed.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control, I did not know what would be discovered and I could only do the most superficial things like provide company and snacks.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected and he is home recovering.

situation: I lost my grandma suddenly four weeks ago yesterday. Me and my mum were there all day. After her CT scan, we were told she had a major bowel blockage and her small intestine had twisted. We were probably in denial all day; we really thought we were going to bring her home. My grandma was unbelievably strong-willed; she beat sepsis at 86 years old, so we really thought we could get her through it all. The doctors on hand were gracious all day, probably because they knew she wasn't going to make it. It was really traumatic watching her die; I've never seen this before and she was so important to me. I wanted the doctors to save her life, but due to her age, she wouldn't have survived the surgery. They said even at 40 people really struggle with such a massive operation. I've been feeling really broken; it's my first permanent loss. I'm angry and broken. Yes, she got to 90—it's an amazingly long life—but she could have gotten to 100 or 110, and it would not have been good enough. I miss her like crazy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened four weeks ago yesterday. It mattered immensely to me because it was my first permanent loss, and my grandma was incredibly important to me. Her passing has left me feeling broken and angry, as she lived an amazingly long life but could have lived longer.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me deeply; it has broken me and led me to grieve for the first time in my life. I'm riding emotional waves every day while helping my mum with administrative and legal aspects, being a mum to my toddler, and feeling burnt out without a break.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible for this. When an elderly person suffers a major bowel blockage, it's a medical emergency requiring a massive operation. Given her age and previous recovery from sepsis, her frail body couldn't overcome it. I'm just glad she's not in pain anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I absolutely did not feel in control of anything. The only thing I was in charge of was speaking to doctors and ensuring my grandma was as comfortable as possible.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: None of it went as I expected. The entire situation was unexpected and overwhelming.

situation: It was a very sad time because my friend had to have her dear, precious dog put to sleep. I've been giving my friend lots of support and care, and I really wish I could have been able to see her more during this tough time. I'm feeling very sad myself because he was a really lovely, friendly dog and a real miss for both my dear friend and me. You feel low and empty when something like this happens. It's important to keep positive for my friend, so I've been telling her about all the wonderful memories we have and what a great life he had with her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event only happened six days ago, and it mattered to me as he was a lovely dog and you never want to lose them. The precious loss for my dear friend is so painful and sad for her to go through.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me to see and know how horrible this would be for my friend to cope with, and I miss not seeing him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible as nature and age is sadly what we all face, as he was 14 years old.
appraisal_reasoning.control: You can be in control of the situation to do the right and kindest action for your precious pet, but you cannot make it better.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: My friend made the correct decision at the right time, but it is always so sad and hard.

situation: My father, who is 72 and has been sick for a while, recently suffered a downturn in his health. He had limited mobility due to a hernia and other health conditions, but recently he fractured vertebrae in his spine and is now bed bound. He's in a lot of pain and clearly fed up with his situation, and it's clear he's going to die soon. I kind of knew this was coming, but it's been very emotionally upsetting knowing it's coming. I'm trying to balance spending time with him before it's too late and also balancing that out with my life here. I've recently renewed my passport so I can travel to see him, and while travel is expensive, I can get help with those costs. It's just the pain of knowing it's coming and trying to work out the balance. It left me feeling stressed. I live in Northern Ireland, having moved here about 18 years ago, while my parents live in the UK. I have a young toddler (2.5 years old), a partner, and a job here, so I can't just drop everything to go see him, but know I will need to soon before it's too late. I can't just go over and spend time with my father because my partner and child need me here.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because it's my father.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurts me because I am facing up to the loss of my father.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that time and the facts of life and death are most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do not feel in control of the situation. No one is in control of their parents dying.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing is going as expected. This is unexpected. I thought he would be healthier for longer.

situation: My father received some very disappointing news from the hospital this week, and it's a worry for us all because we felt that his recent treatment had been successful. We had hoped he was better, but it's sad to receive further upsetting news. I'm really concerned that my mum will not cope very well with all of this. It makes me feel helpless and unable to support them, and I wish I could do more for them. I just worry about what the future holds.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This week my father received a phone call relaying bad news about his health. This is a worrying time for them, but I feel helpless in the support I can offer them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This has made me feel anxious as I am worried about what the future holds.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I'm fearful due to a lack of control.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I am not in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things have not gone as expected. We were not expecting a phone call with bad news.

situation: My wife had been talking to our neighbor, and he told her he had been diagnosed with cancer. We've known him for 20 years, so we were both shocked. I needed to comfort my wife. The news made me feel personally vulnerable, thinking, 'Who is next?' Of course, my first thoughts are for my neighbor and his family.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It just happened today. It matters a lot to me. It made me question the point of life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It's literally close to home and it has made me afraid for the future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody is responsible, but I feel that it is time the world worked together to beat cancer. My brother died from it also, so it brought up memories.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, just feeling apprehensive.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It's early days, We will see what comes.

situation: I had a job interview for an internal promotion, and I was rejected. I really wanted to get the job because my current position doesn't pay very well, and I needed the money. Being turned down left me feeling disappointed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event didn't matter to me that much in the great scheme of things as I would just continue as normal, but it was disappointing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I was rejected for the job.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was only in control of myself; I wasn't in control of the quality of the other candidates.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as I expected because the other candidates were more experienced than me.

situation: I visited my elderly father, who lives four hours away. I wanted to see him because he doesn't get out much on his own, and I was glad to be able to take him places. The experience was bittersweet.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last weekend. It mattered to me because my father is very old, and I am aware that he may not be around for much longer.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The visit helped me because it was nice to see him in person and made me feel happy that I could make him happy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because I decided the time and duration of the visit.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, and we had a nice time.

situation: I recently had to write a report for work after being suspended due to a false allegation and a poor investigation that victimized and harassed me. The report was meant to prove that management and HR had not acted on Occupational Health letters and that management and other staff had been bullying me and putting my health and safety at risk. I was trying to show that what had gone on for 6 years was unacceptable and went against policy and the law. It also aimed to highlight failures in management and HR not acting when they should, as well as serious health and safety risks and bullying that have occurred—all with proof and reference to the policies and laws. This whole situation left me feeling emotionally and physically drained, mentally exhausted, and still with a low mood and depression due to what happened. The suspension was for a false accusation of violence that never happened and was proven not to happen. The workplace then tried to change accusations when they found I was innocent and find alternative ways to accuse me of things I had not done. Having my mother to support me was important, as she attended the meetings I have been to and witnessed the abuse I have faced in this investigation along with the false information supplied by managers. The important part is that certain workplaces are immoral and unethical in their practices, and someone low down such as me is continually bullied in a cover-up exercise. The hope is that this can be taken to tribunal after and justice can be served. I have faced coercion in this process and over 6 years of grief.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The main event happened over 7 months ago when I was suspended for shouting and swearing in distress due to not being treated with dignity and facing derogatory behavior. It matters to me to prove what is going on and the problems I faced. The problem is my manager never deals with problems and the head of department won't tell the truth.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation hurt me, there has been no help except my mother. Previously my union reps have bullied and coerced me so I have given up on them. Health damage has been caused being diabetic. Twice in meetings I have left and considered suicide. The workplace is spiteful and abuses me. Mentally I am lacking energy to continue.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Senior management investigating this were responsible for not accepting evidence and excluding it from the investigation report. HR and a director are responsible for trying to change the Terms of Reference in the suspension letter later from Violent to Aggressive. HR and directors allowed false information or twisted it. Supporting charities were excluded from intervention and effective health from the CEO and executive directors ignoring supporting letters and passing off to Occupational Health rather than dealing with the serious matter.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had my mother in this process, but nothing was in control. The control came from the deceit from the persons investigating and the lies told by managers later on.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing went as expected, I was not given agendas or the correct information from the outside. The investigator changed the policy straight from the start using a policy that was not active and changing the rules to suit themselves. There has been nothing positive. Time frames in policy have not been adhered to or followed.

situation: A few Saturday evenings ago, I was preparing to meet some friends when I received a call from a local vet. They delivered the heartbreaking news that one of my cats had passed away. I had to drive to the vet's office to confirm her identity. Seeing her lifeless body at the vet was devastating, and a wave of deep sadness washed over me. She was only around 18 months old and had so much life ahead of her. She was always venturing into nearby homes, eager to explore and make new friends. After returning from the vet, I decided to still go out to see my friends because I needed a distraction and didn't want to dwell in sadness. I still feel sorrow when I think about my cat. Now, I have to consider keeping my other cats indoors, but I believe they deserve their freedom and shouldn't be confined all day.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered deeply to me because the cat that passed away was only around 18 months old and very friendly, unlike my other cat. I still feel sorrow when I think about her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by causing deep sadness, but it also made the time I spend with my remaining cat feel more precious.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt it was my cat's fault because I had seen her nearly hit by a car a few weeks earlier and hoped she would become more street smart.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I had no control over what happened.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The vets offered to cremate my cat, which was unexpected, and I accepted their offer. Her ashes are now downstairs.

situation: It was my deceased husband's birthday, and I just wanted to get through the day. I knew I would be upset since it's only been a few years since he passed away. The day left me feeling extremely upset that he is no longer here with me, but also very grateful for the time we had together. It was important to have my family with me, and my new granddaughter in particular brought me joy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal. If my husband had still been alive we would have celebrated his birthday together, maybe going away for a short break or getting together with the family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me to know that he was no longer with me and milestones like birthdays would come round and be a reminder of all the good ones that we had previously shared together.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was to blame or was responsible. I suppose that it is just a fact of life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't really in control. I just had to let the day play out as it would and try to keep my emotions in check.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, the day went pretty much as I expected it to. I was very sad and that sadness continued on during the week.

situation: My husband and I had an argument about money. It got pretty loud for awhile and it made me cry. I was trying to get him to sit down and budget because I want him to take it seriously. We need to get better with our finances. The whole situation left me feeling drained and sad. He needs to realize it's the only way we will be able to live. It's important to me that we work as a team to get better financially.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened this past Tuesday evening at our home. It mattered a lot to me because we are in debt with medical bills.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because he is always talking about getting better with our money and then he reacts like that.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My husband's stubbornness.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't want to be in control. I just wanted us to work together.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No everything didn't go well. He still has an attitude.

situation: I was diagnosed with ADHD at 30 years old. I wanted to feel better and have better focus and memory. Getting the diagnosis left me feeling bittersweet because, on one hand, I'm glad I got help now, but on the other hand, I wish I knew this sooner when I was younger. Right now, I'm just trying to find the right medication that works for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 3 weeks ago when I first sought out help for it all. It mattered a lot to me because I need to focus better for work and school.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me understand I do have the illness. It's challenging to find the right medication that works for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't feel it in a negative way. It's pretty much trial and error until I find the right medication and dosage that work for me best.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I do because I started the process and I know I can stop it at any time if I am uncomfortable.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they did at first, but then I had to switch to a psychiatrist who is re-diagnosing me, so just waiting on those results for now.

situation: Last week, I went through an emotional experience when my relative was hospitalized and diagnosed with a serious health condition that has impacted her entire life. She's in pretty bad condition and hasn't shown any improvement so far. I was trying to be there for her and assist as much as I could by speaking to doctors and gathering as much information as possible. I wanted to ensure she had everything she needed and was properly supervised while under the care of the physicians. However, I was left feeling discouraged because most of the doctors didn't seem very helpful, and asking them questions seemed to annoy them. This left me stressed and feeling like we needed more answers. The most important thing to me was helping my relative recover and get back to her normal life.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event started last weekend on a Sunday. My relative started feeling light-headed and dizzy after a long stressful day. She called me up to talk about how she was feeling and just brushed it off as if she was maybe coming down with a cold or flu. Hours later, the symptoms worsened and she was unable to move her left side of her arm. She was then rushed to the ER for further evaluation. This mattered a lot to me because no one wants to see their loved one deal with critical health issues, and it has taken a toll on my well-being.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation mostly hurt me because no one wants to see their loved one deal with critical health issues. It has taken a toll on my well-being and left me feeling powerless, due to being unable to change the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like my relative's job is to be blamed for my relative's health condition, due to the hectic workloads and high levels of stress within the work environment. She has been overworked and disregarded when asking for time off.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control because all I was able to do was offer advice.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing went as I expected; in fact, her work hours and stress levels continued to increase, which made her health condition worsen.

situation: My grandad's funeral was on Friday, and it was a sad day. He was very popular, so it was a big service. I was trying to ensure others in the family were okay, and I felt they needed some humility during this time. Despite the sadness, I felt strong about it because he lived to be 90 years old.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was a close family death, it meant a lot as it affected loads around me. It was emotional.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt as we will no longer see him, but we will have the memories.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel I need to ensure my dad is okay and check in on him as he saw my grandad daily.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We are all quite strong. I feel the age was a factor for me which made it easier.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: All was good and we all supported each other.

situation: My children were being returned to their mother after staying with me, and they didn't want to leave. They were upset with me for taking them back, and I was trying to keep them happy and focused on the fun times we had together. I wanted them to accept the situation and be happy with the decision. It left me feeling very sad. My priority and focus was the children and their wellbeing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Sunday afternoon, and it mattered to me a great deal because I hate seeing my children upset or angry with me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt that my actions were hurting them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The responsibility lays with all of us. I need to be better at communicating my needs to them and they need to understand what the current family situation is too.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt partially in control because I was leading the conversation, but I also knew that there were feelings of theirs that I could not control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did go worse than expected as previously they have not been so upset to be going home.

situation: In the last few days, I got the news that my last grandparent had managed to beat cancer. I wasn't trying to do anything specific, but I needed to be strong for someone else because it was a positive outcome, even though I still feel doubtful. The situation left me feeling unsettled because cancer can always come back, but I've accepted that for now, it's gone, and hopefully, it'll be the last of it. It was important for me to keep my negative opinions to myself and focus on the positive aspects.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me as my grandparent has been fighting cancer for years, so it was important to me that they were finally able to beat it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me as I have been able to stop thinking about the situation as it was consuming me waiting to hear the results.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My grandparent, as it was down to them to ensure they were getting the treatment they needed and continued to be positive. I think those things contributed to them coming away with a positive outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control as I could not do anything about the situation apart from encourage them to keep going to treatments, but again, this is not down to me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did not go as I expected, but only because I knew my grandparent was old and I did not think she would pull through and actually beat cancer.

situation: I had a new kitchen, and I wanted a complete new feel. The transformation was total, and I feel great that it turned out well. It was important to me that it turned out so good because we did it all ourselves.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event started 3 weeks ago because the old kitchen was old and dated. It mattered quite a lot, especially if people came around, as I got so embarrassed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped as I got a new kitchen but was sad to see the old one go as it belonged to my late mom.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The age of the old kitchen was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in total control as I was the one picking all the fixtures and fittings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things mostly went as expected.

situation: My partner had a health scare that landed him in the hospital. Thankfully, he has now recovered and is well. Throughout the whole ordeal, I was there supporting him every step of the way, going to the hospital with him and ensuring he had everything he needed. The situation left me feeling exhausted—emotionally and mentally. I didn’t sleep much, and it was really worrying. Honestly, the only thing that mattered to me was making sure he got healthier.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because my partner means a lot to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was scary and brought a lot of worry about him and our relationship. Positively, it made us stronger as a couple. Negatively, it was incredibly hard on the mind and body.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There was no blame to place - he simply became ill.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Absolutely not. His health was totally out of my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Thankfully things improved relatively quickly.

situation: I was really struggling because the food shopping we had bought ran out four days before payday. We have five children, so I was very stressed and upset. I felt like I had failed the children and had no way to fix the situation. I needed help because I had no way to feed my kids for the next four days. I didn't want money from anyone; I was more looking for food banks. I've been suffering with depression, and my prescription was messed up, so when this situation was happening, I had been off my meds for about two weeks. I was feeling everything so intensely and had convinced myself that everyone was better off without me. I reached out to a local in my town who knows about a lot of different charities that help people. She signposted me to a place giving out vouchers for supermarkets. I was able to get some vouchers, and we were okay. After asking for help and being able to get some food shopping, I felt so happy. I was so grateful and reminded that not everyone is bad. It really lifted my spirits to see people rally around and help us for no reason other than they just cared. All that mattered to me was that my children had enough food.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week. It mattered a great deal to me because I have never been in this situation before, so it's important I remember their struggle so I can learn from it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped restore my faith in humanity. However, I was hurt that I had failed to make money last and that it had impacted my children.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible. I'm in charge of money and their food shopping, so the blame lay entirely with me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Absolutely not. Everything was out of my control. I was trying to do the best with the resources we had, but things still kept going wrong.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things didn't go as I expected. I didn't expect the food shopping to not last, nor did I expect to have to ask a complete stranger for help.

situation: I watched an interview with Eric Dane, which was set to be released after his death. It made me tear up. I really wanted to see Eric Dane and hear about his experience with ALS. The whole situation left me feeling sad. What was important to me was his grace in dealing with the disease.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last weekend, a few days after his death. It was on Netflix. I remembered him fondly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Helped me to see the grace of acceptance.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: His own personal history of challenges.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at the time as I was a child. Now I have put it in perspective.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I made a few mistakes along the way. But I am content now.

situation: I went to a local rehabilitation center to get an assessment for substance abuse treatment. This was an extremely difficult decision for me to make, and I almost didn't go through with it. I was trying to seek treatment for my addiction, even though I didn't want to do this, but I felt strongly that I needed to. When I arrived for the assessment, I was told based on my test results that I was unable to move forward that day. I felt defeated and embarrassed, but I made an appointment to return in a few days. The experience made me anxious and upset with myself, but I think I will be calmer and more level-headed going in for the second time now that I've gotten through it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me and changed the way I felt for the next day and beyond. It made me take an even clearer view of my actions and needs than that I had needed to take to show up in the first place.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because it was a reality check, and because it gave me a clear path for moving forward, calming some of the anxiety I had before. It hurt me in that it made me embarrassed and ashamed.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel I was completely responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel fully in control of the process, but I feel responsible for the outcome after the fact.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not quite go as I expected, as I was unaware that the assessment wouldn't be possible if I failed the testing. In a more positive way, it was unexpected how courteous and compassionate the rehab center employees were.

situation: My husband had been very sick for some time, and I went away for the afternoon. When I came back, he had passed on. It was such a shock. I actually had a very vivid dream of it last night, me finding him. I was happy to see his face in my dream, but I just wanted to hold his hand. I don’t get emotional that easy and actually cry, and I was crying.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I found my husband dead. The guilt of him being alone as he died breaks my heart.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I haven’t forgotten him. But it hurt me because I was just thinking about all the variables and not being there with him. I kept thinking, well, what if I was there, would he still be alive?
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt guilt because I went away for the afternoon, and when I came back, he was dead.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I had zero control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Finding my husband dead was completely unexpected.

situation: I'm feeling really frustrated because I don't have enough money to pay down my credit card debt. It's like I'm being drowned in bills and I just can't manage my debt adequately with my current income. This whole situation leaves me feeling like I'm sinking. On top of that, it's important for me to handle this without stressing out my elderly mom, who's prone to anxiety.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It's been a consistent issue, but the moment I'm thinking of was in the past week. It matters a lot to me, as it's the main issue that's been plaguing me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It's only been harmful, as it constantly adds stress to my life without any upsides.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Ultimately it's on me for not making enough money from my job to take care of my family.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I'm doing my best but the situation is devolving out of control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected, but my expectations were incredibly low to begin with.

situation: I felt overwhelmed by a recent stream of difficult events. First, I got food poisoning, then I caught a cold, and on top of that, work was really stressful. Plus, there were some negative personal events happening as well. I was just trying to get back to a baseline, to feel like I didn't have more than I could manage. The whole situation left me feeling overwhelmed, powerless, stressed, and frustrated. It was really important to me to have people be understanding during this time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The situation mattered a lot to me because it affected my work, relationships, and daily activities.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me see my strengths and ability to manage difficulties well, but it also took a toll on me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that mostly bad luck was responsible, with my work stress being the fault of upper management.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt a loss of some control. I knew that I could control how I handled it and did a good job staying calm while finding the best solutions, but it felt like so much was happening to me that it felt like a loss of control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Unexpected elements were each time a new problem arose. Otherwise, things went as expected.

situation: I was on a training course over the weekend and learned lots of new things about activism. I wanted to understand what is involved in activism and what support and training is available. Now, I feel more informed to make a choice which is likely to have consequences. Meeting like-minded people and knowing we had similar concerns and hopes was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was very recent, last weekend. It mattered to me because I believe strongly in the cause and wanted to get more involved.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The training was an introduction and more specific training and support is provided when an action is planned. This initial training was about finding out the risks and rewards involved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The trainers and organization were responsible for laying it out without sugar coating it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because the organization does not force things on people and provides the information to make a choice.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Some of the role-playing was eye-opening and certainly made me think.

situation: My great uncle got the all clear from cancer. He was diagnosed last year, and it was worrying us all. A few days ago, he had surgery, and they got all of the cancer, and he was given the all clear. I didn't really need anything; I was just basking in the relief of his all clear. I felt on top of the world, like all of the worry just evaporated in an instant. It was important how it brought all of our family together.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because this great uncle has been a fairly significant part of my life, so I have been extremely worried this past year. Learning he was cancer-free was a great deal of stress evaporated in an instant.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me deeply as I was worrying a lot, but then in the past week when we got the all clear, it actually helped me. It made me realize that I can handle stress just fine and taught me I'm fairly resilient.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Probably my uncle's doctors. Without them getting all of the cancer, I wouldn't have this feeling of relief.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Absolutely no control whatsoever. My uncle was the sick one, and there was nothing I could do to make him not be sick. I could support him, but not much more than that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected. It was a pretty quick turnaround from his diagnosis to him being cancer-free. We were expecting it to take a fair bit longer than it ended up taking.

situation: It was my late mum's first birthday since she passed away last October, and it was especially hard for my dad. I supported him by going to her mum and dad's grave to tidy up, and I spent time with him since it was also Valentine's Day. It was emotionally sad but also positive. I wanted to let my dad know that I'm still here for him because I used to be a carer for her alongside him, being at the house every day with carers coming in and out. I think dad feels lonely in the house now, and I needed to make sure he was okay and knew that I'm here if he needed me or just wanted to talk about mum, which he did. I felt nostalgic and sad, a mixture really. When I left, I felt drained but happy to know that we are a close family and support each other through life. I'm not one for standing at a grave to grieve, but dad wanted to. We looked through photos, talked about mum, and I let him know I haven't forgotten. It's good to talk about sad things and good memories.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on February 14th. It mattered a fair bit because she is my mum, he is my dad, we support each other and celebrated mum's life before she became bad and chairbound with Parkinson's. We talked about the good bits and the hard stressful bits as it wasn't easy, and I wanted to let dad know it's okay that things got heated at times as we are all only human and we did the best we could. She wanted to stay at home, not go into nursing care, which she desperately needed then but was so scared, so we muddled through and she died while at home. It wasn't really a good death, and the paramedics did CPR for 17 minutes and she came back round but there was no brain activity, so the last days were in a hospital but she wasn't aware of it. We were, and it was a chance to say goodbye although it was distressing at the time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I have already told you, good memories, bad memories, talking things through and moving on and making sure dad is okay as I will have to look out for him also in the future. I want to know for my peace of mind how he copes and what he may want in the future regarding care, etc. Putting things in place now makes it easier to deal with.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible; it just was.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of my feelings and what I chose to do. Dad decided to go to the grave and I went with him, so he controlled the time there and us being there.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect; I went along and as things unfolded, I went with it. I have learned there isn't much point in expecting from a situation that I don't know how will turn out. It's wasted thinking time, and I am happy to not plan and impulse choices on the day are fine. I am not a planner.

situation: A long-standing colleague was retiring from the organization I work for, and many old colleagues joined us to celebrate. It was quite overwhelming emotionally. While we were celebrating, there was also a strong negative sense of time passing, which was quite draining. I didn't need anything specific; I just wanted to spend time with her and some current and ex-colleagues. The situation left me feeling quite drained and with a strong sense of time passing, getting older, and thoughts of death. These feelings, both good and bad, were heightened by alcohol, as is often the case in celebrations.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event didn't hugely matter to me personally in terms of having repercussions for my life, but I was keen that it was a fun positive event for the sake of the person retiring.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help or hurt me; that wasn't really the point.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Life? God?
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was generally in control of my emotions but definitely affected by the sentiment on show, both at the time and reflecting on it subsequently. Many people felt overwhelmed by speeches that were emotionally charged, recalling past events and speaking to time passing and change.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing was particularly unexpected. Emotional impact is part of these events, like certain birthdays, funerals, etc.

situation: I was getting my son to sleep after a long day of work, and it made me emotional. I wanted my son to get to sleep, but I was happy spending time with him. I was tired but happy. I don't have much time with him during the day, so it was important to spend time with him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I enjoy spending time with my son but don't get to do it as much as I'd like.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me feel closer to my son, but it was tough to fight through the exhaustion.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Work was responsible for the exhaustion, but my son was responsible for my happy feeling.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn't in control. He falls asleep when he does.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected. Can't time the moment when he falls asleep, but he usually falls asleep in a certain window.

situation: I was out at breakfast with my short-term girlfriend, and everything seemed normal at first. We were just having our usual Saturday morning scene, but then things took a negative turn. She seemed to brace herself before telling me she wanted to break up. I was shocked and didn't know what to say. I just got up and walked away, trying to maintain control and not verbally lash out. The whole situation left me feeling empty and down.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was everything a routine of contentment and safety meant to me. Now she is gone.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: My intimate world is now gone. My trust for anyone continues to be eroded.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She was, obviously.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Only in control of leaving the table and the cafe. She had control over the decision to end the relationship, which left me feeling powerless in that moment.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Walking in with a girlfriend, walking out without one.

situation: I had to go and speak to the Store Manager of the supermarket branch I work in about the way my shift supervisor spoke to me, which I found belittling and patronising. I wanted to be listened to and treated with more respect, so that I didn't dread coming into work or go away feeling upset. After the conversation, I didn't feel great - I didn't feel that he particularly agreed with my analysis or that he was very sympathetic. None of this is necessary, since the other three shift supervisors I work with are lovely. Which is another way of saying the problem is him, not me!

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event made me feel shitty, and I came away from the shift so angry that it affected my entire weekend. I am 44 years old and should not be spoken to like that.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel belittled and talked down to, which is not what I want at the best of times (and this is NOT the best of times).
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My supervisor.
appraisal_reasoning.control: The only control I had was over how I reacted. There is a power imbalance in that situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No; I did not expect to be treated this way when I got the job.

situation: I had a fight with someone I care about, and it made me really emotional. I think it started as a misunderstanding, but somehow it grew into a big deal. I wanted to see my friend, but my partner didn't want me to. I needed him to be understanding about it. The whole situation left me feeling upset and confused.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened 2 days ago. It mattered a lot because I trusted my partner to understand.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because the person won't talk to me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the ability to not look at the other's point of view was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do not feel like I was in control because his reaction was not how I would have reacted.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it didn't go as expected because he still isn't talking to me.

situation: My son got his learner's permit, and I took him driving yesterday. He did great, and we also ate lunch together where he shared a lot of things with me. I felt very close to him. I was trying to help my son learn how to safely and confidently drive for the first time on a busy road. He was nervous and asked a lot of questions, but he did a really good job. I left the situation feeling very connected to him. I enjoy his company and want to stay close to him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened yesterday. It mattered a lot to me because I am responsible for ensuring he is a safe driver before he gets licensed. I enjoy hearing his stories about his life and his friends and having deep conversations with him about life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation did not hurt me in any way. It helped me because I will not have to worry about him driving if we teach him properly. It helped me to feel close to him due to the conversations we had.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were both responsible for this, as we both were open to each other.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control. I cannot make him open up to me. I let him drive a car, so I was not in control of the car.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Mostly everything went as expected. I did notice that if I feel nervous when he is driving, it makes him feel nervous. I have to control my reactions because I don't want him to be nervous when driving.

situation: I was working with a patient who shared about the abuse they experienced. I was trying to assess and support the patient during our session. Hearing their story left me feeling sad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week, and the severity of the abuse was high. It mattered to me because of the nature of the abuse shared by the patient.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation did not help or hurt me directly, as I had to maintain professionalism. However, I managed my emotions by discussing it with my clinical supervisor to debrief.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No-one was responsible; it just was.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I am trained to manage my own emotional response.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Some of the details the patient shared were unexpected.

situation: I nearly got run over when crossing the road. A car coming down the road was late to spot me and then had to brake quite hard to avoid hitting me. I just needed to cross the road safely, but the situation left me feeling quite shaken and annoyed that someone nearly killed me. That particular road is quite bad for crossing by foot, and I see it as a result of too many people driving through the town.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Tuesday evening, and mattered a great deal since I was nearly hurt, or potentially dead.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me emotionally, but physically I was fine.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The car was definitely most responsible, as I was crossing a pedestrian crossing.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control really, as the responsibility was entirely on the driver.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected that a driver would pay so little attention when driving through a town centre with lots of people and other cars around.

situation: It was my mother-in-law's 80th birthday this week, and I felt emotional as I took the time to buy her a personal gift that I knew she would love. I really wanted to get her something special that would have meaning to her. When I saw her joy upon receiving the gift, I felt very happy and emotional. I was glad that I had gone to so much effort, and it was important to me to let her know how much she is loved by our family.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Wednesday this week. It mattered to me as she is so kind and good to me and my children, and I wanted to do something that would let her know how much she is loved and appreciated by us.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped as it gave me an opportunity to do something nice for her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt like I was in control as I chose the gift for her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected as she loved the gift and was very appreciative and happy.

situation: I was scrolling through YouTube, just trying to relax, when I came across a video about a woman rescuing a sick and unwanted calf from a dairy farm. She nursed it back to health, and I was really touched by her compassion. It made me feel good knowing there are people willing to help animals like that. At the same time, I felt bad for the billions of farm animals who never get rescued. The woman's kindness really stood out to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was about a week ago. I guess in the bigger scheme of things it didn't really affect me. But it did give me a sense of hope and I really felt for the calf.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It lifted my spirit knowing there are still kindness in this world. But it also reminded me of the suffering of the billions of farm animals everywhere.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Humans are responsible. They turn a blind eye to farm animals and eat their flesh just because they like the taste of it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. I can't control what the 8 billion people in this world do or not do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes it went expected. The calf found a forever home with the woman.

situation: Last week, I spent some time playing cards with some new friends from church. We were playing a card game and enjoying a time of fellowship. I really need to get out more and relax with people, and it was so nice to be in a situation where I wasn't stressing about something. It's hard for me to meet new people, so this was a great opportunity.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a week ago Friday. I arrived at 4:30 and stayed until 9:00. It was a very important step for me as I am trying to rebuild relationships after having been sick for a long time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to overcome the anxiety I have being around new people. It gave me a new confidence. It hurt because I now realize how lonely my daily life is.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My new friend Amy was the one who invited me, but I also know that I am responsible for the willingness to take a chance.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't plan the time or place but I had complete control to choose what I participated in.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It played out the way I expected but I was surprised at how relaxed I actually was in the situation.

situation: Scenario: My partner and I were watching TV news together when an article came on about a lower league football team. I recognized the team's location as Witham, Essex, and mentioned it to my partner. During the rest of the piece, she also said it was Witham. I pointed out that I had already told her that, but she insisted that I hadn't. This annoyed me a bit, so I asked if she hadn't heard me. She said she had heard me but claimed I had mentioned a completely different village closer to us, which also started with a 'W'. I joked that maybe she needed hearing aids, like I have, which didn't go over well. She got annoyed, and we ended up in a stalemate silence for a while. I just wanted her to admit she hadn't heard what I said, but as usual, she argued with me. It left me feeling like she always has to be right. I thought it was a waste of time to continue arguing about something so trivial, and I felt sad because this type of situation was becoming the norm. I've tried in the past but she will never accept that she could be wrong. I really don't know how to change it. I handle it by removing myself usually from the room. Instead, I decided to try a different approach. I took a deep breath and suggested we both might have misunderstood each other, and maybe it was just a mix-up. I asked if we could agree to let it go and enjoy the rest of the evening together. She seemed to appreciate the gesture, and we moved on from the disagreement without further conflict.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered because it was a repeat of other situations where she has argued rather than accept that we can have differing perceptions and opinions. I don't want to do this any more.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Your suggestion of ending it is helpful and I will give it a try. Right now I feel she will argue with that! It makes me internalise and get lost in thoughts.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: null
appraisal_reasoning.control: null
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: null

situation: I was attending a meeting and actively participating when a work colleague made a comment that really angered me. It felt like my authority was being undermined, and that left me feeling pretty upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week and it mattered because it was a live departmental meeting with all staff.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It angered me. Yes, I had to control my emotions and remain professional.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The colleague who made the comment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, as it felt like an ambush.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was controlled by the chair of the meeting.

situation: I feel like my wife and kids have no respect for me, and I'm treated as their servant. I have to do everything, including dropping them off at school, picking them up, and cleaning up after them when they come home because their clothes are just chucked to one side. I just want them to do their own thing and leave me alone sometimes, just give me a break. This situation leaves me feeling negative, but a good thing is they went to my in-laws for a few days. I just want to let loose at someone or just let out some rage.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happens every day, including yesterday and today, and it matters to me because I have to work and work around them all.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurts me because it makes me feel like a slave and leaves me feeling negative. I feel like just letting loose and releasing rage.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the wife and kids are most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I don't feel in control because no matter what it is, they don't care as long as dad is around. It's good; he'll do it, he'll even switch off the lights.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, at this point it's anticipated.

situation: I was having such a lovely day and just wanted to relax and have a peaceful time at home. But my brother started shouting and slamming doors, which made the environment in the house really bad. I don't talk to him, so there was nothing I could do except stay in my room until he finished having his tantrum. The situation left me feeling really upset because all I wanted was some peace. I was also pretty angry at him for disturbing my peace. I ended up calling my mum to complain about his behavior, and I guess he heard me on the phone because he soon stopped.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and mattered a lot to me because I had just passed my exams and was in a good mood, which he ruined.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by disrupting my emotional state, leading me to have a good cry and journal about it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My brother was entirely responsible; no one else.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn't in control. I don't talk or engage with him, so I just had to wait for the situation to die down.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went pretty much as expected as he did finally stop shouting and slamming doors.

situation: My partner went on holiday for a week, and I was trying to say goodbye. Even though it was only for a week, I knew I was going to miss him. I was trying not to cry, but I got emotional. I felt sad, but I was also happy he was going to have fun.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 weeks ago. It mattered a lot as we live together and he's the only person I see every single day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did neither really. It helped I guess as it reminded me I can cope on my own. I wouldn't say it hurt me, but made me appreciate him more.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Him as he left.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, as it was just me so I had to be.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went to plan, as well as they could.

situation: I got into an argument with my housemate about cleaning the kitchen. I wanted him to clear up after he had cooked for himself so that I could then cook my dinner. I was angry and frustrated because this issue is a recurring problem. As soon as I start having to clean away his mess, he suddenly wants to do it. It shouldn't get to that stage.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Sunday. It mattered to me because I know he likes a routine and I didn't mind using the kitchen after him, but he cooked and ate his food and then just watched stuff on his tablet. Around an hour later, I went into the kitchen and started to wash up, and he then came running in saying 'would you like me to do that,' and I end up saying thank you like he is doing me a favor.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation frustrates me because he doesn't ever seem to learn to clean up after himself until I am at the point of doing it for him. He must know he has never had to do the same for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He was most responsible for all of this.
