appraisal_reasoning.control: I have no control over his actions and what he does. However, it's a shared place/space and he needs to factor that into his actions and what he does.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was, sadly, exactly as anticipated!

situation: I was out cycling to keep fit and enjoy the nice weather when a car driver passed me really closely. It left me feeling shaken and annoyed. Thankfully, I escaped without being hit, injured, or worse.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Tuesday. My safety matters to me greatly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was scared and annoyed that a poor driver almost injured me with their crap driving.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The fault was with the driver.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I stayed calm, the incident was recorded so I knew I had the evidence for the police.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The driver kept going and I haven't heard back from the police as yet.

situation: I had a fantastic day on Saturday. The weather was nice, so I decided to get out of the house and run some errands. I needed to pick up a few groceries and drop off some recycling. Everyone I met was friendly and happy, which made the experience even better. I came home feeling happy and content, having accomplished everything without feeling anxious.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Saturday and mattered a great deal to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped me realize that everything is not always difficult.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt like I was in control because I chose to spend the day this way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went as expected.

situation: I was looking into colleges for my oldest daughter and became emotional because I realized she's growing up and will be out on her own soon. I was trying to help her with the paperwork for a college she wants to go to. It left me feeling a mix of emotions; I'm very happy for her, but it also makes me sad to know she'll be leaving the house soon.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me quite a bit because it is a big milestone for both of us.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I will miss spending so much time with my daughter. It helps because I know I am doing what I need to do as a parent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't think anyone was responsible for this; it was just the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because in this situation I need to be strong for my child.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I think everything went as expected. Overall it was positive but just sad at the same time.

situation: I recently spoke with a friend, and we bonded over the fact that we both lost our grandfathers in recent months. It made us both rather emotional. I guess we were both looking for a little reassurance or friendship in one another, just knowing that this is okay and something that we all go through. We wanted to be together and support each other. It was obviously emotional at the time, but definitely beneficial and good long-term.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened one evening during the week after finishing work. It mattered to me at the time and was an unexpected conversation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt at the time because it involved reliving harsh emotions and discussing a tough situation. However, I feel better afterward and now have a new bond with my friend that we can continue to talk about.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both my friend and I were responsible, as we talked individually about our experiences and feelings before realizing we shared similar sad emotions over losing someone. These moments allowed us to reflect and appreciate life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I think we were both equally in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had no expectations going into the conversation; it was an unexpected conversation.

situation: I went and sat with my baby brother, who is 64, while he had his chemo treatment. I'm very sad that he has to go through this, and it doesn't look like his chances are very good, but he's a fighter. I sat with him for 2 hours, and he and all the other chemo patients in the room were talking and having a good time joking about their situation. It was uplifting, but also sad. I was trying to give him moral support. It left me feeling sad for all the people that have to go through this type of thing. It also made me feel glad that I could be there for him, especially since his wife died a few years ago and I didn't want him to be alone. Just being there to support him was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me, because I was the only one he has to be with him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me to see him going through this. It also made me feel happy that all the people there having treatment had a positive attitude.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The cancer that everyone is going through was responsible for the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt like I had no control over the situation. If I could change the outcome I would have done so.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went smooth and he did okay. He was quick sick afterwards and remains very tired.

situation: My computer, which I rely on for making income, seized up and stopped working. This caused me to not only miss a day of earning money, but I also had to spend money on a new computer. I needed my computer to do what it's done for over a decade and simply work, so I could earn income. The situation left me frustrated and upset because I already had to go beyond my means to afford a computer to replace my old one, and I haven't been able to catch up financially to the money I missed making.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered greatly as it is my only source of income.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I missed a full day of being able to make wages, and I had to spend money beyond what I had to be able to replace my computer.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nothing and no one, really, beyond my computer being over a decade old.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I was not prepared; I was trying to save up towards a new computer because I knew I couldn't afford it right now, then I was forced to get a new one anyway!
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not at all, I wasn't expecting my computer to stop working when it did!

situation: I was out in an open area playing with my German Shepherd mix. She suddenly spotted something in the woods and dashed off deep into them, where I couldn't see or hear her anymore. I kept calling her repeatedly, hoping she'd come back quickly. Several minutes passed, and she finally returned, but by then, I was so anxious I felt like I could throw up. I wanted her to respond readily to me and come back in short order. The whole situation left me feeling like a bad dog mom, thinking there must be other ways I could have prevented this. Even though I felt like she would probably emerge okay, the experience was still traumatizing for me. I reminded myself that God is in control, so I should trust Him, and I felt grateful when she came back. I love my dog's playful and exploratory nature, but I really need her to respond to me when it's critical.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because this dog is my world every single day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation is yet another reminder to continually work on her training and recall. Emotionally, I had a sense of loss and grief immediately.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Dogs are dogs so it is just what it is.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control but I wished I was.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things eventually turned out as I desired but I wasn’t completely sure what to expect.

situation: My father had collapsed and was taken to the hospital to be checked out. I was really anxious because I didn't know what had happened or how serious his condition was. I was comforted by my boyfriend, who was very understanding of the situation and how I was feeling. I wanted to get some news from the hospital on my father's condition, but initially, I couldn't get through to other family members to find out more. It was important to me to ensure the other members of the family were OK too, especially my Mum.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a couple of weeks ago, around 8pm in the evening. It mattered that I found out what happened and how my father was.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I found out that night how much my boyfriend cared for me. He completely understood how I would be feeling in that situation and helped to comfort me. So although the situation was very stressful for me, my boyfriend was brilliant.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I really don’t know what had happened. No one was at fault. My father just hadn’t been feeling well, and wasn’t well that evening.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn’t feel like I was in control at all, because I didn’t really have much information for about two hours. I knew my father had been taken to hospital, but there was no further information. So, I couldn’t influence or change what was happening.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, and by 10pm I had more information, and felt a little more in control. The hospital were able to give my father lots of advice, and a plan to go forward.

situation: For a very long time, I accepted verbal abuse from a family member. Recently, after so many years, I finally decided that I wasn't going to accept this treatment anymore and cut this person out of my life. What I needed was peace. At first, I felt emotional and upset about the whole situation. But now that some time has passed, it feels like a weight has been lifted off my shoulders. I had to consider certain factors, like the fact that I would never see other family members again because of this decision.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: At first when it happened it upset me because it was a shock.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has made me grow as a person and has made me realise that just because someone is family doesn't mean you should accept this treatment from someone.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The other person was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control of the initial situation but was in control of what followed.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: When I said I wasn't going to accept the treatment and I'm done, I had no response.

situation: I was going through old photographs, including some recent ones, to put together a book of photographs as a present for my brother. I had been asked to provide some family photographs for him to look through because a health professional had advised it. As I was sorting through them, I found it slightly distressing because most of my relatives are dead. I enjoyed seeing some of the photographs, but I was feeling a bit upset about my brother, who has Alzheimer's. There was maybe some pleasure in thinking about my children during this process.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a moderate amount to me because I was doing something that might provoke an emotional response in my brother, and I was aware that this might also include mixed feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by providing the satisfaction of completing the task and the pleasure of seeing the photographs. However, it also hurt me with the pain of loss.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't attribute responsibility for things to anyone or anything. I can talk about perceived causal influences, but not responsibility.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I'm never in control. I just do what I most want to do, all things considered, and it just happens without any need for a concept of being in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things mainly went as expected. One or two photographs turned out not to be suitable because the quality wasn't good enough.

situation: I was watching a TV show, trying to relax, when a sad funeral scene came on. I was already feeling stressed, so this scene just added to it and left me feeling upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I was watching a sad scene on a show I have been watching and felt connected to the characters, so I felt their pain.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It heightened my already strong emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think me feeling off did.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I felt overwhelmed from the day.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting to be so affected by it.

situation: I applied for a new job and got an interview, but unfortunately, I wasn't correct for that role. I was looking for a change in job role and wanted to earn more money by working more hours. The whole experience left me feeling not good enough and disappointed. I've been with my current employment for years, so it took a lot for me to apply for a new job.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened Monday of last week. It mattered to me as I am struggling with bills at the moment and I could do with a higher income.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by having an interview as I haven't had one for years, so it gave me practice. It hurt me as the interview went well, the interviewers were nice, and I was getting positive feedback.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I was responsible as I didn't have whatever attributes they were looking for and they chose someone who did.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I thought we were equally in control. I got to learn about the role better and they got to see if I was suitable.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Because I got such good feedback, I thought the outcome was going to be positive, but it wasn't, so that was unexpected.

situation: My sister, brother-in-law, and two nieces were traveling over from Spain to come back to the UK for a few days, and I went to see them during their visit. Saying goodbye to them was difficult as always, because it sometimes brings back memories of other tough goodbyes we've had with parents and others. I was just saying goodbye and reminding them that I'd see them again in a few weeks or months. I really just needed them to know that I loved them. The whole situation left me feeling bittersweet, with the joy of seeing them mixed with the sadness of saying bye for a while. It was also important to me to let my nieces know that I loved them too and to give them a nice farewell.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot because they're family and we don't often get to spend time all together, and some family members are missing now. It's where I grew up but sadly it's not a situation where we all have a house with a shared history to go back to.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped because it was an opportunity to share fun together again. It hurt because there is still some unresolved grief between us all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were all responsible for our own emotions, as it's a common situation to say goodbye to family.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I've had similar situations before so was mentally prepared for the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected - I think we all got through it OK through and around our feelings.

situation: My sister-in-law was talking to me about an eating disorder that she previously had issues with. I was helping her to fill in a disclosure form for a job. I was surprised by what I'd learnt and hoped I'd dealt with it sensitively. Nothing was more important to me in that moment than to show care and consideration.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered hugely to me because my sister-in-law was disclosing something sensitive to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation did hurt me but it didn't help me either. It was just one of those uncomfortable things in life that you need to get through.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My sister-in-law was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control; my sister-in-law was. I was completing a form on her behalf.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected. I knew the questions we had to complete were sensitive.

situation: I was confronted by my boss for doing a bad job on a project. I didn't deliver a report on time and was pulled in to go over the reasons. I was trying to manage my responsibilities and needed more time or support to deliver the report. The whole situation left me feeling negative about the company and manager. His tone of voice was important to me in this situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week, before the end of the month when I had to deliver. It mattered because it was part of a larger project.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt my opinion of myself in the wider team.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was most responsible for all of this because I didn't manage my time correctly.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control because there were too many other things going on.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I was expected to deliver a report but didn't.

situation: Yesterday, my spouse and I had a disagreement about communication. I was trying to express my preference for how we should allocate our monthly budget. However, it left me feeling unappreciated because my spouse seemed to dismiss my suggestion in favor of her own ideas. I felt like I wasn't heard or acknowledged in the conversation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event occurred two days ago. It matters to me because both communication and financial matters are important to a solid relationship, especially as we have a number of upcoming bills and are trying to figure out which ones to prioritize.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: By more or less dismissing my suggestions, I felt invisible. This situation was quite hurtful for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like my spouse failed to consider my suggestions. She already had her mind made up before I even broached the topic.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control since my suggestions were dismissed rather abruptly.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected. While I wasn't sure my partner would wholeheartedly agree with my suggestions, I assumed she would at least consider them.

situation: A recent situation that made me really emotional was the death of my dog. She had been part of our family for over 15 years, and I had a really hard time processing it. All I wanted was to be able to spend more time with her because making memories is the biggest thing for me. But in this case, I had to let her go because she was in too much pain. It left me feeling really lonely and sad. Coming back home without her was crushing. The biggest thing of all was knowing she wouldn't be around any longer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered more than anything because she was a giant part of our family, and there is a huge hole left behind now.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me realize just how integral she was in our lives. It hurt because she left us for good.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Life in general. It is so unfair that dogs have such short lifespans compared to humans.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Somewhat. I had to make the call to let her go, which was even harder. But I knew deep down it was the right thing to do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went as expected. Nothing surprised me at all.

situation: This happened at work this week when my boss spoke to me in a rude way. My boss was undermining my efforts and hard work on a recent project, asking why I didn’t have certain bits of information that were irrelevant and information I wouldn’t have, just to catch me out. I was seeking recognition and respect for the hard work I put into the project, hoping for understanding and support rather than being put in a difficult position. This situation left me feeling angry and emotional, like my hard work was not recognized. I think my boss was under pressure, which might explain why they acted the way they did. However, this still wasn’t acceptable, and I didn’t appreciate being spoken to this way.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot as I feel under a lot of pressure at the minute at work due to team members leaving and my workload increasing. I feel like a bit of recognition would have gone a long way rather than the criticism I received.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as I feel like I am always giving my all to this job and feel like I am not valued.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think my manager was most responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control. I felt like my manager was out to get me and I couldn’t say anything to defend myself.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn’t expect the incident to happen when it did and I was caught off guard.

situation: After church on Sunday, I was in the church hall where tea and coffee were available. The place was bustling with people chatting and children happily running around. I noticed a group of five foreign-looking young men standing together, chatting among themselves. No one from the church group approached them to make them feel welcome. I decided to speak with the men and found out that they were asylum seekers, new to the area and living in temporary accommodation, with limited English language skills. I really wanted to see these young men being approached and included in the social gathering, but instead, I felt embarrassed and ashamed of my fellow church attendees for not making them feel welcome. I was left feeling disappointed and disheartened by the lack of engagement from the congregation. It's a sad reflection on us as a Christian congregation when no one seemed interested in these young men. It made me feel very sad and somewhat ashamed of my fellow church attenders. These young men were strangers in a foreign land, and they came to a Christian church. It felt like the parable of the Good Samaritan had been forgotten by my fellow church members.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened after church on Sunday. It mattered to me because there was no clear indication that the young asylum seekers were wanted or welcome there, which made me feel sad and somewhat helpless. I did my best to make them feel welcome.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I was upset and very sad, feeling as if my church were not willing to extend love, welcome, or warmth. It went against my values and was difficult to witness.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my fellow church members were responsible, as they seemed to pay lip service to their alleged Christian faith. The church is responsible for extending love and welcome to all, but that did not happen in this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt alone because no one from the church joined me when I approached the asylum seekers to welcome them. I was out of my depth because I was in the minority and started to feel as if I did not belong there either.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected. The asylum seekers were not made welcome, and I was sad and really upset because of the clear rejection they must have experienced. The way they were treated was unexpected and unchristian.

situation: My sister gave birth to premature twins, and I was trying to support her and her partner through it all. I felt emotional, excited, and scared at the same time. It was really important to me to ensure she had all the medical help she needed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week. It matters so much to me because family is everything and my sister has waited a long time to become a mum.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation didn't hurt me but made me immensely proud and happy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control apart from trying to keep control of my own emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The birth was earlier than expected.

situation: My wife was diagnosed with early stage breast cancer, and all I wanted was to find out what steps needed to be taken to get rid of it. I felt very anxious because I had Hodgkin's 24 years ago, and I know treatment can be difficult. It was important to me that it gets resolved quickly.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot. I am worried that my wife is going to be ok.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I had cancer 22 years ago so it brought back bad memories for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: God.
appraisal_reasoning.control: God. The cause of breast cancer is unknown.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: So far we are still finding out what stage it is and what needs to be done.

situation: Me and my husband had a massive argument that really upset me. I wanted to know that we are still a team, but the situation left me feeling neglected and hurt.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the morning when my husband usually drives me to work, as he has done for the past 17 years. This morning, he told me to walk even though it was raining. It mattered a lot to me because it was so out of the ordinary and left me feeling neglected and hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt like I had done something wrong. It was so out of the ordinary, and I couldn't understand why he was being cold and distant.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like I was most responsible for all of this, as if I had done something I wasn't aware of.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control because I cannot drive, so he had full control, and I had to walk in the rain.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. I kind of expected him to drive me like always.

situation: I caught up with an old friend, and it brought up some deep emotions that I thought I was over but realized I'm not really over at all. I had believed I had an identity outside of work, but this conversation made me question that. It left me feeling mixed. On one hand, I felt like I had actually done some growth and introspection, but on the other hand, there was much more work than I had anticipated before I could consider myself whole. It made me feel small, like I wasn't all I thought I was cracked up to be. It was odd because these feelings surfaced from a conversation with someone from years ago, and it kind of appeared to come out of nowhere.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened this weekend, and it mattered a ton to me. I'm not sure why it mattered so much.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation made me feel small, but it also helped me realize that I have far more growth to attain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My ego is my best guess for what was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control at the time, but later I felt quite loose and not in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole thing was sort of out of left field. I did not see it coming.

situation: I'm struggling with my financial situation due to health issues, and it's causing me a lot of stress to pay the high price of my health insurance. My partner's benefit check also got delayed, which has added more stress, making it difficult to manage. I've been feeling very sad, anxious, and stressed out trying to afford basic necessities to live, and it's caused me a lot of pain and exhaustion. I'm trying to find any way that I can to make more money and support my partner and myself. It's been a challenging road, and I need more money to feel okay. The situation has left me feeling sad, anxious, stressed, and exhausted, and I also feel some shame. It's important to me that my partner and I have enough money to survive.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened around January when I had to take a trip to the Mayo Clinic to see some specialists for my health issues. This has put me behind on rent and other bills coupled with trying to pay the higher price for my health insurance this year.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation has hurt me by adding to my stress on top of the health issues I'm already facing. I guess it has helped me stay resilient.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think that I'm a little responsible for struggling to manage my financial needs. I think the economy and government is also to blame for the higher prices of everything.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do not feel like I'm in control because I don't set the rates for my healthcare.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected but they still suck to an extent.

situation: I got let down for a promotion at work despite being told I was nailed on to get it. I really wanted that promotion because it was my next step, and it meant a little bit more money for my family and me. Plus, it would have been a great time to get it. I had to do a presentation and a strength-based interview for it. I felt so disappointed, angry, and like I let people down. More than anything, I was disappointed because my manager reassured me that I should be applying and that I would get it, as they also had a say. I felt really confident going into it, felt like I prepared well, and assumed it had all gone well.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot as I was put forward for it and the expectation was that I’d get it. I prepared well and felt confident only to get poor feedback. That left me underwhelmed and frustrated and probably angry.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to realise that hard work and determination won’t get you everything in life and that you have to go above and beyond in some cases. It’s made me thicker skinned and not to take someone’s word for it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I’d have prepared even more and only applied when I chose to, not on recommendation. I should have felt confident in my own ability.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control and confident. I maybe was a bit overconfident and naive to the situation, but my manager never helped that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I expected to be given promotion.

situation: It's coming up to the anniversary of my mother's death, and I always get very emotional when I think about her and the loss I feel. Life changes when you lose your mum. I decided to go for a long walk to remember her as she was when she was healthy. I wanted to clear my head and try to dispel the overwhelming sadness with some positive memories. I hoped to feel or see a sign that she was okay and happy wherever she is now. But I felt sad because I didn't get that feeling that she was somewhere and she was okay. Still, it's always good to get out in the fresh air in beautiful surroundings with my dog, so it wasn't an altogether unsatisfying time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week. It mattered a great deal because I wanted to feel better and happier about something that blights my life, which is the loss of mum.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped by just getting out and seeing nature, which reminds me of mum as she loved nature and animals. It hurt because it didn't ultimately give me what I wanted, which was closure.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody. It's just life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, to a great extent because it's my feelings, nobody else's.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing was unexpected.

situation: I've been participating in fasting for Ramadan last week, and it's made me feel spiritually connected to God and brought a sense of calmness. I need to focus on my own spiritual self and renew my intention during this time. It's left me feeling good and light, and I feel like I can be a better person inside and out.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event has happened in the past week and it greatly matters to me as lately I feel lost and no peace within me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me realize I can be a good person.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself and trusting God.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I did feel in control as I was making all the decisions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went better than expected.

situation: I went to a concert on Friday evening to see someone who I've liked for a very long time. I just really wanted to see him in person and enjoy a fun night out to celebrate. It left me feeling very happy and refreshed, and also nostalgic. Plus, it was the anniversary of me and my boyfriend, so it was a very special occasion all around.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Friday evening and mattered to me a lot because I grew up watching this person on TV. Knowing that I would actually be able to see him perform in person was very exciting for me. It was like getting a piece of my childhood back.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The concert made me feel happy and refreshed, and also nostalgic. It didn't hurt me at all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The person performing and the film I watched growing up, which he acted in, were most responsible for making the concert memorable for me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had control in the sense that it was me who purchased the tickets and chose to go. However, when I was actually at the concert, I felt I didn't have as much control because there were no seats, as it was standing only, so it was very much an 'every man for himself' situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I would say that the whole concert went as expected.

situation: I was watching a documentary about the war in Gaza, and it made me uncomfortable and very sad. I wanted to see for myself what life was like in Gaza rather than relying on reporting. I wanted to know the truth because there is so much misinformation out there. The situation left me feeling very sad and angry. The people there are living in unimaginable conditions.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because these poor people have done nothing wrong to deserve this treatment.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me knowing that there is nothing I can do to support them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt Benjamin Netanyahu was most responsible for all of this, as he has taken this too far.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control of my surroundings, but I wasn't in control of the situation, which made it even sadder as there was nothing I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected the documentary to be sad, but I didn't expect it to be so revealing.

situation: I attended a follow-up consultation to check that my cancer is still in remission. It was confirmed that I currently have no secondaries in my lungs, which was a big relief. I wasn't trying to do anything myself, just attending a medical consultation. I wanted a positive outcome, which is what I got. The situation left me feeling relieved and optimistic. It was important to me that my condition is being closely and carefully monitored, and that's exactly the reassurance I received.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered enormously to me because I don't want cancer to reappear. It was important to me that my condition is being closely and carefully monitored, and that's exactly the reassurance I received.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by providing reassurance that the careful monitoring I am receiving will allow early action should the cancer reappear. It left me feeling relieved and optimistic.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that the whole medical team who I have come into contact with since my initial diagnosis was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control to a limited extent because it is incumbent upon me to identify and report any suspicious symptoms to my medical team.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: All went as expected during the follow-up consultation.

situation: I went to a sex club in Manchester, UK, and met a person for sex, which was a really positive experience for me. Being single, I wanted sex because it's emotionally supportive and satisfies a need I have. I felt wonderful afterward because I got exactly what I wanted from similar individuals. The surroundings and facilities at the club were important to me, as well as its proximity to where I live. The personality of the other people I had sex with that afternoon was also an important factor in my experience.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday at a club in Manchester, UK. It mattered a lot- as this is where I get sex from other people.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped very much, as it satisfied my emotional needs, and made me feel really good and positive.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was me personality and charisma, and being able to attract other people that also wanted a sexual afternoon.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes- very much. Because I could either accept or reject their advances.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was exactly what I experienced I go to sex clubs on a vey regular basis, and love it.

situation: I was rejected for disability benefits, which was really tough. I've been eligible for them for a long time, and I finally struck up the courage to attempt to acquire them. I knew it'd be hard because even the most disabled people can get rejected, but I really need them to improve my quality of life. Getting rejected left me feeling really dejected and emotional, like there's no point in trying to fight against what I see as an injustice. I just want to feel seen and like the people I'm approaching for help and support can understand my perspective, but that's not the case.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a whole lot to me as it was the one thing I was focussed on at the time and there were some things that counted on me being approved for them, such as being able to move to a home that suits my needs.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me a lot, as it feels like a big set back and as if I cannot win here, even though it's likely that the decision will be overturned on appeal, it's just a lot of stress and hard work to get there.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The nurse who did my medical assessment absolutely threw me under a bus. I requested a written copy of the assessment and some of the things she wrote are so inaccurate that it's very disheartening.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I had zero control in this situation, and as if it all depends on the whims of a couple of people and how they feel that day and how they assess me in a small 20 minute window.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No they didn't. I expected to be understood a lot better, and that they would realise how bad my health is and see things from my side, but they didn't.

situation: Recently, I let a friend borrow my car to get to work. While it has mostly been fine, the other day, he had problems getting it started and had to get a ride back, leaving my car there overnight. We were worried that either the battery needed replacing or, worse, an even more expensive part. Thankfully, the next evening, he was able to get it started just fine. We figure it was just very cold outside and my car wasn't dealing with the weather well. It was very scary having to consider dealing with car repairs or replacement parts and the monetary hit it would take. I wasn't trying to do anything; I was just briefly worried about affording car repairs. I'm thankful it was mostly a false alarm and was a problem with the weather as opposed to the car. I was definitely very worried. I'm already struggling to afford things, so the idea of having to pay for sudden car maintenance was very concerning. I felt much better after learning there was not actually anything that needed to be fixed. No, not really! Just another day with a stressful situation that turned out to be not so bad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This was obviously very important because without a car, I couldn't get places as easily, and having to spend money on car repairs means less money to spend on other things I want and need.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I'm generally pretty anxious by default, so situations like this always make me really stressed out. I was not prepared to deal with these types of situations both emotionally and monetarily. I of course felt much better after learning it was a false alarm, but I do still worry about my car's health and the eventual decline it will face.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Given how cold it was over the past week, we figure it was a result of the weather that prevented my car from starting. I've experienced this in the past, so it made a lot of sense, and we haven't had any problems since then.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Definitely not. Not only was I not the one driving the car, since I'd lent it to a friend, but I also worried about paying for it. I definitely felt out of control of the situation, and very worried about what to do next.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I actually expected to have to pay for repairs, but thankfully, nothing actually needed to be done aside from waiting for the weather to warm up. It was a nice surprise to learn that after stressing for hours about what to do, that nothing had to be done. It was unexpected, but pleasant to learn.

situation: I was walking my pet dog and decided to take him off his lead. Suddenly, he ran off and headed straight across a road. I was really scared he might get hit by a car. I ran after him as fast as I could, but I simply couldn’t catch him before he reached the road. I wanted him to stop, but he wouldn’t. Fortunately, he was alright, and I ended up getting him back on his lead. I was absolutely relieved that he was okay. I have a very strong bond with him, and I was literally terrified when he ran off. I am so thankful nothing bad happened to him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was very stressful because my dog is a central part of my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it made me feel extremely anxious.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible for the situation by letting him off his lead too soon.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn’t feel that I was in control at all because I couldn’t do anything to stop my dog from crossing the road.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I dreaded that he might get hit by a car. Fortunately, this did not happen, which was a total relief.

situation: Scenario: I was facing a challenging situation at work where we received a collective grievance from the hourly paid employees. Although I initially felt the grievance was unfair, I recognized the importance of addressing their concerns objectively. As the HR Manager in the business, I am committed to ensuring employees are satisfied in their roles, so I take it seriously when they express dissatisfaction. I was actively engaging with the new employees by discussing their terms and conditions to ensure their happiness and compliance with the law. The most important thing to me is maintaining legal compliance while fostering a positive work environment. This situation prompted me to reflect on my approach and seek solutions to improve employee satisfaction and communication.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event really mattered to me and made me feel sad and disappointed for a few days because it is important to me to do a good job.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Not really, I just felt I had let people down and my employer.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was 50% responsible for this and their line manager was also responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel I was in control as the employees have sat and written a long collective grievance together.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting the grievance, as we had met with them recently and verbally agreed a resolution.

situation: I had a conversation with my mum about scam calls. I tried to explain that answering the phone at all increases the chance of getting more calls because of robo dialers checking if the phone is live. But she flipped the situation into me suggesting she was stupid and thinks I believe she's going to get scammed. Despite explaining multiple times that I was just trying to reduce the amount of calls she gets, she made it a personal attack on herself. I was trying to educate my mum and help her reduce the frequent scam calls. I needed her to say thank you, I'll check the number first. The whole situation left me feeling frustrated, sad, and with a sense of detachment, like I was talking to someone with a victim's mindset. There wasn't anything else particularly important to me in this situation; I was just trying to help and educate.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered somewhat, she frequently complains about scam calls and acts as if catching them out is a big win when they're just going to immediately call someone else who calls them out too. I really wanted to help reduce the frequency so she deals with less disgusting people like scammers.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: She treated educating her as an insult to her intelligence (despite acting bewildered when I said the number they call from is irrelevant because they can spoof any number) and then despite my frustrations of explaining several times how genuinely I'm trying to help only to be met with a stone wall of her stating she isn't going to get scammed when that wasn't the point of the discussion hurt me because I wasn't being listened to or treated like someone with good intent trying to help and instead as a villain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Her victim's mindset, poor listening skills, and unwillingness to accept new information if it contradicts her opinion.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, anything I said clearly wasn't being heard correctly because the response remained in line with the narrative she isn't stupid.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went exactly as I expected to be honest, it's always been that way.

situation: I recently found out that I got my dream qualified job in an adult community mental health team as a clinical psychologist. It's been what I've been working towards for 10 years, so it was just amazing to have that final validation that I'm good enough. I felt so overwhelmed and happy, but I did have a huge crash of energy afterwards. It was really lovely to celebrate it with my partner though!

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered hugely to me because it was the summation of so many years of hard work and sacrifices.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me significantly by giving me job security in a very uncertain job market.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible for all of this, and that’s what made it feel so satisfying—it was the validation of my hard work.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel powerless and out of control whilst waiting for the call back, but getting the job reinforced a sense of control, I think.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn’t expect to get the job really, so that was unexpected!

situation: When I thought back on how I lived my life, I felt like nothing but a failure. I wanted to stop doing certain things, but I felt sad because I can't stop doing them. I also felt like a big piece of shit and overwhelmed by how big a failure I am. I experienced deep feelings of frustration and helplessness because what I want most cannot be fixed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I did not know better.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation harmed everybody I have ever been around because I treat them bad due to hating myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that I am most responsible for all of this because I did it when I was younger.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I did not know better.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because I have not fully fixed it.

situation: I was happy to see the Iranian dictatorship struck. I wanted to see the Iranian people helped, and I felt happy that they have a chance of ridding themselves from the dictatorship. Justice for them was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event is ongoing. It matters to me because I wanted to see the Iranian people free from oppression.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It gives me happiness because I wanted to see the Iranian people free from oppression.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The Islamic dictatorship there is most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I have no control; I am just an observer.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things are going well so far, as I expected.

situation: My brother has recently recovered from cancer, and we've been discussing his ongoing follow-ups and physio/fitness program. Talking about it made me feel emotional. I'm relieved that he's considered cancer-free, but there's always the fear that it might return. He's 77 years old, and his fitness regime seems quite tough. I want to support him, but we live a long way from each other. I felt okay knowing he's being monitored by a qualified health professional who specializes in cancer aftercare, so rationally, I know he's in good hands. He tells me he feels fit and gauges his fitness by how well he can now climb the stairs to his flat. He's never asked to do anything that causes pain or discomfort.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It felt important because he is my only surviving brother and he has had a life-threatening illness which obviously makes you think about how life is really so short and nothing is promised.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because I'm happy he is thriving and doing well and in charge of his own body now. I try not to dwell on the fact he is getting older regardless and concentrate on the now rather than the hypothetical future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I'm responsible for my thoughts be they positive or negative.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Well in control of me during the narrative. I was not in control of my brother. I'm proud of how he has recovered from such a serious illness and enjoying his life again.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The conversation we had was pretty much as expected. We exchanged family news, shared a few laughs and he updated me on his health which was positive news.

situation: I was at work, trying to come up with a solution for my art project, but I was really struggling. I couldn't figure out how to draw what I wanted, especially when it came to replicating a certain style for drawing hair. I was aiming to get that 3-dimensional volume, but it just wasn't coming together. It left me feeling frustrated. I really want to become better at drawing, and not understanding why I was having these problems made it even harder to solve.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I put a lot of effort into improving.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt like I should have been able to do it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in total control because it was only me working on it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did not go as expected because I thought I was going to be able to do it.

situation: Great Britain were beaten in the final of the curling in the Winter Olympics, and I was really hoping they would win. Watching the match, I felt sad when they didn't come out on top. Despite the loss, I think they played well and we should be proud of their performance.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few minutes ago. It mattered because I wanted them to win.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel disappointed.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The whole team but they did well too.
appraisal_reasoning.control: There was nothing I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They lost, the other team was better.

situation: I was at work, feeling stressed and angry because my manager forced me to take on additional tasks. I had already planned my work items for the next two weeks, and this new workload was beyond my capacity. I felt it would have been better to hand it to someone else on the team who had less on their plate. I was trying to remove myself from the situation, but it left me feeling frustrated. My structure and well-being were important to me, and this situation was affecting both.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot because I have an important project to deal with.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me more than anything because it meant I was overloaded and likely to feel pressure and anxiety.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My manager was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I tried to be in control because I dismissed his words and went against it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: In the end, things did go as I expected because I went out of my way and told my colleague to do it.

situation: I felt frustrated with a colleague who invited me to a meeting, only to discover upon joining that my presence was unnecessary. I was eager to focus on my tasks but found myself trapped in an uninteresting one-hour meeting. This experience left me feeling upset and irritated, with a strong sense of having been misled.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened recently, and it mattered to me because it was annoyingly disruptive, causing me to become irritable and snappy during the meeting when spoken to.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by stopping me from doing some important work and also meant I did not have a lunch break.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the person who invited me to the meeting was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control during the situation. I had joined the meeting and within 5 minutes realized I was not really required but was unable to leave without appearing rude.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing unexpected happened during the meeting.

situation: I had a lot of pain come on in my body all of a sudden. I've been trying to treat the pain and get it better on my own because the doctor hasn't been helping much. This whole situation has left me feeling worn out and exhausted, kind of sad, and I've been having bad dreams as a result. It's important to me that I can handle this situation by myself.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event started about 6 days ago and it matters the most.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation of pain has stopped me from doing all of the things I love to do. It has been mostly negative.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one just health issues.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of treating the situation but the pain was out of my control because I did nothing to start it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as usual I have to take meds and wait for it to hopefully pass.

situation: Last night, my 30-year-old son told us he's going into the armed forces for school purposes. I would have liked to have been kept in the loop because everyone else in the family knew, and he was scared to tell me. I need honesty. I'm happy for him, but also scared.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It just happened last night. It mattered a great deal to me! He's my son.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was just slightly hurtful that he waited so long to tell me. He's known for months. I hate to say it but at this point in my life I'm always waiting for the next shoe to drop. I've been sucker punched so many times by life at this point I feel punch drunk.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't know! Is there something about me that made him scared to tell me? Why do people feel the need to keep things from me? Maybe. I think I've said in the past to my sons 'I'm so glad you guys don't want to go into the military!'
appraisal_reasoning.control: No not at all. He's an adult and his choices are his own. It's not up to me to make those big calls for him anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes they went ok. I told him I was proud of him and I loved him.

situation: I applied to go on a leadership programme at work and got accepted. I wanted the chance to be able to apply for higher roles in my company, so getting accepted was a big deal for me. I felt emotional, happy, and surprised because there were a number of applicants. Not being rejected was really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Thursday. It mattered a great deal to me because I was really surprised, having had a number of rejections in the past for other roles. The reason why it matters is it gives me the opportunity to further my goals.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation helped me as it boosted my confidence and made me feel more valued at work.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The HR person who composed the email.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt like I was in control as I was calm and excited.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Waiting a long time for the email, I had self-doubts and was convinced that I was not successful, so then I had the nicest surprise.

situation: I'm a support worker, and one of the lads I support asked if I'd be his key worker because he trusts me. I wasn't trying to do anything at the time, and I didn't want or need anything from the situation. I felt really touched because this lad doesn't trust easily. It was important to me that he wanted me as his key worker over others who have worked there longer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a great deal because it meant I was doing my job well.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me realize just why I do the job I do, reinforcing my sense of purpose in my work.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible for it. It took hard work to build up the trust that resulted in him wanting me as his key worker.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected that he wanted me as his key worker as he hadn’t wanted anyone before.

situation: Earlier this week, my mother-in-law, who I'm very close with, had a stroke. I wanted to know about what kind of care someone needs after having a stroke. The situation made me feel useless and frustrated. Obviously, how my wife and her siblings are feeling and how they are going to cope is important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: On Monday, she had her stroke and it mattered because we are close and she has been my mother-in-law for 20 years. Obviously, how my wife and her siblings are feeling and how they are going to cope is important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Well, it has affected my wife more than me and I want to support her and I'm not sure how.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well, I'm not sure responsibility could be given to any one person in this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control over this event.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: She has been in hospital for 5 days and seems to be getting a little better than she was on the first day.

situation: I was trying to work when I saw the news about the missile strikes in the Iran war, especially those in Dubai. The images of the missile strikes in Iran, Lebanon, Dubai, and Cyprus were quite emotional for me. It was very upsetting, and I needed to stop what I was doing to take some time to settle down. Overall, it left me feeling bad. It was a very negative experience.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me. It was very upsetting as this is another unnecessary war. Additionally, I have colleagues living and working in Dubai, so it is personally upsetting.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as I now have to worry and fear for the safety of my peers.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Donald Trump and Israel are mainly responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt no control at all. The US and Israel are war mongers.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected given how stupid and dangerous the US and Israel leaders are.

situation: I was trying to cross the road when a car suddenly pulled out on me. The driver was going straight on a roundabout and then turned towards me without using her indicators. We ended up having a verbal exchange because I was really annoyed at her for not signaling. But, on the bright side, I didn't die.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday. It mattered to me because I was really annoyed at the driver for not signaling.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation neither helped nor hurt me; it just annoyed me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the driver was most responsible for all of this because she was not paying attention.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control because I was on my own.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because the driver turned into me without signaling.

situation: I was talking to a colleague about how emotional I felt about not seeing my 19-year-old daughter as much these days. She still lives at home, but she's so busy with her college work, two part-time jobs, and a packed social life with her friends and boyfriend. She's barely home! I was just venting to my colleague, who is in a similar situation, and it felt good to share. I surprised myself by just how emotional I felt about it all. It was really appreciated that my colleague found the time to actively listen to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It meant a lot that someone was listening to how I felt. This is because my husband does not quite understand how emotional I feel as I head towards an empty nest.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped to have someone to empathise with my feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There is no one really responsible for how I am feeling, least of all my daughter, who is happy and independent, and greatly enjoying this phase of her life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes and no. It did surprise me just how upset I became talking about it - I almost cried!
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The colleague was more understanding than I imagined. She is not someone I am usually particularly close to or share with.

situation: Yesterday, I stumbled upon a photo of my daughter on Facebook, showing her as a 3-year-old, taken 8 years ago. Seeing it made me emotional because I've lost a lot of time with her, and she's growing up so fast. She'll be 12 in just three months. I wasn't trying to do anything specific; I just felt a wave of nostalgia and longing for the younger version of my little girl. Realizing how much she's grown and knowing I can't get those years back hit me hard. I sent the photo to her as a text, but she didn't respond since she was at her friend's house. That added to my emotions, thinking about how she's growing up and doesn't rely on me as much anymore. I felt sadness and longing, just wanting to hold her in my arms and kiss her because she's my baby girl. I miss her a lot these days since she's often with friends or involved in after-school activities. This situation also triggers some family trauma for me, things too personal to discuss here, but there's been a lot of conflict in my family causing relational issues.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I'm nearing my period and that's when things tend to hit me harder. I've just been feeling emotional and moody, so seeing that just added to the overall feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me more than anything because I know I can't go back in time to a younger version of my daughter. I know she's almost a teenager again, and I worry about her and her future. The world is a scary place, and I worry that I'm not always going to be able to protect her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I would say nobody is really responsible for this. It's not really anyone's fault. It's just how I was feeling emotionally. Human emotions are normal and I can't really place the blame on myself or others for it. I have a hormonal imbalance from a thyroid condition, so that tends to magnify my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I never feel in control with my emotions. I always get stuck inside my mind and ruminate on things. It almost feels like OCD or something on the outside of myself controlling my thoughts.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, normally if I see a photo of my daughter younger it does illicit these kind of feelings for me. I'd say it's pretty normal. I ended up feeling better about 45 minutes after it.

situation: A few days ago, I was upset with my dad because I realized I truly will not ever connect with him emotionally. I was trying to have a conversation about why his Temu car jack stand might not be the safest, but he took it as an offense. The first thing he said was that I just don't understand 'how it works,' targeting my intelligence. He always does stuff like this. It left me feeling annoyed because he can't have a normal conversation without feeling threatened or saying something mean back, like doubting my intelligence. It feels like he doesn't respect me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday and it only mattered a small amount. It's just something that made me really annoyed, because he does things like this often where he says things where he obviously sees me as this stupid, little girl, when I'm 23.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because he sees me as a little girl that he raised and rather than an adult who's clearly been to college and lived her own life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My dad.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because he gets to control the narrative and decide the outcomes as he is my dad.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I mean somewhat. Like I thought it'd be a normal conversation but he just turned it into something mean.

situation: I was in a shop, trying to buy treats and dog food for my dog. I spent about 20 minutes there, and when I got to the counter to pay, I realized I couldn’t find my wallet. Someone had picked it up and walked out with it, and I lost all my money. The whole situation left me feeling frustrated, upset, and annoyed. I didn’t know what to do. To make things worse, the staff seemed not to be bothered about the situation. I needed help, but they didn't want to help me, which left me disappointed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday, which was Saturday. It mattered a whole lot to me because I couldn't get what my dog needed, and he had to go without.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me upset and angry. The situation didn’t help at all because I suffer from mental health problems. He’s not just my dog; he’s a part of my life and family. It hurt me because I couldn’t do anything about it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like I was responsible, which I am to a certain extent, but at the same time, I feel like the shop is responsible too for not helping me when I asked them for help.
appraisal_reasoning.control: In a way, I was in control to a certain extent, but when the shop wasn’t willing to help me, I felt helpless. So I left the store before I got more angry and upset. That’s when I knew I wasn’t in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It didn’t go to plan; it got worse. It was unfair for me to be treated like that. I won’t be shopping in that store again.

situation: My dog just passed away after we had to put her to sleep because a very large tumor was found on her liver. I'm grieving the loss of my dog, and I feel absolutely devastated. My heart is broken, and sometimes I go through times of pure panic at the thought of never seeing her again. She was my soul dog, and I will never get over her loss.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on a Friday and it mattered the most to me out of everything. I would give anything to have her back, but only if she was healthy. She was in our lives since she was 8 weeks old and helped us through multiple issues in life. She never failed us and gave us everything.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because she died. It's very simple. It helped that I was there with her when she was put to sleep because I was able to see that it was incredibly peaceful and there was no pain or suffering for her. I felt at peace with the decision that we made and that healed my heart a tiny bit.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Cancer was responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control in the sense that it was mine and my husband's decision how to move forward (i.e. do we put her down now etc.) but at the same time, I didn't really have much choice since I never would want her to suffer any longer than she already had.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The day did not go as expected as I was expecting to take her to the vets to get some medicine for an upset stomach and then got told my dog had a tumour and needed to be put down. But the actual putting her to sleep did go as expected. It was as peaceful as I hoped it would be.

situation: I was cycling on a small road where there's a 30 mph limit and plenty of space. Suddenly, a man in a fancy white Range Rover almost ran me over. I felt angry and slightly scared. I knew I was in the right and he was in the wrong, but it frustrated me that no justice would ever be served.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened this morning, a Sunday morning when not many people are around. It mattered a lot to me as I felt it was the reason many people are lazy and get in a car instead of cycling.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation only hurt me mentally, having negative effects on my mental health.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the driver and society generally were most responsible for all of this, due to being car-centric and car-focused.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt partially in control; I was in control of my 'vehicle', but if the car had clipped me then I'd have no control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The incident was never expected but played out as expected that the car driver didn't even realise they'd done wrong, being that the cyclist pass law is now 1.5 metres or more and they passed me more like 20-30 centimetres.

situation: I had some blood work done and was really worried about the results. I wanted the results to be quick and positive, but trying not to worry was very consuming. The doctor called with a plan, and things are much better than I was expecting. I was extremely relieved and felt that a huge weight had been lifted. Now, I have a plan of things to do in the next three months before I am retested.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This was within the last week, and it mattered to me a lot as I have some health issues.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It gave me reassurance of the actual situation instead of the things I was thinking in my head.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible for going to the doctors and they were responsible for letting me know what the results were.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not initially as I had no idea what the results were going to be, but now I feel there are some positive steps I can take.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected as I feared being put on medication straight away.

situation: I went to a car auction, and after spending a lot of time checking out the three cars I wanted, I lost all three during the bidding. I was trying to buy a car because I needed one for a trip next week. The cars were lovely and would have been great to drive, but now I'm stuck at square one again. I felt sad and deflated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it mattered a lot to me. My life a week on is much harder now because of it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it meant I had to borrow a car from my partner, and they don't like lending me the car as they are now without one.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible as my other car I had previously has died.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control; there was nothing I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I was expecting to get a car and now I still don't have one.

situation: Me and my girlfriend are in a closeted lesbian relationship, and we're facing religious and cultural barriers. We were having a serious discussion about eloping to a different country and getting married for legal purposes. We went back and forth on the idea and eventually decided that we would save up and move once I'm done with med school. It's a really big deal for me because I've never had any intentions of moving countries, so I was trying to navigate it all. I needed clarification and comfort throughout the conversation. The whole situation left me feeling rather torn. My partner's well-being and concerns are really important to me. I don't want us to feel the need to do all this because of family, but we're left with no choice.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me as it could potentially be the biggest decision I ever make. It's really risky, and the ball wouldn’t be in our court.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I know the woman I love is taking this relationship seriously. However, it hurt me because leaving pretty much everything in my life behind is weighing down on me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Families are most responsible for all of this; none of this would’ve been a problem had they not made it one.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Neither my girlfriend nor I have any control; we’re merely navigating through it with the little control we have, as where I’m from, the elders decide everything.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected; nothing was unexpected.

situation: I had a plan with my boyfriend that he cancelled at the last minute, and it deeply upset me because I was really looking forward to what we were going to do. I needed someone to support me that day since I had been going through a tough time the week before. Initially, I felt deeply hurt, but we ended up having a good conversation about it and what was going on in his life, which was a silver lining. It was important for me to understand where he was coming from and to accept that it wasn't because of me that he cancelled. He offered insight into his mind, and I appreciated the open communication.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot. Quality time means a lot to me, especially quality time with my partner. Cancelling felt like the world had ended for a moment.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt through the disappointment I experienced. It helped through gaining more knowledge about his life and his current situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like it was on my boyfriend. He left things build and start to weigh on him without letting me in to help him. The overwhelming emotions he experienced could have been avoided if he’d opened up sooner.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt lost in it originally, because my plans had been changed so last minute. But with the conversation we had I started to feel better. I was in control of the questions asked and knew how to approach him during.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things were unexpected, but not in a bad way. I learned a lot that I never knew, and that was welcome to me.

situation: I overheard a work colleague, whom I consider a friend, calling me a very offensive name. I was devastated to hear that this is what they say about me when I'm not around. I wanted my colleague to be genuine and honest, just like they are when I'm with them. The situation left me feeling sad, hurt, and above all, disappointed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was a surprise and a shock when it happened, and I have thought of little else since.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because the name I was called behind my back is a terrible name to call anyone. I have lost a person I thought a friend and am left wondering if everyone else thinks the same about me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My colleague who called me this name was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn’t in control. I overheard it when passing a door.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect to hear this at any time. It was entirely unexpected.

situation: I've been feeling really negative emotions lately because of this recent war with Iran. It's heartbreaking to see the number of innocent people who have lost their lives. What I really wanted was for people to come together and fix this problem before it escalated to such a tragic loss of life. It's left me deeply sad that it actually came to war. What's important to me is recognizing how this war is affecting everyone worldwide in a negative manner.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It all started about 10 days ago. This matters a great deal to me because since then many people have died meaninglessly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Besides hurting me mentally and emotionally, it is having a great impact on me and my loved ones economically.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I believe it's rich men in power trying to prove how powerful they are.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I feel like a boat without a sail because I had no control over what these rich powerful men were doing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as expected because this war has caused people on both sides to die. It is affecting economies around the world in a bad way and citizens are going to suffer.

situation: My first son moved out of the house and into his own place. I'm really excited for him because it's a great opportunity for growth. I'm feeling proud of him. I also need to make sure his mom and my other son are okay with the change and adapt well.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal since it is a massive life change for him and I want to make sure he feels supported.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt a bit just that I will not see him as much but at the same time it helped knowing that our guidance as parents is paying off with a capable child turned adult.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody is responsible, just a part of life and growth.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No too much, he is old enough to make this decision himself, but he did consistently look for guidance which felt good.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went very good and all of us, including him, are adapting well.

situation: I had a falling out with my son after he returned home two hours later than we agreed. I wanted him to realize that I wasn't asking him to be home by a certain time to annoy him but instead to keep him safe. It made me annoyed that he doesn't see that it's for his own good. I wanted to make it clear that he shouldn't do this again ever.
