appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me because all I want is my children to be safe and to do as I say to help them stay safe.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as I was called some terrible things by my son when all I want to do is help him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son and not taking his curfew seriously.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I started shouting at him and called him selfish.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: He has not been out again yet, so I don't know if he listened to me and learned or he will do his own thing again and ignore me.

situation: I adopted a rescue dog three months ago, having thoroughly researched the process, which indicated that significant milestones would occur at three days, three weeks, and three months. Just last week, her behavior shifted, and now it feels like she truly belongs with us and appears genuinely happy. I'm seeking closure for my rescue dog, hoping for signs that she's fully settled and less anxious. My emotions are mixed—mostly joyful, but there's a touch of sadness for what she endured. Every time I see her, I'm amazed by what a wonderful dog she is. The passing of my elderly dog last year adds to the emotional complexity of this situation. I'm not exactly guilty, but reflective.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: There was a time within the week that my rescue dog fell into my arms and I cuddled her and she leaned into that cuddle and looked like she was smiling. She seemed so happy and that mattered a lot to me. It felt like at last she was home.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This experience helped me because not only are we helping out a dog who needed a new forever family but she is helping us to heal the pain of our grief.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both of us, I think.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, to some degree, as I nurtured her the best I could but she was also in control of her nervousness.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It's hard to expect perfection when you're dealing with an animal but things went as well as could be expected. We got there in the end.

situation: My dad has prostate cancer and recently had his yearly blood test. The results came back, and unfortunately, his condition had worsened. He was supposed to receive a phone call from his doctor on a specific day to discuss the results, but the call never came. I was really worried about what would happen next and was hoping for some clarity and communication from the doctor regarding my dad's condition. The situation left me feeling annoyed and still worrying, which could have been avoided if the doctor had called as planned. Since it's cancer, time is always crucial. The quicker they act, the better the chances of it being able to be helped.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened this past Tuesday, it mattered very much to me and my Dad as he had spent the whole afternoon waiting in for the phone call and we were expecting to find out if he would have to have more treatment and if so what.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt that they hadn't even bothered to let him know that they wouldn't be keeping the appointment.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am not sure it might have been the Doctor or his office.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I didn't feel like we were in control at all as we then had to leave a message on an answer machine at the hospital and wait for someone to return the call.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Finally someone phoned back and apologised and said it should never have happened but that the Dr was away for nearly the whole month so my Dad has to wait until the end of the month now before he goes for an appointment at the hospital.

situation: I was at a family get-together and had a great time. I love spending time with my family, and this gathering left me feeling very happy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was on Friday at my mum's house. About 15 members of my family got together for food and drinks.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was a fun and happy time. Plenty of laughs and giggles.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My mum organised it all.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I did feel in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went great.

situation: My sister and I got into a tiff about something small. We were just talking about a tense subject and both got a little defensive. It left me feeling a little frustrated and upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event didn't matter; how it affected my sister and I was what mattered.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Neither really. It was upsetting at the time but we were able to move past it quickly.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both of us equally--we just got frustrated and weren't communicating effectively.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Control isn't a word I would use when talking to someone. We were on the same level.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well..I didn't expect the conversation to go one way or another.

situation: My best friend is going through a separation and possible divorce, and I'm really worried about the impact it will have on my godson, who is very important to me. I was trying to figure out how to support my best friend during this tough time. The whole situation left me feeling upset and worried about both my best friend and his son, who is my godchild. I'm concerned about how best to help them and how to come to terms with my own worry.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened within the last two weeks. I have love for both my best friend and his son, who is very important to me, especially his wellbeing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I'm upset and worried about the impact it will have on them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There is no one to blame; it's just part of life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I'm not in control. I can only react to the situation and support my friend and godson the best I can.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things are still confusing and no resolution.

situation: I had an argument with my wife because I needed some help with something, and she didn’t want to help. The situation left me feeling angry.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on a day when I was working from home and had no time as it was. She had more time availability than I did.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt like I had to do everything.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: A lack of communication and expectations on both sides.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. Because I could not express myself properly.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: As expected. We had an argument and had to do it anyway.

situation: Just this week, my father was rushed to the hospital because he had numbness in his leg. They later determined he had a series of minor strokes, which caused this numbness. He can move his leg, but he isn't very stable. He's getting old, so these things can happen at his age. It's very sad to see him and my mom struggle with this. I really would like my father to regain his mobility; that would be ideal. It left me feeling sad for both him and my mother. I guess I hope that something like this wouldn't happen to either of them. It's important that he keeps his spirits up even though his mobility is restricted at this point.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened a few days ago and my parents' well-being is extremely important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation made me very concerned for their well-being not only now but in their immediate future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He recently had a surgery and the surgery itself could have led to this stroke.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control of the situation. I was only informed of what was happening.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I really didn't have any expectations.

situation: I've been finding it really hard to get to sleep and stay asleep at night, and it's really getting me down. I was trying to get some sleep but without success. I just wanted the ability to go to sleep rather than stay awake at night. As you might expect, I felt tired and exhausted after getting little to no sleep. Getting more sleep was really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It has been happening during the last 7 days. It matters to me as getting no sleep means I am tired when I get up the next day and it is not healthy being unable to sleep.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I got no sleep so that hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't know - perhaps you can tell me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because I could not sleep.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well I expected to get some sleep and I did not get much.

situation: My daughter had a medical procedure, and I was very nervous and worried. I was trying to stay calm and relaxed to be supportive for her, but the whole situation left me feeling exhausted.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened three days ago. It mattered a lot to me because it was an important medical procedure.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me to see her in pain. It made me sad that I could not help her at the moment.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I did not feel like it was anyone’s fault. It was just something she was born with it had to be completed.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was controlling my emotions, but not in control of the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they always expect that everything turned out well.

situation: I finished reading a book that made me really emotional. It was a tragic love story, and by the end, the two main characters couldn’t be together. I didn't really want or need anything other than entertainment; I just wanted to read a good story. Even though I felt sad at the end because the characters couldn’t be together, the emotions were more bittersweet. It was a very good story, extremely well written and enjoyable.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It didn’t matter too much. After all, it was just a book, nothing that affected me personally.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I don’t know that it either helped or hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The book was definitely responsible, although I suppose if you wanted to, you could say that the author was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: In a sense, I was in control. After all, I could have stopped reading at any point in time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things did go as expected. I frequently cry while reading sad books, so I was fully prepared to have an emotional reaction to the ending.

situation: I got into an argument with my partner, and it was so intense that we almost broke up. In that moment, all I wanted was comfort and reassurance, but instead, he said he didn't care about me anymore. That left me feeling awful and empty.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Monday night and it mattered to me because it made me feel like I wasn't as good enough for him as his ex-girlfriend was.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because they were further along in their relationship in a year, and we have been together for a year now and aren't in the same place they were in as a couple.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My partner was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel like I was in control because he was telling me I was in the wrong over and over.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. I expected him to understand me, but he didn't.

situation: A good neighbor of ours had their very special dog hit by a car last week. It was very upsetting and sad. They did surgery, but unfortunately, the dog passed away. I spoke to the owners a few times, offering to help in any way I could and providing comfort and someone to talk to. I'm feeling mostly sad about the whole situation. I feel so bad for them. I'll miss their dog too, as he was a friend and constantly around.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered quite a bit to me because I felt our neighbor's pain, which made me feel bad. It also mattered because I will really miss the dog as well.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as the dog was a constant presence in the neighborhood and like a friend, so his absence will leave a hole.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one really was responsible. The dog got out, went exploring, ended up on a busy road, and ran out. I don't think the driver had time to stop.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control as it was not my dog and I had no control over him getting out.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I guess things went as expected. The dog was taken to the vet, they tried to save him with surgery, but it was too late.

situation: I had a tough conversation with my boyfriend about our long-distance relationship. He doesn't think he can continue doing long distance, so we were trying to see if we should break up. I wanted to see if breaking up was the right decision because he doesn't think he can keep going with the distance. This whole situation made me feel really sad since he means the world to me. I just don't want us to break up.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened after I visited on Valentine's Day right before I flew back to Chicago. It mattered a lot to me since this relationship means a lot to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me by making me anxious about our relationship.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel angry at him for not wanting to do long distance.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I was not in control since it was hard to communicate and understand each other's views.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I just wish that we were able to reach a good resolution.

situation: My football team lost a 2 goal lead and ended up drawing with our biggest rivals. I really needed my team to score again. The whole situation left me feeling angry and frustrated. Winning was the only thing that mattered to me in that moment.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Sunday. It mattered because my team could go above the rival team in the league, and this was important to me as I strongly dislike the rival team.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as it caused me stress and anger.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The players of my team were terrible in the 2nd half, and I felt they were most responsible for the outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of the situation as I wasn't playing or managing the game.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things didn't go as expected. The team were 2-0 up at halftime, and I didn't expect the rival team to come back.

situation: My cousin and I got into a fistfight at the family reunion. He was drunk and treating his wife badly, and several people asked him to chill, but he didn't listen. So I had to take it to the next level because I needed him to stop cussing her or leave. It left me feeling bad, but it was something that had to be done. I have really bad anxiety, and I didn't need all the drama at a family reunion. Everyone knew it had to be done.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened about ten days ago. It mattered a lot to me because he was an embarrassment to me and my family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Besides the broken hand, it didn't hurt me and definitely didn't help.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He was of course.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control or I wouldn't have stopped hitting him.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, he left and his wife stayed. He came back a few hours later and apologized to everyone.

situation: My husband and I have been trying to get pregnant for a little over six months now, but we haven't gotten lucky yet. This past month, I started using ovulation testing kits to track my fertility, hoping it would help us in this process. I found out that I was mistaken about when my peak fertility window was within my cycle. I was so excited and feeling really hopeful about getting pregnant now that we knew when my fertility was. However, this past week, I got my period, and it was emotionally difficult for me. I felt a wave of sadness and disappointment wash over me, leaving me feeling a bit defeated. My husband was incredibly supportive and comforting, offering me his love and understanding during this challenging time. His kindness and empathy helped me cope with the emotions I was experiencing, and I felt grateful to have him by my side.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because we had already been trying for so long and I thought the effort we took to track my fertility would pay off.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It will help me in the long run to get pregnant, just because tracking my fertility didn’t work the first month we started doing it, doesn’t mean it won’t help us in the future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don’t think anyone was really responsible or to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all and it’s a bit frustrating to be so helpless.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected to get pregnant and finding out that I was not was the unexpected.

situation: Our central heating system developed a fault, even though it had only been installed six months ago. It was still under warranty, but the thought of having to contact the engineer, get them to acknowledge the issue, and arrange for a call out was causing me stress. The fact that something went wrong so soon after installation made me feel annoyed and slightly angry. I was also feeling fed up and depressed about having to sort this out. Emotionally, I felt exhausted and just didn't want to deal with it all again. There was also a worry that the engineer who fitted the system might not be in business anymore. Things change so much these days, and there's no guarantee he's still doing the same job.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The realisation that the heating system was not working properly gave me a hollow feeling in the pit of my stomach. How could this be, it's a new system? There was also the additional emotions and annoyance shared by my wife, who also had to deal with the situation. She has health issues that require a good basic level of heating, so that added more stress to the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me in the sense that I could not sort it out myself, which I normally try to do. That realisation that you need someone else to come and fix it does not sit well with me. I'm very independent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was no one's fault; everything was fitted correctly to start with, but it was a mechanical failure. I suppose the biggest problem was the object itself. It was a good brand, well fitted, and it still failed, which of course can happen to anything, but it still doesn't make it any easier.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Initially, I didn't feel in control. Once I had established contact with the engineer and the date of repair was fixed, I started to feel a bit better.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go to plan. The engineer called on the right day at the agreed time and replaced the faulty part. He didn't charge me for the part, as it was under warranty. He didn't even charge me a call-out fee or labour. That was a bonus which made me feel much better.

situation: I recently had a close work colleague fall out at work. She was ignoring me and being rude around me, which was really upsetting. I was trying to solidify our relationship more and be closer both in a work and personal sense. I made an effort to repair the relationship, and this week she has been friendly and receptive, making work much easier. I went through all sorts of emotions—first upset, then anger, and finally joy and relief when things were patched up. I believe I did the right things in trying to repair it, and it played out well, so I'm feeling good about things now.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot as I spend so much time at work and this person is within my small team and someone I felt closest to.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: At first it hurt as I didn't understand why it was happening and felt like it was personal and professionally could become very harmful. Over time and with a zoomed out perspective, I realized this person is very sensitive, so I should handle it with more caution and be patient, which worked.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Partially me and partially my teammate misunderstanding each other and two strong personalities colliding.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt out of control for the whole bad part of this situation but better now.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected it to repair quickly but didn't, then now it has been repaired it feels sudden.

situation: My husband flew to Montana to work for an entire month, and it's really putting a strain on our marriage, our finances, and child-rearing. I wanted him to be at home, working his normal job and helping with everyday tasks. I'm feeling stressed because he's missing out on important time with the kids.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last Monday. It mattered a lot. I do not feel safe or secure with him gone. A month is a very long time to be apart.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me emotionally and mentally. I also do not feel safe or secure with him gone.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My husband is responsible for all of it because he did not have to go. He volunteered.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had zero control. I told him he needed to do what was best for his career, but he also needs to consider his family. He preaches to his employees 'family first' but he does not make decisions for himself with this mindset.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went exactly as expected. He hopped on a plane and won't be home for 3 more weeks.

situation: Recently at work, a random girl about 14 years old entered the shop crying and bleeding. She told us she needed help because her friends had left her in a bad situation. A man, potentially someone she knew, had jumped her and attacked her. She was scared, and we ended up helping her by calling the police and security to assist us. This was very scary, but we helped her and protected her until the police arrived and dealt with the situation. We needed stronger and legal help, so calling the police was the best option for her safety and ours. We kept her in a safe place, called her parents, and gave her medical attention and water. The whole experience left me feeling scared and worried. I was generally concerned about the safety of other young women and the fact that situations like this could turn aggressive and unsafe. It was important to me to help her out and learn about women's safety in my area, and think about what we could do to make it safer so that situations like this are limited and few.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened on the 21st of February 2026 at about 3pm, so very recently. It mattered to me because it was a busy Saturday in a busy shopping mall in broad daylight. The fact that that could happen was scary.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me learn to be more sympathetic and serious about the situation. It generally hurts me to think that it could happen to such a young girl.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the general issue could have been the man, whether they had a bad relationship or he just didn't like her, is scary. The thought he also didn't think it was too bad, and he had the right. This is something that men can't do or think is right.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. I had no control as I didn't personally know them. However, I felt empowered in protecting her and helping her get the help she needed. I also have no control over what others think or what their actions are towards the minorities or women, and this scares me for the future.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think the response time and, in general, our helping the girl out of the situation went as expected. The man didn't come to keep abusing her or asking about her, and after the police turned up, the responsibility and investigation were in their hands. This was expected as a member of the public like myself wouldn't want to hold that responsibility.

situation: The situation that made me emotional was when my partner brought someone home with him. They stayed in the bedroom together, and they were naked in bed. This happened out of nowhere, with no communication, and it made me very emotional and still hurts a lot. I'm not sure what's going on anymore or what to do. I wasn't trying to do anything; I didn't know what to do. I kind of froze and shut down and have been mostly numb to the whole experience. I wanted and needed transparency and communication, respect, and answers. I feel hurt, confused, at a loss, and devastated. My partner and I live together, and this also raises a lot of housing insecurities for me, which is very stressful too because I have nowhere to go, especially so abruptly. We also have two cats together.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When the event happened, it mattered a lot to me because this is my relationship and we've been together for 7 years, and I love my partner. This wasn't established as an okay thing to do or discussed as something that's a part of our relationship. This is also our home that we share. I am heartbroken and feel very low and down.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hasn't helped me at all; I can't imagine how it would be helpful in any way. It has hurt me a lot and I've already explained how.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well obviously my partner is responsible for their own actions just like any other person. So I feel they are.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt quite the opposite. Like they controlled everything, even me and my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole situation was unexpected, so it made the whole thing very bizarre to me and our friends who were around for it.

situation: My nephew was born, and I didn't need anything in particular; I just wanted everything to be safe. I felt excited and pleased for my brother. As I was thinking about the whole experience, I started imagining how I can't wait to have my own kids someday.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event really mattered to me because it was my family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me realize I want my own kids.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible really; it was just life happening.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really because I couldn't control them having a bat.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected.

situation: My friend's place of work burned down, and all I could do was try to support her through this difficult time. It left me feeling very sad and lacking control, wishing I could do more to help her. What was important to me was being available as a place of support.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It meant a lot to me. I witnessed it happen in real time, and it was very difficult watching the destruction of the building as many businesses were in it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it was sad to see so much damage, and see my friend's life upended.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was truly responsible, it was an accidental fire caused from a vape shop.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control as it was a very uncontrollable event. All I could be in control of was my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected as the amount of damage was beyond what anyone expected to happen.

situation: I visited my nan for the first time in over 2 months and gave her her Christmas present, which she really loved. I was unsure about it, but I think it's the best thing I've ever gotten her, which makes me so happy. I wasn't trying to do anything other than visit my nan—I didn't need anything from her. I've been a lousy grandchild recently and haven't seen her nearly enough. It left me feeling really happy afterwards. I'm so glad she likes her present so much. Just catching up with her and making sure she knows how much I love her was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The visit mattered a lot to me because she's my last living grandparent and I love her dearly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped me to see that I am valuable to her and I should be present more often.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that I was responsible for taking the initiative to go and see her after so long, and she was responsible for being so gracious and not holding it against me that I'm not there all the time.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Me and my nan were equally in control. It was a relaxed and loving visit, and either of us was free to do whatever we wanted.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting her to like her present so much.

situation: A week ago, my uncle had back surgery, and it was a little bit crazy. We thought he was going to have a stroke after the surgery, which made the situation stressful. I wanted my uncle to be okay. There was not a lot we could do, but thankfully the doctors were able to control the situation. I was feeling so bad and scared.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Last week, it really mattered to me because he is my favorite uncle.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It really hurt me to see him like that but I also remembered that it is important to let things in the hands of God.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I guess there is no responsible person.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I didn’t have any control of the situation because it was a medical situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything is fine now.

situation: My therapist stopped working with me because of safety issues, and it was really frustrating. I was in trauma therapy, and we were using hypnosis to try and change the pain from my trauma. But then I hurt myself because of the trauma, and that led to the therapist stopping the sessions. It left me feeling very annoyed and anxious. It feels like no one wants to help me, and I really relied on those sessions. Now, I need to find a different outlet.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week and it matters because I am in recovery for substance abuse and it nearly made me relapse.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I was doing so well and because we were doing work around my childhood and I was emotional and I was crying and I was too emotionally hurt that I hurt myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself and my therapist because I gained trust with her and I don't trust anyone, so I can see why she can't see me anymore but I will go to the group she leads for now.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control and that's the problem as I know that when I lose control I don't react well.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it didn't go as expected but it put me back a bit.

situation: I just had a dog pass away from cancer, and it's been very hard for me. I'm feeling tired, but I really want to give another dog a good life. So, I went and got another dog.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: She was a part of the family... Just like losing a brother or the like.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Just that all of this is hard to go through right after she died.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: A Seresto collar for flea and ticks is what I think that killed her... If I could take them to court I would and take all their money and give it to the poor.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Is that people don't care about the harm that they do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Death goes as expected it hurts and is painful.

situation: I work in healthcare, and recently I helped support a family when their loved one was dying. The family was understandably distressed, and even though I witness situations like this fairly regularly, it's never easy for me. I was trying to support the family as best I could, but I felt like I needed support myself and was unable to seek it. After the family had left, I was left feeling sad and found it difficult to carry on with my work. I feel that I would have been able to deal with it better if I had time to reflect before I had to restart my work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the middle of my shift. It mattered a lot to me because you only get one chance to get things right when someone is dying, and I wanted to be as supportive to the family as possible. During this time, it was difficult to think of the other patients as the family needed me more.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me professionally as other members of staff saw how vulnerable I am. It also reminded me of a difficult time when I supported a family member who was dying.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am responsible because I was the only person involved in supporting the family during this difficult time.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was unable to control my own emotions during the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as expected.

situation: I was trying to move my favorite chair back to my desk when it suddenly broke—the back snapped. I felt sad, depressed, and disappointed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it was my favorite chair.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by taking away a precious object.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that bad luck was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control; it felt out of my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. I didn't expect the chair to break.

situation: My son had the winning hit in his baseball game last weekend. I was trying to enjoy the moment, and I felt proud. It was important to me that he performed well under pressure.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last weekend and it mattered a great deal to me because I am competitive and want to see him succeed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by validating the hard work he and I put in.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control. He had to perform.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected him to break through.

situation: I've been really upset about breaking up with my boyfriend, and last night I ended up getting too drunk while I was feeling sad about it with my friends. I guess I just wanted to talk to someone about how I was feeling. Now, I'm left feeling embarrassed because I know I shouldn't have been drinking like that. It's important for me to apologize for my behavior.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last night. I don’t want to lose friends over it. I’m already lonely.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me by potentially saying mean or rude things that I don’t remember.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because I was drinking. I should have had food.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No. I just wanted a fun evening with friends.

situation: This week was World Book Day, and I didn't receive the communication from the school in time, so I was too late to get my son a costume. All the children at his school were able to wear a costume on Thursday, but because I didn't know about it, my son didn't have one. I tried to find one of my eldest son's older costumes but had no luck. I really wanted to ensure my son could participate and feel included in the event. I hoped to find a way for him to be part of it and not feel left out. The whole situation left me feeling bad and guilty because I just didn't want him to feel left out.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Wednesday when I found out that the next day he needed a costume and it matters to me because I want my son to be happy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I felt bad and guilty that day while he was at school but then after school I realised that he was actually okay and that it didn't matter that much to him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well the school states that they sent an email however I could not find any email about this I put the blame on me though because it's certainly not my son's fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control as I was not organised and I realised I need to check up on important school dates more.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did in the end go as expected and everything worked out okay.

situation: I felt sad that I, as a father, did not do enough to prepare my daughter for some tests last week. I did some revision with her, but last week she moaned a lot that she did not do enough, and so I felt bad and sad that I did not support her enough. I was trying to support my daughter with her test preparation and wanted to ensure she felt confident and prepared. I felt upset and like a failure as a parent. It was not a real nice feeling. While I was feeling this way, I never shared my negative emotions with my daughter because I did not want her to know or carry this on her shoulders.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The actual test and upset feeling happened last week. It mattered loads to me as this is my daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me on the inside as I felt upset and down about myself and my ability as a parent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I took on this responsibility so I felt upset and bad that she did not feel prepared and I felt a failure because of it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all, felt like a passenger.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was hoping I had done enough and she was prepared, but over the course of 3 days with multiple exams, I knew I had not done enough. So I felt bad.

situation: Last week, I had a disagreement with a friend about a small issue. At first, it made me feel upset and stressed, but later we talked and understood each other better. I really wanted to solve the problem and understand each other. In the end, the situation improved and we felt okay again. I felt better and more relieved after we talked and understood each other.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was quite important to me because our friendship matters. I didn't want the conflict to damage our relationship.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: At first made me feel stressed, but in the end it helped us understand each other better.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think it happened because of a misunderstanding between us.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, a little, because I could talk with my friend and try to fix the problem.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes.

situation: I almost got fired last week, and it was a really tough situation. I wanted to keep my job because I have to pay a $500 fine, and losing my job would make things even harder. The whole situation left me feeling anxious, worried, and uncertain about what was going to happen next.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week, and it mattered a lot to me because I live paycheck to paycheck to pay my bills.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me financially and left me emotionally upset.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was responsible along with my bosses.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was not in control because my bosses took control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went well and I got to keep my job.

situation: My daughter was having a bad time at school, and I received a call from the school saying she isn't happy. I really wanted to help her when she came home. The whole situation left me feeling upset. It was important to me to understand what her problems were.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it is not nice to know she is having a hard time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I didn't know she was suffering that much. I tried to be more understanding and nice when she came home.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The divorce and her dad not calling her were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control because there is not much I can do about it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because she has been in a bad mood since it happened.

situation: I am trying to sell my house, and we had a cash offer last Friday. But then, two days later, the buyer dropped out of the sale. This was a really negative emotion for me and very stressful. I wanted to sell my house, but it didn't happen, and now we are back to square one. I'm feeling very sad and very negative about the whole situation. It's important for us to move to be closer to family, so it needs to happen.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it was extremely stressful. It really, really matters to me and my family because we are trying to move closer to family as a family member is gravely ill and we need to be close by.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt us because we are trying to move closer to family due to a family member being gravely ill, and we need to be close by.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The buyer backed out of the sale.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control as the decision to back out was made by another person.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Of course, things did not go as expected as she backed out of the deal.

situation: I went out to eat to celebrate my brother's birthday. I was trying to make him as happy as possible while also celebrating the occasion with my entire family. I bought a gift for my brother and he seemed to really enjoy it. It left me feeling satisfied because I knew that my brother had a great time and it meant a lot to him. It was important to know that I could create memories from the situation with my family.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I knew that I was making someone else happy by celebrating a big occasion for them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me financially because I had to spend my hard-earned money on a gift for them. However, it helped me feel like a better person for knowing I did the right thing.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible for this because I was the one that chose to go to his birthday and buy him a gift.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was that in control because I felt pressured to go to his birthday party and to buy him a gift as well.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected because we were able to create plenty of memories together.

situation: I experienced a bad case of Delhi belly while I was in India, and it was pretty scary, making me feel vulnerable. I just wanted to feel better, get proper medicine, and prepare for my flight back to the UK. The whole situation left me feeling vulnerable and negative. To make things worse, the hotel staff weren't sympathetic at all and didn't offer any help. They even overcharged me, which made it impossible for me to trust them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because I was scared and worried for my health due to being dangerously dehydrated.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me very unwell, cold, and weak.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that the restaurant where I ate recently was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all. I felt alone in a foreign country.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I expected to get well before the flight, but the illness lasted at least a week.

situation: I saw some photos of my children when they were younger—babies—and it made me feel sad that I won't get that time again. Back then, my amazing father was ill and later passed away, so I didn't appreciate those moments properly. I wanted to go back in time and feel like I did before everything became sad. Seeing those photos left me feeling sad for the loss of my father and guilty for not valuing the time with him and my children when they were younger. I didn't know what was going to happen, but it still doesn't stop me from feeling guilty and annoyed with myself for not immersing myself more in memory making. It's a lesson that I need to live more in the moment and take time to appreciate all of the good things I have going on, even though I know deep down I will never feel the same way again and will always have a deep sadness for my father.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters greatly to me. My family are the most important thing to me in the world.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because the sense of loss is overwhelming but helped me see that the future is made up of 'nows' and so is the past or at least it was when the past was the present.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The loss of my father and me not being able to handle it. I am still in a state of shock and it was 6 years ago. My children are getting to an age where they don't need me as much and that hurts too.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No not really, because it brought a lot of emotions out and I don't always deal well with my feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes it was unexpected, I had expected to see the photos that triggered the memories.

situation: My estranged father and sister have been reaching out to me, wanting to know about my tax return and refund. My father has implied that I'm broke and even suggested buying me a deep freeze and filling it with food, which just feels off to me. My sister, on the other hand, refused to invite me to her baby shower because I wouldn't share my financial information. I was really trying to keep my life private and protect myself from them. Both of them have a habit of trying to destroy my life and gossip about me heavily, and I wanted to prevent all of that. I felt a little angry about the whole situation. I should have been at the baby shower, and I think it was ridiculous on her part to exclude me. I'm also angry about the deep freeze thing, as my father has called me twice about that.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The privacy about my finances mattered to me a great deal. I don't trust them at all. The baby shower mattered a little. I mean, in a normal situation I would have been there and it is sad that this is not normal.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think it hurt my feelings a bit. I feel like I am under attack. It helped me because I could see what was going on and protect myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think both of them are responsible. They want to destroy my life in order to build theirs up.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt mostly in control because I knew what was going on and didn't fall for the head games.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I think so. I had a feeling that I would not be invited to the shower. She called me last year and point blank asked me how much I make and where I work and I didn't tell her. Then she gossiped about it and I found out so I knew she was upset that I didn't tell her. She made it sound like I was freezing her out of my life because of it.

situation: I was in a situation where I wanted to comfortably express my own opinions without being ignored or treated like I'm dumb. Quite frankly, this left me feeling frustrated and irritated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened several evenings ago. It mattered a lot, because I didn't intend to go into this discussion to begin with. I know this person's attitude on certain things and I really didn't want to be barraged with their thoughts, because mine are different. I just wasn't up for hearing it. Not that I feel like I know everything it is just that sometimes you are not up to the debate.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I don't like having my opinions and feelings dismissed. I am intelligent and entitled to my own thoughts and feelings just like the other person is. I don't believe it is good to make someone feel bad for how they think and feel.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well, I guess I could say that I don't have to let the other person's attitude affect me, but I am only human and am affected by others. So I would say the other person was more at fault, because they couldn't respect my thoughts and feelings or the fact that I didn't want to get into a huge debate only to not be listened to anyway.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because the other person didn't really want to hear what I was saying.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Pretty much, because this person is not very yielding once they feel they know the 'right' answer they don't really want to hear much else.

situation: I had an interview for a job and made it to the final round where they offered me the position. However, the salary they proposed didn't meet my expectations. I wanted a higher salary that could meet my family's expectations. I tried to make a final call about it, but the CEO was so oppressive that I couldn't. This left me feeling like I wasn't properly evaluated by them. I was really confused about whether to agree or not because, on one hand, it was an opportunity to learn something new.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters a lot because it could change my life whether positive or negative.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It can help me to grow a better career or gave me nothing.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel the company didn't properly realize my situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not because I wanted something but they deny.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I didn't get a good promise so refuse.

situation: My daughter and husband weren't speaking to each other after getting into a small fuss, and they went a couple of weeks without talking. Living in the same house made it so awkward. I just wanted them to start acting like adults. I felt caught in the middle and wanted to be the peacemaker. I think their personalities are so much alike that they butt heads a lot. Thankfully, it has resolved itself now.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal to me because I hate it when any of my family are fussing with each other. It makes me sad. Life is too short for that.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I already suffer with severe depression and anxiety, then to have to deal with this was just too much.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was my daughter, she says stuff she shouldn't, and when she said it, my husband didn't respond; he just got up and left the room.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, definitely not. Had I said anything, they would've assumed I was taking sides, and one of them would've been mad at me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went as I expected. I knew they were going to be upset with each other.

situation: My wife found out that a coworker she liked and found fun was killed over the weekend. Seeing her so upset made me sad as well. Primarily, I wanted to console her. There wasn't much I could do but hug her, but I think that helped. She expressed frustration that she takes on the pain of others too much, thinking of her husband and other coworkers who are also suffering. I tried to explain that that is fairly normal, but I understand where she's coming from.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday. It mattered to me because I don't like having my wife feel grief on top of other struggles she goes through.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt bad because of the situation itself as well as seeing my wife in pain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The person who hit them while driving was most responsible. It's suspected she was not paying attention to the road when she hit them with her truck.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control on the outcome, but I had some control in trying to ease my wife's pain by being there for her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Pretty much. There's not much you can do but express your grief and recover as best you can.

situation: I was attending a singing workshop with about 40 other people. I was there to enjoy the experience of singing with others. I felt a sense of camaraderie with my fellow singers. The songs we learned were great.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was last Saturday. It mattered to me as it was something I could do with my friends to a common end.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I can't really think of a way in which it helped or hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The leader who actually led the session and those that organised it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I just did what I was told.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was pretty much as I expected the pace of learning the songs was slightly faster than other workshops I have been to.

situation: My daughter called me from university, sounding stressed and worried about her academic work. I was trying to reassure her and calm her down, hoping to help her see her concerns from a different perspective and a wider view so they wouldn't seem so overwhelming. I wanted to feel that I had given her effective emotional support. I experienced a small amount of stress myself and some frustration because she regularly becomes stressed in a similar way and about similar things. I also felt empathy and recognition, as I can remember being her age and having such similarly strong emotions. It was important to me to show that I'm still a good parent, even though she's left home to go to university, and for her to end the call feeling more positive.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Thursday evening. It mattered to me because she is the most important person in my life and I am one of her main sources of support.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't either help or hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My daughter is most responsible for leaving her work until, what to me feels like the last minute, and placing too much pressure on herself to perform excellently academically all the time.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I was in control of the conversation to a certain extent because I was more neutral and detached than her, but she was ultimately in control of how the situation is resolved.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went pretty much as expected in that she thanked me for my reassurance and seemed calmer and more logical and had a plan by the end of the call.

situation: I recently decided to invest a large amount of my savings to take advantage of this year's ISA allowance. I did this just before the Iran War started, and my investments dropped by a large amount. I was investing my savings in the hope that they would increase in value. This situation left me feeling upset and unlucky because I timed my investment very poorly. I guess there are many worse things that can happen.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered because I am retired, and I was hoping the investment could boost my savings. Instead, it has had the opposite effect.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it means I have less money and may affect my future plans such as moving house.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No-one really was responsible; I was just unlucky with the timing of my investment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control in that it was my decision to invest, but I now feel powerless to influence things.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was not expecting there to be such a large conflict that could have such global implications to the stock market.

situation: We had space taken from us at work and were forced to move, so we completed the move this past Friday. We needed to move books, shelves, and supplies for shipping, which was physically taxing and made us sweaty throughout the day. I was tired during the move and had to take several breaks, but I was satisfied with our progress and accomplishing it all in the matter of a day.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It didn't matter much. It was simply a task that had to be completed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt in that I had to delay getting other work done.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: People at the top of the organization were responsible. They chose the space to move others to.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, pretty well in control. I could move myself instead of waiting for someone to be assigned the task and moving our things for us.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected.

situation: I was at the grocery store yesterday morning, trying to figure out the math in my head of how much I could put on my EBT card and how much cash I had. I was feeling flustered and a bit overwhelmed. Then, out of nowhere, this lady bought me a loaf of bread, and it made me cry. It was such a simple act, but it meant a lot to me. I felt a mix of emotions—scared, proud, nervous, and even a bit stupid. But now, looking back, I feel proud. The kindness of a stranger really touched me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday morning. It mattered a lot to me because I was homeless for a really long time, tried getting help, and finally pulled myself up by my bootstraps to get into housing. This was the first nice thing someone had done for me since getting into housing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I'm eating.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: A chance meeting was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control but didn't realize I was in control at that moment. Now I realize yes, I was in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as planned; it went much better than I initially thought it was going to.

situation: Last Friday, my neighbor came to my door, banging frantically. I opened up to find her in a panic because her husband had fallen in the car park after having his photograph taken with the car they were selling. He tripped on the gravel, hit his head, and was losing a lot of blood. We called an ambulance and got some blankets to keep him warm. My neighbor had a wet and dry cloth to place on his head and face where he was bleeding. He was in quite a state by the time the ambulance arrived, which took about 40 minutes. When it finally came, they put him on a stretcher and took him to the hospital, where he still is now. We needed to stay calm for our neighbor's sake, as she was really on edge waiting for the ambulance. I gave him a cushion to sit on instead of the cold ground, wrapped him in blankets, and tried to reassure him that everything was going to be okay. Watching him on the floor so helpless and his wife panicking about the late ambulance made me feel a bit sick to my stomach. It was important to keep reassuring him that all was going to be fine and try to keep her under control.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Friday afternoon gone, and it mattered a lot because our neighbor was in a frantic situation and had no one else to turn to, just us as her closest neighbors.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was just the thought of this happening while we were out; I can’t imagine what would have happened if the neighbor had to cope on her own, as she is already a bag of nerves.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Probably the neighbors, if he hadn’t come downstairs to get the picture taken, none of this would have happened.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, me and my wife were in control of the situation. The neighbor was so panic-stricken, we had to take control of the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as expected, only we were not expecting the ambulance to take as long as it did.

situation: I had a plumbing issue that needed fixing, so I needed a plumber. My wife wanted to call an emergency plumber, but I said I couldn't afford it and suggested we wait until the next day. This sparked our usual argument over money, which always annoys me. I needed my wife to give me more support, both emotionally and financially. The situation left me feeling angry and frustrated because she never addresses the issue. It's important to me that my wife takes more responsibility for the household finances.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last night and it is still very raw. It matters to me because I can't keep shouldering the financial struggles myself.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it is a constant struggle to make ends meet while my wife just spends and spends.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel my wife and her mother are most responsible for all of this because they don't live in the real world.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because my wife won't discuss the matter. She just shouts and cries, but nothing gets resolved.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, but not as I hoped. Nothing gets resolved and I end up sorting out the mess.

situation: Scenario: My beloved grandparents began discussing their funeral plans, expressing their wishes for when they eventually leave this world. They wanted to ensure everything was arranged, including a deposit for a crematorium and detailed plans for their final farewell. This conversation was incredibly difficult for me; it filled my heart with sorrow and fear at the thought of losing them. The mere idea of life without their comforting presence is unimaginable. I felt an overwhelming urge to convey the depth of my love for them and assure them that their memory will forever be cherished in my heart. I am profoundly grateful for every moment shared with them, and their impact on my life is immeasurable.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week when I was visiting my grandparents at their home. It mattered greatly to me because the conversation filled my heart with sorrow and fear at the thought of losing them, and the mere idea of life without their comforting presence is unimaginable.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it put in me a fear of death and losing loved ones.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My grandparents started the conversation and kept the conversation going.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control. I did not want to talk or think about it, but my grandparents were passionate and keen on having the conversation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect to have the conversation.

situation: I was extremely stressed with work and hadn't been able to sleep much at night for several days in a row. On top of that, I was dealing with sudden house issues, which made me extremely angry and stressed. I needed to fix the HVAC, which went out during the cold, and I also had to meet work deadlines. All of this left me feeling like a shell of a person. The most important thing for me was just getting everything fixed so I could ultimately have peace of mind.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened last week and everything mattered a lot because work deadlines are mandatory and having working HVAC is also a matter of survival.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me by making me really angry and distracting me from having any free time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There is no one to blame, it is just life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No not at all because I felt that things were happening to me not because of me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well the timing of both events was unexpected and to be honest the stress and magnitude of the troubles were unexpected as well.

situation: I had to share some important health information with my family. While the news was positive, both the news itself and their reaction made it an intense and tiring emotional experience. I needed to keep them up to date with an evolving situation, especially since the news directly affected them, meaning they would have to cancel a cruise booking. Sharing the news left me feeling relieved. I was nervous about telling them and felt rather stressed about the whole situation, but after sharing, it felt like a weight had been lifted, and I could focus on other things. Their response was even more positive than I was expecting, which made it a positive experience overall.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday. It was important - I needed to share this news. I'd been preparing myself for a couple of weeks to tell them, and couldn't wait any longer. This made it a significant event for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was overall positive. My family reacted positively to the news, and it was a relief to get it off my chest. However, the wait to share the news was stressful.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was a health situation directly affecting me, so it was very much my responsibility, both the impacts and sharing the news with people.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes. While my hand was somewhat forced in sharing the news, the situation was a result of my own choices and wishes.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It actually went slightly better than I expected. My family reacted very positively and were supportive.

situation: I took my kids to Disney on Ice, and they loved it so much. It made me incredibly happy to see the joy on their faces. I was just trying to provide a fun time for my kids, and I was glad I got to experience it with them. The performance was based on two movies that are beloved in our family, and it was great to see the kids loving them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday. It mattered so much to me because my kids loved it and seeing them happy made me so happy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me. I was feeling in a rut and this just made me happier and more positive about life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my wife was responsible for this. She found the event and then bought the tickets.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because I drove the car to the event. I was in charge of keeping the family safe and getting us to where we needed to be.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as expected.

situation: I got a good result at court for a client at work. I was trying to ensure that a case against my client was thrown out at the earliest possible stage by the court. I wanted to make sure this happened to relieve my client of the stressful burden of the matter. It left me feeling great, and that all my work was worthwhile. It was also good for me personally, as I continued to learn and make strides in my career.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered quite a lot in a professional capacity because I had done my job properly and got a good result for a client. Although it made me feel good, it was not as important to me in a personal capacity as I tend to try and keep work and my personal life separate.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me as it made me feel good, and it also helped me to develop new skills and expand my professional knowledge.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There are a variety of factors responsible for the outcome. My prior knowledge and the knowledge I had been given by my colleagues and supervisors were key factors in achieving this result. There was also an element of my own hard work and thinking.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control to a degree. I was able to control how we prepared for the hearing and presented our case. However, I was not in control of what happened at court, how the other side presented their case, or how the judge would see the matter.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went largely as expected.

situation: My mom, whom I'm supporting financially, continued to make bad financial decisions even though I asked her to stop. She's in a debt management plan, and we had an agreement that all of her day-to-day spending should be charged to my credit card. However, she keeps buying things on sale and tries to hide it by paying on PayPal. I was trying to help her manage her finances more effectively and stick to the agreement we both had. I wanted her to be transparent about her spending and avoid making impulsive purchases. She's supposed to be either using extra money to pay down her debt or save up money. I've asked her many times to stop, and she won't. I felt betrayed, angry, and disappointed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It has happened over the last month. It matters because I have given my mom thousands of dollars of support so I feel like I've earned respect and she refuses.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I am spending an insane amount of money on her and I am getting tired of it if it isn't going to change anything.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My dad left my mom in a bad financial situation but my mom needs to be more responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't feel in control at all because she won't listen to me even though I've been abundantly clear.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I would think she would show more appreciation but I guess not.

situation: I was dealing with a situation where my kids were not doing what they were asked, which was very effective at winding me up. I was trying to get them to take responsibility and do what they have been asked, without asking 8 times. I felt angry because they didn't do what was asked and it feels like they lack respect. I ended up doing it myself.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the last week, and it matters to me because I'm constantly picking up after them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It doesn't hurt, but it's not helpful. They want stuff done for them, and it's about having respect for their parents and each other.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The kids are most responsible as they didn't do what was asked.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't really feel in control. It would be nice if they do it without asking.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was expected as they still leave things lying around. It's about them taking initiative and clearing up after themselves.

situation: I was dealing with a disagreement about my living situation that made me want to move. It's just a personality difference where the people involved are extremely selfish and self-centered, and they don't see things from an objective point of view. I have a severe distaste for this kind of behavior. I just can't understand how people can think this way.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened about a week ago and it matters a lot because relationships with this personality type don't seem logical or seem like a good place to spend my energy on continuing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has made me feel like I need to change my living situation, which I have already made plans to do. It will be positive to get away from the situation, but it is an inopportune time which has caused distress.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Strictly their personality type. They seem to think they are always right, they are hateful, think they are better than everyone else, and can't grasp any logical argument that doesn't align with their view.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because there is no reason to argue with them because it is a waste of time. My only option is to remove myself from the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They just acted very angry which I tried not to respond to as much as possible.

situation: A situation that has made me emotional this past week was having to adjust to a new psychiatric medication. I wanted a solid treatment for my depression and anxiety. I'm feeling okay, I guess. It's been up and down as my brain and body adjust to the medication. It's left me feeling a bit down and anxious at times, but I'm hopeful that as I build up to the correct dose, I will feel better. I'm just feeling a bit anxious to get the adjustment period over with.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last Friday I guess? It matters to me a lot because I want to get my mental health under control so that I can function better in life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It's helping that I'm starting to feel better mentally but it hurts because the adjustment period is difficult. My moods feel a bit up and down and I have some stomach upset from adjusting.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My poor mental health I guess. I have depression, anxiety, PTSD and BPD.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I didn't feel very in control because I went on the new medication and then had to pause for a few days because I had a bad reaction due to also needing an antibiotic after a root canal. Now I'm back on so it's really been all over the place. I'm starting to feel a little more in control I guess? But I'm tired, and my stomach doesn't feel great, and my emotions are still a bit all over the place.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No things haven't really gone as expected but they are starting to feel more as I expected now that my body isn't reacting quite as badly to everything.

situation: I've been feeling overwhelmed with everything that's going on. I'm trying to sell a house, make sure my son graduates high school with all the scholarships he needs so he won't have student loans, and my wife has Lupus and needs treatment. It's not easy to handle all of this. I'm trying to get one thing done at a time, but it's tough because I work both a part-time job and a full-time job. All of this has left me feeling worn out. On top of that, I need to ensure we have enough money since all the prices keep going up.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event is everyday I am overwhelmed. Rather than get things done, I am doing the dishes and cleaning. What I mean by this is I deal only with the day-to-day, and not the things that matter.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I find if I don't do the day-to-day, the house has issues, my wife is mad, and it's a bad day for me. If the big things don't get done, then nothing happens. I hate it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: All of the above.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like everything is falling apart. I am also fatigued as I have PSA.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I drink a lot of coffee and beer to cope. It bothers me that my wife and son both need to take a bit of the issues.

situation: My partner didn't move my photography equipment when the decorators came in and it ended up covered in dust. I really wanted her to understand that my gear is important to me and that she could have easily moved it to prevent this. I was hoping she would acknowledge the situation, apologise and then clean it for me. Instead, she told me I should have moved it myself which left me feeling frustrated. Being understood was really important to me in this situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the past few days. It was very important to me as photography is my job and my passion. She is aware of how important it is to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because my equipment could be damaged and I could not afford to replace it. Not being understood was also hurtful.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my partner was most responsible for all of this because she did not inform me of the works being done until it was not possible to move the gear myself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all as I wasn’t aware of the works taking place until it was too late to do anything myself.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. We still haven’t been able to clear the air.

situation: I had a fight with my girlfriend about something stupid. I wanted her to understand that I don't look at other women, either in real life or online. It made me upset at the time because I do so much that proves my love and dedication to her. But now, I think she understands and sees that what I say I mean. What was important was that we understood each other in the end.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened two days ago late at night and it mattered to me a lot because I didn't want her to feel like I don't love her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I know she acts this way because of her past relationship but it helped bring us closer because I reassured her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't think anyone is to blame really, it just happened the way it happened.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I was in control of the situation because it didn't take long for things to cool down between us.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected and I'm pleased that they did.

situation: I helped a client return home to their parents after not having contact with them for 15 years. The client has had a difficult time over those years being estranged from their family. They have complex PTSD from their time in Afghanistan as a British soldier. I've been supporting them to try to return home for 5 years. It's been tough over the years, with many difficult moments including multiple arrests, prison, and substance use. Now they are free from their pain and ready to go home. I made a connection with them; they trusted me and only me. It's been the greatest reward for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I met them when they were rough sleeping on the streets here, and they had a bad reputation with services being cautious about working with them due to their erratic temperament. It was an important moment for me to be able to connect with someone who had never trusted anyone.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was a most positive connection.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Making a connection with someone takes two people, one to be empathic and the other to feel heard.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Never, it's not my place to control anything. My role is to show the person they are valued, and to do that I have to listen without judgment.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: After 5 years, he returned to his family; this is the ultimate.

situation: I was falling asleep yesterday before taking a nap, and I got pretty existential about being alone and where my life was actually going. I ended up screaming in frustration. Before I go to sleep, my brain goes into a different type of mode that I don't have when I'm fully awake, so I wasn't actively doing anything almost. I was just feeling the negative emotions; I wasn't hoping for anything. It left me feeling negative, like my life wasn't improving. But when I woke up, the feeling was gone.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event didn't matter much to me overall because the person I am when I'm falling asleep isn't technically the person I am most of the time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It reminded me that I'm not happy with my life subconsciously and I have to do everything I can to change it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My choices and what happened to me in the past were most responsible for these feelings I experienced.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I didn't ask to feel that way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole thing was unexpected; right now I have the same life but I don't have those feelings.

situation: I went for a country walk with my wife and children. I wanted to spend some quality time with them, just enjoying each other's company. The walk left me feeling happy but tired.
