It was really important to me that my children didn't complain about going for a walk, and thankfully, they didn't.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened today afternoon. It was important to me because I wanted to spend quality time with my family and ensure my children didn't complain about going for a walk.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by allowing me to leave the house with my family. Emotionally and mentally, it was very peaceful, and the exercise felt good.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My wife was most responsible for all of this because she found and suggested the place.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control during the walk because we discussed the route.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The beauty of the place was more than I expected, which was a pleasant surprise.

situation: I went skiing in France with my family for the weekend. At one point, because I ski slower than the rest of my family, I became disconnected from them and was left on my own for quite a while. I wanted to get in touch with my family, but I knew they wouldn't be able to answer their phones or receive messages for quite some time. I was worried they might not realize I had been left behind—or maybe they did realize and didn't care—but I didn't want to make a fuss about it. The whole situation left me feeling confused and insecure. I didn't want to spoil the day for my family, especially since we only had a short period to ski. I was also worried about safety on the mountain, as there have been lots of avalanches lately. I was scared that I or one of my family might be in an accident. Eventually, we managed to meet up again at a mountain-side cafe.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was quite short-lived, but it mattered a lot to me. I felt left out, betrayed, and confused.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Once we reconnected and I could look back on it, I realized I over-reacted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I blamed my husband because he's the oldest and should have been the one who noticed I wasn't there. You can't blame the teenagers because they are meant to be thoughtless.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt a complete loss of control. I had placed my trust in my husband and he had let me down.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I hadn't expected this at all. But next time, I will be more in control—for example, I will arrange a place to meet in case we lose each other.

situation: My situation regarding my future career is quite upsetting because I've never had a job before, and I feel like I'm falling behind. I see entry level jobs as stepping stones, but stepping stones with spikes on them as I can't see myself enjoying it at all. I want to have a clear goal and to be able to enjoy the process, not just what's at the end. I feel confused and sad about the time I've seen myself 'waste.' Every decision I overthink, and it's just a loop of negativity. Being surrounded by people who believe in me and help me has been very helpful.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot, as it's ongoing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as in it's a painful reminder of the situation that I'm in, but it always helps me push forward.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am responsible for everything that happens.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Sometimes I am, sometimes not, I get a lot of bumps of motivation, but then I can easily distract myself with other things which are comfortable to hide.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They didn't, I applied for multiple jobs that I think I would enjoy, I either didn't get a reply or I was turned down. But I know it's because of my lack of experience.

situation: My son was being teased by some older boys at school, and he came home crying. It was really upsetting for everyone, and he couldn't sleep. I was trying to help him understand that sometimes others can be unkind, and I just wanted him to feel better. The whole situation left me feeling deflated and a little angry. It was important to me to make sure my son was okay and that it didn't happen again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened when I picked my son up from school, this is when I found out about it. It mattered to me more than anything because you want your children to feel safe and happy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me learn how to deal with these sorts of things; if it happens again, I know what to do.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the other parents of the children who were being unkind were responsible really.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, not really, as there was nothing I could do except reassure my son.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected him to feel worse for longer, but he bounced back quite soon.

situation: When my long-distance girlfriend went back home, I had to take her to the airport so she could catch her flight. I wanted her to stay, of course, but I knew she couldn't as she needed to go home. I felt sad. The fact that I will see her again in not too long, which is unusual for a long-distance relationship, is comforting.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 3 days ago. It mattered a lot to me because she is my girlfriend and I love her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I had to say goodbye and couldn't see her anymore for a while.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I guess I felt a bit uncertain about the level of control I had. It's not really a situation I can be in control of or not.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went as I expected.

situation: Last weekend, I participated in a Bridge competition that was not only fiercely competitive but also profoundly challenging. Leading up to the event, I was filled with anxiety, fearing that I might perform poorly. However, to my astonishment, we ended up in the top third, which felt like a monumental achievement. This unexpected success brought me immense joy, as it was a testament to our hard work and perseverance. My Bridge partner and I were determined to perform our best and avoid any significant blunders, a task easier said than done. The day was all about maintaining a steady pace, and together, we accomplished just that. The sense of happiness and pride I felt in our achievements was overwhelming, coupled with a deep relief that things hadn't gone awry. Overall, the experience was incredibly positive and uplifting. Playing Bridge with a partner holds a special place in my heart, and my foremost hope before the event was not to disappoint them, especially since I am considered the stronger player on paper. I was overjoyed that I could fulfill this aspiration, reinforcing the bond and trust between us.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Saturday at a school around half an hour from where I live. It mattered to me greatly because I always try to put in 100% to everything I do, and I am a very competitive person.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The competition helped reassure me that I am as good, if not better, than I think I am at Bridge. It made me realize that I can achieve good things and that participating in these sorts of competitions is worthwhile and rewarding.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I believe I am responsible for the success and am primarily responsible for my own emotions. My Bridge partner also contributed to the success, so they were important too.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It was probably a mixture. At the start of the day, I perhaps didn't feel like I had much control. However, as the day progressed and we realized that we were actually doing quite well, my confidence and my control certainly stabilized, and I felt more positive and grounded.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected because I wasn't sure if we would do well. I was delighted that I managed to exceed all my expectations.

situation: I was listening to a regular podcast about news and politics, trying to stay informed about the ongoing war in Iran. The presenter's comments about a specific action in the war hit me hard, leaving me overwhelmed with sadness and a degree of disgust. It wasn't that I was unaware of the action they referred to, but their comments made me focus on it more deeply. This situation left me feeling heavy, as world news seems to have become increasingly gloomy and negative over the last few years. I sometimes wonder if I'm catastrophising when I think about this, but I suspect that I'm probably not.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It doesn't matter to me at a local/personal level, but it affected me at a broader emotional level, as I wondered about the state of the world.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me worry that individuals from a country that I am broadly appreciative of are going down a dark path, which in turn made me doubt my thoughts about said country.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The United States.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Definitely not, I have no locus of control in relation to a war happening overseas and made by a country other than my own.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: A specific military action took place. Many people were killed. A government official spoke about this in unpleasant, gloating terms, and there was no sense of shared humanity with the deceased people.

situation: My mum is waiting for her diagnosis after her cancer treatment was finished. We've been anxiously waiting for over 2 months to hear the results. The doctor phoned us last week saying they need to do more tests. We wanted the all clear, but that is something the doctors can't say currently. I'm feeling nervous for the future and what will happen. I guess my mum being disheartened by the news is important to me too.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened around a week ago. It's the most important thing in our lives currently as it feels like our lives stopped when my mum got the disease.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It makes me nervous for the future as we have already lost my brother to the disease, so it makes us more scared of it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It's all luck based. You either get lucky or get cancer.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, the doctor has all the control and we were just waiting.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I guess it was kinda expected and unexpected at the same time. We weren't sure what news we will get.

situation: A friend of mine, who I wish to get closer to, came to me for emotional support during a negative event in their life. We talked about it in some detail, and although my friend's situation was a negative one, ultimately afterwards I felt more positive that our friendship had leveled up and that my friend can trust me with their personal issues. I wanted to be supportive and helpful in dealing with my friend's problem. After the conversation, I felt glad. I'm not sure how helpful my words were during the conversation, but I felt glad to know that my friend trusted me enough to talk to me about their situation. I just wanted to be there for my friend and to let them know that I will be there again should they need to talk about other issues.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because I would like to be closer to this friend and be able to be there for them when necessary.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me to see that my friend does already trust me a good amount.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think perhaps I was most responsible for this, by showing that I am someone who is caring and a good listener during my previous interactions with this friend.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I neither felt in control or out of control. I don't think control was a factor in this instance.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: My friend initially reaching out to me with their issue was unexpected.

situation: A family member passed away suddenly, and I found myself trying to keep my other family members calm and loved during this difficult time. The situation left me feeling exhausted, and it was important for me to make sure I got therapy to help cope with everything.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it involved a close family member who was mostly healthy before rapidly becoming sick.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was sad and upsetting, impacting my sleep and focus. I had to take time off of work.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible; it was a health condition.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control; I felt like there was nothing I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected that my family member passed away so quickly. We thought we had more time.

situation: My wife gave birth to our second child, and I was there to support her and be there for my daughter, taking care of them both. I felt great; I love my new little girl so much already and can't wait to welcome her into my family. My wife did so good during labor. It went so quick and she was laser focused. Just fantastic, made me proud as her husband.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was the most important thing in my recent life. Nothing could be more important.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me happy. I am excited for the new addition to my family. My daughter is so excited for her new sister. And she's happy and healthy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My wife was. She was carrying her and birthing her after all!
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes and no. I wasn't in control, but the situation was under control and taken care of.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was easier and quicker than expected! Labor was maybe 20 minutes max. My wife was so quick and did so well.

situation: I wanted to start fostering dogs, especially seniors and those with medical conditions, because I know they're less likely to be adopted. My partner was initially supportive of the idea, but when I checked one more time before submitting the application, they said they don't think they have the time to help. I really want to help dogs by getting them out of the kennel rescue environment where I'm sure they're uncomfortable and scared. Plus, I love dogs but am not ready to have another of our own after losing our adopted senior years ago, so fostering seemed like a perfect solution. I was very sad that I wouldn't be able to have dogs around the house. I was also very frustrated and annoyed with my partner's communication, or lack thereof. My partner acted like I was being unreasonable, as if I should have known they couldn't free up enough time in their hectic work schedule to help out. I feel like it's somewhat an excuse, too.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal. For all the reasons I laid out above including my love of dogs and wanting to help them. It also mattered because I felt like my partner wasn't being helpful or thoughtful.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I want to help the dogs and have their company.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My partner.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because I don't think I can realistically give the dog all the attention and time outside they need. My partner okayed the decision to foster and never shared that they would not assist in the responsibilities. It also made me feel like my time and responsibilities were being minimised next to theirs.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did not go as expected because I was under the impression we were on the same page. I had already run all this by them and we agreed to proceed. But then when I checked again, just to be safe, later, they gave a different response as if earlier conversations hadn't occurred.

situation: I received a letter from the IRS, and I needed to know what it was about. The letter just said I had to call them, which left me feeling scared. Even though I've been honest with them, I have income from different sources, so it is complicated. I was worried that I might not be able to get my explanations across to the person on the other end of the line, at least I hoped it was a person.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Thursday and I was utterly shook because I could not imagine what I had done wrong.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me by causing a lot of anxiety.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Because I do not trust government agencies like the IRS even though I know that is paranoid.
appraisal_reasoning.control: When you are dealing with bureaucracies you are never in control. They have a 'decision tree' and there is no room for reason.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected as far as taking a huge amount of time to get through to them. I guess it was also expected that they did not really give me an explanation. They just said they had to verify identification information. So, I guess it is resolved.

situation: My mom told me she can't afford to pay her mortgage anymore, and I really wanted to help her find a solution so she would have a place to live. But it's frustrating because my mom and my siblings just won't listen to my advice and warnings. It's important to me that they're wise and take care of things, but it feels like they're not paying attention to what I'm saying.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened about a month ago. It matters a lot to me, because if something isn't figured out soon, my mom and my sister and brother will be homeless.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It is hurting me because they will not listen to my advice. It is affecting me emotionally because I care for them, and I don't want them to end up without a home. It also affects me personally, because they like to spend time with my kids, but if they are homeless, they won't get to see them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think it is a combination of my mom, my sister, and my brother. They don't plan well for life. My husband and I warned and advised them for years as to how to take care of this situation, but they continued to ignore our advice and warnings.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't feel like I am in control. I can advise and suggest and warn, but it is ultimately up to them what they end up doing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not really. They are still planning on trying to stay in the house without the means to afford it. I was hoping they would listen, sell the house, and use the proceeds to rent.

situation: I was out for a meal with my wife and son, celebrating my birthday, and I felt very positive and happy. I was enjoying spending valuable time with my most loved ones. The whole experience left me feeling happy, grateful, and content. It was important to me to just be able to reflect and be grateful for my family.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in Sheffield and it mattered to me a lot as it was celebrating my 40th birthday and was part of a weekend away.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by reflecting on the most important things in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself and my family.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control of this situation and my feelings. It was just me, my wife, and my son.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as planned.

situation: My brother died the day before yesterday. I was watching my brother die in a hospital bed. I wasn't trying to do anything or needed anything. It left me feeling pretty devastated, probably the worst experience of my life honestly.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I watched my brother die, and surprisingly it mattered a lot. It was probably the worst experience of my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was devastating. I've been crying about it regularly, and it was probably the worst experience of my life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Cancer was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really, no. I have no way of stopping cancer spreading through someone's body.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was quicker than expected, so it was perhaps less traumatic than it could have been.

situation: I was recently taken off this medication I was prescribed for anxiety, and it's frustrating. I had to stop taking a medication I was prescribed, and it makes me uncomfortable. I was hoping to make my anxiety and depression better, but instead it made it worse. The situation left me feeling worse. I should be able to get back on the medication, so that's good.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I started taking the medicine 2 years ago and thought it worked great but I would stop taking it after using it daily and would experience the worst withdrawals.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me get through the depression I was feeling and I'm more active when I'm on it but whenever I stop taking it I'm almost useless.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I took the medicine at too high of a dose and should have tapered off of it slowly if I have to stop it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I wasn't in control because when I first started taking it I didn't know the withdrawals were this bad.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect it to work as good as it does but I also didn't expect the withdrawals to get worse overtime.

situation: I was listening to my wife's stories from work, and they were really negative. I just didn't want to hear it because it was hard to listen to. I felt like I needed a break from the stories; that would have been good. The whole situation left me feeling mind numb.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days back, exactly 3 days ago. It mattered to me because I want my wife to have a nice working life, but she does not.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it hurt to see my wife hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She takes on a lot from work, so she needs to vent.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I couldn't get her to stop talking about it even after everything was aired.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected it, yes, as this is what usually happens.

situation: At the beginning of the week, my Nan suddenly went into the hospital because she wasn't feeling well. It was a scary time for me because I was anxious and scared, worried that we might lose her. All I wanted was for my Nan to be okay, to get better, and to be discharged from the hospital. Luckily, it turned out to be a false alarm, and she was discharged two days later. Throughout this situation, I was also really concerned about my uncle's wellbeing since he is her carer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday (it is now Saturday). It mattered a huge amount and was the only thing on my mind those 2 days.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help me but it also did not hurt me as nothing bad ended up happening.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible for what happened. It is life unfortunately.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel in control but my emotions were high.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not have any expectations as you never know what might happen in these situations. I just wanted her to get better. The entire situation was unexpected.

situation: I was walking my dog, feeling frustrated because she kept pulling on the lead and not listening to me. I needed her to behave better, especially since she's been trained to do so. The whole situation left me feeling annoyed and frustrated. I'm just trying to make sure this doesn't happen again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered quite a bit to me because I was struggling to hold on to the lead and she was potentially putting herself in danger.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me physically as it was painful to hold the lead. Beyond the physical discomfort, it did not have any other impact on me, either positively or negatively.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the dog was most responsible for all of this because she was not listening.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control during this situation because I was trying to be in control and I wasn't.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because it was unexpected that she smelled another dog that I had not anticipated being out.

situation: My father died, and it was a moment that brought up a lot of emotions for me. We had a very complicated relationship over the years, and I found myself wanting answers that nobody could really give me—not even him. Sometimes, I felt almost void of anything, and then there would be a rush of sadness or a rush of joy. What mattered most to me was that at the end of his life, I forgave him, and we had the relationship that we deserved.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on January 31st. It mattered to me because it was a significant moment that brought up a lot of emotions, reflecting the complicated relationship I had with my father over the years.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me when he left and when he died. The in-between was filled with every emotion there is. Despite the hurt, everything I've gone through in my life, the good and the bad, has led me to who I am today, with what and who I have in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: For him leaving, he was responsible for that, as he was for coming back.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of me, for the most part. I was given a warm and loving home and raised by my mom's mom and her brother and sister.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What is lived and what I know is all I know. I guess everything that has happened was expected.

situation: One of my best friend's father passed away, and I knew his dad quite well and always liked him. He had been ill for quite some time and was pretty old, but I'm really sad for my friend. Even though he's in his 50s, I think this is his first close experience with death, and it's hit him quite hard. I'm trying to help my friend get through it without resorting to platitudes. There's a bit of a conflict because I don't want him to be distraught, but he does need to grieve. I'm trying to use my greater experience to help him somewhat, but it's not easy. I feel a little bit helpless because I can advise on practical things, but this is something deeply personal for him. I've tried to share how I felt when it happened to me and how I got through it—not as a blueprint for overcoming grief, but more as a statement that whatever can get you through something like this needs to be embraced.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because my friend was devastated. I wanted to be there for him or for him to at least know that he had someone to talk to.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience brought back memories of my own loss, which was somewhat sad. But I am over that now. I just wanted him to know he had a friend to call on.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Obviously my friend was most responsible for the emotions and dynamics in this situation. Any emotions I was feeling were weak by comparison. It's as if I was upset by proxy.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't think anyone would be in control of the situation. It's about grieving in whatever way feels right at the time and knowing there are people around who can be supportive.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had no expectations. The process is famously different for every single person.

situation: I've been feeling emotionally confused by this guy I'm dating because of his behavior. When we're together in person, he's extremely chatty and forward, and I feed off his energy, feeling really positive. But then, when we're messaging, he can be distant, which leaves me feeling negative and confused. We went from having a super positive and enjoyable date to me not really hearing from him for the next few days, and then suddenly he's really chatty and talkative again. What I really need is consistency and security. Open and honest conversations are important to me, and while I feel like I get that when we're together in person, it doesn't seem as clear when we're communicating via message.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot as I am very interested in this guy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It got me very confused and made me worried I was getting my hopes up too soon and that things maybe weren't what I was led to believe they were.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel he was mostly responsible for being distant but perhaps I was overthinking the situation when he was just busy.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel like I was in control because I was waiting for responses.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things felt normal and good again next time in person but it seems to be a bit of a pattern.

situation: I watched the movie Always. It's a film I've loved and watched many times over the years, and it still gets me emotional every time. I just wanted to feel something enjoyable and emotional, both. Watching it left me feeling nostalgic. It's a love story and also about loss, and it never fails to make me emotional.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered because I've loved this movie ever since I first watched it over twenty years ago.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Watching the movie made me feel happy for the way it all turned out in the end.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The actors, the director, and everybody involved in making the movie were most responsible for all of this emotional experience.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of the remote, and I just let my emotions flow freely.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected while watching the movie.

situation: I was hit with the realization that the holiday was over, and I felt a wave of sadness about coming home. I needed to not be coming home because it's just too difficult for me to cope with. Alternatively, I needed a solution to this situation. The whole thing left me feeling unhappy, sad, worried, and tearful. It was important for me to acknowledge that I can't face normal life anymore. I have to be on the move all the time, and being in a house is the catalyst to my sadness.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was yesterday and it mattered because it's the centre of my mental health struggles.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me worried about facing the normality of life even though I am only here for 10 days before going away again.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am responsible. It's up to me to try to work out why the boring humdrum of life has become such a terrible mental health issue to me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control. I had to come home yesterday as there are a couple of things that have to be done and staying away wasn't possible.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was hoping they would not go as expected ie upset as I'm tackling the issue with support but sadly, and unexpectedly, they did go as per they were expected.

situation: I've been feeling really happy and content lately. Some friends are going to be moving in nearby, and I'm looking forward to that. I don't really need anything right now, but I suppose I want them to move in, and they are, so that's good. Overall, I'm feeling good and content.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It made me feel good to hear some friends will be moving in nearby. It made me feel I'd made the right choice by living and staying here and that made me feel validated.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has reassured me that I made the right decision living here. There hasn't been any aspect of this situation that I feel might have been challenging or less positive for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just luck really.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not hugely but that didn't matter.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting my friends to say they're moving in nearby.

situation: I received a call from my insurance company, and they informed me that the car accident I had last year was determined not to be my fault. The other company would be taking responsibility, and I was going to be sent a check refunding what I had paid for repairs. I was really hoping to get that refund because the money would be very useful to me right now. I felt happy that it was confirmed it wasn't my fault and relieved that I would be receiving the money. It was also a big relief to be able to put this situation behind me. It felt good to be cleared of any responsibility for what happened.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a fair bit to me because I wanted confirmation that I wasn't at fault. Additionally, the money will be very helpful to have available.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by clearing me from any fault and by improving my short-term financial situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the arbitrators who reviewed the accident were responsible, as they took an impartial look at the information and came to the decision that I was cleared.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control. At this point, all I was doing was waiting and anticipating the decision to be made by others.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't sure what to expect, but I'm not surprised at how it resolved, as I didn't feel that I was responsible.

situation: Yesterday was the anniversary of my dad's death, and the whole day was really emotional for me. I had to work as usual, trying to have as normal a day as possible despite everything. By the end of the day, I felt emotionally drained. What really mattered to me was how well my friends and family supported me through it all.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Yesterday, it mattered a lot as I was very close with my dad.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped because trying to maintain a normal day helped keep me focused.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me, I was my most responsible for keeping my mind focused.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Mostly I was, however there were times I felt overwhelmed and I couldn't control my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes mostly as expected.

situation: Recently, I received a diagnosis from the doctor regarding the symptoms I've had for a while, and it turns out I need surgery. I was really hoping to get some information and find out the best solution moving forward. The whole situation left me feeling sad because it put everything in my life into perspective. More than anything, I wanted reassurance that everything will be fine.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event was extremely important as it was a life-changing event.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation both helped and hurt me. It helped because I found an answer, and it hurt because the answer was not what I wanted to find out.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible. It was just a fact of life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt I had no control. It is not in my power to solve it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I would say that all went as expected.

situation: I was told by my wife that I am the best husband and father, and it made me feel really special, bringing me to tears. I wanted to feel special and appreciated for working so much, and her words made me feel like the hard work I am putting in is appreciated. She also gave me a little necklace that my daughter made for me, which made me feel really loved.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This mattered a lot because we were having a nice picnic and hearing this made my day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me stay motivated. I've been working over 60 hours per week which is very exhausting, but I am doing this to pay off my debt and mortgage.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like it was a result of a combination between my wife and daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did because it made me feel really special. I was also barbecuing for them so it made me feel really special, especially because they gave me the chance to share my appreciations.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I would like to think so. There wasn't anything unexpected from this conversation, because we ended up having a nice picnic and everyone was happy.

situation: I was recently in my appraisal at work when my line manager told me that I'd been nominated for an organisational award. I was just doing my work, and the award I've been nominated for is the 'Unsung Hero' award. Honestly, I feel embarrassed by it and think there are more deserving colleagues in the Trust. I can't shake the feeling that I'm a fraud.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 3 weeks ago. I haven't stopped thinking about it. I'm a little worried it'll put me in the spotlight across the trust.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think that it will help me; I feel that it makes me realize that people appreciate the work that I do.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My manager has put forward the nomination.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I had no idea that this was happening and would have tried to dissuade them from doing it!
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't know about it; I only found out after it had been done. It was out of my control, but I've just got to accept that others feel that way about me.

situation: I caught my partner flirting with a woman, being all smiley during a live video, which made me feel frustrated, angry, and very much irritated. I wanted her to understand how her actions made me feel as a human being and a man. The situation left me feeling so depressed that I was unable to get out of bed the following day for a large part of the day, not even being able to speak to my partner because she showed zero understanding. I kinda wanted to know if she was actually attracted to the woman in question or if it was just women in general, and is that the real reason she treats me so bad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Tuesday evening after I had just watched football, which was kind of distracting as she spent the whole match giggling to this woman. It mattered to me because she never shows me that kind of attention, so I was looking for a reason why.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it made me feel even more lonely than I felt before the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My partner was responsible for the cause of the issues, but I was responsible for acting the way that I acted.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control as she would not hear my words and take them in, which then made me feel ignored and as if my feelings and emotions were irrelevant.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things didn't really get a conclusion; the next day she admitted zero responsibility and expected me to apologise like I was fully at fault.

situation: I was having quite a bad day for my mental health recently. Things had been piling on, and I was worried about a few different things. On the same day, my little boy gave me a really big cuddle and told me about his day, and I immediately started to feel much better. I found it quite emotional. I wasn't sure that I was trying to do anything in particular; I was just having a bad day, and then my child fixed it. The situation left me feeling definitely positive. It made me realize that I shouldn't stay too internal and should let myself notice and focus on other things like my children.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal to me. It was very unexpected but powerful. It made me realise there are more important things around.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was a mindful moment that stopped me thinking too much. It gave me a topic to focus on when I feel things building up again and need a reset.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My child.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Probably not in control but I was happy to go along with it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was an unexpected situation so I didn't really expect anything.

situation: I decided to put two new knuckles on my vehicle, opting for cheaper ones to save some money since I know how to do the work myself. Unfortunately, those parts turned out to be junk, and I had to remove them and install new OEM ones, which ended up costing me more. I was really hoping the cheaper parts would last more than a day, but they didn't. I went ahead with the better parts because I'm planning to use this vehicle for travel. At first, it was discouraging and I was upset because it meant doing way more work than I anticipated. I was worried it wasn't going to work out for a bit, but now that it's done and everything worked out, I feel OK and I'm happy it did.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was upsetting at the time because it’s hard work and I’m not getting any younger, so I wanted to for sure get it done right. It mattered because I was planning to use this vehicle for travel, and I was worried it wasn't going to work out for a bit.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me learn how to do it, so I could do it much faster if I have to do it again. Initially, it was discouraging and I was upset because it meant doing way more work than I anticipated.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: A lot of it was me because I was trying to save money, but the parts were bad, so it was both I suppose.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control while I was doing it. I just felt like I wasn’t in control when I was waiting for the new parts, waiting for the shipping, waiting to get everything I needed to redo it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it didn’t go as expected because I expected it to get fixed the first time. I didn’t think the parts would last quite as long, but I didn’t think they would go out immediately.

situation: Earlier this week, I tripped while getting a drink from the kitchen and hit the table, knocking off a very sentimental item that my wife loves. It cracked at the top and a piece fell off. I managed to super glue the piece back on, but there's a noticeable line now where it broke. I knew I had to tell her what happened. The next day, I sat her down and told her. There were tears in her eyes, but after thinking it through, she forgave me. I just wanted a drink, and I'm clumsy. When it happened, I was so shocked I didn't know what to do. The only thing I needed was to be honest. I didn't want to conceal what happened; that would be wrong. At first, I was scared and stressed, not knowing how she would react. Then I was just left sad seeing how it hurt her to find out about the situation. I'm feeling better about it now as she reassured me she loves me. The only thing important to me was being honest with the woman I love. She deserves the truth even though it hurt her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened earlier this week. It mattered a lot to me because as a man I feel it is my job to protect my wife. In this case, my actions will cause her emotional pain and that is something that is hard for me to deal with.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me realize my wife loves me because she forgave me even though it made her sad. It hurt me in the sense I feel that I failed my wife by causing her sadness.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was solely responsible due to being clumsy and careless.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I had control in either telling her or not. She often is not very observant and I could have gotten away with my quick fix. In the end though I had to do the right thing and be honest.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected. I thought she would be mad for a while and not talk to me, but she appreciated me telling her and she showed me love.

situation: My friend passed away, and I was really in need of some comforting. The whole situation left me feeling bad. It was important to me because my friend died.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because my friend died.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because he died.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: His heart gave out.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control of the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected because he died unexpectedly.

situation: I was watching sports on TV, looking for some entertainment and a bit of fun by betting on the game. I felt happiness and contentment as I watched, with excitement and intrigue building up as the match progressed. The outcome was important to me, and I was really focused on who would end up winning.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot because I enjoy the sport besides betting.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me keep up to date on what the outcome is. It also helped me to follow it live.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The athletes and the network broadcasting it were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I could choose if I wanted to watch or not.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. I was entertained and content on the outcome.

situation: I had to deal with a lot of stress at work, but I managed to finish everything before the week ended. It required me to work a lot of hours and stay late at the office to get everything done on time. The whole situation left me feeling stressed, but once it was over, I felt relieved and happy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it is important for my work evaluation that I am able to meet these deadlines.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I learned new things, specifically about time management. However, it affected me negatively because it was stressful and I did not get to spend much time at home with my family due to working too much.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My employer requiring me to finish a deadline was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I did not set the deadline; it was assigned to me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as expected, with no major issues.

situation: I was feeling really emotional because my children were misbehaving. I had very little sleep and was in pain, and they just seemed to push all the right buttons. I was trying to stop them from hurting themselves, but I was so irritable. Honestly, I needed more sleep. The whole situation left me feeling frustrated and angry.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the morning while I was waiting for my wife to get up. It mattered to me because I could not help them or stop them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help me at all. It hurt me because I was already low in mood and it made things worse.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My children were responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control - they were. I couldn't help things and they didn't see how much I was struggling.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They went as expected when my wife woke up and had a different approach.

situation: My best friend's mother passed away, and I really wanted to do something to help my friend. But honestly, I didn't know what to do. I felt sort of useless, to be honest. It was important to me to be there for my friend, who was very obviously upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 8 days ago and she died suddenly. I knew her well and have been friends with her son for many years.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was shocked and upset. It was difficult as we were both upset and I did not know what to do to try to help him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It is just the cycle of life I suppose.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control, but that's just my makeup and personality. I reflect on things when I have some quiet time on my own.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Her death was unexpected so everything was unexpected.

situation: I had a week off work with my girlfriend, and we had planned to go on a few small trips and walks together. Unfortunately, I accidentally caused her to have an injury. She has poor knees, and I accidentally knocked her knee, which led to her needing my assistance throughout the week. I was trying to tidy the apartment and left the hoover in an awkward location, which she didn't see. She took a small fall, more of a trip, and that was enough to really hurt her. I felt really upset because we hardly have any time off together anymore, and we had quite a lot planned for the week. I felt apologetic and guilty. It was important that I didn't keep apologizing because she doesn't like that. I knew I had to show her support and assistance for the rest of the week as much as possible to make up for it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I was tidying the apartment for our week off, and we wanted to make sure the apartment was clean and an afterthought for once, rather than a constant every evening worry or job that we always have to see to. It was especially upsetting for me because it felt like a shot in the foot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because seeing my girlfriend in pain always upsets me, especially when it's my fault. I knew how much she wanted to visit this nearby town and cafe on Thursday.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt most responsible because I was the person who placed the hoover awkwardly and in her way, and didn't tell her it was there. I can also blame the hoover because it's falling apart, but it's still my fault for not doing that sooner and for leaving it around in a hazardous way.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do feel like I was in control of the situation and I was really helpful in monitoring and taking accountability, and ensuring it doesn't happen again.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect for any of this to happen, and I specifically stated that I'd hoover and throw the hoover away, as it's in such poor condition this was literally its last use. Unfortunately, I finished the job and just left the hoover hazardously on the floor, which was practically broken in 3 or 4 different places, almost inviting my girlfriend's injury. It was a really big regret straight away.

situation: I was working when I noticed water marks on the ceiling, which led me to discover a leak in our roof. I went up to the attic and confirmed the leak, so I contacted a roofer to get a quote. They're scheduled to come and repair it on Tuesday. Initially, I felt very angry and upset about the situation, and later I was annoyed and frustrated. Right now, I just need my roof patched so I can focus on my work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I was worried that it would be very costly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it caused emotional distress and will be a financial burden.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that nature was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel like I was in control. There was nothing I could do. I had no control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went as well as expected.

situation: I was emotional when I found out about the passing of my grandma. I was crying and it hurts so much. I miss her. I was trying to call her as I do each day, but she didn’t pick up, and then I found out she was gone. It left me feeling sad. Knowing that she was free from pain and in a better place was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I lost my grandma. It mattered to me because I am close to her and we would talk a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I can no longer talk to her. I can no longer see her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I would have to say both time and god. We only get so much time on earth.
appraisal_reasoning.control: This is not something I or anyone can control. Death is a natural process.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No I did not expect her death to come so soon. I did expect to be sad.

situation: I had a big argument with my wife today, and it was very emotional. I wanted her to start looking for work because she had been avoiding it, and it left me feeling angry. It was frustrating because she couldn't see how much this situation was affecting me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This afternoon, it's important because she has spent her savings and I will have to find extra money to keep paying the bills.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: She refuses to address the problem and says she is too ill to work. I'm very angry and upset.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She's responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was getting increasingly frustrated.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, the issue is not resolved, I expected her to take responsibility and say she would do something.

situation: My husband's business slowed down so much that he was barely able to pay me anything at all. This caused all of our bills to fall behind, and my stress level was through the roof. I was trying to get my normal weekly pay from him for his business, and I needed it to be the same amount we consistently get that I had planned for. I felt stressed, anxious, and angry at the surprise. I needed my husband to kick it into high gear and figure out how to turn this around, which created a lot of tension between us.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened last week. We are living paycheck to paycheck and I counted on this money to pay the bills on time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me by causing financial uncertainty and insecurity about our future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My husband's lack of motivation with his business. He has been unable to sell it and is sick of doing it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. He is in charge of making sales to make the money.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not at all- he took out 1900 less for his check than he normally does. This was a huge change and we didn't have enough to pay our bills on time.

situation: I realized just how addicted I was to video games and the huge impact they had on my life. It hit me that I needed to change because continuing like this wasn't sustainable and was ruining my life. I felt like I had to leave behind a large portion of my time and life to make this change. Salvaging my relationships was really important to me, and I knew it wasn't going to happen without making a change.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because I felt like I wasn't in control of my life anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I was able to see how much damage I've done, but it hurt me for that same reason.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible for it; I am responsible for my own life and what happens in it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control because my addictions are very strong and hard to overcome.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I don't honestly know what I expected, but it worked out in such a way that I found what I needed.

situation: UK citizens were trapped in unsafe countries, specifically holiday destinations, due to the onset of war. I was really concerned about these innocent citizens who found themselves in such dangerous situations through no fault of their own. I just wanted them to be safe and well. The whole situation left me feeling really anxious for them, and their safety and well-being were really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened about a week ago. It mattered a lot to me as so many innocent people were caught up in a situation beyond their control.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me to think of the impact it had on others.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The mindless actions of world leaders.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Definitely not. The only people in control are those that initiated the war.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes they did.

situation: It was a difficult week because my uncle's funeral was on Monday. My father is ill, so my brother took my mum to the funeral since it was her brother who passed away. I had to stay home to look after my father, and we watched the funeral on a live stream on the TV. It was very hard, especially seeing my upset mum on the screen. I wanted to be there for my mum, but I also needed to look after my elderly father. I really wanted to pay my respects to my uncle by being at the funeral, but sadly, I couldn’t do it all. I felt terrible, to be honest. I felt desperately sad, and I hated not being there for my mum when she needed me most. It was important for me to be with my dad who also needed me. It was definitely a conflicting situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: My uncle passed away 2-3 weeks ago but the funeral was only on Monday. He had been ill with Alzheimer’s for a few years and it had been terrible for his wife and son. My Mum was very very close to her brother so has taken his illness and now his death very hard. It mattered to me that my family was suffering but also I was gladdened that my uncle was no longer suffering. He spent a lot of his last months confused and scared which was awful to see.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me mostly as I am very close to my Mum and I struggle to see her in pain. I also am quite an emotional person so I struggle with death and watching others suffer even when they are not that close to me. This situation was the most hard.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: That’s a strange question. fate was responsible I guess. No one else.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn’t in control in that I had to stay with my Dad who also. That was the only way my Mum would agree to go, if she knew he was being looked after. I wanted to go to the funeral but I knew I couldn’t whether or not I wanted to.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn’t expect to find the funeral as distressing. It was more distressing as it was streamed in the tv and I saw my Mum upset a long distance away and I could not do anything to comfort her.

situation: My mother was very ill and had to go to the hospital. I really needed to stay with her, but it was impossible because of the hospital rules. This left me feeling frustrated. It was also important for me to keep my family updated about her condition.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on New Year's Eve and it mattered a huge amount to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I was scared as it was a heart problem. It was negative because I was helpless and everything takes a long time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt helpless.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control, as I needed to rely on others.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as expected.

situation: I went to the funeral of a relative, hoping to achieve some closure. Being there left me feeling accepting of the situation. It was important for me to see other relatives and friends, as we shared in joint grief.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week. It mattered a great deal as we were a similar age.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped to close and accept a life well lived.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The service and the celebrant.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in total control as I accepted the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It all went to plan and was well organized by the deceased's children.

situation: A friendship of two years ended abruptly with no explanation, and I was left feeling lost and confused. I wanted to at least have a conversation to know what went wrong, some kind of closure. Instead, I've been feeling so sad, and I don't know what to do. It's a deep sadness that makes my heart ache, and sometimes I'm angry. I felt like I meant nothing to them because being able to abandon a friendship without any word shows how heartless you are.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a week ago, and it meant so much to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me so much that I lose sleep over it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think equally but mostly them.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I wasn't in control at all. I feel like I was ambushed.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The unexpected thing was how they acted after the friendship ended.

situation: I found out that a friend I used to work with had died. I was trying to accept it, but it left me feeling sad and concerned about my mortality and those around me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week and it mattered because we were close friends for many years.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as I had lost a friend. It made me down and depressed.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was just natural.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, as it was not something I could control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: She was not ill so it was completely unexpected.

situation: A group of men came to stay in our village from London, and they were trying to break into cars and houses, which was really intimidating for the residents. This was very scary because things like this don't usually happen around here. I needed to go to the shop, but I knew they were hanging around there, so I decided to go without and stayed at home instead. I also stayed up late, feeling scared in case they tried to break into my home. Living on my own, I felt scared and lonely. This whole situation made me realize I need to make plans, just in case scary things like this ever happen again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 5 days ago. It mattered to me because I should not be made to feel scared in my own home. I moved away from a town to the countryside to avoid experiences like this.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me come up with an emergency escape plan, just in case another situation like this occurs and I need to leave my house. It also made me realize you are not safe anywhere, so it made me scared and unsettled.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The men being threatening and causing the damage were the problem. They decided to do this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control, but others called the police. I was too scared and anxious.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The men got arrested and were not allowed back into the village, so this went well.

situation: A work colleague got very emotional while talking about a traumatic event in their life. I tried to comfort him and let him speak about the experience, offering what support I could at work. Honestly, I felt uncomfortable because strong displays of emotion unnerve me. But I knew it was important to be there for him and provide whatever help I could.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened during a team meeting about mental health. It mattered to me to comfort him because I would class the person as a friend as well as a colleague.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation made me shut down as I do not typically like emotional displays; I'm a somewhat cold person.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The employee was sharing a mental health episode someone close to them had previously that resulted in suicide.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control, nor did I feel I had to be in control. It was important to let them air their emotions in a natural way to them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as expected given the situation.

situation: I was working and chatting with my boss about a problem that wasn't quite going to plan due to some technical difficulties. There was a permit that had an incorrect section. All applicable species should have been listed, but there was one missing. I felt disappointed that it was missed. Making sure the permit was correct was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because it looked bad on me that it wasn't correct.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it disappointed me that a mistake had happened. The only positive aspect was that I picked up the mistake and could rectify it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible as the officer in charge.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I was in charge of this job.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things didn't start as I expected, but I turned things around.

situation: My cousin's son died from a totally unexpected brain hemorrhage, and it was incredibly traumatic, especially since his dad, my cousin, had taken his own life a few years ago. It just seemed so unfair that this could happen to one family. I wasn't trying to do anything in particular; it was just an overall feeling of sadness that overwhelmed me. I didn't need anything, but I felt incredibly sad for the most part. My cousin's suicide had already affected the whole family, as you might expect, and then this - it just seemed so unfair. I reached out to my other cousin, as I am closest to her, to express my condolences, but there's not much you can do in these instances.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered deeply because the kid was just 22 and just starting out on his life as an academic.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help in any way but it hurt me to the extent that there was just nothing to do - just a bad situation all round.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that this death compounded my cousin's suicide and left the whole of his closest family in real pain.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in no way in control as there was no 'control' to have and it wasn't my close family so nothing for me to do to help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: At the moment we are just waiting for the funeral.

situation: I was chatting with a friend online, and they ended up rejecting me. I wanted to meet with them, but they said they didn't want to meet on my terms. This left me feeling numb, sad, and alone. I also felt deceived because my friend was changing what he had told me before.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I was alone at home. It mattered a lot to me as I had been looking forward to it for a long time and now I was suddenly rejected.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me and left me alone.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt it was totally the other person's fault, they were unkind and did not respect me at all.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control, they decided on their own.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did not go as I expected as the other person did not compromise at all.

situation: I had an argument with my partner about my lack of ability to actively plan things with her in mind during my trip with her. She felt that I was just dragging her along to plans rather than actually planning things with her in mind. I was just trying to make the most of my trip as we rarely see each other due to our status as a long-distance couple. The situation left me feeling like I needed to improve a lot more and work on things to become a better person for her and to meet her needs. I also told her that I needed her to also work on her communication abilities.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I rarely get to see her in general and I felt like I was messing things up.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because it helped me to think about what I need to focus on.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I was the most responsible for what had happened because I was planning things.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control in general because I was the one making plans with my friends and girlfriend and I had knowledge of everything.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: In general, I believe things went as I expected. I apologized for what I had done wrong and she also apologized for the argument.

situation: I had surgery, and when I was released from the hospital, I was emotional. I wasn't really trying to do anything, nor did I need anything at that moment. I felt relieved. It was important to me that I survived because I had been worried about that. Also, it was nice to have an end to all the emotional buildup.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me. This was major surgery deemed necessary by the doctors.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me physically insofar as I am now healthier and am not likely to experience complications. It hurt me in the short term as I am now in a lot of pain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control. I was in surgery for a congenital cyst.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: There were some discoveries during the surgery that made it so the surgeon had to do some different things.

situation: I went out with friends for dinner and drinks and then we headed back to one of my friend's house, where his sister was hosting a birthday party. It was my first time going out since I decided to give up alcohol, and everyone else was pretty drunk. I found myself feeling quite shy and within myself. I was really trying to have a good time and be sociable, but I ended up feeling disappointed, like I need a lot more practice. On the bright side, I managed to not drink any alcohol throughout the proceedings, which was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last Saturday. It mattered to me because I had opportunities to have a lot of fun and further relationships.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Made me feel unconfident and dependant on alcohol, but also that I will get better with time and I'm strong enough to not drink despite the drawbacks.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself, wanting to stay sober.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in terms of not drinking, but emotionally I felt like the situation overawed me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was unsure what to expect to be honest.

situation: I was emotional as I watched my nephew play live in his school band. I went to see him at the school, and he was playing drums in the band live in performance for the first time. I really wanted to watch him perform live, and seeing him up there brought a tear to my eyes and a funny feeling in my stomach. He's quite young, only 10 years old, and it was a proud moment for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when my nephew performed live in his school band for the first time. It mattered to me because I really wanted to watch him perform live, and seeing him brought a tear to my eyes and a funny feeling in my stomach. It was a proud moment for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was positive for me. I was happy and proud.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My nephew was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, it was his performance.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected.

situation: It was a weekend afternoon, and my partner and I were enjoying some time at a nearby community park. We were having a great moment, doing some minor running to ensure I stay physically fit. As we were running, we unexpectedly bumped into a long-term friend. I felt quite excited to meet them, and the happy moments we shared were amazing. We loved this.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This occurred over the last Sunday. It was a great moment to cherish and make some memories.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was helpful to meet a long-term friend.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It just happened because we were out there having good times.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We were both in control of everything that happened.

situation: I found out that one of the people who recently interviewed me as part of a panel had a personal relationship with the successful candidate. Even though I have extensive direct experience for the role, this discovery made me feel quite angry and depressed. It was like realizing that no matter how good I was at the role, I was never going to be chosen. There wasn't anything specific that I wanted or needed from the situation, just a level of disappointment. I also suspect that they didn't declare this relationship to HR, as I believe they should have.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened in the last couple of weeks. It mattered a lot to me as this was a job I was and still am a subject matter expert in.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it was embarrassing and meant I had basically wasted my time trying to prove myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The person who was advertising the role and who was my direct manager and part of the interview panel.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Well not in control but I thought I had an equal chance at the role. So an element of control. But it was quite clear on reflection that I had no control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I suppose that it didn't go as expected as I expected to be treated fairly - and upon reflection it is quite clear that other factors were brought into play. That is even clearer as the weeks go by as the person who got the role is in no way evidently more effective than me.

situation: This week, I arrived home from work and my son said his first word. I was ecstatic—out it came, his first word! I didn't want anything else in that moment; I just wanted to absorb the enjoyment. I was amazed, overawed with proudness! This moment felt like a total change in life for me. I have never been so proud of anything in my entire life, and I don't think I will ever experience such a feeling again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened on Tuesday night around 6pm - It meant the world to me as it was my only child's first words.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation made me feel such positive emotion, it has helped me enjoy the little things in life a lot more.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son was responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I definitely did not feel in control but I did not need to be in control, I was just living in the moment and enjoying every second of it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: All of it was unexpected, I had no expectations or thoughts that he was going to speak at any point soon, this was a complete and inspiring surprise.

situation: I saw my father for the first time since 2023. He doesn't live locally, so I seldom see him. He messaged out of the blue to say he could pop in and see me at work as he was in the area. It was just a chance for us to connect in person and talk. Obviously, my father is an important person in my life, and it was good to see him. Our meeting was pleasant, and he was in good spirits, which made it a positive experience for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened after a 26-month gap since I last saw my father, which mattered quite a bit to me because it's important to stay in contact with him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by making me feel more connected and nostalgic.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I saw my Dad a lot more when I was younger, so it conjured up a lot of memories from the past.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt partially in control. I was at work, so I had to disappear at times to do tasks, but he was okay about it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went probably better than I expected. He was in a good mood and not rushing off after a few minutes.

situation: My son and his girlfriend ended their relationship, and I found myself lending a sympathetic ear. I felt sad for them, knowing how tough breakups can be. While it hasn't really affected me directly, I'm concerned for their mental health and want to make sure they're both okay.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event did not matter too much to me, but I could see they were upset.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because they split up. It made me feel sad for them, but it didn’t affect me in other ways. I just got on with my life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son, as he couldn’t be bothered in the end in the relationship.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, as I wasn’t directly involved.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected.

situation: I'm involved in this prayer group, but I feel like they don't truly understand who I am. They constantly shower me with praise, and honestly, I can't believe they really think that highly of me. I would rather they be open and honest with me. This whole situation makes my heart feel heavy. I feel like they're afraid to say anything negative, and that's important to me because I want genuine interactions.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened this past Thursday. It actually mattered a great deal because if they are being disingenuous I would rather separate myself from the group.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It affected my trust as well as my mood. I do not know if my interactions in the future can be transparent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The new lady in the group Sarah.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control, but Sarah comes off like she is more knowledgeable than the rest of the group, so the others then agree with her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No!! I couldn’t believe how the others acted as if she knew it all simply because she had been at the church the longest.

situation: I had to sit with an athlete who was diagnosed with a torn ACL. She initially thought it was just a sprain, but it turned out the ligament had torn. Mostly, I just sat and waited to see if she had any questions. I told her she was strong and would come back even better than before the injury. I felt sad for her, knowing there would be lots more ups and downs in the recovery, and it would take a while for her to get back. Since she lives far away from the school and her parents couldn't be there, I believed it was important to have an adult there to show support.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I feel this is part of what my job is as a head coach of the team and to show each individual athlete and in turn the team support.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I do not think it helped or hurt. Part of job and the ups and downs of being a coach. I have to stay level headed and think about whole group.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just an injury, no one's fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control on how I reacted to show the person support who was in a much harder situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they did, just sad to think the athlete will not be able to play their sport for a while.

situation: I went to my future baby's scan, hoping that everything would be great healthwise. I felt happy because everything is going smoothly. It was important to me that my partner felt fine emotionally too.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Tuesday last week and it mattered because when you have a new baby, you want it to be completely healthy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me feel more content and relaxed about the baby's wellbeing and that everything is on track.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My partner as she is holding the baby but then also myself for contributing to her wellbeing and helping her feel comfortable.
appraisal_reasoning.control: To some extent we were not in control as we relied on medical staff, but we had control in the ability to see the medical staff in the first place.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went perfectly as expected which is great.
