situation: My dog got into a bunch of chocolate cookies, and I was really worried about him. I was scared he might develop bloating from eating all the plastic they were stored in, or even pancreatitis. I felt very scared and concerned, and I'm also worried that he might do it again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered greatly to me because I was really worried that he would die.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me very anxious.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all because he is very sneaky.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because he vomited up all the plastic, which I wasn't expecting.

situation: I was waiting for the bus and felt anxious about going to work. I was trying to go to work like a normal person, but honestly, I needed the day off. The whole situation left me feeling drained and tired. It's just something I deal with.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot, as it's a day to day thing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel inept.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No specific person.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was somewhat in control, once I concentrated on what was important.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing was unexpected.

situation: My dog has been having a skin issue that got much worse this past week, and I was really worried about her. I had to take her to the vet because she looked like she was really declining. I wanted to figure out what was going on so I could fix it, but I was frustrated with my inability to solve the problem myself. Plus, I was concerned about not wanting to pay a huge vet bill.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened this past week. It mattered a lot to me because I don't want my dog to suffer.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt to see my dog suffer and to have to pay a vet bill for her to get better.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She is my animal, I feel responsible for her care.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt mostly in control as it was me who decided to treat her and when I could not resolve the situation myself to take her to the vet. However, once at the vet I felt I didn't have much control over the cost.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The vet visit went better than I expected and I'm happy I found a really good vet who doesn't charge high fees.

situation: I was in a shop, queueing to buy some milk. There were two tills open, both protected by perspex with suitable openings for the cashier to take money. While I was waiting, I noticed an elderly gentleman at the furthest till who seemed confused about how to use his bank card. He accidentally dropped his phone, and the woman being served next to him, who looked to be around 30, picked up his phone and kindly explained how to use his card. Once everything was sorted, the elderly gentleman was so grateful that he hugged the woman. Watching this sweet interaction made me feel good and happy. It seemed like the entire queue and the cashiers were experiencing the same feel-good moment.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened two evenings ago, around 7pm. It mattered because everyone seemed to appreciate the situation. No-one got impatient. It mattered because the elderly gentleman was willing to accept help and showed gratitude, and the woman, though she picked up his phone immediately, was obviously hesitant about interfering with his bank card. She tried at first a verbal explanation; but then the elderly gentleman indicated that he trusted her to take his card and do the transaction on his behalf.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was a reminder that it's okay to ask for help, it's okay to offer help. The queue moved forwards. I was served by the cashier who'd served the elderly gent. I'd interacted with this cashier only once before.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that both the elderly man and the younger woman were equally responsible. But if I had to choose, I would say the elderly gentleman seemed very sweet. He was obviously a little confused, but he remained calm and accepted help graciously.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was a witness to this episode. The only control I had was to wait patiently and demonstrate with a smile etc that I was willing to wait. I could have acted differently, showed impatience, but I chose to see the interaction for what it was.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect the hug at the end. The old gentleman thanked the woman profusely, then opened his arms, and she moved in for the hug. So that was all extra sweet and uplifting.

situation: I went to see a bungalow that we wanted to buy. It was absolutely perfect, a lovely home with a beautiful garden and a large garage. We live in a 3 storey house and my wife struggles with the stairs, so we were looking for a bungalow. The bungalow was also in a pretty town on the edge of Dartmoor, which made it even more appealing. But then we found out that an offer had been made and accepted, so we were too late. I felt pretty sad and flat.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened today. We have been looking to move for some time. It's important because my wife struggles with all the stairs in our current home.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I suppose it helped in a way by making us look at areas where we hadn't considered moving to before and it hurt us because the bungalow we saw would have been ideal for us.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible. I think it was just bad luck, but if it's meant to be, it will happen.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I was not in control. We were willing to pay more, but our house hasn't sold yet, so we are helpless until we get a buyer.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it didn't. We were hoping to be able to make an offer and hopefully move fairly quickly.

situation: I'm moving on from goal planning and don't feel the need to map out my future anymore, which is actually a positive experience for me. There are some negative emotions tied to it because my family hasn't been that supportive. They still expect me to journal about my future plans, and I was hoping they'd be more understanding. They don't seem willing to change their habits or personalities and still label me as having issues. I've been communicating with them through my journal, letting them know what I'm up to, but they still think they can manipulate my future for their own benefit. They can't use my intrusive thoughts against me or manipulate my future if I stop talking about it. Their main goal seems to be pushing me into the peer support industry. I'm managing my anxiety through journaling, which helps break down the cysts in my hands. I don't want to keep doing this forever, and I'm planning to move on from it soon. Journaling helps me move on from my past, and I have a positive outlook on the future. I understand my finances and am ready to move forward if certain areas of my life improve. It's all in my control, and no one can change that. Once I feel I've made progress, I'll do what's necessary to move. Moving on from the past is a great goal for my near future. My priorities when journaling aren't about planning my finances, body, or career; they're focused on mental health, which I'll also need to put behind me soon. My old journals and goal plans are unfolding as I intended, and my priority now is to move on from this dopamine detox. I'll work on improving my cardiovascular health slowly over the next year. Privacy might help with improving my overall health, and I might need my own place to speed up this process when it feels necessary.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: A couple of my ex-family members are now suffering and they lied about their age. My aunt is a little older than my father, and my Uncle David is younger than my aunt. She's getting old, and I'm very happy that she's now suffering from her lack of self-control. She should've left me alone, and I cannot change what I planned for my future. My sister, father, and mother have a say in this, and she doesn't account for what they want. A lot of guidance that I've received is with the input of my family members in the north. She blames it on me when everyone that I just mentioned were the ones that want it this way. She doesn't respect my decision-making skills, and that's also disrespecting the family that I mentioned.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has helped me because people that I once knew were relying on my old goal plan. I don't ever want to talk to them anymore now that I'm better off financially and physically. Removing negative influences from my life improved my future. The ex-family shouldn't try to counter my plans that I made for myself over the next twenty years. I had a lot of guidance from my cousins from northern California, and they don't want me to see certain personalities in the south. My southern California members are understanding, but they're also selfish with what they want. They're worried about their future because they lost too much time over the last 10 years. They cannot ever let go of the past at this stage of their life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The ones that are responsible for this are the people in my ex-family that live outside of San Diego. They don't understand anything at their age. They don't account for what other people need, and they shouldn't make plans for my future if it doesn't fit my personality. They don't understand how to raise a good kid. Her offspring all took on her personality traits, and bad parenting is common in their bloodline.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I'm in control of my future, and her attitude is toxic. She dragged down everyone else in the family with her selfish ambitions. I control everything now that I changed my personality to fit my family. I moved on from the past, and I can look the other way for what happened. They don't want to look at it like it's a major change. They still want to judge me for my plans for the future. She doesn't love or respect anyone outside of the family, and I was told that she was caught red-handed. She was talking about ruining everyone else in the family for her own son and daughter. She told her husband that no one else matters but her family and her grandkids.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was expecting a resolution to all of the problems that I created for my family. I was positive about my future when I first moved out, and I made the first attempt to resolve the situation. I used my uncle to my advantage and looked the other way when he didn't respond. My deceitful ex-family members did everything that they could to ruin my relationships within the family. No one really cares about what I journal about because it's all a big delusion. Not everything is a delusion, and I still need to judge people for how they treated me in the past. My ex-aunt was always a demoralizing personality that didn't understand to respect other people. I need to judge their past actions and use my intrusive thoughts to my advantage.

situation: My dog has finally received the all clear from the vets after undergoing major surgery a couple of months ago. When the vet told us she was going to be fine, I felt emotional, but in a good way. I really needed the surgeon to be competent and fix my dog's injury, and then I needed reassurance that she would be okay once she had time to heal. I was hopeful for good news because I could see how well she was recovering, but I was nervous until we got the all clear from the vets. I was also prepared for more vet bills, which made me anxious. The long-term prognosis was important to me because if she wasn't recovering, we wouldn't be able to go on holiday with her or plan for the year ahead.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in mid December and it mattered hugely to me as the dog is a huge part of our lives and we will be so sad when she isn't with us any more.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has hurt us financially as the insurance cover we had did not cover the full extent of the vet's bills, but we are fine with that as she is our world.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The groomer who injured her was responsible and we are trying to get legal recompense.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, we were not in control at all. The control was put into the surgeon's hands and the outcome was down to him and his team, which was scary for us.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went 100% as we had hoped and she recovered pretty well afterwards, but the first few days after she came home were difficult as we were used to her running around and playing and obviously she was still partly sedated and in some degree of pain whilst she healed.

situation: I was not doing the productive things in my life to help out. I needed to help out with the house chores, exercise my body, make money online, and work on my art. Once I accomplish these things daily, I feel more alert and happy throughout the day. If I do these things every day, they will add up, providing me with a sense of purpose.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was yesterday. The day before I did nothing, and felt depressed. This feeling leaked into my personal relationship with my girlfriend, in a negative way, making her and myself unhappy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I didn't want to feel depressed anymore. So, yesterday, I became proactive and began to follow a list of goals I wanted to accomplish that day. Once I did everything on the list, I felt better, and that improved the way I came at my relationship with my girlfriend, making us both happy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Not having the motivation to do the things I need to do every day.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel more in control of my day when I do things that I think matter in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything felt better once I finished my chores. This was the outcome I was expecting for accomplishing my goals.

situation: My wife and I have this little tradition where we buy scratch-off tickets from the gas station each week just for fun. This time, we both won; she got $15 and I got $10, which was awesome. Even though it wasn't a huge amount, it felt great to finally win. The whole experience made us feel good and was really positive. We were just trying to have fun and enjoy some time together, and winning money was a nice bonus. It made me feel like a winner, and spending that time with my wife was really cool.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened this past Friday. It mattered a lot to me because it was an overall positive experience that had a good thing happen after a long week.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by providing me with more money, of course, but also a positive experience.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I would say we were, because we were the ones that bought the tickets.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes and no. We knew we were going to buy the tickets, but we couldn't control whether we won.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, we weren't expecting to win, but we did.

situation: My Nan recently passed away. It wasn't unexpected since she was 92 years old, but it was still a moment to reflect on her life. She lived a great life, traveling the world and getting to see six great-grandkids. It's left me feeling sad that she's gone, but also thankful for the life she lived. It was important to me that she passed peacefully and comfortably.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 weeks ago, and it mattered a great deal to me as she was an important figure in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me emotionally as I was grieving from the loss.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don’t think anyone’s responsible, death is guaranteed. She’d lived a great life, better than most people could wish for.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel in control, the death was expected. And I regulated my emotions well.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected as it could when a loved one passes.

situation: I had a big argument with my partner about housework, and I was really out of my comfort zone because I'm not very good at arguments. My partner is quite hot-headed, which meant the argument escalated to an unnecessary level. I don't respond well in these situations, so I needed a calmer way to deal with it. To try and diffuse things, I decided to remove myself from the immediate space because I needed peace. The whole situation left me feeling stressed, anxious, and upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened on Monday, it was a very big deal to me as I'd already had a really difficult day at work and was not emotionally prepared for a big argument. The issue was menial however was escalated way beyond the initial point.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as hurtful things were said and we were not acting like a partnership.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The initial issue was a joint issue however my partner took it to a level it did not need to go to.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I'm very out of my comfort zone in arguments so I never feel in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It lasted for longer than expected but once resolved it was as normal.

situation: I had heard that someone was talking about me behind my back. I was trying to work out what they were saying and how to sort the situation. It made me angry. It was causing issues with other people as well.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 days ago and it mattered quite a bit to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt my feelings and made me angry.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: One person telling another things about me that I did not do was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt that it was outside of my control as I could not explain things to people.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected and I had to go after and sort it out.

situation: It was the 4th anniversary of the death of my daughter, and I was trying to support my wife while keeping my own head in line. The day left me feeling exhausted and very sad. I was also trying to remember the positives about what we experienced with her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on the 4th anniversary of my daughter's death. It mattered greatly to me because it was important to remember her so she's never forgotten.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as it's always a painful time of year. It made it very difficult to concentrate on my day-to-day life, and my work suffered, although I don't see that as important.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that my thoughts wandering elsewhere were responsible for the difficulty in focusing, not seeing the importance of other things.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I tried to control it as much as I could, for the sake of my and my wife's feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. I managed to keep on top of most things and helped my wife through it.

situation: My little brother reached the milestone of turning 18, and I traveled to visit my family so we could celebrate together. We wanted to mark this special occasion and I was eager to be present and enjoy the time with everyone. The experience left me feeling truly joyful. It was crucial for me to be there, and it was wonderful that everyone made the effort to gather on this significant day.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot, seeing that he is quite younger than me, the fact that he is turning 18 was very strange as I have always seen him as my little baby brother. But he is now an adult, so we were talking about the times he was a baby and all the cute moments.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me reminisce the past with my family.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were all responsible, we all had different memories that we brought up.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I did. Well yes it's a party, and I was there so.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was expected.

situation: My friend promised he was coming over for dinner, but he never turned up. I thought I was going to get some company for the evening, but as the night passed, he didn't come around or even bother to let me know. I felt empty and a little bit upset. It was important to me because I had cooked dinner for him.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Saturday night. It mattered to me because I cooked dinner for them and could have gone out elsewhere if I had known that they weren't coming.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me that they didn't let me know so I could have made alternative plans.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: They are inconsistent and impolite.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all, just left waiting.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not at all, they didn't contact me until the next day.

situation: I went to a football match and we won. It was so fun. I needed a win so we could save the world, since the whole world was watching hating us for what we were. It made me feel anxious and annoyed but we got through in the end.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me as it has been a painful 6 years of process.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation made me feel accepted and welcomed in the community.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was mainly the institution that was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control because I was a spectator in all this on the sidelines as it always has been.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went unexpected because that is how it always is with us.

situation: My niece was admitted to the hospital, and I was trying to keep in touch with her mother, my sister, to understand why she was there and what was being done. I stayed in touch and offered support to both her and my sister. I felt worried, but being able to offer some help gave me a sense of purpose, even though I felt a bit helpless since there wasn't much I could do to help my niece.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week, I received a text from my sister. It mattered a lot, since we are all close.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help or hurt me, except that I was worried and that made me anxious.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My niece was the cause of my worry, but through no fault of her.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control, since there was nothing I could do, except offer verbal support at that time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected, she had some tests done and was released a few days later.

situation: I made a mistake at work that got me in trouble. I spilled a drink on a customer while I was trying to give it to them. It left me feeling really upset because the customer wouldn't accept my apology, which was distressing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened at work in a bar when I tripped while carrying the drinks. It mattered to me because it left me feeling really upset, especially since the customer wouldn't accept my apology.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it made me upset and I got in trouble with my manager.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control during the incident because I tripped.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected.

situation: My dog passed away in my arms, and it was extremely traumatic for me. He's been with me since I was a kid and into adulthood, and I've never felt loss like that before. In that situation, it was hard to do anything, but all I could do was be there for him in his last moments, making sure he wasn't alone and never was. I'm left feeling totally broken because he was my best friend and loved me unconditionally, so I owed him the same. It's important to me that the pain I feel for a loved one dying means I truly cared for them. I'd rather feel the pain so he's with me forever.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 6 months ago. It mattered greatly to me because my dog had dementia, was scared, and aggressively bit me. Despite the pain, it was important to me that the pain I feel for a loved one dying means I truly cared for them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I realized he had to be put down. I have kids, and I couldn't let that happen to them, no matter how much I loved my dog.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It's not anyone's fault; it's just life at the end of the day.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control after the incident. I made the decision that will probably haunt me for a while, but it was for the greater good. He was suffering a lot longer than I was when it happened.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect how vivid and stressful it would be watching him get put down. Nothing prepares you for that.

situation: Last week, I booked flights back to my home country to visit my family. I'm taking my girlfriend and my best friend with me. I haven't seen my family for a while, so it'll be really nice to have a holiday and just relax back there with them. I was trying to find flights for the cheapest price and the best dates, needing it to be at least 14 days and under 1200 pounds return. I left feeling very good as I was able to successfully get both cheap flights and 16 days of holiday.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Monday, and it mattered to me a great deal because I want my girlfriend to meet my parents, I want my best friend to meet my family, and I wanted to see my family again after a long time living apart.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because I now have dates that I will be going to see my family. I can look forward to this.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was the most responsible for this as I organised everything from budget to dates to experiences whilst we are there.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yeah, I did feel in control. Everything I searched for managed to work out. Every criteria I had was met.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as expected. I got the flights for a good price. The dates lined up perfectly for everyone and we managed to book some experiences for a good price too.

situation: I watched a film that made me feel emotional about the loss of my parents in the future. The film depicted a person slipping deeper into dementia, which was very sad. I needed some comfort because the film was very sad. It made me think I should speak to my parents more before it is too late. I really enjoyed the film; it was very thought-provoking and shot in a very realistic way.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I watched the film three weeks ago on a weekend. The realism struck a chord with me the most.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me think about things in a different way and almost gave me a better understanding of getting older.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible as I chose what film to watch at the time.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in full control as I could have stopped the film at any time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was much more emotional than I thought it was going to be and was so realistic seeing the feelings of loneliness and loss.

situation: I was doing a spring clean at home, clearing out some boxes of paperwork and memories. As I was going through the items, I came across some things related to someone who passed away 18 months ago. Seeing these items brought back a lot of memories, and I found myself feeling quite sad. I was trying to have a clear out, but I stopped to pause and look at some of the items. I'm not really sure what I needed or wanted in that moment, maybe someone to talk to about it. The situation left me feeling sad, as it reminded me of things I miss about that person.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday, and it mattered to me a lot because I hadn't looked at these things for a long time and had forgotten some of the memories associated with them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was both painful and comforting. The reminder of the loss itself was very painful, and I felt more emotion than I expected, with a lot of memories of that person coming back very vividly. On the other hand, it was nice to have tangible reminders, and I felt fortunate to have good memories and shared good times with this person when they were alive.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think grief is responsible for that.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control. I chose to look at those things and wanted to be in the moment.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I felt more emotional than I expected I would; my reaction was stronger.

situation: I had a great time at my kids' high school basketball game. The crowd was rowdy, and the girls' game was intense. I was there to cheer for the Timberwolves, but I also needed to understand the game a little more, so I ended up talking to a really nice opposing fan. I felt great, especially because the other fans were awesome too. It was important for me to support my children who play in the band, and it was great to see them with their friends having fun.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot, because my wife was with me too, and we were there as a family. We rarely do things outside the home as a family, so it was a beautiful experience. The kids even spent extra time at home with us after the game that evening talking about the game and all the fun we had.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me bring back memories of my own high school and middle school sports activities. It also strengthened the bond in our family, and it felt good to support my kids.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was mostly responsible for getting my wife and I to the game because it was my idea that we should attend to support the school and our kids.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt very in control. I decided the time we would leave and I drove us there.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected. The game was very engaging, and it was fun interacting with our kids and the game and at home afterward.

situation: Workers drove an hour to deliver a storm shelter, but it was too wet from the rain the night before for them to install it. I needed them to install it, but they couldn't get to the slab for it. The whole situation left me feeling angry.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event just happened and it matters a great deal to me because I paid a lot of money for it and tornado season is here.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because now they have to come back. I have severe anxiety and hate to wait.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Rain last night.
appraisal_reasoning.control: If they had been told it had rained, they would have brought proper equipment.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. They had to leave and take the shelter back to return later.

situation: We saw our supreme leader, Sir Rodney, telling us how our energy bills are coming down as is inflation. Strangely, my new energy bill landed the same day, and it's exactly three times what it was 28 months ago. We've just had another winter without heating, so it's pretty emotional when your leader lies to your face and has been actively trying to kill us pensioners since he got the job. I need a Reform UK PM ASAP, as along with the ever-increasing food inflation, we now miss some meals. We are and have been for many months now distraught. My wife is disabled. She feels the cold, and life is very tough. It's as bad as it can get, I reckon. Nothing to be done that is within my power. If I get a job and stop looking after my wife, I just lose my rent help and get a tax bill, so we just carry on cutting things out of our life.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It started when Bozzer locked the country down and crashed the economy, and we saw that tougher times were coming as inflation and profiteering got out of control. Now we have a Marxist regime and a chancellor who knows nothing of economics but much about Marxist dogma and hatred of anyone with funds or ambition. There is only one way this can keep going.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: We abandoned all leisure and pleasure a long time ago as debt is not a solution and keep cutting back to make ends meet. Many of my friends are in the same boat.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Politicians making the wrong decisions about where our country should be heading. Sadly there is no money for the likes of us, but illegal rapists and criminals from low IQ Neanderthal countries that have nothing to offer but hate have a line of credit as long as they want.
appraisal_reasoning.control: They say money does not make you happy! Rubbish! It does, and when you need 20 quid for food and there is 2 quid left, there is no legit way out of that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was all expected. The actions of the Tory destruction of the economy had very obvious outcomes, and to put Marxist higher taxes and bad policies in place just compounds the situation. All clear to see and predict, and if you have a big bank balance, you can ride it or afford to get out. We don't!

situation: A dear friend of mine had a terrible accident where she fell and broke her neck in two places, along with her tailbone, hip, and pelvis. She also has COPD, and the hospital overdosed her twice, making her oxygen levels very bad and hard to control. I've been following her situation closely and talking to her, but she's not out of the woods yet. I sent her a bear that says 'I f...... love you,' which is a good support for her neck and cheers her up. It's tough because I live in Michigan and she lives in Oklahoma, so I can't see her in person. I have COPD too, so I guess I'm more worried about the pain she's going through and the unstable oxygen levels she's experiencing, along with her lungs filling up. I just don't want her to be in pain.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on February 18 at around 5:00. It mattered to me greatly because I was totally shocked and dismayed. It hurt me because I couldn't be there and I couldn't care for her. I think I was put on this earth to care for people and animals. I cared and helped take care of my BFF for years, my father, my mother, and a few others. I enjoy taking care of them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I couldn't be there and I couldn't care for her. I think I was put on this earth to care for people and animals. I cared and helped take care of my BFF for years, my father, my mother, and a few others. I enjoy taking care of them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel bad because her foot went asleep while we were talking on the phone for about 2 hours. She got up and fell.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. She is there and I am here. I couldn't control the situation. I know it isn't her time yet. It is a miracle from God that she is still here. It brings back the bad memories of when I had to help decide if the plug should get pulled on my BFF. That was agonizing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things look like they are on track now. I am breathing easier knowing that they are getting her stable.

situation: My daughter told me she's now in a position to move out of home and quite a distance away. I'm really happy for her because she had been extremely unwell for a long time, and I honestly didn't think she would ever live independently. I've always wanted her to get well and live a fabulous life. It's a bittersweet moment for me. I'm delighted for her, but I feel a bit redundant now. I'll miss her terribly, though. Even though she has a new job to start and a partner to move in with, I'm nervous in case things go wrong for her. I'm also aware that I'm going to have to rebuild my own life after such a traumatic 8 years of severe illness she suffered.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: She received the paperwork she needs to begin her new job last week, and so she was excited to know she can move. I am excited too, but it is tinged with a little sadness; my baby girl is flying the nest!
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It only hurts because I will miss her terribly. It's positive for me in that she is recovered and thriving, and I will have space to heal from the trauma of thinking she would die.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was all her, I think, and her girlfriend. They are very much in love, which is so beautiful.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, my daughter is an adult. I can only support her decision.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was surprised and happy at how quickly she got her DBS back, which means she can work with vulnerable people.

situation: A coworker shared some updates about upcoming changes at my workplace, and it was a challenging conversation emotionally. I was absorbing the details about these difficult changes to our business, and it left me feeling unsettled.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week in the morning. It mattered a lot because some of how our workplace functions is changing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It removes part of what the entire business does. Not really right now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Poor management at the top, and changing market condition.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not in control at all. I had no say in the matter, and change is always hard.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, not as expected. I expected our business would remain the same for the next several years, but now this change is coming now.

situation: My daughter had her final parents evening before leaving school for good, and she got amazing feedback, which made us feel very proud and it made me a bit emotional. I was trying to find out how she had been doing at school and whether she is on track to do well in her exams. I wanted feedback from her teachers. I felt very proud and happy due to how she was doing. I also felt a little sad that it was her last parents evening ever and that she would be leaving school. It was just important for me to be there to hear what the teachers had to say and to fully engage in what was going on as it was her last parents evening.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it felt quite significant so I would say that it mattered to me quite a lot. It felt significant as there would never be another chance to get feedback from her teachers as she is going to be leaving school.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me to understand how she was doing and what her likely grades would be. It didn't hurt me at all as it was a very positive situation but it was bittersweet in a way.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I thought that my daughter was partly responsible due to the hard work she had put in and that her teachers were also responsible due to their helping her.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was really in control as I was really just listening to feedback and how things were going. I was quite passive in the situation other than listening.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes they did mostly go as expected. If anything the feedback was even better than we expected.

situation: A member of my family went to a private hospital for a scan, and due to negligence, they ended up with a major burn. This was really upsetting and stressful for my family. The burn was severe enough that it required a visit to a specialized burn unit, and they had to be put on antibiotics and morphine. Every other day, the burn needs to be dressed, which adds to the stress. What we really wanted was an explanation about how and why this happened. The whole situation left me feeling extremely upset and stressed. I couldn't sleep and had to take time off work for hospital visits. It's important to me to get answers about why this happened in the first place and to ensure that it doesn't happen to anyone else.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because my family member was in extreme pain, and it was very upsetting to see.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me mentally and emotionally, creating a stressful environment.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the private hospital was responsible, either due to an inexperienced person conducting the scan or faulty equipment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt completely not in control of the situation in any way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The investigation is ongoing, and we will have to wait for answers, which was unexpected.

situation: I was running to a selection board to find out if I would be given an extension in my job contract. I was really hoping to be selected based on my annual reports, but I didn't get it, which was pretty upsetting. Out of 29 people, I placed 20th, and only the top 5 were offered the contract extension. I felt sad that I didn't get it and even more upset about placing fairly low. It was important to me to be recognized for my hard work, which I felt I had earned. I didn't really think I would be offered the extension, but I did expect to place higher than I did.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered some to me. I did not think I would get it and I have many other opportunities over the next few years, but my low placement was disappointing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt my feelings as I felt I had performed better than was indicated.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel the system is unfair and not geared for those fairly new to the job. It puts more weight on you being close to the end of your current contract.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I am in control of how I perform but not in how that performance is judged.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes and no. The overall result was as expected but not how low I placed.

situation: We recently had to make the difficult decision to put our cat down. She was an outdoor/indoor cat who developed a bad cough, so we took her to the vet. We were really hoping there could be a cure that we could afford, but it was very tough because, in the end, she was suffering, and it would have cost too much to even try and make her better. My wife was devastated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: She has been under the weather for a few weeks. The event mattered to me because it was a challenging time, and we were really hoping there could be a cure that we could afford.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: At the end, it gave us peace of mind that she will not be suffering anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: When you have an outdoor cat, there is always the chance this could happen.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It was hard to even get her into a crate to go to the vet, and she was suffering. I faced challenges in feeling in control during this time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: We were hoping for a cure but knew going in that the result could be putting her down. We were prepared for the possibility of having to make a difficult decision, even though we were hoping for a different outcome.

situation: A close friend's sister was diagnosed with Leukemia, and it really shook me. I was in the middle of arranging to meet my friend, but now her time is consumed with hospital visits. I wanted to be there for her emotionally, to support her through this tough time. Hearing the news left me feeling upset for her and shocked and unsettled myself. It's been hard because I'm also dealing with family health issues of my own, but I'm trying my best to offer support.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened while I was messaging my friend about my own family health issues, and it came out of the blue, knocking us both for six. It mattered to me because her sister's situation is obviously a lot worse than my own issues, and it's shocking to have someone you know personally suffering in this way.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me realize that others have their own issues, which can be worse than mine, putting my own issues into perspective. However, it has also made my worries and concerns even worse.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible; it’s life. I’m just struggling with how to deal with it all.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I have no sense of control over these situations or how my brain is now permanently set to ‘catastrophising’ every little thing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, we never expected to get the news about her sister.

situation: I was just killing time the other day and came across the Olympics on TV. I started watching, and when the American athlete won the gold medal, it made me emotional. I couldn't help but think about all the practice and effort they must have gone through to achieve that victory. It was an unexpected response, but it just felt emotional. I think some things can't always be explained, and trying to overanalyze them can take away from the experience.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened the other day when I was watching the Olympics on TV. It mattered to me in an unexpected way because I had a moment of pride for the American athlete who won the gold medal, although it didn't have any significance that I can think of.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was an enjoyable moment, nothing more, nothing less.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I guess I am most responsible for allowing my emotions to show.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I never really thought about it that much in depth, but upon reflection, my emotional response felt more spontaneous.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I watched a program, saw them win, and got emotional. It was an unexpected response, but I can't say much more about it.

situation: I got my driving license back after a ban. I really wanted to get my license back so I could drive again. When I finally got it, I felt pleased but also nervous.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I got it through the post and it meant a start to getting my independence back.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I won't be as reliant on other people. However, I faced a lack of confidence driving.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control as I didn't make the decision.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The process did not go as I expected because it took longer.

situation: I finally got a phone call from my adult son who is in prison. He wasn't allowed to contact anyone for 30 days, and he finally got transferred, so I was able to talk to him. I really needed to hear that he was okay because not hearing from him for such a long time made me worry that something happened to him. Talking to him left me feeling happy and joyful, but still kind of sad because he doesn't deserve to be in prison. The most important thing was the relief of hearing his voice instead of just wondering in my head if he was hurt.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This was very recent and mattered to me a great deal because I have been waiting for what seems like an eon to hear his voice again. Also, today is one year since he went to jail.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped to ease my mind about whether he was hurt or injured.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The person responsible for this was a person that made false accusations against my son and the court system believing her. That is the person responsible for all of it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel out of control all the time about this. I just want to go get him and bring him home but I can't and I feel helpless.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: If you are talking about the phone call and hearing from him then yes, things went as expected.

situation: I've known this woman for a long time because she's a close friend of my closest friend. We've always been polite to each other, but we've never really hit it off. Over the years, she's treated me rudely and ignored me in public, which is super awkward and always makes me feel upset. Her poor treatment of me has gotten worse over the past few years. Recently, at a party, she tried to avoid saying hello to me, and I ended up focusing on her the whole time and emotionally shutting down. I was trying to enjoy myself at the party and wanted to set better emotional boundaries so her behavior wouldn't affect me, but my feelings get hurt every time. I felt hurt, angry, and upset with myself for letting it get to me so much. I want to spend less time around her, but I know there will be questions since our friend group is pretty small, and I don't want to put my closest friend in the middle. This situation is similar to what has happened many times before.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened two days ago. It matters to me because when this woman treats me this way, I feel that she is trying to exclude me from the group. This is an old trigger for me which stems from how I was treated in my family of origin. So it mattered a lot to me because it brought up old feelings in addition to how I felt about the current situation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help me. It hurt me because I felt that I was not accepted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The woman I am talking about.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel like I was in control. When I first arrived and it was obvious she was ignoring me and greeting everyone else warmly, I decided to force the issue so I went over and said hello and hugged her. I then felt annoyed with myself because I felt like I had given in.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected except that I didn't expect to feel so hurt by behavior I've encountered many times.

situation: I volunteer at a pony charity that helps young people with learning disabilities experience riding. Recently, someone cut the fences, and the ponies escaped. We managed to retrieve them, but they had puncture wounds and were clearly traumatized. Now, the ponies need time to rest and heal, which means the children are missing out on this valuable experience. We have to cover the vet bills and repair the fences, so we've all come together to help the ponies recover and fix the damage. It's really sad to see the ponies and the children affected like this, but I'm relieved it wasn't worse, like a car accident involving the loose ponies.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last Tuesday, and it mattered so much because I love the ponies.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt that someone was so thoughtless.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Person or persons unknown.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No not in control at all.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The ponies are recovering as hoped.

situation: I visited my daughter's house and saw the grandkids. We hugged, and I noticed how quickly they are growing up. I wanted to spend time with my family and feel connected, and I also wanted to see the kids and catch up. I felt happy and a little sad at the same time, which I don't know why. I also felt content and a bit aware of how fast time is passing. I don't take these moments for granted. I want to be present when I'm with them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered quite a bit to me because family time does not happen as often as I'd like, and I value staying connected.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by reminding me what matters. It did not really hurt; it just reminded me how quickly things change.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't think anyone was responsible. It was just life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel any way really, in control or not.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected, it was fun. We talked for long.

situation: My sister unexpectedly passed away, and I was trying to understand why it happened. I wanted an explanation as to why and how she died. The situation left me feeling guilty that I wasn't there for her more to help her with her struggles and her health. It was important to me that I was there for my dad and my brother during this difficult time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When the event happened it mattered to me a lot because I was hoping that she would get better and when I heard that she passed away it was hard to accept it as reality.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I am no longer going to be able to speak with her or spend any time with her. It helped me to become closer with my dad and make sure that we spend as much time together as possible so we don't have the same regrets as I do about my sister.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel she is mostly responsible for this because she allowed herself to get sick and she didn't take care of herself. Although she wasn't happy with her childhood and how her life turned out she could have done things to better herself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because I couldn't do anything to help her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No I thought because she was young that she would get better and not die.

situation: My brother, who owns the home where I live as a caretaker, suddenly announced his plan to sell the house and move me to a Tiny House that he intends to build on a lot he doesn't even have the legal right to build on. He didn't give me any timeline, which left me feeling like my life was about to be thrown into total disarray. His motive was to take the proceeds from the sale of the house and invest them. I wanted to reason with him and convince him that this idea had no merit and should be abandoned. I felt helpless, but then I found a solution. I asked my neighbor to communicate with my brother and request that he not sell the house while the neighbor and his wife were still alive, since I'm a friend and an aide to their needs as they are elderly. My neighbor wrote a beautiful letter to my brother and managed to convince him that selling the home was a bad idea.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week. It mattered because my shelter depended on it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was high stress. I managed it. I am proud of myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My brother is a terribly damaged narcissist. He causes needless stress.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Learning that his behavior is narcissistic, I can handle a narcissist.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The cooperation of my neighbor was welcome and unexpected in that it was performed perfectly.

situation: I decided to quit my family group chat because everyone in there has the opposite political views from me, which is fine. The problem was that I had asked one person multiple times not to post political stuff in the family chat, but she just kept doing it, so I left. I really wanted my wishes to be respected and for the group to stay politically neutral, focusing on other topics instead. This whole situation left me feeling sad and angry. I realize it's just one person causing this, so I avoid her and have one-on-one conversations with the others. It just showed me how politics have completely destroyed some people from a mental health perspective.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: About a week ago. It matters because our parents are gone and we don't all live in the same state. I want to stay connected, but feel it threatens my own mental health to keep subjecting myself to my sister-in-law's rants.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because I wish my siblings would stick up for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My sister-in-law, for not respecting my very basic boundaries.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I felt attacked because she was laughing (but usually ranting) about political beliefs that are important to me and my husband.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No. Several people left Facebook, where we used to have the family chat. One of my sisters created a text chat. I thought for sure that sister-in-law had gotten the 'no political posts' message by now, but by the second day in the new text-based group, she was already doing it. I asked my sister to remove me immediately.

situation: My wife just passed away, and I get emotional when I see her things around the house. I wasn't trying to do anything specific, and I didn't have any particular wants or needs in the situation. It just leaves me feeling empty, knowing I will not see her again in this life.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was when I would go into the bedroom and see her things. This mattered deeply to me because it was a deeply emotional experience.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It certainly doesn't help you. It makes you feel sad and depressed.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody is responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because you can't control death.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, because I didn't expect her to die.

situation: I had an argument with my father, who wants me to move out. Right now, moving out isn't possible for me because of income-related reasons. The argument got pretty heated. I wasn't trying to start anything; it was him who initiated the argument. All I wanted was for it to end. Afterward, I felt a bit frustrated and like I wanted to leave and not turn back. The thing is, I actually do want to move out, but I feel restricted right now.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when my father was picking me up from the train station, a relatively routine and mundane task. It mattered to me because I felt frustrated and restricted, wanting to leave and not turn back.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The argument didn't really hurt me; I got a bit angry and frustrated. I would say that there was no point in it at all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My father was most responsible for the argument, as he was the one who started it. I pay him to pick me up from the train station to cover fuel costs.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I was in control during the argument, as it was more a nuisance than anything.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I mean, in an argument, can anything really go as expected?

situation: I experienced a pretty emotional situation where I thought someone I didn't know had ordered prescriptions online from my medical centre. I had ordered my usual medications and picked them up, but then I got a text saying that the items I collected had been ordered again, and I hadn't done that. I let the pharmacy know, as well as the medical centre, that I hadn't ordered duplicate items. I was trying to stop a third party from accessing my medical items and wanted help from the other parties involved. It left me feeling like my personal state was being interfered with, and I was the one trying to control what was happening. I didn't want anyone, especially the medical centre, to think I was careless in re-ordering items I had collected the day before. Also, I didn't want them to think I was abusing the system by trying to get more medication than I was entitled to.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 11 days ago, the day after I collected my items. It mattered in the context that it was personal to me and why me? My personal information had been obtained to make the order.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to analyse what I did that caused the event to happen and to avoid it happening again if I could identify what went wrong. It hurt me as it was a great inconvenience to me and only me should be able to action what happened. I caused worry for me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was probably responsible as I was perhaps careless with my personal details.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I was in control in not letting the problem develop into something bigger. I contacted the relevant parties concerned that were in control of the ordering and delivery.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not quite as expected. Other items were ordered which were not on the original order and they were issued for collection. I had requested the pharmacy to request identification should anyone at anytime collect medical items in my name. When I went the following day to check on the ordered items I was given them without ID being requested.

situation: My cat had to be put down because it had kidney failure. I loved my cat very much, so I needed to do the best I could for it. At the same time, I had to be kind to myself because I was really upset. The whole situation left me feeling bereft, and I still feel a deep sense of loss and sadness. It was important that my wife and I were able to offer each other emotional support during this tough time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was around 10 days ago, we have had our cat for 13 years and it was the most important thing in our lives almost.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: As I said I was bereft and suffering real grief. It certainly didn't help me in any way - bereavement is awful in all of its forms.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The cat's terminal diagnosis.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control, to ease my cat's suffering there was only one choice.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes they went as expected as the cat is now dead.

situation: I learned that an old friend had passed away. I was thinking about her, so I decided to search the internet and found out she had died. I was seeking information and perhaps some closure about my friend. The situation left me feeling sad, and I felt bad that we hadn’t stayed in touch. I also wondered what her life was like and what happened to her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a little to me and made me feel kind of lonely when I thought about it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me a little, but we hadn’t been in touch for years. It made me realize that as I get older, this is going to happen.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I had been hurt by some things she’d said about me, and I wished I had confronted her about it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt more lonely and not really in control; it was just one of those things that happen.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it all went as expected, and I didn’t think about it again until now.

situation: I belong to a social group and I'm on the committee. At our last committee meeting, our treasurer didn't attend and didn't provide the requested information. There was a lot of complaining about him, especially because he's allowed our bank account with £5,000 in it to be locked by the bank due to lack of use. He refuses to get it re-opened, making many excuses. I offered to speak to him since I'm supposed to be the second signatory. I was fairly firm and recognized in our interaction that there was a power issue at play. The committee chairperson sent me a private message saying 'well done' for sticking with it, but a couple of hours later sent another message saying I should deal with it differently since the person in question is 'easily stressed'. I was annoyed at this change of perspective and what I saw as withdrawal of support. I didn't go to the club night that week. I wanted the person in question to commit to approaching the bank to re-open the account and to download the change of mandate form to make me the second signatory. I was initially quite positive that with the backing of the committee, I would get things moving in this direction. However, the withdrawal of support left me feeling annoyed and somewhat 'backstabbed'. This situation has been going on for 6 years, and it should have been dealt with long ago. Why has the situation been allowed to persist?

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because I felt a lack of support and that the person in question had probably been let 'off the hook'.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I feel that there has been a level of disrespect since there has been much side-stepping, avoiding, making excuses. It is difficult for me to just let it go, knowing the person concerned will likely continue doing nothing unless others chime in with obvious support. This means I feel disregarded by the group if that indeed proves to be the case.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The chairperson and possibly also another member. I feel some conversation led to the change of opinion on my dealings with the person concerned but am not sure exactly who that was although I have my thoughts on that.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control when dealing with the treasurer because they had been avoiding approaching the subject with me and I felt quite sure there was a power issue going on. I now feel a lack of control because I am not sure what has gone on 'behind my back' so to speak and I almost feel scapegoated.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I don't know what the outcome is. I did not attend the social club night the following day and no one has followed up with me. I suspect however that the matter has gone cold again.

situation: I was arguing with my disabled son, and things got heated quickly. He started insulting me with some pretty vulgar terms. Arguments like these aren't uncommon for us, and he tends to get upset easily. I find that shutting down the conversation can solve the problem, at least temporarily. It's nothing new for me; I've been absorbing verbal abuse for 10 years now. I'm starting to think maybe there's a better long-term solution out there. I try to remember that he has behavioral disabilities, and his behavior is at least partially driven by that.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event plays weekly, maybe even more frequently, so it's not a one-off.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I'm pretty well conditioned to the assault, so 'hurt' is not a big concern. Solutions would be nice.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There isn't blame to be assigned. He doesn't like his trajectory in life, he was late being diagnosed, and since I'm the most convenient parent, I get the criticism.
appraisal_reasoning.control: What I control is walking away or shutting down the conversation by hanging up. Not much more.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: This version was no different than the last 50. No new topics.

situation: I was in my room late at night, debating my career path and got really emotional. I realized that I should have tried harder earlier in college, and it hit me hard. I was trying to figure out if I should pivot to tech or continue on my CRNA pathway. I wanted a clear resolution to this dilemma. The whole situation left me feeling disjointed and confused, but ultimately, I am still choosing CRNA. It's not just about the money; the work-life balance and security aspects are also important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When this event happened, it mattered to me a great deal because it was going to determine major parts of my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I gained some minor clarity, it hurt me because it made me feel negative emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Ultimately I was responsible for this mess, because I slacked off in college.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Well not really I had a host of untreated mental illnesses but I still kind of blame myself.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected, I just redid the math and concluded that CRNA was still the superior play.

situation: I got into a disagreement with my boss at work. We had different views on why we weren't hitting our numbers or getting the results we wanted. I was trying to explain things from my point of view, hoping he'd understand that we were short-staffed during certain times and overstaffed when it wasn't necessary. I suggested changing the scheduling, but he didn't like that idea. It made me feel upset and angry because I really wanted him to see my perspective, but he didn't take me seriously. What's important to me is that I held my ground. Normally, I cave in and just accept things, but this time I was much more direct.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago, it mattered a lot to me because I feel responsible towards our workplace results.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think it helped because now me and my boss get along after the situation. We don't have negative feelings towards each other. We both understand how frustrating the job can be.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that we are both equally responsible for this. Since both of us are managers, even though he is the higher rank.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I had control over the situation, I was very direct, I spoke with confidence, I didn't allow any interjections.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things kind of did go my way, the schedule is changing a little more, even though I would like more changes, I am happy with what is being done currently.

situation: I was at a local bowling venue for my grandson's birthday when I discovered that my car was damaged in the car park. The only satisfactory outcome for me would have been if the person who caused the damage had made contact with me to resolve the situation. I was very cross about what happened. I contacted the venue to find out if the area was covered by CCTV.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because it will cost a minimum of £750 to repair.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Paying out £750 hurts me a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that the person who damaged my car was most responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, how could I be in control?
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing went as expected. Nothing was unexpected.

situation: I couldn't stop crying while remembering my brother. I was hoping he is at peace. The whole situation left me feeling sad and emotional. Listening to music and looking at pictures were significant aspects of this experience for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened this week. It mattered to me because I was upset.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as it made me cry. No, nothing can help.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don’t know.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn’t in control. My emotions overwhelmed me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I understand it to be a natural process.

situation: For the first time in 6 years, my direct deposit did not go through, leaving me in the negative. I notified my boss and told him that some of that money had already been spent. I wanted to get an answer on when my paycheck would be deposited. At first, I felt uncertain, until a few days later when it finally hit my account. I had the fear that my account would be overdrawn.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week. Since I work in exchange for money, it was very important I get paid.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Luckily nothing bounced so no harm no foul.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My HR department.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I didn't get paid. I felt frustrated I would be overdrawn.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: My check did get deposited a few days later and luckily nothing bounced.

situation: My daughter did really well during her parents' evening, and I was filled with pride and emotion. I was just so happy for her; seeing what she had achieved was all I needed to feel content. The whole situation left me feeling really happy. What was particularly important to me was recognizing how much effort she had put in to achieve her success.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Friday, and it meant the world to me to see her achievements that she has spent so much time on.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me a lot as I went out of my comfort zone to speak to different teachers.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My daughter for doing her best.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control as such positive feedback from the teachers was so uplifting.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as expected.

situation: I watched my favorite football team play, and they lost again. They're now facing the possibility of getting relegated, which is something that should never happen to a team of this stature. I really wanted my team to win and survive in the league they play in, but they lost. They have 9 games left to save their season or face the possibility of relegation to a lower league, which would cripple the club. This whole situation left me feeling depressed, down, and hopeless. I'm fearful for the long-term future of this club. Football is my form of escapism, but when it's not going well, it affects my everyday mood negatively.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The match happened yesterday. I watched my favourite team, a team I've supported my whole life and am heavily invested in, lose. This loss comes after many previous defeats and has seen this team drop close to relegation, something that a club like this should not be involved with. Relegation would cripple the club.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as I don't like seeing my team in such disarray. I fear the long-term effects of relegation could do to this team.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There are a few things responsible. The ownership of the club who have not worked hard enough to create a competitive football club. The managers of the team too, who have managed poorly. The recruitment team as well. They have not made good player signings.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was not in control at all. All I can do is support my team, but beyond that it's up to the players and the management team.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Unexpected. We are not meant to be battling relegation, so this is very unexpected and unprecedented for a club like this.

situation: We were delayed on a flight home from a recent holiday, and I was really anxious to find out how long the delay would be. The uncertainty made me feel helpless, especially because missing this particular flight meant we were in danger of missing our connecting flight.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened last week. It mattered greatly as I did not want to miss my connecting flight home.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The delayed flight was a very stressful situation. There were no beneficial outcomes of this situation. The stress made me pace around the departure area and increased my blood pressure.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The airline was at fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control in this situation, as it was up to the airline when the plane was ready to board.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Eventually the plane was ready to board and we made up the delay on the flight. As a result, I was able to get on my connecting flight and arrived home close to the time I had originally thought that I would.

situation: A friend's mother passed away this past weekend. Even though it was expected—she was 96 and had been in ill-health and under hospice care for some time—it's always emotional to lose someone who has been part of your life. I wanted to help and be there for my friend and their family. Unfortunately, my friend had the flu and didn't want anyone to come over. I didn't really need anything other than to support my friend, which I did as much as possible from a distance. I suppose it left me feeling 'OK'. At my age and with my experience, death is becoming common and I know how to deal with it. No, other than we will miss the mother.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Friday night, and I was notified on Saturday morning. It mattered a lot to me because it was a friend.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation didn't really help or hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It's life. No one is 'responsible'.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I certainly wasn't in control of the death as it always happens to all of us.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wanted to go over to support them, but they were not feeling well, so I stayed home. That's OK.

situation:
This week at work was a whirlwind of emotions for me. We finally hit adherence targets in multiple areas for the first time in months, and it felt like a huge accomplishment. 

My area, which consists of me and a few others, usually hits our targets on the night shift.

 I work 12-hour night shifts and attend university for my master's degree three times a week, which is mentally and emotionally draining. 

With my direct manager away for two weeks, I decided to run things the way I wanted, and it turned out to be more effective. I managed workloads and motivated people to push and do their best, even though my usual colleague has been off for two weeks, leaving me to work with a mix of people who float. It was challenging, but hitting these targets without him made me feel a little sad, although the positive emotion overruled this. 

I can't wait to show him the new process next week, along with my direct manager. Having the director come to me at the end of the week to discuss what was changed and what should be implemented in the future to keep us on track was an ultimate sense of gratitude. We shook hands, which had never happened in six months. 

 I finished my shift heading into the weekend, motivated so much that I didn't feel the usual fatigue and worked a lot on my dissertation. 

As a SOC analyst, I handle managerial roles and IT infrastructure to keep things running smoothly. This week, the target was minimal downtime across systems, all orders completed and shipped, and updates to the app so all employees are onboarded and can access it via an iPad attached to the machine. By the end of the week, there were zero outstanding IT issues, all orders were finished with zero mistakes, and programming PLCs to prevent downtime was performed during operator breaks. I felt motivated at each handover meeting, exporting from the app downtime and production quantities. Every day we were in the green, leaving me feeling happy and positive. Completing risk assessments on time and ensuring compliance was stressful, but getting the green light on pen testing made me smile, as I did back when I was younger at Christmas! 

Going into the weekend, I felt amazing that this could now be a regular thing and progress my career. I have other projects for my dissertation, but my ultimate goal is pen testing, so with the momentum from such a great week, I've been running my test server, simulating the work network and pinpointing weaknesses. Having great colleagues who support each other and respect us all is really important. This week, we put differences aside to tackle challenges, and everyone seemed positive. I let them know that this performance could increase their bonus and encouraged them to keep up the momentum throughout each day, week, and month. The most significant moment was hitting adherence before the week ended, completing my own role tasks, and doing so without my direct manager and his old, stubborn ways that have been holding us back.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened at the start of the week, like any week. I wake up at 4am Monday, leave for university at 6:30am, return home at 4pm, and go to work at 5pm as I like to catch up before the 6pm - 6am shift. This event mattered a lot as it means a positive step forward for all employees. They can strive to hit their bonus, adherence is met so we are not behind.
