I can focus more on my actual job, which makes me happy, and focus more on university, even more positive. These new procedures I implemented need to be concrete and stick. This means so much to me to see the business thrive I left university for in my undergrad and coming back in my master's and making these changes, it all feels a little surreal but I am grateful that the employees assisted and have such positivity for the future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me a lot. I can now focus more on my actual role. The managers above my direct are happy with the changes. The app rollout has been successful for tracking. All infrastructure was operational on this 4-day week of 12-hour shifts, and it's been good. For the first time in a long time over the weekend, I can switch off from work and focus on my dissertation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: A team effort for sure, but with my direct manager being away and on night shift, no replacement, I was able to implement and guide team leaders who observe the operators in the correct direction. I showed them how to export from the app and present to the next team leader on shift with a full breakdown of all justified downtime and exact numbers.
appraisal_reasoning.control: 100%, everybody was on board after the first day of the targets being green. After the 4th day, it was set in stone. I felt full control by day 2, I would say, and 'steered the ship,' some may say.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yeah, things went as expected. The most unexpected thing to happen was the absence of staff, which is normal sometimes with operators; they were on training courses. As I mentioned earlier, this did not affect numbers and proved we now have a solid method.

situation: My mum has been in excruciating pain with her back and has been in and out of hospital. I really needed support because I'm very close with my mum, and being autistic, my routine was thrown up in the air. This whole situation left me feeling really anxious and stressed, and at times, even angry. It was really important to me that my mum got the help she needed, but it felt like lots of medical professionals didn't seem to care.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was last week and it mattered a huge amount to me because this whole situation left me feeling really anxious and stressed, and at times, even angry. It was really important to me that my mum got the help she needed, but it felt like lots of medical professionals didn't seem to care.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I had to sit in a waiting room for 2 and a half hours watching my mum writhe in pain and it broke me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The NHS didn’t prioritise her considering her pain and secondly she’s always had a bad back.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all, I nagged nurses to help and they just said she was one of the next, that’s not exactly next! I also knew I couldn’t leave until she was seen although we did!
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: We unexpectedly left even though they said she was one of the next (we forgot her painkillers so she couldn’t take it).

situation: I had a tough time at work, pulling a 12-hour shift in retail. I was all over the place, working the tills, handling deliveries, and maintaining the shop. I wanted to make sure the store ran as smoothly as possible. By the end of the day, I felt very tired, especially since I was fasting. Ensuring that I rested appropriately afterward was really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I was tasked with making sure everything in the store was okay, and it mattered to me because I wanted to make sure I was okay.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation exhausted me, and I had to rest a lot to make up for it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The store's decision to cut hours was most responsible for all of this, as they are trying to save as much money as possible and reducing hours.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control as I was simply told what to do and it was minimal help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I finished as expected, but I truly expected to be supported during this and I wasn’t.

situation: My football team scored a last-minute winner to keep us in the cup. It was such a tight game, and honestly, we didn't play well. Right up to the very end, it felt like we were going out, but then we managed to score a goal with the last kick of the game, which put us through to the next round. I really wanted to win and feel that thrill, so I just needed to watch and hope we could get the goal. I was there to support the team. When we scored, I felt a rush of joy at first, and then just relief. After everything settled down, I felt quite tired. Sharing the moment with friends made the experience even more intense because we all felt the same way.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot. I have followed the team all my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me as it gave me a positive feeling. I felt connected to people which I enjoyed.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The last-minute goal changed the mood in a second. It was a big moment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt out of control as I could only watch and hope.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected we would push to the end. I was thankful we scored but I did not assume it would happen.

situation: I came home from work and found that my cat had kittens. I went to check on the mama kitty, and she was in her bed with the babies. I felt happy and relieved seeing them all together. It looked like everyone was healthy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened around 5pm on a warmish (almost) spring day. It was quite important to me because while at work, I was wondering how my mama kitty was doing, and I didn't want anything bad to happen.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I was no longer concerned about the birth. I also noticed mama kitty seemed proud of her litter, which brought positive emotions for both of us.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Mama kitty was most responsible for all of this. Her actions and instincts played a significant role in the outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control. I had no idea when the kittens would be born, and I didn't know if they would be healthy.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went well, and things went as I expected.

situation: I was able to see my baby nephew and he was walking. I didn't want anything else but just to appreciate the moment. It left me feeling emotional.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened when family came over. It matters a lot because it shows that he is growing up and he's my nephew.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I get to see him growing and walking early. It was positive.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Not sure.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really because I wasn't the one who was walking at the moment.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected because he wasn't walking before.

situation: I was relaxing at the end of a busy working day when I checked my emails and noticed a message from my landlord. The email said that when we vacated our flat two weeks ago, we left it dirty and would be charged approximately £1k for the condition of the flat. I was absolutely full of anger because I knew, and have photographic evidence, that the flat was cleaned to the highest of standards. I felt the adrenaline and was very, very upset. I needed somehow to calm down, as there was nothing I could do in the moment and it would have been unwise to fire off a return email. Instead, I vented to my mother via WhatsApp, and she calmed me down. The situation left me feeling very upset and drained. I felt like my landlord was trying to screw money out of me, and I can't afford to lose £1k. It was around 10:30 pm at night, and I still wanted to get a good night's sleep, so I needed to calm down before bed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened around 10:30 pm at night, after a busy working day. It mattered a lot to me because I knew the landlord was basically lying to extort money from me, and I felt powerless.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by causing my blood to pump faster and making me feel the adrenaline. I also felt further powerlessness because I couldn't immediately put it right.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the landlord was most responsible for all of this, as he was telling lies to gain money from me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control because I felt the balance of power is with the landlord and not the tenant.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I'm still in the middle of resolving it, but I will be challenging his attempt to gain money from me by raising a dispute with the deposit protection scheme. This gives me a little hope as they are a third party.

situation: I work as a dietitian in a stroke rehab hospital, and one of my patients hasn't been progressing and is now, unfortunately, end of life, which is really upsetting. I was trying to help them meet their nutritional requirements using an NG tube. It's been tough because the patient is the same age as my own grandad, which makes it feel even more personal and emotional for me. On the bright side, they have lots of family around them, and it's nice to see the support and love they are surrounded by during this difficult time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Monday at the stroke rehab hospital. It was important to me as I like to give all my patients the best possible care.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt as this patient was not progressing with rehab and it was determined they were for end of life care.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: This was due to the severity of their stroke unfortunately.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of the care I was able to give but not the outcomes of that care.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, unfortunately they did not go as expected as the patient did not pick up/progress from the care given. It was expected they would start eating and drinking orally but they were unable to do so.

situation: My daughter came home from school and threw up all over the bathroom. There was sick everywhere, and I was really worried about her. I needed to get help to get her to be sick into a bowl instead of the floor, but I was shouting and my husband didn't come to help. I felt annoyed that he couldn't hear me shouting, stressed that there was sick everywhere, and worried that she was unwell.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday, and it mattered a lot to me because I don't want her to be ill. I also want to know that when I need help, someone will be there for me, and they weren't.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as I felt like I was alone in dealing with it.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My husband should have been close enough to help instead of shutting himself up in a room at the end of the house.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I wasn't in control and there was sick going everywhere.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It didn't go as I expected as I ended up having to sort it all out by myself.

situation: One of my roommates ate my food, and this time it was my entire box of Quaker oatmeal. I wanted to take that particular food to work because it's easy to just heat up and go. I was upset and ended up being hangry since I didn't have money to buy food. I have a lot of roommates, and I was frustrated because they could have just asked for some instead of stealing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on a Tuesday and it matters because I need to eat.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me in general but now I know to keep non-perishable foods in my room.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My roommates.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because they stole it likely when I wasn’t home so idk which one didn’t.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No. I just have to buy more and keep it in my room.

situation: My best friend's daughter got married and didn't tell anyone. She married someone she has only known for a couple of months, and this has been very upsetting for all of us. She has mental health issues and tends to make bad decisions, which is worrying. We were trying to get more information about the person she married, but at this point, we can't do much else except try and support her. Chances are there will be problems ahead. Overall, I'm feeling sad and frustrated about the whole situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters a lot. I have known her since she was a baby. She is like a daughter to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I feel hurt because I was left out and also worried because she hardly knows this person.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She is definitely responsible for her decisions.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, not in control. She didn't ask me for any advice, so I had no input.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Hard to say at this point. She is still married.

situation: My mom forgot my birthday. I was really hoping for some acknowledgment and recognition from her because it's my birthday. The whole situation left me feeling sad and alone. I always make it a point to remember and acknowledge my family members' birthdays, so it felt important to me. I don't get much contact or outreach from my mom, which made this even more significant.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week. It mattered because my birthday is important to me. Everyone, including me, likes to feel special on their birthday. When your own mother forgets it, it hurts.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel as if my mom did not care about me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My mom is most responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control. My mom controls whether she acknowledges my birthday.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: In a way, they kind of did go the way I expected. This is not the first time my mom forgot my birthday.

situation: I had an argument with my wife about how to best set up a room for our newborn baby. We both had different ideas and disagreed on the approach. We needed to rearrange the bedroom since the baby is on the way, and it was important for both of us to speak our minds and come to a common ground. In the end, we sat down and discussed our perspectives in a calm and thoughtful manner, which led us to reach a compromise. I felt stressed during the disagreement, but also relieved that we were able to resolve the problem.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few days ago. It matters as me and my wife usually do not argue but this was important we didn't argue.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It allowed us to heal and vent any frustration. I was reassured because we put our differences to one side.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was me. I let my emotions get the better of me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did to a certain extent. But I also let my wife have equal input.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went expected.

situation: I was diagnosed with a medical condition, and I really wanted guidance on what that meant for me. I felt confused about everything, and understanding how this condition would impact my quality of life was really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and was quite important to me as I had been waiting for a diagnosis for 3 years.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by confirming the diagnosis.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that no one was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I was experiencing symptoms but did not know what it was.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected, but it took longer than I thought to get a diagnosis.

situation: I recently ended a long-term friendship because I felt I was being treated insensitively by someone I trusted deeply. I've been dealing with some mental problems, and it seemed like this person wasn't sensitive to how I was feeling. They kept trying to push me into 'getting over' those problems before I was ready. It left me feeling hurt and saddened by my friend's lack of care. What made it particularly painful was that I had been there for this friend when they were going through similar issues, always treating them with care and respect. So, it felt selfish when they didn't do the same for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few weeks ago, and it felt devastating because they were a very close friend that I had spent a lot of time with. I still miss spending time with them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt deeply, losing such a close friend while also going through other problems.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that my friend was responsible for not being sensitive to my feelings, although I also feel I could've handled the situation somewhat better.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was not in control. I was very emotional and could not get my friend to understand my point of view.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect such a close friend to treat me that way.

situation: I started dating someone new and immediately got a UTI. It's driving me crazy because I had one 6 months ago, and I still feel off. I feel like this is my new normal. I'm not trying to do anything specific, but I'm trying to feel normal and avoid infections, which is affecting my mental health. Overall, the situation left me feeling bad. I just want to feel healthy, but I don't.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It started again on Tuesday after sleeping with the man I've been seeing. My body feels off each time and I think I have another UTI. It makes me never want to date again.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It only hurts. I feel like I have chronic UTIs now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Probably aging and other problems or a bad gut biome. I don't know that's the problem. I'm trying everything to try to stop them.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No...I can't control getting an infection.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I don't know how to answer that. No, getting UTIs did not go as expected as I still feel off.

situation: I've been really affected lately by how animals are being tested on. It breaks my heart and makes me so sad. I want the government to care more about these poor animals. We're more advanced now, so I question why this is happening. People need to stand up to those responsible for the pain caused by animal testing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week where people were trying to rescue these animals and the police stopped them. I hate this world we live in; who gives humans the right to take life?
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was so amazing how these people broke into these places to save the animals. This needs to stop. It breaks my heart that no one is listening to the plight of these animals. I love my animals so much I can hardly believe no one will stop this.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The government knows what is going on and does nothing to help.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, we have no control over what the government does. They don't listen to the people.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I hoped these amazing people were listened to. I expect this to stop; we are so advanced we don't have to experiment on animals anymore. Things need to change.

situation: My youngest child was diagnosed with a very contagious illness, and it was a very stressful situation. I had to make sure my youngest was taken care of while also making sure my oldest didn’t get sick, all while trying to work full time. I felt very stressed, drained, anxious, and worried. My husband provided me a lot of support during this time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me because, as a parent, we hate to see our children hurt or sick. I am very protective and want to keep everyone healthy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by taking a toll on my mental health and impacting my quality of work.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: For the situation, no one was responsible. But for the stress it caused, I am responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because nothing I did would impact the time it took my child to recover, so it was totally out of my hands.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than I expected. I felt proud I was able to navigate it and felt very supported by my spouse.

situation: I told two family members about how they hurt me when I was growing up and that I wouldn't be able to have consistent contact with them because I'm trying to heal. I needed to let them know why I haven't been in contact with them much and why I was upset. I also wanted to make it clear for them not to contact me at this time because I feel triggered and hurt after almost every interaction with them. I wanted them to at least acknowledge and possibly apologize for the way they've treated me in the past and also in the present. The situation left me feeling sad because neither one of them acknowledged or apologized for anything. It also made me feel validated for feeling the way that I do about them. I feel like they are emotionally immature and unable to accept fault for anything. Even with me pouring my heart out to them, they didn't seem to care. I'm finally starting to stand up for myself and trying to bring myself peace.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The events happened when I was a kid, with the earliest flashback from when I was probably around 5 years old. This was not just one event but many happenings from early in my childhood up until now.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation has made me retreat into myself and trust nobody. It has caused me a lot of emotional and mental pain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Both of these people are equally responsible for their actions. They are manipulative immature people stuck in patterns of substance abuse.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do for once feel like I am in control of the situation. I cannot control what their reactions are from this point forward but I can control my contact with them and what I am willing to share with them about my life. I am still trying to figure out what our relationships will be going forward.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, the situation happened as I expected.

situation: My horse got cold and wet in the rain, and I needed to get her inside to dry her off and warm her up. It was a bit of a struggle because other horses were trying to come in too, which made it difficult to manage. I felt really angry about the situation because my horse's wellbeing is so important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Tuesday and mattered a lot to me because my horse's wellbeing is very important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me angry as I had to fight off other horses to get her out of the field.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible for all of this as the other owners were not around.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt slightly in control as the other horses do listen.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected in some ways, but not entirely, as I wanted to get her in faster.

situation: My father hadn't been in the best of health and had deteriorated a little bit, but he's looking better now. I was helping him by going over once a week to do all his housework and everything he needed. I just needed a bit of support during this time. The situation left me feeling sad because of his ill health and also drained as I tried to fit in time to help him while managing my normal life. It was important to me to make sure my dad got the help he needed, especially since he can be quite stubborn.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot because I haven't seen my dad become ill like that, so it was such a shock.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation hurt me because I saw my dad ill, and it made me full of worry.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It is his heart problems that were responsible for the issues.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I can't do anything to help him get better; that is down to himself and his body. So definitely not in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't really expect anything, just more hoped that he would recover, which he did.

situation: I have been working tirelessly at my agency, always striving to deliver my best work. Despite my dedication, I have not received a pay raise in several years, which has left me struggling financially. I've repeatedly requested a salary increase, but my pleas have been consistently overlooked. This week, during a meeting, one of the directors criticized our team for not being proactive enough, even though we've been receiving positive feedback from our clients. He suggested that we use some of the planned uplift money allocation for additional training, which made me feel undervalued and invisible. It was as if my efforts and contributions were insignificant. My manager often assures me that he cares and has discussed the salary increase issue with our client. Recently, he claimed that the raise has been approved and the funds should be with our company soon. However, I have yet to receive any confirmation of a salary increase, leaving me uncertain whether he is being misleading or dishonest. This situation has left me feeling angry, sad, and frustrated, as it seems that no matter how hard I work, it is never enough to be recognized or appreciated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot. I've been struggling to put food on the table so am in desperate need to uplift money. The fact that my potential salary increase can be allocated to training is just treacherous and shows a blatant disregard for my effort and work.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it has convinced me that my hard work will go unnoticed and that I should be ready to move on from this employer and role.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My manager and the director at our agency. They can take these decisions about salary.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt the opposite. I can't control the cost of living, nor can I control people's expectations of me. I'm expected to do better but am constantly told I shouldn't expect anything in return. I can't keep pouring from an empty cup.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No they didn't. I thought our director would finally come to his senses and tell us we were appreciated for what we do and were being given a raise. Instead he questioned our abilities and hard work.

situation: I took my dog to the vet for his annual check-up, and he needs some further investigation. I was just doing my usual care and checks to maintain his health. He's generally in good condition, but he's lost a little weight, which is okay but something to keep an eye on. Since he's getting older, I'm always vigilant for signs of decline. I'm very conscious that he can't tell me if anything is wrong, so regular checks are important to me. Plus, I like to travel, so I need to know that he's well enough to come with me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week. It matters very much because his health is my responsibility.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to know that he seems generally ok. I’m a little concerned about the routine treatment he needs because there are always risks.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible for- it’s just part and parcel of having an aging pet.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes because I have always been aware of what condition he is in and my vet explains things well. I also felt in control because I know I have adequate pet insurance in place.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Mostly as expected but I was surprised that he had lost some weight.

situation: My daughter was having a fight with her fiancé and was considering moving back home. She has a 2-year-old and a 5-month-old, so moving back would involve big changes. I work from home, so it would be difficult to manage. I felt mixed feelings because it would be fun to have them back home, but I don't want her to be broken up and the kids going back and forth. I needed to know that my daughter and granddaughters were healthy, happy, and safe and that things would work out. I felt pulled in two directions because I wanted to have them around, but that would mean a breakup with her fiancé. I also want to be able to work in a quiet, laid-back home without screaming and crying. It's important for my daughter to remain an adult and not have me step in to make things better all the time. She's grown and needs to keep adulting and face the decisions she's made.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened last week. It mattered a lot to me because she is my adopted daughter and I've always felt that she hasn't felt fully loved due to her very awful beginning in life. I don't want her to think that I wouldn't take her back in because I've always told her she can come back anytime, but she does have 3 dogs, 4 cats, a gecko, a snake and her daughters, which would really fill our house and make some issues.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me continue to know the deep love I have for her, but it hurt that she had kept her problems a secret and some lies for a few years now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that it is her responsibility because I begged her not to move out when she turned 18. I told her adulting is hard and that I would help her find an apartment with 3 other girls and that she can wait and save up money till then. She chose to move out and 2 weeks later was pregnant and homeless.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt totally out of control and I like to be in control when possible. I felt like there wasn't anything I could do to help her make better choices. She's always been very independent and strong-willed so she's usually had control anyway.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was unexpected how she ended up living with a boyfriend and then pregnant because she lied and told me she was moving in with her friend Ally and I believed her. There were so many lies that I always fell for. I always wanted to trust her but found out that it is very hard to.

situation: My daughter achieved a great result in maths, and I was really proud because this is something she's always struggled with. I want her to feel proud of her achievement, but I also want her to knuckle down and work hard since she needs to keep improving. While I'm proud, I'm also worried because she still has a long way to go.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 3 days ago and it mattered as I worry about her progress with maths at school as it is such a required skill.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me as I had faith that she could keep moving forward and catch up with her peers.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She was most responsible for working hard.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I was not in control I can only help and encourage I cant control her abilities.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They did go as expected as I was hoping for improvement as I have hired a private tutor.

situation: I had my first child! I'm still coming to terms with the fact that I'm now a parent and need to provide for and look after this person. Before the birth, I tried to learn everything I could, but I've quickly realized that it's impossible to predict everything. I really want to nurture and be the best parent possible, and I know I'll definitely need help and support from the people around me to get the best for my child. Overall, I'm feeling very happy. It's important to me that my partner and child are happy and healthy, and that's what I care about the most.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened on Monday. It means the world to me as I've become a parent and get to support and grow a human.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think it will hurt my social life but that's part of parenthood. It's helped me grow into a good person.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think taking advice from my parents was responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes and no. I am happy everyone is healthy but with childbirth you never feel in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes all went as planned thankfully.

situation: My wife of 29 years recently passed away from Stage 1 small cell lung cancer. Now, I'm going through the house and sorting her things to give to family, friends, and charity. I'm focusing on her clothing and jewelry, making sure they go to people she loved and cherished during her lifetime. Doing this has finally given me a sense of relief, as I'm glad to be doing something other than grieving and being depressed all the time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened in the last week. I started on Monday. It matters to me because doing this has finally given me a sense of relief, as I'm glad to be doing something other than grieving and being depressed all the time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This helps myself in moving forward in my life and continuing on. It especially hurts knowing I am giving away pieces of her accumulated over the past 29 years with her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one person is to blame for her death. Death comes to us all at one time or another.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I am in control to a certain point. I sometimes breakdown and cry but force myself to think of the good times we had together to take my mind off things until I'm ready to start again.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, for the most part. I sorted her things and found some items I thought we had parted ways with years ago. She placed them in the storage boxes instead. She was sort of a packrat.

situation: My daughter came home on Friday and told me she got another girl's phone number. She doesn't have any siblings and often feels lonely, so I'm really happy she has a friend now. I also substitute at my daughter's school, so I know her friend, and she seems like the most caring and sincere friend my daughter has had so far. I felt elated hearing this news. Plus, I know the girl's dad—we were pretty much friends as teens.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened Friday. It mattered a lot because my daughter doesn't have many friends.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because my child would have a better social life. She doesn't have a lot of kids to play with, especially being that she's an only child.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My daughter (she asked to exchange numbers).
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn't around my daughter at the time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes.

situation: I visited an emotional historic site where many people died. I was in the country and this site was a must-visit due to the significance of the events that took place there. Being there left me feeling hugely sad for the loss of all the innocent lives. It was important to me to act respectfully during the visit.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week on a weekday in the afternoon. It was part of a planned series of visits, but this one was particularly important to me as an act of remembrance and to pay my respects.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The visit left me feeling overwhelmed by the scale of the impact of the event and how survivors were treated in some cases. It highlighted the gravity of the historical events and their aftermath.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that the country that authorized the bomb was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control of my emotions and reactions as I had no personal connection to the site. However, I was taken aback by my strength of feeling in relation to some of the individual stories within the wider event.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, all went as expected during my visit.

situation: I've had quite an emotional week at work, where a few patients I was quite fond of passed away. I'm now off work for a week, and honestly, it couldn't have come at a better time. It's been really emotionally draining. I was just trying to get through the workday without letting my emotions get the better of me. I guess I just wanted to not feel as frustrated or sad about the situation. The whole experience left me feeling quite sad, and at that moment, I really didn't want to go back to work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened over a few days, it does matter to me because I do care about people. It isn't just the patients but the relatives as well who have seen their loved ones die.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I am quite empathetic so emotions like these are quite strong. I left work feeling quite burnout and anxious.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: People get ill and people get cancer so this is why it happened.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't feel like I was in control because there was nothing I could do but be a shoulder to lean on.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I probably would not say expected because people passed away unexpectedly.

situation: Scenario: Last week was Lunar New Year, and I found myself contemplating whether I should reach out to my parents. Ultimately, I decided against it, primarily due to a lack of motivation. Living in America provided me with a convenient reason not to make contact since Lunar New Year isn't widely celebrated here. The tension stemmed from my complicated relationship with my parents. I maintain communication with them mainly out of a sense of duty and obligation. The day went by without any contact from either side, leaving me with mixed emotions. I was uncertain about reaching out. My feelings towards my parents aren't positive, yet I experience guilt when I feel I'm not fulfilling my role as a daughter. I didn't have any specific needs or desires; I just wished these complex emotions didn't cause me anxiety. The situation left me feeling uncomfortable, guilty, disappointed, and resentful. I'm questioning whether there's anything left to salvage in my relationship with my parents. Not reaching out makes me wonder if perhaps there isn't.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me enough to cause anxiety and discomfort because I felt guilt and fear about being a bad daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me a little bit by showing that I'm not that close to my parents anymore, so it's okay not to reach out for Lunar New Year.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The negative relationship I had with my parents as a child was responsible for this. I learned not to trust my parents when I was young, so I detached from them emotionally. As I got older, I had to pretend to care about them to feel like a good daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, not really. I was wondering the entire time if my parents would reach out, which they didn't. I felt like I had no control over that. If they reached out, I would feel bad that I didn't. I get a shot of anxiety every time my parents contact me, and I don't have control over that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was a little surprised they didn't reach out, which gave me a mild feeling of disappointment but also relief. I was a little surprised at myself for not reaching out because I felt internal pressure to.

situation: A colleague of mine made a mistake at work. He misunderstood the content of a document sent to a client and emailed them saying I made a mistake. When I told him that wasn't the case the next day, he then asked that I email the client to let them know. I wasn't really trying to do anything. I had completed a task accurately and my colleague stepped in inappropriately. I was very annoyed and frustrated with my colleague. I feel like it's indicative of a larger problem with the sales team (my colleague is a salesperson). They consistently make errors and are never really called up on it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me quite a bit because it felt like another instance in a long line of unresolved problems with the sales team, which haven't been addressed by senior management.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation hurt me as it made me look incompetent to the client and put me in an awkward position with my colleague, requiring me to correct him and refuse to email the client myself to rectify the issue.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like my colleague was mostly responsible for handling the situation poorly. I also think senior management is at fault for not addressing the long-standing issues with the sales team and their interactions with other teams in the company.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control because I don't have the authority in the company to reprimand another colleague or create better processes.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't really have any particular expectations as I hadn't expected this situation to arise at all.

situation: I had a rough day at work, and when I got home, I decided to shower and impulsively cut my bangs. I didn't have the proper scissors for a haircut, and I ended up cutting my bangs way too short. This led to a meltdown over my bad haircut. I was trying to change my appearance to make myself feel better, but instead, it left me feeling stupid and ugly. I wanted to take control of the situation, but ironically, I ended up feeling even less in control.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I care a lot about my appearance. I like to feel beautiful.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I actually made myself look worse than before.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was definitely most responsible for my own bad haircut.
appraisal_reasoning.control: When I was cutting my hair I felt in control, but the subsequent results made me feel out of control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, definitely not. I was not expecting my bangs to be that short.

situation: I heard a story about some young men abusing an ewe, and it left me feeling really disturbed and emotional. I wanted to talk to my boyfriend about it because I needed to understand what leads someone to do something like that. I was hoping to find a way to prevent it from happening in the future.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was today I read about it, it mattered to me a lot because I love animals.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Just makes me feel sad and worry about this happening to other animals.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The men involved.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because I was reading about it, I don't know them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, expected, unexpected story though.

situation: I recently had to move from Hawaii to Florida. I had been living in Hawaii for nearly 10 years, but after the pandemic, my business took too much of a loss, and I lost everything, including my life savings. I haven't been able to come back from it, so I decided to come back to live with my parents in Florida and redo my life here. I was trying to find ways around moving to Florida, as my parents asked me to come live here a year ago. I really tried my best to find ways around it, but I couldn't. Now, I will have to find a job here in Florida, where I don't know anybody, and I will have to find some 9-5 job. I get sad sometimes because I miss my life and community back in Hawaii. There's nothing like it where I'm at now. At first, I really put off moving. Most days I'm okay, but if I talk to a friend back in Hawaii, I miss it so much and I get sad again. I decided to start looking at the positives. My parents live in a beautiful home near the beach, and I am just taking it day by day.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It didn't matter much in the grand scheme of things. I think what I am feeling is normal and a part of my life is completely changed. What triggered it was talking to a friend back in Hawaii, and I began to reminisce about my life back there and how happy I was.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has helped me so that I can start saving money and be able to be in a more financially secure living situation. It's challenging because I don't have my community that I was very close to back in Hawaii and I had a lot of freedom and fun there. There's not many people in this town, and I just really love Hawaii, the state. It's just something I have to accept.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The pandemic was the beginning of the end of my business and way of life. From there I have just been constantly struggling to pay bills. It's hard to make a living there. As far as the feeling of sadness and emotion last week, I think it's just part of my grieving process as I just moved a month ago.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I don't. Because there was no way to control the end of my business and trying to survive like everyone else. This was out of my hands. As far as my sadness this last week, yes I was in control because I was able to move past it quite quickly. I was only emotional for a few minutes.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They have been better than I thought! Yes, my parents have been incredibly supportive. I was concerned how we would get along as we have a history of getting into arguments over politics but we agreed not to discuss politics and they made it clear they want me to do better and I can see how kind they are being.

situation: Some of the staff were being rude about another colleague, and I felt it was important to challenge this behavior. I told them they shouldn't be making those comments because what they were saying was incorrect, not fair, or right. Unfortunately, they turned the situation around and told that colleague that I was the one making the comments, simply because I had told them not to. This has made my work very stressful now. The colleague now refuses to talk to me because she believes I was at fault, which has left me feeling really frustrated. I think if she had believed me, it would have made our relationship stronger, and that was important to me, but unfortunately, she did not.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The events happened on Sunday and had continued to cause conflict this week. It mattered to me a lot as the person was my friend.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Because there were lies about me this has caused me a lot of hurt and confusion.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The two girls that have made up lies about me to my friend.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I had no control, because the conversation has been manipulated and lied behind my back.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No. I’d never have expected this and I would have expected my friend to believe me.

situation: I was scrolling through social media when I came across a post from a man who was in tears because his dog was lost. He was devastated after several days of searching, and it was frustrating to see people telling him he should have ensured the dog couldn't get out. The dog wasn't even with him when it went missing; it was with a dog walker who let it off its lead when they shouldn't have done so. I wanted people to read the story of how the dog went missing rather than tearing into him without understanding the situation. It annoyed me that these people had no compassion and offered nothing but horrible remarks instead of being supportive or just keeping their mouths shut with their insults. I felt compassion for the owner and upset for the dog, imagining how devastated I would be in his position, having dogs of my own. It's important to me that people realize how cruel they can be with their cutting remarks on social media. They should walk a mile in another's shoes before judging.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I saw the post a few days ago, and I have even gone back to it to see if there might be an update of the dog being found, but there are no updates. It matters because I have dogs, and I know people who have lost animals, which sometimes end in tragedy for the animal. I hope this one had a happy ending though.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Thoughts of how I would feel losing my dogs or just one, and upset at the way the owner was treated.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The dog walker letting the dog off lead without permission and the cruelty of strangers online.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I have no control over the situation but did chip in calling out those who were cruel, suggesting empathy not judgement.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I ended up blocking 2 people who were nasty in reply, most just ignored my comment, hopefully they went back, read the story, and felt remorse for their harsh judgement.

situation: My dad became unwell and had to go to the hospital for a few days, which was really worrying. He's okay now, but during that time, I was trying hard to stay calm and relaxed. It was tough to take my mind off of it until he was discharged and back at home. Once it was all over, I felt a huge sense of relief, but I'm also nervous about the possibility of it happening again, especially since my dad is quite old now. It's likely to occur more often in the future. One thing that really mattered to me was seeing how my family reacted. I thought I might be dealing with it alone, but others were supportive and helped a lot. I still had to work during that time, so I couldn't be there as much as I wanted.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was immediately the biggest issue in my life. Other things didn't seem very important once that happened, so it made me feel quite single minded. Obviously when your parents become ill it will always be a very important thing you have to deal with.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I would say overall it was an unpleasant experience. Even though there were some positive things I noticed, my overall feeling was worry and stress. It made me feel much less focused at work, luckily my employer was understanding, but I was still not happy with how I was as a person during that time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I didn't really feel like anyone was responsible as such, it is a normal part of life. I suppose I felt responsible for my own actions during that time, but I'm not sure how much I would be able to change that in the future.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I didn't, there was nothing I could do to really influence the situation. I just had to wait and hope that things would end well. Luckily they did.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Overall it went mostly how I expected. I was slightly surprised with how supportive my extended family was though, so that was probably the best thing to come out of the experience.

situation: Soccer season is starting again, and I'm feeling really positive about it. I love watching my children play and just enjoy educating them about the game. Seeing them out there makes me feel happy and proud.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few days ago and it meant quite a bit to me because my children are very important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The soccer season helped me by keeping my children busy and active, also providing social interaction.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Not one person in particular was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt a little in control but not much. My children playing soccer is not within my control or how they play, but me encouraging them is within my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had no expectations other than my children would try their best.

situation: I was already running late for work when I discovered my car had a flat tire. I needed to change it to a spare, but at the same time, I was trying to take care of my daughter. I wanted to make sure the car was safe because I had to drop her off at nursery on the way. The whole situation left me feeling stressed, upset, and angry. My daughter, being young, didn't understand that I was stressed. Despite everything, ensuring her safety was my top priority.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the morning around 9am and it mattered a lot as it was the start of the day and I had responsibilities.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was alone as the only adult so it wasn't helpful. But I guess my daughter being happy helped a bit. She is a toddler so didn't understand the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am not sure as I do not understand how the tyre was flat, maybe bad road conditions.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Kinda, I know how to change a tyre but was difficult to control both situations of the car and daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected I changed the tyre but it took longer than it normally would.

situation: I found out that one of the bills I pay was paid twice because the company made a mistake and paid next month's bill early. I discovered the error on Saturday night, which was super frustrating because I couldn't get in contact with anyone at the company until Monday morning. I needed reassurance that the situation would be resolved and I wouldn't have to pay fees to my bank for an overdraft. I felt very upset and worried. It was important to me that the company correct their error.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Saturday night. I saw the notification in my email. It mattered a great deal because I knew that I was going to be negative in my bank account on Monday.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation caused me to not be able to buy groceries for the week or be able to buy my mom a birthday gift for her birthday that is tomorrow.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: AT&T was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I had zero control over the situation. I did not make the error and was unable to correct the error myself. That is infuriating.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Once I spoke with an agent on Monday morning they assured me that it was their error and it would be corrected. However, it will take 5-7 business days to get my money back. I'm not happy with that resolution.

situation: A friend that I had a falling out with a couple of years ago just recently contacted me, and I haven't responded to him yet. I just want to know if he's in a good place and if he's wanting to change from how he was before when our friendship ended. The whole situation is mostly negative for me; it's stressful and causes me anxiety. I'm worried about how I will be personally judged after making no life progress in the last couple of years since we last talked. I feel embarrassed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened recently when my friend contacted me. It matters to me because the situation is mostly negative, causing stress and anxiety. I'm worried about being personally judged after making no life progress in the last couple of years since we last talked, and I feel embarrassed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation has mainly caused me stress. I had grown used to life without this friend, even though I missed him frequently. The challenge is that he and one of my other close friends had issues with each other, so bringing him back into my life could also bring back potential tension between them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like he is the one most responsible because he was causing problems with my friend when my friend was not being problematic. He also had issues with alcohol that were changing his personality.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't feel entirely in control. I can't know how to feel about him until we truly have a conversation, but I fear that the conversation may make me feel worse.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because I didn't expect him to reach out in the first place. We have yet to actually talk, as I haven't responded to him beyond acknowledging his reaching out.

situation: I had a situation where my friend got drunk and stole his wife's car, then drove to his brother's house. We managed to locate him the next day, and the car was indeed at his brother's place. During this whole ordeal, I was trying to calm him down and find him. The situation left me feeling disappointed and upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a great deal. He is a good friend and I was very concerned about his safety and the safety of others.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think that this situation was very impactful to me and let me know that I am not in control of all the people's motions and will have to deal with the consequences of their actions at a later time. The best thing that I can do is provide support.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My friend was most responsible for this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control. I was at the mercy of him in his time. Whenever he was able to respond because he left his cell phone and left the house without any issues.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected, and I still only have one side of the story. I will sit down and talk with him and have a very deep conversation about this and try to get him professional help.

situation: My daughter was accepted to her first choice high school and got a really great scholarship package. I was hoping she got accepted, so I was really excited and wanted to share the news with her. I was really happy and felt relieved that the application process was over. I knew it was the best choice for my child, so there was a lot of relief about where she would go next year.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I got the phone call yesterday. The application process took several months and involved a lot of work. I was worried she wouldn't be accepted anywhere.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It really helped because if she wasn't accepted it would have meant attending public school. It would have been a terrible and stressful time for her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think my daughter was most responsible for her success.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt a little bit in control because I could help guide her on where the best place to apply was. I also I am the one contributing financially.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: She didn't get into her safety school which was a surprise. It made it more of a relief that she got into her first choice.

situation: I had a disagreement with my aunt. My wife and I have been sending her gifts for years every holiday, and we recently found out that she has been piling those gifts up in her garage, along with many other things, like a hoarder. I wanted her to respect how much we care about her and clean that mess up. I needed her to understand that what she did is not okay and that people don't live like that. It's not normal and needs to be cleaned up. It was important to me that she realized it's hurtful to my wife and me. It's so disrespectful.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It's been happening for the past couple weeks but actually started last spring. We recently got photos from her on how bad it is and it's bad.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt us to know how bad her garage is and that she doesn't care about the gifts we send or the fact of being clean.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She was absolutely responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. I felt she was sneaky and did this for years and we had no idea until last year.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No things didn't. Once again she promised to clean it all up and has done absolutely nothing.

situation: On Monday, I went to my son's high school for his freshman orientation. They held the meeting so parents and students know what to expect for the next school year when he starts high school. My emotions got to me knowing that my son is growing up and it has gone so fast. It caused me to reminisce how it just seemed like yesterday he was just learning to walk. It made me realize how fast time goes and to cherish all the moments, because they will be here and gone quickly. It's also hard to accept the realization that he is close to being an adult.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday, and it mattered a lot to me. I want and need to know what to expect so I can best support my son during his first year of high school. I'm sure it will be fun for him, but I'm almost certain there will also be challenges.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think it helped me by realizing how impactful and important this step in his young life is. Knowing that prepares me to be there to support him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The orientation itself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yeah, I felt in total control. It helped that I'm sure I wasn't the only parent feeling this way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as expected.

situation: I was just walking out my front door to throw some trash in my dumpster when a vehicle drove down the street. This vehicle was heavily damaged from some kind of accident and could barely execute the turn onto our road. Suddenly, several police cars swarmed this damaged vehicle. Officers approached the vehicle with weapons drawn, directing the driver to exit the vehicle. The driver exited but quickly reached around and produced a gun. The police fired several shots at the person, who dropped to the ground. He was pronounced dead at the scene. I was just trying to take my trash out. I was very shaken. I'd never seen someone shot to death before. I understand that the police officers were being threatened with a gun but I wish they could have used a non-lethal method to apprehend this person.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal to me because I abhor violence. I also live in a very quiet area, so it was disturbing to see something like this happen right in front of the house.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I found it hurtful to see police gunning someone down.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like society at large is ultimately responsible. This person was most likely desperate, hence why they fled from police and felt they had no recourse but to fight to the bitter end.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was absolutely not in control. I was just a witness.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No. I thought the police would apprehend this person peacefully. I did not at all expect to see a shooting.

situation: I made a new friend who is a member of my community, the LGBTQ community. We have a lot in common, including enjoying the same music. She is very down to earth and really fun to be around. I was trying to make a new friend, specifically someone who is a member of the LGBTQ community, and I needed someone who was friendly. The situation left me feeling completely fulfilled, like I had succeeded in finding a new friend.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot. I had been seeking this type of person for a long time. I was in disbelief because the friend who introduced us did not mention their sexual orientation. Instead I learned their sexual orientation while speaking with them.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because I have someone I can share specific things with. I would say it could hurt me because I now have a new person to care about.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My friend was invited to a bar to hang out with her friend and I just happened to tag along.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, definitely. I was driving that night and it was my decision whether or not to go to the bar.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: For the most part. My friend and I weren't given directions to the bar and missed the turn. However, when we finally found the bar, we ended up having a great time.

situation: I had been talking to a guy online who wanted to see my face. Despite feeling insecure and often thinking I look ugly or like a boy, I decided to send him a picture. This made me incredibly nervous. I was trying to make him happy and wanted comfort and reassurance afterwards. When he didn't answer immediately, I felt really nervous and just went to bed. I wanted to feel validated and be sure I was his type.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few days ago. It mattered a lot, because I like him a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel more confident afterwards because he did indeed find me pretty.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: HIM!!! He kept asking for it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really. He kept begging, and I sent it to get him off my back.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was... unexpected. I didn't expect him to like me honestly.

situation: I was watching the news about war, just sitting there thinking it's crazy. I really wanted peace. The whole situation left me feeling a little bit sad. There wasn't much else on my mind, except maybe wondering whose news to trust.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event is happening this week, right now, and it matters quite a bit to me because war affects all of us. I want everyone to be safe.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation didn't help me; it hurt my feelings, seeing war.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that governments and money are most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected to an extent, meaning bombs were going off.

situation: I attended a school's performance last night at the opera house in the Winter Gardens, Blackpool. My son was on stage, and I felt emotional thinking about the age of the building, my own age, and the fact that after 40 years, with the most recent 20 spent overseas, I am living here again. I am almost three years post-stroke, and I feel my emotions are sometimes affected. I didn't want or need anything; I was just there to watch. I felt grounded seeing my son on stage and thinking I could never imagine being back there after so many years. Maybe knowing my son has a lifetime ahead was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Last night it mattered to be there with my wife and daughter to support him even though he could not see us due to the lights.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Helping would be valuing my life but also that makes me emotional due to my age and possibly health.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: What as the opera theatre must be 100 years old and had wartime activities for troops.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control but felt like crying.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I didn't expect to feel so emotional but it wasn't a problem.

situation: I got a message from someone, and I really appreciated it. I had bought a gift for this person, and they sent me a text message to thank me for the gift. I just thought it was a really nice gesture. I wasn't expecting anything, but it came out of the blue, and it was really lovely to receive the message. It left me feeling very happy and pleased that my small gift had gone down well. The individual also sent some lovely photos, and they were really lovely to see.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because it was lovely to be thanked. Everyone likes to be appreciated.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because the message made me happy. No hurt was involved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The individual themselves thought of sending the message, so they were responsible for the outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It was not a question of control at all. I thought I would do something nice for someone and it was reciprocated, that is all.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I suppose it was a lovely surprise.

situation: Scenario: I decided to increase my dosage on my anti-depression medication from 20mg to 30mg, but it turned into a big hassle. I had to jump through a bunch of hoops, including talking to a doctor and having my pharmacy call my insurance company. It was a very frustrating experience and took a lot of effort. I felt a little frustrated and disappointed that this process was so difficult to achieve. On top of that, my cost more than doubled, and it took almost 2 weeks to get approved. Now that I have the new prescription, I am hopeful that my mood will improve a little.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters a lot because I have cancer and I am going through hormone therapy, and my mood has been very low.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped because after all the hoops I jumped through, my approval just came today for increasing the dosage.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible for taking steps to get the dosage increased, however, it could have been a much easier process for sure.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was not in control and at the mercy of the insurance company on whatever they decided.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They did in the end go as I expected, it just took longer and was more frustrating than I would have expected.

situation: I was coming out of a store when a solicitor stopped me to ask if I would like to donate. I said no thank you, but she blocked my way. As I walked past, she called me rude, and I turned around and told her she was the one being rude, and that I was polite by saying no thank you. She started yelling at me, telling me to get the store manager, and I told her she was harassing customers and should stop. Then she started asking for my name and said she was calling her supervisor. I looked at the donation table to get the name of the organization and proceeded to leave, but she followed me to my car. I just wanted to pass her by and leave the store, so I said no thank you. But she wouldn't let me leave easily. I wanted to get away. I've been in a situation where I was assaulted in my past, so no means no, but she didn't want to accept no as an answer. I felt like I should stand up for myself and for all the customers being harassed by her. I was shaking so bad, I couldn't stop crying, and I was scared. Justice was important to me. No one should be treated that way. So I called the store manager, I called the local police, and then the organization she was representing. In the end, they were told if they kept harassing people, they would be asked to leave, and the organization said it was an independent marketing company providing this service and they were going to stop using them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When it first happened, I was so upset I couldn't calm down. After a few days went by, I was better, especially knowing justice was served in the end. It matters to me because I did not have a voice in the past, but I did this time, and no means no, no matter who is asking or what is going on.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: At first, it hurt me because I felt scared and attacked, and my past trauma made me feel like I was making a mountain out of a molehill. But, after it was resolved, and especially after talking to a representative from the organization, it helped me to see that I am very strong and that no one can take my power from me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The person most responsible for this is the solicitor. If she had accepted the 'no thank you' answer, nothing else would have happened.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at first, but after I left, I felt in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They did not go as expected. I thought the store manager, the police officer, and the organization would all say that I was making a big deal out of nothing, but instead they all took it seriously and resolved the issue.

situation: I got engaged last week. I've been with my partner for 11 years and finally decided to propose to her. I found a beautiful spot by a lake to do it. It was a cold and windy day, but my resolve was strong. It was an emotional moment because I expressed my love unconditionally, and my partner cried. I wanted to show my love and create a beautiful experience to share together. Afterward, I felt extremely happy and relieved, like a weight came off my chest. It was important to me that I did it right so that the moment would remain special forever.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened one week ago. It mattered a lot to me because it was an important moment for me and the person that means the most to me in the world.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because it allowed us to move forward to the next part of our lives.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible for creating this situation and for pushing it forward.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like it was in my control where it happened but I had to find the perfect spot because several spots weren't appropriate.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected because she said yes but there were some things that weren't as expected, such as the location. I had to adapt on the fly.

situation: I was at work, focused on a document, when I got a call from a friend. He told me that an old school mate had lost his dad. The news hit me hard, and I felt sad and emotional. I couldn't really function well afterwards. I had to reach out to my friend to find out how he was doing. There wasn't anything else on my mind; I was just devastated by the sad news.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened at work, in the afternoon while I was still working. It mattered to me because it was a close friend.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Mostly just hurt me, and also made me realize again how fickle life is.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself, I'm quite an emotional person so things always get to me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I think I was in control, was just a momentarily feeling.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yh eventually everything turned out fine.

situation: My mother-in-law was taken ill and admitted to the hospital, which caused quite a lot of anxiety and worry in the family. It involved a 3-day hospital admission and various tests and scans. She was admitted last Monday following a small fall. She has various medical conditions, and the fall made her unwell. We were unsure if she had broken or twisted her ankle, so we had to take her to the doctor first, who recommended hospital for tests, x-rays, and blood tests, etc. We wanted certainty that she was safe and had suffered no long-term damage or injury. The fall impacted her mood, appetite, and how she took her various medications. It left our whole family feeling worried, and it was only after the various tests were carried out that we felt reassured she was safe and not suffering any long-term medical issues. We did not want her in the hospital for a long period as she likes to be at home around her family.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When it happened it felt very bad like an emergency. We had a similar situation with an elderly relative who had a fall and she required several weeks in hospital, so we naturally worried this may be the same situation with my mother-in-law.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not help; it sort of hurt us mentally due to the anxiety and uncertainty.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: As a family, we all take responsibility, but due to her gender, my wife probably has the most responsibility.
appraisal_reasoning.control: To be honest, I did not feel any real sense of control as we relied on and trusted the medical opinion from the doctor and hospital.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: In the end, it worked out well thankfully. We could have perhaps had a day less in hospital, but we had to rely on the hospital doctors to authorize being released to go home. It could have been worse, and we were grateful it worked out well despite the rushing back and forth and initial anxiety.

situation: I went to the library with my daughter, and we ended up playing chess together. It wasn't just any chess set; it was a giant floor chess set, which made the whole experience really fun. Originally, I just wanted to get some books with her, but the unexpected chess game turned out to be a highlight. I felt happy because we had a lot of fun together, and I'm glad we decided to play even though it wasn't part of the plan.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: We went to the library around 2pm. No one was there. The library felt empty. It was just my daughter and me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped since we were able to focus on each other and had fun playing a chess game without any distractions.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: An old homeless man eventually wandered in the library. He started to watch us play.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt a bit uneasy knowing I was being watched. I did make a stupid move and he laughed at my move which made me feel even more unsure.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, the man eventually walked away and we finished the game. We still had a lot of fun.

situation: I attended the funeral of a male coworker. I was there to support his family during this difficult time. I felt sad, but I was glad I could offer some comfort to them. It was important to me to talk about how much of a great person he was.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: My coworker died the week before last, but the funeral was this past Friday. It mattered to me because I wanted to support his family and remember him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Attending the funeral helped me personally by being there for the family and remembering him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt most responsible for offering words of comfort to his family.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control because I showed compassion and was there.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as I'd expect.

situation: The situation I'm thinking about is a work project that has finally come to an end. I wanted to be able to complete the project while still being friendly with my coworkers, without getting too upset with them. Now that it's finished, I feel a bit glad that we got it done, but I'm also feeling a bit run down. There wasn't anything else particularly important to me in this situation besides just wanting to get the project finished.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened at work, about 3 months ago. It mattered a lot to me because I wanted to get the project completed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It impacted me by taking up my work days and making me tired. There was a positive aspect by letting me work with my coworkers more closely.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like we were all responsible for this as a team.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control during the project because everything somewhat ran smoothly.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The did go as expected.

situation: I'm starting to lose my hair because of the chemotherapy, and it's making me feel really nervous and sad. My scalp is painful and itching, which just adds to the discomfort. I feel torn because I want my hair to come out, but at the same time, I don't want it to. I'm anxious about wearing a wig and whether it will look real. Overall, I'm feeling anxious, worried, and sad. I just want to feel and look normal.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I had my first chemotherapy two weeks ago. The itching and tenderness has just started in the last few days. It matters to me because I don't want people to feel sorry for me and I want to be able to do my normal daily life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It makes me feel sad that I will lose my hair. It's making my confidence low.
