appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The chemotherapy. I also think that if my doctor would have caught it or listened to me earlier I wouldn't have needed chemo.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really. My doctor told me she didn't think the mass was anything to be concerned about and we left it alone for over a year.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not at all. Once she had it removed it came back cancerous and then when they removed it they found it had spread.

situation: This week, my husband had to undergo many health checks, which was really emotional for us. I was anxiously waiting for the results of the tests. At the time, it made me very nervous because I was basically trying to put our minds at rest.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened at the beginning of this week and it matters very much to me because it concerns my husband's health.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because of the unknown and the uncertainty about outcomes. It made me nervous and anxious.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the doctors and hospitals were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because it seemed like the doctors and hospitals were in control. The fact that other people were also waiting for results didn't help me feel more in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: At this time, we are still waiting for the outcome. There are always unexpected surprises, but that's life.

situation: I was informed that I had received a promotion at work, which meant I would be working my last week at the store I was currently at. I was trying to improve my standing in the organization with this promotion, and I needed positive reinforcement from my employees and peers. Overall, I felt positive about the promotion, but it was also bittersweet because I had grown close to a lot of the employees at my old location, and I will miss them. It was important to me to receive validation from my former employees that they enjoyed working with me and felt I did a good job.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened at the beginning of last week as I was informed at the beginning of the week. It was important to me because I had been working hard to receive a promotion.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me financially as I will be making more money. My new store is closer to home so I will have less of a drive and it helped me achieve a goal. There’s much more pressure on performance and setting up a new store will be intense and require many hours at first.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself, my employees, my peers, my supervisors.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Some of the time yes because it was my job to inspire and motivate the team. However there were times things happened outside my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: For the most part, they went as expected. I felt I had a chance to get promoted last year but it didn’t happen.

situation: I traveled from London to Nottingham by coach to meet a great friend and see a tribute band perform at the theatre. We had planned to meet and treat ourselves to dinner first at a top local restaurant. I arrived an hour early to give myself a time buffer in case of traffic problems or delays. I got there in good time and navigated my way to the restaurant for our booking, but the mobile phone reception in Nottingham was poor, and my GPS kept cutting out. I got to the restaurant with 5 minutes to spare, and as I arrived, my phone rang—it was my friend. Unfortunately, we couldn't hear each other because mobile reception was so poor. I tried texting her but kept getting errors saying 'message send failed' after sending. I didn't want us to lose our booking—they only give 15 minutes leeway—so I went inside the restaurant to take a seat at our reserved table. My friend kept trying to call, but I couldn't hear her, and this went on for 10 minutes. I tried connecting to the restaurant wifi but was forced to sign up with my email address, which they emailed me a confirmation code that I couldn't receive because I couldn't get any signal. Somehow, I managed to get a voicemail from her explaining she was still 75 miles away, stuck in stationary traffic on the M1, and would not make it in time for dinner. She said I should order, eat, and meet her outside the theatre at 7pm (the gig was due to start at 7:30pm). I did as she suggested, ate, paid the bill, and walked to the theatre. I waited outside in an area with no mobile signal but somehow received a text from her that she was still 20 miles away, stuck in a long tailback on the M1. She sent me an image of my ticket and said to go in for the start of the performance, and we would meet during the interval. I was so despondent that we weren't going to see the gig, that we've waited 6 months for, together. I felt terrible—as much for her being stuck in traffic and missing out, as for me. I knew she would be so stressed when she finally arrived very late, through no fault of her own.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Tuesday. It mattered a lot because I had been waiting 6 months and traveled 300 miles to see her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because she and I will always remember this night for all the wrong reasons.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Whoever caused the huge traffic problem on the M1 is the person responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I had no control during this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things didn't go to plan. My friend did not arrive until after the interval, so she missed over half the gig.

situation: When my dog died, I was really struggling and needed support. It left me feeling very bad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened quickly and hurt. It mattered to me because it hurt my soul with no best friend left.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me deeply, leaving me without my best friend.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that God was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of anything during this time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it was sudden and unexpected.

situation: A few days ago, I was trying to relax and read a book when my cat got into a fight with another neighborhood cat that had wandered into our yard. Suddenly, my cat chased the other cat over the fence, and it scared me because I thought he might run away. I felt high on adrenaline because I was so surprised and alarmed by the whole situation. During that time, the only thing that mattered to me was my cat's safety.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago and it mattered a lot to me because my cat means everything to me. He's my best friend, and during that time, the only thing that mattered to me was my cat's safety.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt my ability to trust that my cat is safe in the backyard.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The neighborhood cat was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control because my cat would not listen to me and chased the other cat away over the fence.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The cat jumping into the yard to scare my cat was very unexpected.

situation: For the past three months, I've been focused on rebuilding a part of my business, specifically outreach through phone calls and text messages. It turned out that all this time, there was something they had no clue needed fixing. I wanted to automate my outreach so I wouldn't spend all day hitting dead leads. Initially, I felt like, 'here we go again,' as if there's always something working against me, trying to take me out of the game. Now that everything is fixed, I'm just making sure to keep moving forward towards the next hurdle or bump in the road. It was really important to me not to lose money paying for a membership that wasn't working.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event started back in Nov 2025. It was/is important because it marked the beginning of things working and moving forward.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me be patient and hurt me through continued stillness.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Ultimately, it is my business, right? However, this was a tech issue that the people who I pay money to couldn't fix the problem in a good and efficient enough time to not hurt or hinder my business.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control because there was nothing for me to 'fix' on my end. Everything was through email with them, and I wouldn't get a response back for days and weeks.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Eventually, things did go as I expected once it was fixed.

situation: I called a number to file a report on my daughter's behalf about the abuse she's experiencing when she visits her mom and three sisters. Even though the case was closed, it's not over. The situation is emotionally charged because the circumstances persist. Even worse, she received much worse treatment while the case was open, while the worker talked to my daughters sisters and my daughter in school! The increased mean-treatment while the case was open and being investigated is a direct result of my own daughter telling me what her sister did! Trying to help herself by telling me so that I can help, and all it did was cause my daughter to get treated so cruel and mean there!!!!  I was trying to get the abuse to stop when she's over there. There are many other details I needed to tell them in person, not over the phone. They were supposed to visit me at our home, but they didn't, so it remains unsolved in many aspects. The situation left me feeling more emotionally charged than I've ever been. I felt hopeless, daunting, panic, and extremely angry inside. These feelings were subsided by my concern that my daughter is the one going through this, normalizing the behaviors, and now even more afraid to tell me things that were a struggle to get her to say. There's no true feeling that describes this; however, it's a very negative feeling, in such a dark deep way. My fear to report has been significant as well. When I finally did report one little thing, I heavily relied on the fact that they were supposed to do a home visit, where I was going to tell them the rest. There's a powerful reason this scares me so much, so the tension, anxiety, and outright fear to report finally, then after relying so heavily on the home visit that they decided not to do, is beyond devastating. Details left out stretch back to years ago, with other major allegations, accusations, and incidents being left unheard now and unresolved. My daughter is not only left unsafe, but her trust in me and the system, which includes individuals in her school, has almost completely evaporated entirely, which is understandable. This case being closed causes even more severe issues now.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered more than anything because my daughter is being treated very badly, which hurts her emotionally and physically, leading to psychological damage she's likely to carry into adulthood. Her sisters and mother think they beat the system again, and are clearly skilled at it, which leaves me with further reservations but a stronger motive to contact a worker in person. I am hesitant because I don't want her mom in trouble, but that line was crossed previously and twice again in the last two days since she came back home with me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because my daughter is being hurt, and I am sure this affects her in other ways I am unaware of. That is a great deal of pain and heart-breaking. I need her safe and no longer hurt, and I need her to know that I haven't caused her to pay so dearly for telling me this stuff, because she certainly has paid dearly for telling me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Her mother and her sisters are most responsible for all of this, but it is her mother's fault ultimately. Her sisters are plenty old enough to know it is wrong, otherwise they wouldn't be able to lie to hide it all, so that leaves me feeling slightly confident in my blame for them as well.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Absolutely not. My control left when I reported it over the phone, and at that point, the control was in the county workers' hands. Considering they were even more mean to her after this report every single weekend since, not only do I have no control due to the system in charge, but they have successfully lied through this while continuing to do these illegal things to my daughter. I would feel more in control if they stopped after I reported, and even more so if they, at the very least, didn't hurt her even worse because she told me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I've stated the outcome and have focused on the stress surrounding this going unresolved. I simply expected my daughter to no longer get hurt from her sisters, but she has only gotten hurt worse due to this report.

situation: It was my granddaughter's 18th birthday last Sunday, and we had a precelebration at my house on Friday. Then, on Sunday, we all met up in Exeter for an Escape Room experience and a meal. I wanted to enjoy the celebration with my whole family, especially with my granddaughter. My family is very important to me, and we don't meet up enough, so I was really hoping for a drama-free gathering, which usually isn't the case when we all get together. This time, it left me feeling really good and appreciative of the special connection we have. I wanted my family to appreciate me, and I certainly think they do. My granddaughter asked me to voice record a special message for her to be inserted in a bear that I had given her 16 years ago, which was being revamped at the shop called Build a Bear. I felt special that she asked me to do that.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Sunday and mattered a huge amount to me. In the past, we have had difficulties as a family, and my children have been to counselling for their own problems, with some blame pointed at me about parenting. I tried my best with what I knew at the time, but it left me feeling that I was not good enough in their eyes. I wanted to create a special memory for my granddaughter and have a drama-free gathering.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me enormously, showing me that we could be the family I aspired to—loving, happy, and caring about each other.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We were all responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control. I thought about it before the event and how it could be made special. I enjoyed the event for what it was and did not make any assumptions of how it should have been or how it could be better.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went better than I expected. The unexpected was that my granddaughter asked me to do a special thing for her; she could have chosen mum or dad. I was flattered and privileged. The other unexpected thing was we got out of the escape room with 30 seconds to spare!

situation: I was helping a 97-year-old lady I support, who doesn't have much family nearby, as she had to move into a residential home. She was very upset about having to leave her home, and I was trying to be positive for her, helping her see that it was for the best since she could no longer take care of herself. I wanted her to feel as positive as possible about the situation, but I felt sad for her because I knew she really wanted to stay in her own home, even though she was struggling. It was important for me to be positive and upbeat, so I tried not to let her see that I was sad.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event only happened this week. It significantly mattered to me as she is a very important person in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I just felt sad for her. It made me think about how I would feel if it happened to me when I’m older.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I didn’t feel anyone was responsible- it was just the situation. She is so independent but she has become very frail and is no longer safe living alone so this is the best solution to keep her safe.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No not really - she has a son who had arranged for her to go into the home so it was out of my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes they mostly went as expected - I maybe underestimated how upset she would be.

situation: Last night, I was picking up a package and the security guard told me she was surprised I was Mexican because I looked like a 'little Jewish girl'. I felt kind of embarrassed and made up a lie that I got that comment all the time. I find myself really perplexed by that interaction. In that situation, I just wanted to escape as quickly as possible because I was very uncomfortable. I don't know how I feel. Maybe embarrassed. What was important to me in that situation was that I got my packages and left as soon as possible.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last night. This mattered to me because people are always surprised that I am Mexican, which is really irritating to me as someone who strongly identifies with my ethnicity.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I feel hurt by the situation because it just reinforces the fact that no one sees me as the ethnic group I identify with.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel the thing that is most responsible for this interaction is just the general misunderstanding that people who are Hispanic or Latino look a certain way.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt a little out of control because I felt like I had to defend my belonging to an ethnic group, which isn't fair since this is the culture that I was born and raised in.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What caught me by surprise was that the security guard named a very specific religious-ethnic group they thought I was part of. Usually people default to describing me as White.

situation: My daughter-in-law informed me she was pregnant with my second grandchild. This was unexpected, so it was a very pleasant surprise. I wasn't trying to do anything at the time; I was just processing this good news that I wasn't expecting. Obviously, I was very happy at the prospect of having a new grandchild. It also meant that plans they had previously told me about were not going to happen now. It felt like it was meant to happen. The consequences of the previous plans were going to cause some upheavals to us as a family. The pregnancy meant we were not going to have to face that now. It was, in some ways, a relief.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal to me. Nothing is as important as family and the continuation of that family.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was just nice to get such lovely news. Life goes by either with not much happening or annoying incidents. This was a completely good news thing.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well my son and daughter-in-law. I can't take much responsibility here.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was being told of something that was entirely not in my control. It was like being given a gift as I know how joyful grandchildren are from my existing grandson.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole thing was unexpected especially as it changed the future plans of my son and daughter-in-law. It came totally out of left field.

situation: We had been having prior issues with our satellite TV box being down for long periods of time, especially after it would freeze up and restart itself. The situation occurred the other night when the TV froze, and we couldn't use any of the buttons to try to bring it out of the frozen state. I needed it to come right back on after I unplugged it. I was a little anxious because of previous experiences with the same thing occurring and then not being able to watch TV for a long time afterwards.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered quite a bit to me because I wanted to watch TV and we had several shows lined up to record on the DVR that evening, which I didn't want to miss.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation didn't help me at all, and I can't think of how it hurt me per se.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the TV provider was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control because there was nothing I could do to fix it if it decided not to come right back up.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things ended up being unexpected, but after I plugged the TV back in, it came right back up!

situation: When someone I considered a friend made a racist joke, I felt angry and confused. I thought this person would not treat me in such a disrespectful manner, but I guess I assumed incorrectly. I was trying to connect with them by talking with them, wanting to have someone treat me respectfully and like an equal. I definitely did not want to be the butt of a racist joke. The situation left me feeling like I cannot trust people as much as I thought I could. I felt anxious and sad as well. It was important to me that when I told him how I felt, he minimized my feelings and did not seem to find the joke offensive despite it not being about his race.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot because I told him prior that I did not want to engage with his racist jokes anymore, and I also have said that the n-word makes me uncomfortable, especially when white people reference it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation hurt me because it made me feel like I was not respected by my friend, and it made me feel like he did not care about how I felt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think my friend was most responsible since they did not seem to want to take responsibility for making a racist joke about black people.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt not in control since I felt like I could not control how much I was being respected or how I was being talked to.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected since I thought he would be understanding when I expressed my frustration, but he seemed confused and tried to minimize the situation.

situation: I was just sitting down, minding my own business, when suddenly, a football hit me in the face over the weekend. It was really painful, but instead of showing concern, everyone just laughed. It was particularly disappointing because everyone around me was family, and I expected them to care more. I felt like no one cared about me, and it would have been nice for someone to ask how I was instead of just finding the situation amusing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Sunday at my parents' house while I was watching TV. It mattered to me because no one cared, and I thought my family would care. It made me feel small and worthless.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me realize that maybe my family doesn't care as much as I thought. I'm already having a bad time with my mental health, which my sister knows, but she was the main instigator laughing, so it hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My nephew did it, but he's a child, so I can't blame him totally; he's still learning right from wrong. My sister-in-law could have told him it wasn't nice to do that, and my sister could have asked if I was okay.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all. I was ready to burst into tears and eventually went to the toilet and cried on my own.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected. I received no sympathy from anyone; all I wanted was someone to ask 'are you ok?' and I didn't even get that. I don't ask for much, but a little 'are you ok' would go a long way.

situation: Two years ago, I was diagnosed with cancer, and now, two years on, I'm still cancer-free. I recently went for my regular two-month check-up, and the doctor told me there was no sign of the cancer coming back. I know I have to wait for the five-year all-clear, but every time I go for my check-up, it's still very emotional for me. I went in feeling nervous as always, just sat there while the doctor had the camera up my nose and down my throat. He took his usual pictures and compared them to the previous ones, and this is the part I fear the most. It's only when he gives me the good news that I can finally relax. As always, I left feeling on a high, a bit tearful, but they were happy tears. This experience gives me the confidence to look forward to the future and start making concrete plans for holidays.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The most difficult news to deal with, being told you have cancer. My wife's first question to the oncologist was, 'Is he going to die?' As you can expect, this was absolutely life-changing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I turned inward, depression kicked in, my outlook was bleak. Nobody can give you a definitive answer. They can treat cancer, but they can't give any guarantees.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was responsible, it was nothing I did wrong. The cancer is linked to the HPV virus, I was just unlucky.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, no control. My life was now in the hands of the medical staff. They gave me the options, they gave me their beliefs, but ultimately let me decide. No way was I going against these professionals.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What they told me would happen did, not to say it was easy to deal with. Weeks in hospital, even longer having radiotherapy and all the good you hear about radiotherapy, there is a very big downside too.

situation: Flying and plane travel have always been a constant struggle for me. I had to get on a flight with my boyfriend for the first time, and we were headed to Belfast for my birthday trip. It was a new airline, a different type of plane, and the first time flying with him, which made the whole experience really scary for me. I don't feel okay until we're completely off the plane, and it left me feeling quite weak, like I'm not making any progress emotionally with dealing with this fear.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me more than anything else; it felt like a complete life or death situation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me as I felt very vulnerable.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt solely responsible for myself. When I am in total panic mode, I am kind of selfish and just worry completely about myself and my safety.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt completely out of control, and that is why I don't like it and then why I panic.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it was all completely fine, and I ended up being totally okay.

situation: I didn't have enough money to take my son out for his birthday. I was really hoping to have enough to celebrate his birthday in a way that felt special. Just like everything in this world, I needed more money. The whole situation left me feeling very crappy. My son's feelings were a significant concern for me in this situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened at a sad time and it mattered to me because my son's feelings were a significant concern for me. The whole situation left me feeling very crappy.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me emotionally; it hurt my heart and made me hate this world more.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the world was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I could be in control by making some side money.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because the amount of money I had was unexpected, but I have come to terms with it.

situation: I just found out that my neighbor had surgery, so I went over to visit her and realized she could really use some help. I went home and made two dinners for her and her family to help her out. I told her that I would like to help her out and do whatever she would let me do. While I was there, I picked up a few things and put them where they belonged, and she started crying, which made me cry too. She said her husband and two daughters don't help her much, and I felt really bad for her. After I helped a bit and brought her dinner for two nights, I felt a little better. If I would have known she had surgery, I would have asked what else I could do to help. I feel like by helping her, she values me not only as a neighbor but also as a friend.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened last weekend. It mattered to me because I like helping people, especially those that don't have any help, or those whose family don't help.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by feeling good by helping others. I like helping others, but still have time to do what is needed at my home, but still be available to help others as needed.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am not sure. I usually see this neighbor getting her mail and we wave to each other, but never really had conversations. After helping her, I feel like she could be a good friend. I got her phone number and now I text her often to see how she is doing.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control, because I knew what would help her out (bringing over dinner) because I didn't see where any food was prepared for a few days.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I believe things went as expected. She was very appreciative, and thanked me several times. She motioned me over to where she was sitting and gave me a meaningful hug.

situation: I had some good news at work; I found out my position was going to be kept. I was really nervous because I wanted my job to still remain, and until I found out that it was safe, I was on edge. But once I got the confirmation, I was overjoyed and felt a wealth of relief. This whole situation made me think a lot about my future, which was really important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was really important to me and my future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me understand that life is fleeting; you can have something and it can just as easily go away at any moment. I just got lucky this time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The big higher ups.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in no control whatsoever and I did not like that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't sure what to expect. That was a challenge.

situation: My car broke down after I had sent it to the mechanic to fix a previous issue that they had accidentally caused. Now, the mechanic has deemed my car unrepairable, and I have to purchase a new vehicle. I was trying to get my car repaired so I could drive it for a couple more years. I wanted the mechanic to actually fix their mistake that they did on my car, not tell me that now the damage is too extensive. It left me feeling extremely upset and nervous. The original issue was caused by the mechanic in the first place, and my car had zero issues prior to bringing it to him. I felt that he should have corrected his mistake and be held liable.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened this past week. It mattered to me a lot because I love my car and now it is broken beyond repair. I cannot afford a new vehicle or extensive repairs.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me a lot. It made me financially nervous about taking on a different car payment and car. It hurt me because the fix should have been a simple fix, but because of his reluctantness to fix the issue right away, it's a massive problem now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that the mechanic is mostly at fault, but I am as well for trusting this mechanic and not getting a second opinion or taking it to another mechanic to fix the issue right away.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was not in control because I had relied on this mechanic to fix the problem and felt like my car was in good hands. I did not have the car at the time of the fixing.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did not go as expected. The car was supposed to be repaired and I would be on my way. He would not fix his mistake so now it's an even bigger issue.

situation: I had a doctor's appointment that was super stressful. I got emotionally overwhelmed and drained because I was nervous about the results and had been sick for so long wanting answers. I needed to get blood work done to try to figure out if I was sick from mold or something else. After the appointment, I felt drained because the doctors did not have any answers for me or give me any medicine that would help me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Friday, and it mattered a lot to me because I have been sick for 6 months with no answers.

situation: My son got into the university he wanted to go to, and I was really excited about it. He was aiming to get into this particular university, and I wanted that for him too. It's a good university, so I was happy he got accepted. On top of that, he received a 100k scholarship to go there, which was really important to us.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me very much, it's his top choice and it's the university I wanted him to go to so hearing he got in on a scholarship too was hugely satisfying.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me in that I know I won't have to bear the whole brunt of the monetary cost of the university.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son definitely, my wife also helped him with applications and stuff like that.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I think so, if I asked how it was going they would tell me, but I was definitely not as involved as my wife.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected him to get in, but the scholarship was a surprise.

situation: A positive experience that happened very recently was my wedding, last weekend. I got married to my now husband after being together for nine years. I wanted a small family, friend-focused day with all our closest loved ones. Initially, I felt a bit worried and fearful about being on show, but eventually, I felt very content. It was important for me to remain calm, stay happy, and remember to enjoy the moment.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last weekend and it was the most important day of my life. It mattered a great deal because it was the beginning of a new chapter in my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped remind me that I'm loved, I'm capable, and a good enough person for someone to put their full trust into.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was half responsible for pretty much everything that happened, didn't happen, or went right/wrong.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I made decisions but in the moment allowed control to go to my husband.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went pretty much as expected as you can be; no amount of planning is ever fully perfect or spot on.

situation: My daughter had an anxiety attack and didn't want to go to school. I was trying to get her to school and needed her to get out of the car and go inside. I felt exhausted, worried, and angry with myself for allowing her to get to this point. It was important to me to get her brothers to school on time as well, so I had to keep her in the car while I dropped them off.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because my daughter needs to get an education and needs to be happy to do so. If she is not happy, then it's a major concern for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Her attendance has suffered because of several instances of this, but we have also discovered a number of available resources that can be used to help her in this situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think we as her parents are ultimately responsible; we didn't notice that she was suffering before it spilled out.
appraisal_reasoning.control: In some ways yes, in other ways no. I managed to convince her to go in, but it took a long time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, nothing went as expected that day.

situation: I went to the funeral of a friend. She wasn't a really close friend, but she didn't have many other people, and her husband was a broken shell. Seeing him stand on his own - this tall but broken man - was heartbreaking. I wasn't trying to do anything; I was attending a funeral. I did not want or need anything during the funeral except to provide comfort to my friend's husband. Afterwards, it left me thinking about my own experience with losing my mum, and how that seemed like such a long time ago even though it was only 18 months. I was reflective. I felt sad, and had a lot of questions about what happens after we die. I think what felt important was that I make plans for my own funeral, and work out how my family will cope when I am gone. I want to make it as easy as possible for everyone.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because she did not have many friends and her husband was her world. I was slightly more concerned about how he was doing, as he is the one left behind.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I don't think the situation particularly helped me, and the only hurt was that someone has passed away.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My friend was unwell for a long time, so no one was to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.control: At a funeral, you do the same things you are expected to do at every funeral. We are gathered there to mourn but also to celebrate the life of the person and learn about them. I do feel that I was in control, as much as I could have been.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as expected. It was a very religious funeral, which I was slightly unsure about but it did seem to go well.

situation: I had a meeting with a colleague who had ignored instructions at work, and I had to give them an official warning. I really needed the team member to follow policies, but it was a bit uncomfortable for me. This colleague works hard and genuinely cares about his work, but he has a habit of doing his own thing. It was important for me to make him understand why the policies were important, but there's a challenge because he often shuts down when he hears things that he doesn't agree with.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Wednesday, and it mattered a lot because the colleague is key to a lot of the work we do. He needs to follow policies or we are at risk as an organization.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I could see he was frustrated and upset. I felt bad as we are close colleagues and I know he cares about his work.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He was responsible for ignoring repeated warnings.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control to a certain extent. The issue will be how much of the conversation he took on board.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected.

situation: Someone I support at work stopped using heroin, and it's been such a rewarding experience. I've been supporting them for three years, helping with housing and drug rehabilitation appointments, and encouraging them to engage in meaningful activities. Seeing their success makes me feel really happy and proud. It hasn't always been easy, and I've had to be very patient and tenacious with my support, but it's all been worth it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was last week I took them to a routine drug appointment and they passed a clear test and they said they had not used heroin for a couple of months. It mattered to me because seeing their success makes me feel really happy and proud.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was really happy and it felt like my support had been worthwhile.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well I felt that the person was most responsible but I felt like I had been a part of their journey and that my support and encouragement really made a difference.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I was not in control they were in control I was just a spectator.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was not expecting this. The person had struggled with it for over 30 years.

situation: I got emotional reading an Instagram post about people reminiscing about spending time with their grandmothers and grandparents. It made me miss my grandmother, and it was also emotional reading all the different things and places they would go together. I was trying to feel close to the stories I was reading, and I needed a hug in that situation. I felt nostalgic and also sad. It was important I had those memories as it's good to remember your lost loved ones.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot because it made me think about all those good times with my grandmother and that other people are in my exact same situation. I am not alone.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me think of fond memories but also made me think about what I lost and did not have anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Reading the different stories and experiences made me most emotional.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not really because I started to tear up thinking about them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected, I expected to become emotional thinking about it. I also saved the post so I could go back to it.

situation: I had a conversation with a friend about my thinking of moving out of state. I was sharing my conflicted feelings, and I wasn't sure I was hoping to achieve much more than feeling closer to this person by showing some insight. Maybe I was looking for some reassurance that they cared. It felt fine, even though I didn't come to any resolution. But I did feel that if I do decide to move, I will have some emotional support. It was important to me that I was able to clearly voice my conflicted feelings in concrete terms.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The stakes weren't very high because this was a relatively new friend - one I'm not especially close with yet.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Being able to clearly articulate my thoughts behind the emotions helped me better understand my priorities.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think it was equal. It was important that my friend made me feel safe to be open and expressive.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes. There was really no need for me to share. I wanted to.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I guess so; I don't remember having any true expectations.

situation: My father died unexpectedly, and it left me in shock because I didn't see it coming. I'm not really sure how I'm supposed to feel right now. I'm upset about losing the father I once knew, not the one from the past few years. Surprisingly, I'm quite at peace with it. I'm also concerned about how my brother would cope with the situation, but he seems to be doing well.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Monday night. It mattered to me because it was closure for me on a painful time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I know now that he will never be able to hurt me ever again. However, it hurt because I always held out hope that he'd be the father I wanted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I blame him, but I am aware that part of it was my stubbornness at not allowing him to treat me badly anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control. I answered the phone if I wanted to or not if I didn't feel strong enough to cope.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected.

situation: I'm in a 12-week medication trial to address my cat's neuropathic behavior, and we hit a setback. I was trying to protect my cat from biting her tail, which has been a big concern for us. This situation left me feeling a bit hopeless because we've been working so hard, and the setback was really discouraging. It's important for me to know that there will be a positive ending to all our hard work.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot. We were at 16 days of no injury, so I thought we were over the hump. When she injured herself again, it felt like all our progress was down the drain. That wasn't actually true, but it felt that way.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Not sure if it was a 'help' or 'hurt', but it made me realize that this is truly a marathon.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I mean ... SHE is responsible for biting herself, but I've learned that her misfiring nervous system means she can't really help it - she doesn't realize what she's doing. However, on numerous occasions I've looked her in the eye and asked her to PLEASE STOP BITING YOURSELF.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I thought I was - I've been managing her gear protection set-up for a very long time, but sometimes it fails. I can't watch her 24-7.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as they have in the past: several minutes of trauma, several hours of settling, several days of vigilance and then we're back to baseline.

situation: I absolutely love my exercise classes, which I do five times a week. But my dodgy back has become really bad over the last couple of weeks. I ended up going to an osteopath and I'm going again tomorrow. Not being able to exercise has had a big effect on me, both physically and mentally. I need exercise because I suffer from anxiety and depression, so not going affects me in those ways too. I like being fit and controlling my weight, and this situation has negatively impacted both. It's left me feeling depressed, and my anxiety has been really bad. I haven't been sleeping well, and I've been comfort eating. On the positive side, I've met a really lovely osteopath who believes he can help me. I need to get better so I can get back to my routine.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It has been bad for years, but it got really bad two weeks ago and it catches when I move, making me cry out due to the pain. It matters a lot because my exercise classes are incredibly important to my physical well-being, but even more so to my mental well-being.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It is really painful, affecting many aspects of my daily life, like driving, cleaning, or simply turning around, and it has meant I am taking frequent paracetamol. On the positive side, meeting the osteopath has been helpful as he is personable, friendly, and knowledgeable, and was recommended by several people.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one is responsible for this situation. If anyone, it would be me, as it is my body after all.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I have felt out of control, which is why I decided to take it to the next level and get some professional help. I have been to the doctor and had x-rays in the past, but there wasn't really any help from this direction.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I have been really pleased with the osteopath, but he said it could take weeks or months to get better, which was unexpected.

situation: Last week, I got an email from my supervisor asking to schedule a one-on-one meeting to discuss my annual performance. As soon as I received the email, I started feeling nervous and worried about whether my performance is good or not. I wish he had been more clear in the email about whether the outcome is good or bad. I try to focus on things I still need to do now, but I always overthink and feel a bit negative. The performance outcome is really important to me because it will influence my salary and future development.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The evaluation matters to me a lot because it will influence my salary and future development.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation did not help or hurt me directly; it is just an evaluation. However, I am nervous about the outcome before the meeting.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel responsible for the outcome, but I think my supervisor could have been more specific in the email by providing more details before our meeting.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do not have any control over the situation because I have already submitted my performance package, and I cannot influence the outcome.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected. I did all my work and everything I needed to do.

situation: My mother's favorite cousin passed away on Tuesday, and my mom was the one who took her to the hospital this last time. I didn't need anything for myself; I was just trying to be present for my mom and be a listening ear. They had spent time together weekly for the last 14 years, and I just didn't want my mom to feel alone. The situation left me feeling sad and also brought up feelings about planning for end of life, especially since her cousin had a will in place. It was important to me because my mom started sharing more about her own end of life plans.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened on Tuesday afternoon. It mattered to me because my mom only has a few close friends and family left, and I was concerned the loss would hit her hard. The discussion we had about her cousin's will led us to a discussion about my own mother's end of life plans.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me honestly, because my mom did not realize what assets she actually had. She now will update her own will to include those assets. That is a relief for me, because my father did not do such things and it wound up costing us thousands in legal fees.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible for the death. Her cousin was in her 80's and in poor health with old age.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of the bereavement situation. Honestly, I'm not in control of my mom's plans neither.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes. I expected her cousin to pass. This was the second time she'd been hospitalized in a month.

situation: The day I won a soccer game and scored 3 goals by myself was a very positive experience during my time in high school. I was trying to work as a team, but I'm exceedingly good at soccer and my team isn't on the same skill level. I took it upon myself to tone down my skills, yet I still managed to score 3 goals without any problem. After the game, I felt like a million bucks. A lot of the coaches were in awe when they saw how good I was. I was holding back because I felt bad for the other team's goalie; I could have scored probably two more goals.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened in high school and it mattered a lot because it stuck with me all my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Yes, this event gave me a lot of confidence at such a young age. I really felt like I was in control and was able to guide my life in a positive direction. I was happy to be able to see my skills and apply it within sports. I felt that I would be able to do anything I wanted. Later I decided to pursue education instead of sports because I knew it would be less demanding. But I always wondered what would have happened if I stuck with soccer. It's just extremely competitive.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was myself. I know my parents were involved in helping me make the most of my life and choose the best decisions. But ultimately the decision was mine.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in total control at that moment. I just had a lot of options and my parents were super supportive of whatever I decided and wanted to do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yeah, I had the choice to be a soccer celebrity player or just choose a more secure life and I had a long chat with my dad and family and I agreed that security over the long term is better having a good education. So I chose that life. I don't have any regrets.

situation: Last week, I found out that my sister received an eviction notice from the home she's currently living in. The section 21 notice she was served only gives her 2 months to vacate the premises. I wanted to support my sister and help her in any way I could. I felt angry, upset, and frustrated because the notice doesn't give enough time to generally find somewhere else and then physically move. In addition to this, she has an 8-year-old daughter, and both herself and her partner are currently LCWRA. Her mental state is important to me. She is currently caring for her partner, her daughter, and our mother, who is currently unable to drive and needs care for medical reasons too. She's under a lot of pressure, and this eviction notice just made it worse.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: My mother told me 7 days ago on the 24th February 2026 at approx. 1300 hours. It matters to me a great deal because my sister has been beset by numerous events in the past couple of years including losing her job, her partner suffering from a ruptured stomach, my mother suffering from seizures, and now this eviction notice. It matters to me because when I lost my father at a young age, I had to step-up and become the 'man of the household' and support my mother and sister the best I could, and I still feel responsible for her despite moving away from home a number of years ago.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it almost feels like an attack on the family. After losing my father, I became much closer to my mum and sister and have supported them ever since, so her pain is my pain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody, everyone is free to make their own choices and decisions, and I don't want to blame anyone for this situation. A section 21 notice by design is a 'no fault' eviction, so the landlord is well within their right to do this, and they can't be blamed for pursuing the legal path to evict their tenant.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not in direct control, but given the pressure my sister was under, I did take it upon myself to research into her options and let her know clearly what she needed to do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It's too early to tell; the eviction process can be very long-winded. My sister contacted the council and was advised to stay put even after the section 21 has expired until the landlord applies for a possession order.

situation: Last week, I was eagerly anticipating the arrival of my newborn baby. We had planned for his arrival about two weeks ago, but he actually came last week. My wife and I are expecting not just a new baby, but also a new house. The whole situation felt overwhelming. What mattered most to me was the condition of my newborn baby.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The well-being of my newborn baby mattered immensely to me because as a parent, the health and safety of my child are my top priorities.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The arrival of my new baby is a significant life event, filled with both joy and anxiety, making the baby's condition my priority. The birth of my newborn was a watershed moment, and I have been having sleepless nights. I have been coping and managing.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I have been responsible for all of these.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because I seek a way to manage my situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected.

situation: It was the 1-year anniversary of my grandfather passing. I just wanted to be with my family, and we were celebrating his life in the form of a party or get-together. Being there made me feel contented, like it took a weight off my chest. Seeing all my family in the same emotional state made me feel like I could express myself any way I wanted.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I saw my grandfather as a role model. He came from nothing and left his kids and grandkids everything.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Seeing everyone there influenced my emotions. Seeing how everyone who cared about him being in the same room celebrating his life shaped my experience.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Seeing everyone there kind of influenced my emotions to how they were.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control of my emotions and reactions. I didn't want to sit there crying; that isn't me. Instead, I'll support others.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It blew my expectations; it was more than perfect.

situation: It was my aunt's birthday last week, but it wasn't a happy occasion like it used to be because she's in a care home now and has advanced dementia. We took her cards and presents, but the atmosphere was quite flat since she wasn't really aware of what was going on. I was trying to bring some joy and celebrate her birthday despite the circumstances because I just miss the way she used to be. Honestly, I felt empty and just sad. It was important to me that we still marked the occasion.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week. It mattered a lot to me that we saw her on the day and marked the occasion, even though her awareness has almost gone now.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me sad, to be honest. It makes me think of my own life that's to come.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't hold anyone or anything fully accountable. It's just life.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control. We did what we came to commemorate her day.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, as hoped.

situation: I applied for an internship position for this summer and went through four rounds of interviews. It took a few weeks, but eventually, I found out I did not get the position. I was trying to get the internship, and even though I didn't want the position so much, it was disappointing not to get it after putting in so much effort. It mostly felt like a lot of wasted time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a bit but was not the end all be all for me. It was disappointing not to get the position after putting in so much effort, and it mostly felt like a lot of wasted time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I dedicated a lot of time to this and was annoyed that my time was wasted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that it was mostly them and me responsible for this because I think the reason they didn’t choose me was because they knew I could not return full time to their company.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control during the process, but after I realized that I could not return full time, which made them not want to take me as an intern.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went unexpected because in the moment I expected to get the internship. But overall it was okay and not the end of the internship search process.

situation: A guy I have dated sporadically came over, and I was hoping we could become boyfriend and girlfriend again. But he told me he only wanted to be friends. This left me feeling confused, sad, and insecure. I know I just need to move on.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered because we are at the point in our lives that I thought we would get back together and start travelling together.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me feel insecure, like there is something wrong with me since he didn't want me anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He was most responsible since he is the one that changed his mind about us.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control, which is frustrating. I had no say and could not change his mind.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I thought we would get back together like we always did in the past.

situation: I was with my partner, and I did something that made them sad. I didn't realize it at the time because my partner never told me. I wanted to count the Scrabble points at the end of the game just to see by how much I won, but apparently, that made my partner feel bad. My partner didn't communicate well, and I got mad. I felt sad and mad because my partner could have just told me that I could count the points to myself.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last weekend, it mattered a lot to me since we've been struggling with communication.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because my partner seems to not be putting in the effort to communicate well.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My partner was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control since it was on my partner to communicate the feelings.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did not go as expected, we both went to bad mad.

situation: I was watching a TV soap, and suddenly there was a confrontation between characters that happened out of the blue. It was a shock because I wanted a bit of warning since the confrontation was not expected. I felt a bit shocked by it, but I understand that it's not real.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the evening when I was relaxing at home and engrossed with the storyline. It mattered to me because I was shocked by the unexpected confrontation.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation unnerved me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The physical fight between characters was most responsible for the unexpected confrontation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: For a moment, I did not feel in control, but then the credits rolled.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was just not expecting the confrontation.

situation: My daughter, who has had her struggles with mental health, made me feel very proud this week. She managed the demands of her new job while also looking after her boyfriend, who is ill. I was just observing how proud I was of her development. I felt very proud of her and wanted to convey this to her without being patronizing. It's important that she knows how proud I am of her, especially since she often feels her brother is 'more impressive.'

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a great deal as I always seize the opportunity to try to build her confidence.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me feel validated that all of our hard work in the past is paying off.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I felt she was and I was pleased to see her take control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected her to need to come home but she didn't. This was great!

situation: My youngest son got a huge promotion at work, which made me really excited and happy for him. He will be promoted to AI Solutions Architect. We were talking about how AI might affect his job, since he's a Senior Analyst at a huge tech firm. I just wanted to see if he had any plans to make sure his job didn't go away. I was worried and concerned until he told me what he had been doing. I've always thought he was about a genius, but he still keeps surprising me. He came up with some valuable insights into how to integrate AI into his current position and more. I was very surprised and happy to hear he was getting a promotion.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal! He has 3 children and a very nice home. He needs to be able to make enough money to take care of it all. The children are all in activities that cost money. His wife loves to shop, but she has a good part-time job as a Nurse Practitioner. I am so relieved that this position has opened up for him due to his talent and diligence.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't directly affect me, but indirectly it removed my worry about AI costing him his position. I enjoy visiting their house a few times a year and can enjoy the fruits of his labor.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son, Tyler, was most responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, and I didn't want control. I just was checking in and nudging a little to make sure he knew what was happening outside of his world. I've been following AI since it went public and was worried.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they did! He presented his ideas to his supervisors, who presented it to theirs, who presented it to the CEO. He then had a presentation of an application he created and was questioned by the CEO himself. All went great.

situation: I interviewed for a job that I thought went well, but it turns out I didn't get the job. I was really trying to land a full-time position to set myself up for a career after graduating university. The whole situation left me feeling dejected. The money was important to me because I'd like to start saving to move out.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in late January, and it mattered a lot to me as it was my first proper interview and the first job where I had a chance to actually speak to someone in person during the application process.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I never really had interview experience before. However, it hurt me because the questions caught me off-guard despite my preparation; I wasn't expecting them to ask what they did.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel both of us were responsible. I received an email with information telling me they'd be conducting a certain type of interview, and then those types of questions never popped up. I suppose I could've thought faster on my feet, but I don't think I was particularly failing.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt both in control and out of control during the interview process. I was in control of my answers, but out of control because I had no clue where it would be going.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The questions were unexpected, but I can't say the outcome was unexpected as they were interviewing many people.

situation: I ended up cancelling plans with someone I haven't had the chance to hang out with. I was trying to make sure I could free up some time because I needed to make something else in my schedule work. It left me feeling a little guilty.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week on Monday and it mattered moderately to me. I was excited for this.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: There was no help and no hurt from the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like I was responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control because I made the call to cancel.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected.

situation: My friend's son was rushed to the hospital with a brain bleed, and it was a really intense situation. I had her puppy with me so she could go back and forth to the hospital without worrying about her pet. I wanted to be as supportive as I could, and having the puppy was one way I could help her concentrate on her son. At first, I was really worried and upset because I thought it might be fatal. I was also trying to think ahead about how I could support my friend if the worst was to happen.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 6 days ago. It mattered a lot as I watched him grow up. The devastation for my friend is what mattered the most.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I've known him since he was born, so it hurt a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Drink... he was drunk, which is why he fell.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because there was nothing I could do. It was up to the doctors.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was very unexpected that he is being discharged tomorrow.

situation: A close family member, my cousin, passed away, and I was unable to attend the funeral because I was sick. I really wanted to be there, but my illness kept me from going. Not being able to attend made me feel guilty, like I should have gone anyways despite being sick, and I felt selfish for not being there.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 2 weeks ago and it mattered to me a great deal.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Thoughts of me not being there for her sometimes come up in my mind. I spent 3 days in bed mourning the loss but feel like if I went it wouldn't have been as hard to deal with.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me being sick.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control because I wanted to attend but my body wouldn't let me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected as they could have went.

situation: I had to leave my family to move for school, traveling over 5000 miles for college. I felt excited and optimistic about this new chapter, but it also made me long for my family. It's important to me because I won't be able to see them for over a year and a half.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened pretty recently, like two days ago. It mattered a lot to me because it made it clear that I wouldn't be able to see family for a while, and that I'll be living in this new place for quite some time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because it allowed me to move. It is challenging because I don't get to see family as often.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I was in control because I booked the flights and stays and things like that.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, for the most part things have gone to plan. Nothing, other than plane delays, were unexpected.

situation: I was just trying to relax, watching TV, when I saw a pregnant woman on the screen. It hit me hard because I've experienced several miscarriages in the past year. Seeing that made me start to spiral and get sad. I didn't really need anything at that moment, but the situation left me feeling upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered some because it's always hard to think about, but it's not the first time I've experienced this.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me sad. However, my husband helped me feel better by distracting me and getting me to think about something else.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control during this situation. It felt like it came out of nowhere, and I was incapable of calming on my own.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I have been able to deal with feelings better than this recently, so it was unexpected for me to get so upset from such a small example of a pregnancy.

situation: I am planning a trip to go back home, mainly for my sons. My son wants to visit for his birthday, and we miss our favorite restaurants. It's going to be the first time since I left 3 years ago. I want to be excited about the trip, but I'm more anxious. I wish I could go home to see my family too, but that will never happen again. I feel sick at the thought of the trip. I'm nervous and anxious. I have horrible memories there and feel completely mixed on the idea of going back. My parents died back to back 4-5 years ago, and quickly my extended family disappeared. It's been 3.5-4 years since I've seen or spoken to any of them. We'll go visit my spouse's family, and I can't have that.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It hurt a lot. I didn't expect to lose everyone along with my parents. My dad died last and I was closest with his family, especially his mother, but even she completely changed almost immediately. It matters a lot because I'd prefer not to be so alone. I don't really like my spouse's family; they are tolerable but not my people at all. I miss what I used to have.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt a lot. It's completely changed me as a person and I no longer trust anyone. I guess it helped me become more independent because there's no one but me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like they are most at fault. I still have no idea why things changed but they did. My birthday was 4 months after my dad died, I had spent every birthday with his family my entire life because within that family 3 cousins almost share the same birthday. My first birthday without my parents they still did the typical birthday stuff, I just wasn't invited, nor did anyone even say anything to me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control when I decided no more, deleted them from social media so they can't see my kids growing up, and moved 8 hours away.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected them to reach out at some point. My grandmother died 5 months ago, before my dad died she was my mother figure, my best friend, and my grandmother. After he died, she hated me. But I still don't understand why they didn't tell me. She also took me and my kids out of the will.

situation: I was just scrolling through TikTok, looking for some upbeat and funny videos to pass the time. I came across a video of a monkey named Punch who was getting bullied and used a stuffed teddy for comfort. Watching this left me feeling sad and sorry for the monkey. I really wanted to make sure that Punch was taken care of.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because I really don't like cruelty towards animals, especially when they visibly express their distress and need to rely on a stuffed toy for comfort.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it made me feel sad and sorry for the monkey. I wanted to help the monkey but knew that I couldn't.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the zoo that was responsible for capturing these animals was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I absolutely did not feel in control of the situation because the zoo is in Asia, and there is nothing I can do.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I've seen rumors that Punch has since been adopted by a loving family, so he is now happy.

situation: Our bathroom sink backed up late at night, and I tried all the easy fixes to get it working again. I was really worried that we'd end up needing an expensive plumber, so I just wanted to get it fixed myself. We looked everywhere for a plunger but couldn't find it, which led to an argument between us. I felt frustrated and anxious about the whole situation. It didn't help that my husband seemed pretty blase about it, and I didn't feel very supported. In the end, we just went to bed without resolving the issue.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It felt like it mattered a lot because we just don't need to spend money on a plumber right now. I was worried it was a bigger problem than just a clog. I am the money watcher in my household, so this stuff stressed me out a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This strained my relationship. We both went to bed upset, which I hate doing.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one, really. The clog is a normal thing that happens. But I got anxious and frustrated, which I think made everything go bad. So that was my fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I didn't have control because I couldn't fix the problem immediately.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They kind of did- my anxiety often can cause situations to get heated if I don't actively notice what's happening and try to handle it myself by reminding myself that it's just my anxiety and not reality.

situation: A week ago, I was the victim of a hate crime. I'm gay, and I was leaving a bar around 3am when someone behind me said 'fuck you faggot,' then shoved me. The area was very icy and slick due to recent snow storms, so I slipped and fell face first into the sidewalk. I didn't see who did it or what they were wearing. I managed to get home and then filed a police report a few days later so that the hate crime was documented. I was just trying to go home. I wanted this to have never happened, and I reported it in the hopes that it would prevent it from happening to someone else. I felt hurt, sad, angry, frustrated, and afraid. It was important for me to turn this into something positive by helping others.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Saturday morning around 3am. It mattered to me because I was physically hurt and left with a severely bruised face and eye area.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It took away my sense of safety in a predominantly gay neighborhood.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The person who pushed me was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control. The only thing I could have done was not drink as much or not go out at all.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The reporting process was much more involved than I thought it would be. It was somewhat intimidating and rough.

situation: My daughter participated in 'World Book Day' dressed as Cinderella and won a prize for the best outfit. I was just needing to be super proud of her. I felt amazing because whenever I send my child out into the world, I only want her to enjoy life. The only thing that was important to me was my daughter having fun and enjoying herself.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened last Thursday. We woke up and my daughter was super excited for the day; she couldn't get into her book day outfit quick enough. After finishing her hair, we got ready and left the house to see her friend across the road, who was also in a princess outfit. It was a great day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me in being a good dad, a good parent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I would say I was responsible as I am the parent, but my daughter played a good part as she provided the happiness.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was only in control of getting my daughter prepared and into school. After that, I am just awaiting to see how her day was.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than I thought. You always want it to go good, but when it goes as well as it could, that's the magic.

situation: I lost weight, and it felt really good because I thought I was not going to lose it. This was a positive emotion for me. I've been pushing myself to go to the gym at least five times a week, trying not to give up or give in to the tempting bad foods and desserts. The situation left me feeling relieved because I've had a hard time doing this for years. My family, friends, and partner were really important to me in this situation because they pushed me, and I didn't want to let them down at all.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week as I checked my weight and I went from 15 and a half stone to 12 stone. This mattered so much to me because I was not happy with my weight at all and felt embarrassed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me be more confident with myself so it helped me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My partner. She pushed me like nobody else and I cannot thank her enough for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes. Very much in control because I did not let anything distract me and I pushed myself to the limit. I was 100% in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes. I mean I had 10% doubt I would give up but I did not so all in all, it went as I expected and I will not let myself get like that again.

situation: I learned that my psychiatrist is going on maternity leave, and I'll need to be paired up with another psychiatrist in the practice that I don't know. I had just started to feel comfortable with my current psychiatrist, so I felt a bit blindsided when she mentioned she'd be gone for months during my last appointment. I would've appreciated more notice to give myself time to mentally prepare for the transition. This situation left me feeling sad and disappointed, especially since I had another psychiatrist who also left for maternity leave but notified me in advance.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: My appointment was last Friday. It was stressful finding another psychiatrist this year because of my change in insurance. I did extensive research to find one within my network that would best fit my mental health needs.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I have already been through 3 psychiatrists because of changes in insurance and it takes me awhile to trust people so I felt anxious and a bit like an afterthought being told last minute.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like my psychiatrist was most responsible. I have been seeing her since January and had no idea she was pregnant.
