appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control of the situation. I was told I would be appointed another provider within the practice for my next appointment and that my current one wouldn't be back for a few months.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was completely unexpected for her to drop this information on me and saying this would be my last appointment with her for a few months. I appreciate that she has someone that can assist me while she's gone because I didn't have that with my previous psychiatrists but I still felt blindsided.

situation: I was leaving the train station to head back to university, and my uncle and father came to wave me off. I was just sitting on the train, offloading my bags, while they stood on the other side of the window on the train platform, waving me off. It was a nice moment. I felt happy but a little bit homesick because my university is far away from home, and it isn’t easy to travel between them, so I don’t get to be home too often. They had brought me several food gifts and snacks for the train journey, as well as some travel money, which was very nice of them and made me feel grateful.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered quite a lot to me. In previous times, I have gone to the station and left alone, but making the effort to come to the station with me and say goodbye made me feel appreciated.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by making me feel appreciated, and the food gifts were really good to have as it was a long train journey. However, it also made me feel a tad homesick knowing I would not see them for a while.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just the general scenario of things; they were simply there because they and I both knew we would not see each other for a little while, so there was a mutual understanding that the moment was important.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control, yes, but there wasn’t much for me to do or be in control of other than sitting on a train for hours waiting.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went entirely as expected, if not better, because it was a kind act to come say goodbye yet not necessary.

situation: I was accepted onto my Camp America agency, so I'm going to America in the summer and going traveling. To get accepted, I had to do an interview where they asked me a bunch of questions about myself, and I really needed them to accept me. When I found out I was accepted, I was very happy because I really want to go, and now I'm really excited that I get to go. I was nervous during the interview, and I'm definitely nervous about going to America on my own for a few months.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When my interview happened, and I was accepted, it mattered a lot to me because I really want to go to America.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation definitely helped me because I needed the agency to accept me so I could go to America and get my visa.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself was the most responsible for this. I planned for the interview and prepared questions.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control to a certain extent. I knew what to expect. However, there were some questions I didn't expect, and so I thought on the spot and did my best.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as expected, although I was nervous, I knew I should get accepted.

situation: I went to a restaurant and ordered my meal, but when it arrived, it was the wrong dish. I decided to try the dish anyway, and surprisingly, it turned out to be quite delicious. The staff apologized for the mix-up and offered me a voucher for a free dish later, which made the experience unexpectedly pleasant.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened one week ago. It didn't matter much to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation wasted my time, which was frustrating. However, it offered a positive aspect as I received a free food voucher.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the kitchen workers were most responsible for the mix-up.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control during the situation because I wasn't making the food.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because I received the wrong order. There was nothing else about the situation that didn't go as I anticipated.

situation: A crane operator died at my workplace recently, and it was such a sad story that I just need to get it off my chest. He wasn't found for 11 hours because someone else signed him out of our registration system, so nobody knew he was onsite. His wife called because she didn't know where he was, and that's when they went looking and found him. I feel like the death might not have been preventable overall, but the delay could have been why he died. What really bothers me is how the aftermath was handled; it felt very much brushed under the carpet to save face.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened around 6 weeks ago. The facts around how it was handled make me feel like if anything happened to me, people may try to cover it up.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did nothing to me personally, I'm just very empathetic.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Well, the death was a sudden heart attack, but if he wasn't signed out he could have been spotted sooner and potentially saved.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was uninvolved.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It didn't go as I expected. I thought people would lose jobs, face prosecution, etc., justice, but this didn't occur.

situation: I tried to contact the property tax office to see if I could make a few payments to cover the bill. I was told no, and having to fully cover the bill all in one go really hurt. It leaves me with very little money to get by on, and it really upset me. I was trying to get the tax office to allow me to make a couple of payments to cover my bill, but the lack of compassion by our government stands out. The situation left me feeling scared, sad, and upset.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few days ago. It mattered a lot to me because now I do not know how I will afford food.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt because now I do not have money for food.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was partly responsible because I did not take care of the bill sooner. But the government is more responsible because they will not allow a person to make a couple payments to cover the bill.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. Because they have the power. I pay the bill, in full, or I lose my home.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They did, I did not really expect the government to have any sort of compassion and they didn't.

situation: Recently, I've been feeling really beat by life. When I go out running errands, I find myself talking to the universe, asking for my rut or purgatory life to either end without harming other people or to give me opportunities to make my life better. I tend to get very intense because I just hate my situation right now. I'm looking for an answer that will never happen, because there is no God, universe that listens, or powers that be. This whole situation leaves me feeling lost, alone, and useless.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The entire thing mattered to me, I just felt like I needed either life to end or some help. I still feel that way.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: So far, nothing has changed. I mean, I just continue feeling stuck. I feel like a coward. Because I believe it actually takes strength, not weakness to end it all.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I mean, probably myself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I feel like no matter the decisions I've made in life, even ones where things felt very good, that life just finds ways to knock me back down.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things haven't changed, which isn't unexpected.

situation: My father passed away, and during this difficult time, I was really seeking emotional support. My wife's support was especially important to me, and having her by my side made me feel a little bit better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when my father passed away. It mattered a lot to me because I was seeking emotional support during this difficult time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me understand why it happened, but I was mad at my stepmother.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that God was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I didn't understand.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because I was shut out of my family.

situation: I was watching the Today show on NBC, which is my favorite TV show, and suddenly, there was news about Savanna Gunthrie's mother being abducted. She's 84 years old, and it was terrifying to hear that someone just came in the middle of the night and took her. This situation really hit me hard emotionally because I had a parent who was lost tragically too a while back. I wasn't expecting to get anything out of watching the show; it just came out of the blue. Now, I keep replaying the news in my mind, and it brings up old memories of my relative who passed suddenly. It's been very emotionally taxing. I think I want to get an alarm for my home, not just a surveillance camera. An alarm would scare off an abductor or killer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened while I was watching the Today show on NBC. It mattered to me significantly because I live alone, like Savanna's mother, and the news brought up old memories of my relative who passed suddenly. It was emotionally taxing and made me consider getting an alarm for my home.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by making me feel fear and concern for my safety, but it also helped by reassuring me that taking steps like getting an alarm could help me feel more secure.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that a random person who broke into Savanna's mother's home and probably killed her is most responsible for the events that impacted me emotionally.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel a little out of control because now I want an alarm. The situation has led to a feeling of urgency and a desire to take action to ensure my safety.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting anything. The news caught me completely off guard, and the emotional impact was unexpected.

situation: A family member had to go to the hospital, but they had to go on their own because there was nobody available to accompany them at the time. I really wanted to be there with them to provide some emotional support and try to take some of the stress away so they could just concentrate on getting the medical attention they needed. Being over 100 miles away left me feeling helpless because I couldn't provide any of these things. What was important to me was that they received the medical attention they needed and that it made the situation better. Thankfully, once they got the medical attention, they started to feel better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered an immense amount to me. I felt like I was in limbo because, although I knew they were in the best place to receive care, I felt I should have been doing more to help.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because when this person needed me, I wasn't there.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel I was most responsible for this, as at the end of the day, I probably wouldn't have been that much help in the important things that eventually led to them getting better.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel like I was in control. The distance and the fact that I have no skills in making this person medically better meant I had no real way of becoming involved in it successfully.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as I expected, as they went into the hospital and came out on a path to look after their health.

situation: I had a medical appointment for a follow-up regarding some concerns my doctors had. As I prepared for the visit, I tried to calm myself and avoid overthinking potential outcomes. Despite my efforts, I was still anxious upon arrival. However, when the ultrasound technician came to escort me, I began to relax. Her kindness and professionalism were reassuring, and the environment was soothing. Throughout the procedure, she kept me informed about each step, which helped ease my worries. Although I remained slightly concerned about the results, I understood she couldn't provide any interpretations. I silently prayed as the procedure unfolded.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot because I have already been through so much treatment and I just want to be able to relax and enjoy time with my family. It takes so much out of me to go through treatment not just physically but emotionally, spiritually, psychologically, and mentally. It almost makes me want to decline treatment but I have to continue fighting so I can be here for my children.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me only because of the toll that it takes on me to even prepare for doctors visits. However, it helps me because it reminds me of how strong, courageous, and resilient that I am! It confirms that I can do anything that I put my mind to as long as I keep God first in the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The challenging part is due to past negative experiences that I just don't want to deal with anymore. I really wouldn't wish those experiences on anyone. The empowering part is mainly because of my faith in God.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control as far as making the choice to attend the appointment or reschedule it and just avoid it. I wasn't in control of what the outcome of the test results of the procedure though.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went as expected.

situation: My son asked me to go to Tenerife with him and my 8-year-old grandson. I was really touched to be invited on such a personal holiday. I've recently divorced under very difficult circumstances, and I needed something positive and meaningful. This invitation made me feel included and needed. It was a warm experience after some very dark times. Being a part of my grandson’s family holiday gave him a memory of good times spent with granny.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was last week and it was a lovely surprise when my son said he would like me to come. This mattered to me because it was a meaningful experience that made me feel included and needed, especially after my recent difficult divorce.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I enjoyed watching my son and grandson on a catamaran as we went whale watching out deep into the ocean. It opened my world from my pain to joy.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think my son for thinking of me and me for rising to the challenge.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had a wobble thinking about going, but am so glad I did.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was better than I expected. There was loads to do together which surprised me.

situation: A friend from our large friend group has been making moves on my husband. During a recent get-together at our house, I witnessed her glide her hand across my husband's chest. My husband whipped away from her hand as it made him uncomfortable. I was furious after seeing her do that. I wanted her to leave my house. My husband was just as pissed at her as I was. The situation left me feeling like we cannot hang out with her anymore until this issue is addressed. This friend is being very disrespectful to me and my husband. She is also dating my husband's best friend, and now I am sad for the best friend. No one wants a girl that openly flirts with others.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened a week ago and it mattered greatly to me as she is interfering with our family unit.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has hurt me because I thought she was a friend. She clearly is not.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: She is the most responsible for this situation. Her behavior is ridiculous.
appraisal_reasoning.control: My husband and I are in control because we talked about it and have a game plan for when it happens next time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: My husband handled her unwanted advances well.

situation: I had an argument with a close friend. I wanted to go somewhere with her, but she told me she was sick. Now, she's begging to meet up on a day when I'm really busy, and it's annoying me. I just want her to respect my time as much as I respect hers.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Tuesday. We were supposed to meet up to go to a dance class, but she said she was sick. At the time, I was understanding of her sickness, so I didn't get angry with her. However, when she kept insisting that we meet on a day when I was busy, I started to feel annoyed because she did not respect my time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation hurt me because it was clear that she did not respect my time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Her pushiness was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control of the situation, because her feelings and wants got in the way of logic.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected, because I expected my friend to respect my time as much as I respected hers.

situation: I had a girlfriend who cheated on me twice. The first time was with her ex, even though she had assured me she would never get back with him. The second time was at her friend's hotel party, where she gave a random guy a hickey. I found out about the second incident through a photo on her phone. Despite these events, I forgave her and decided to work things out, but I became paranoid and eventually blocked her. She reached out through her mom, asking me to talk to her, which I did. Two weeks later, I blocked her again on my phone and everything else I knew her on. I unblocked her to talk, and she was hurt, suggesting we should be friends and start over from the talking stage. I pulled back, barely putting in effort, and went hours without talking to her. She would spam text me, saying she loved and missed me, and would call, but I wouldn't talk on the phone. Now, I'm at the point where I barely answer her messages quickly and am mentally checking out. She still texts me that she loves me, but when I don't say it back, it seems to bother her, even though she said we are friends, which I don't understand. I wanted her to be more honest and not to do weird things like that to me. The situation left me anxious. Every time she went hours without speaking, I assumed she was doing something bad again. To me, I just had to avoid talking to her to be at peace and feel sane. I have self-respect for myself, and I wouldn't want to chase or stay where I'm disrespected, so I've decided to take the friend role and stay as detached as possible.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When the event happened, it mattered to me a lot because I really cared for her and saw her like the only girl in the world, but she betrayed me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me know that I can't put my full trust in a mere human being. It hurt me because I don't think I'll ever see women the same way again.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that she was most responsible for this; I had nothing to do with it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, of course I was in control. I had to be in control to manage myself so I don't spiral.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected. I controlled myself, and now I'm at peace.

situation: My brother-in-law's mum passed away last week, and it was a very emotional time for the family and me. I didn't really want or need anything specific; it was just very sad. However, I'm glad she passed away in a pain-free way. I felt very sad for her husband, who she leaves behind, but I tried to focus on the positive aspects of her life, which was full of joy and fulfillment. It was important to me to ensure that everyone was okay and that support was available if needed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: She passed away last Thursday the 26th February. It matters because even though she was not a blood relative she is part of our family and I have known her for 40 years, so it is just a very tough thing to process.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurts because I know her husband will be very lost without her as they have been together over 60 years and that upsets me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody is responsible for it, this is what happens in life, people get ill but it doesn't make it any easier.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I wasn't in control of anything, you can't control something like this, it is just nature taking its course.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Well she did pass away as expected if that's how you want to word it so yes in that regard.

situation: I had some trouble paying my bills this week, and it was really killing me inside. I was behind on work and not making enough to cover my expenses. I was overworking, trying my best to catch up, but it really took a toll on my mental health. I had to reach out for help, both mentally and financially, which terrified me. Luckily, I got help from both sides and managed to calm myself down and pay off some of my bills so far. I needed to catch up on bills to avoid fees and protect my credit score. At first, I felt terrible and hopeless, almost wanting to give up and not care. But the guilt crept in, and I had to explore my options, even if some of them were a no. It was important for me to know I had a good support team around me who understood I wasn't just trying to use them for money and that I would pay them back once things start coming together. I want them to realize it might take some time. I also want these bill places to know that the bills will get paid. Everyone just needs to be patient. I understand deadlines, but it's a tough time now, and I'm doing everything I can.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened last Monday and it mattered to me because my week was starting off terribly, and I was afraid it would impact my emotions for the rest of the week. Additionally, I couldn't stop thinking about the guilt of 'not working enough,' even though I was working a good amount and I don't like my job.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me at first, but once I was able to get my ducks in order and reach out, then I felt better, but still not that great.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was most responsible for all of this because I didn't save money and wanted to spend it. This situation could have been avoided if I was more careful with my finances.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control. I felt like I could've been in control beforehand, but then it landed in the laps of these collectors and my support system.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected because this has happened before, and I just repeated what I knew.

situation: I was coming close to the deadline of having to move with no place to go, and it was really stressing me out. I felt like my head was hot, I had constant headaches throughout the day, my back ached, and the world felt dizzy. I just needed a place to live, somewhere I could lay down in my bed and feel settled. Then one day, I found an awesome place to move into. We make just enough to afford it, and now everything is settled. I'm feeling more calm and happy. Being able to calmly make some pasta was important to me, and now I can do that without all the stress.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about a week after I received the notice of raised rent that I couldn't afford, which upset me and necessitated finding a new place quickly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Finding a new place was eye-opening and brought a sense of comfort and belonging, even though it was in an area some might call the hood. It offered a new perspective and perhaps more space or opportunities.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My stress deserves the responsibility for how things unfolded.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control, akin to being in an airplane going down but not yet crashed, navigating through a challenging period but managing to stay afloat.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected.

situation: A patent application that I have been working on for 3 years was granted by the USPTO office. It was very emotional for me because I had a lot of blood, sweat, and tears go into that project. As an inventor, my livelihood depends on getting granted patents and licensing those patents out to collect royalties. This achievement made me feel proud and relieved, knowing that all of the resources that went into it were not wasted.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Over the past 3 years or so. It matters a great deal. As a small business owner we only put resources into our best ideas and we take a risk that they are not granted.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It gave me a significant morale boost, made me proud and energized and relieved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was not most responsible for this. Although I have a team, the original concept was developed by myself alone.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No not really. During the process you go through prosecution and you work closely with your IP lawyer. Most things cannot be done by yourself and you rely on the IP lawyer and his/her skill.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes everything went to plan.

situation: My mother-in-law suffered a major stroke, and I spent many hours over the next 10 days in the hospital with her until, sadly, she passed away. Because I had no power or control over the situation, I just needed to talk to people about it. I needed people around me. It left me with a feeling of complete emptiness. I have never watched anybody pass away before, and the sorrow was tangible. My wife was really important to me during this time. With it being her mother, I had to try to deal with her grief as well as my own.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: With my parents dying years ago, my mother-in-law became like another mum to me. She was always there for me, and losing her was like losing a very important part of my life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt in ways that I still struggle to put into words now. The gap she left can never be filled.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The stroke she suffered was responsible. The hospital staff did all they could, but there was no chance of recovery.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I had no control at all. The fact that we knew the stroke was life-ending for her meant the only say my wife and I had was if we stopped the care and just let her pass away.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing was unexpected once we knew that she would pass away; it was just sitting and waiting for it to happen.

situation: A friend of mine from Spain called me back and reconnected last week. It had been over three decades since we last spoke, so it was very exciting, and there were a bunch of tears early on. We met in graduate school, hit it off, and spent much time together. Eventually, I had to return to the States, and life took over. I wasn't even thinking about him when he called, but when he did, it ignited deeply passionate memories with him. The call left me longing to see him again. It was also important for me to know about his health and how he was doing in life.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: He called last Sunday evening. I was about to watch a movie, so I paused it. We spoke for over 4 hours. It was very exciting, and there were a bunch of tears early on. The call left me longing to see him again. It was also important for me to know about his health and how he was doing in life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It brought me great happiness.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He read a book which reminded him of our relationship so he called.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We were both in control equally participating.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They went far better than expected.

situation: My daughter decided to be home schooled because she had been missing a lot of time in public school due to frequent illness. I just wanted her to decide what was best for her. I'm a little concerned that her emotional maturity will fall behind being at home learning. I want to make sure that she does enough schoolwork to not fall behind.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened today. It was my wife's decision, but it will matter to me because I work from home and it will interrupt my day.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It will be fun, but will be harder for me to make money.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My wife.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No really. It is my wife's decision.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It has been a challenge today. I didn't think she would be so demanding of my time.

situation: My cousin passed away, and I was alone at home while my parents went to my relatives' house to figure out what was happening. I really wanted someone to talk to, but I didn't have anyone to reach out to, especially since I was by myself. Not knowing what was going on left me feeling a little down and lonely. I wasn't informed about what happened until much later, so I spent that time alone and clueless.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened a few weeks ago on the weekend. I was not really upset as I never knew my cousin, but the situation of knowing someone has passed away and being left alone yourself made it a little more unsettling.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I just felt that I had no one to guide me through the situation and help me. It felt as if time was not moving and that I would be alone for even longer without knowing when the end of it all would occur.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I do not think anyone was responsible for my feelings as it was a very upsetting situation for everyone and everyone was experiencing and feeling their own emotions which may have been worse than what I was experiencing.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control of the home, as I managed to organise and tidy everything by the time my parents came back home, however, I did not feel in control of the time as it felt like the day was dragging along.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I am not too sure as I am still experiencing the effects of the situations and it is still very traumatic for everyone involved.

situation: I was watching news reports about the war in Iran and saw Keir Starmer showing what I consider absolute cowardice in the face of the enemy, refusing to support our allies. I was trying to stay informed about the progress of the conflict because I think it's vitally important that our country should not be seen as betraying our allies due to Keir Starmer's self-serving decision based on political expediency and appeasement of the Islamist Muslim vote in the UK. This situation left me feeling extremely angry and embarrassed for our country that this individual is its political figurehead—a leader in name only. It was also important for me to see that my views were commonly held and expressed widely by others.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because it affects how this country is viewed in the world, especially by its most steadfast ally. I was very annoyed but not surprised by his actions.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation did not hurt me or help me personally, but it informed me that Starmer is not to be trusted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Keir Starmer was most responsible, though he tried to hide behind a collective cabinet decision. He even overruled the opinion of the UK Defence Secretary, which I find incomprehensible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I have no control over this.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Starmer is a coward, so it was not really a surprise.

situation: I'm currently in a licensed reactor operator class, aiming to become a licensed reactor operator. Fifteen years ago, I didn't succeed in completing the class, and now I'm back at it. On my first test, I scored an 80, which is the minimum score required to pass. This brought back all my past emotions from failing the first time, making me feel uneasy and stressed. I need to ensure that I score a 90 or higher on the tests. I'm having doubts about my ability to learn the material at the level required, especially since I'm over 50 years old. I'm the oldest in the class and also have the most experience, so I feel the pressure of mentoring my classmates who have less experience.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters a great deal to me. My current job requires me to be in extreme temperature environments, along with climbing and crawling on occasion. I feel that I am getting too old to physically perform my job. Having the license allows me to be in a more comfortable environment.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: At first, the situation hurt my ego and made me doubt my abilities. After some soul searching, I realized that I needed to be more diligent in my efforts.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: For the 'who', I have 3 sons, 2 in college and 1 still in high school; I want to set an example for them. My desire not to fail this class is responsible. Having the license opens more doors of opportunity for me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do feel like I am in control. I know how much I need to study.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: So far things have went as expected. My grades have increased each test. The last test I only missed 1 question.

situation: I had a stressful talk with my partner about our living situation. His parents are in their 80s and are starting to need more support. We decided almost a year ago that we would move in together so they were closer to town and I could take on some caregiving duties. My father-in-law is stubborn and sometimes doesn't think of others when he wants to do something. He can be inconsiderate. This time it was laundry. My daughter was doing her laundry and he wanted to do a load of laundry and pretty much disregarded her laundry. He threw it on the kitchen table. I needed to talk it out and wanted to get buy-in for an idea I had to alleviate this issue. The conversation actually went well and I felt like I was heard and had come up with a solid solution. It was important to me that my partner would be a partner in enforcing the solution.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago and it matters a lot to me because my daughter already feels like an outsider. She is not the biological grandchild and there is favoritism.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation allowed me to attempt to repair and build a stronger relationship.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My father-in-law is most responsible due to his actions. I also see my daughter taking a small part because of how she chose to take it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Sort of. I was able to work behind the scenes to come up with an amenable solution.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I am happy that it seems to have the outcome I had hoped for.

situation: I spent the whole week redecorating the bathroom, which involved getting the tiles off, retiling, painting, and grouting. The bathroom hadn't been updated in 10 years, so it definitely needed a refresh. Luckily, we have three bathrooms, so we didn't have to rough it for too long. At first, I wasn't happy about doing it myself and would have gladly paid for an external builder to complete the job, but none were available. By late Sunday night, you wouldn't have thought I felt a sense of achievement, but I did when I finally finished. You really need to take care with the smallest room in the house because everything is magnified there, and people tend to spend a little more time analyzing your work. Just some cutting in to be tidied, and the job's a good one.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It took me a week, and yes, I was being nagged, which is good as I would have procrastinated. Once you start, it is quite therapeutic and a total change from my normal work.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation earned me brownie points with my wife. To be fair, she is very supportive and helped me a great deal when she had time in her busy schedule.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I guess I was the most responsible for even bringing it up, but once it was out, it snowballed. You can't put the genie back in the bottle, they say.
appraisal_reasoning.control: The only pressure I felt was purely of my own making. I could take as long as I wanted but I set myself a target so as not to leave it half finished.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Mostly, but I did have to get my brother-in-law in to disconnect the shower and radiator. He is not a plumber but is better at that kind of thing. For that I had to wait, and apart from the occasional trip to the builders' merchants it went smoothly.

situation: I was texting with my ex-boyfriend of three months, and we were chatting like cool and chill friends. Out of the blue, he asked me about another girl. I didn't need anything from him, but I felt it was inconsiderate to my feelings. The situation left me feeling sad and even shaky for a while. However, what's important to me is that I didn't let it affect me for too long; I got over it very easily and quickly, which is an improvement for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Tuesday and it did not matter much.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt because I felt he was moving on too fast and he probably never liked me. It helped because I knew that gradually I had gotten over him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He was responsible because he could have asked someone else.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control because I did not overreact.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it went as expected. I answered how I wanted to.

situation: My cat died two weeks ago. He became deadly ill after he got his rabies yearly vaccination shot. He was eight years old. I was trying to save him from being sick by feeding him through a food syringe and trying to keep him warm inside. It made me feel sad and stressed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened two weeks ago, and it mattered greatly to me because losing him hurt me deeply. My family thought getting a rabies vaccination and checked out would make him feel better.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me greatly with losing him.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There is no one to blame.
appraisal_reasoning.control: My family made the decision to take the cat to the vet.

situation: I injured my knee while riding BMX, and my wife didn't seem to care. I was having a great time riding with friends, and at the end of the session, I tried something new that I thought would be easy. But after the injury happened, I needed medical treatment because my knee was extremely swollen, and I couldn't put weight on it. I was upset that she didn't care, especially since this followed a recent time when I discounted her knee injury because she did not express how painful it was for her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Sunday. It mattered a great deal to me. I felt like I was not getting support from my wife when I needed it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I was in physical pain from the wreck and emotional pain from not being supported.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I chose to ride my bike.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Clearly they did not go as planned. No one plans to wreck their bike and not be supported by their wife. I didn't think I'd wreck. I didn't think my wife would fail to support me.

situation: The weather is finally starting to break, which means outside activities, especially golf, are possible. This change in weather makes me happy and energized. I need the weather to get warmer, and for the snow and ice to stop. I'm trying to golf and take long walks to enjoy the fresh air. I feel excited and impatient. It's only March, so there is still time until the weather is consistent. Being able to enjoy some of those long walks with my wife is important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event has happened over the last week, with the weather improving and temperatures getting better. This change matters to me because it makes me happy and energized, and I am excited and impatient for consistent warm weather.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by getting warmer, which positively impacted my mood and energy levels.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that nature taking its course is most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do not feel in control because I cannot control the weather.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected as can be.

situation: I was sitting outside on my porch, watching the snow fall and realizing how much I'm going to miss living here, since I'm being kicked out. I just really wanted to take a moment to sit and relax, soaking in the beauty of the snow. It left me feeling grateful that I got to stay here for as long as I did, and it also left me feeling a bit sad. Honestly, just actually taking in the beauty of the snow was the most important thing for me. I'm sure where I go next will also have snow, but there are two trees in my front yard that look really beautiful with snow on their branches.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When this happened, it didn't necessarily matter to me all that much originally. It was just sitting outside and watching the snow. But it slowly gained meaning the longer I sat outside in the cold.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation helped me. It helped me regulate my emotions a bit and allowed me to process a bit of my grief over my overall situation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Honestly, it was my decisions that led me to getting kicked out. I'm responsible for my situation, overall, and accept my role in it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: In this particular situation, yes. I felt like I was in control. In terms of the decision to have me get kicked out of my home - no, I didn't feel as though I was in control of that situation at all. There was a communication breakdown that led to me making the decisions I did, that if that breakdown had been corrected, I would've made different decisions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as expected, at all. I expected to be able to stay here for at least another year to get my things all situated.

situation: I'm about to turn 70 on Monday, and I specifically asked my husband and daughter not to include my son if they planned anything for my birthday. I was shocked and upset when I found out yesterday that she had invited my son to a birthday dinner. My daughter ended up cancelling the reservation, and right now, I have no idea what's going on. I'm trying to prevent any uncomfortable situations with my son, who hardly talks or looks at me when we're together. This whole situation has left me feeling very emotionally stressed. I just wanted this time to be with my daughter and my husband.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It has not happened yet and I do not want it to. It mattered a lot to me. He makes me depressed every time I see him treats me as if I am not even there.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It would really hurt me if he comes. I am turning 70 and I want to enjoy the last few years of my life. I always go home and cry so I do not want that.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just his anger towards me for taking a job in another state and being away 20 years.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I have no control over it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: As far as I know is my daughter has cancelled the dinner.

situation: It was the day I found out my application for Medical Financial Assistance was lost, and I had to start the process all over again. This program is supposed to help by allowing me to pay half of my copayments and drugs in my health plan. So, I had to start a new application and upload all the proof of income again. A few days later, they told me they actually had the original application, which made me really angry. And to top it off, I still don't have the approval.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It is very important for me and my family, it saves us a lot of money.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I might have to cancel doctors appointments and refilling of drug until it is approved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The health plan.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I am not in control, they are.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was already on the program but they make you requalify every six months. I reapplied in January.

situation: I was reading about this baby monkey in Japan that lost its mother and became very famous because it was getting bullied in the zoo by other monkeys and just wanted affection. It was all over social media, and I kept seeing this monkey just wanting love and not getting it. I wasn't really trying to do anything; I was living my own life, but when I was on social media, this story was so emotionally touching that it just hit me, and I felt responsible for this monkey I didn't know personally. What I needed was to feel like this monkey was okay. I felt quite upset that the zoo was letting it get bullied and that nothing was being done to support him. It was important to me that he was going to get treated better and get the support he needs.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: At first, it didn't matter much as it felt like a running joke, but I became more invested as it was talked about online. People started to care, which made me care more about this monkey in a funny way. There was support for him, and it felt unfair for him to be treated like that.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't physically help or hurt me, but it brought emotional sadness for the state of the world. The existence of such hurt made me feel hurt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible for this random baby monkey that got dealt a bad hand and was being treated unfairly. The media attention made me care more.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't feel like I was in control, as I couldn't really control the situation. It was just a sadness for the animal, and I wanted it to get better.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It seems like the baby monkey ended up getting support and making friends with the other monkeys, and the story turned around for the better. I was happy and got what I expected.

situation: I took my 15-year-old dog for a check-up and found out she has a heart murmur. It was supposed to be a regular appointment, but I wanted to ask the vet about a lump we had found, which seems like it is okay. We weren't expecting to hear she had a heart condition. She's getting on now, so any treatment will have to be assessed carefully. Initially, I was quite scared for her, but now that we've had a few days to consider it, we're learning what sort of things to look out for to see if it deteriorates at all. We've had her for 12 years, so it will leave a huge gap when we do lose her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Thursday last week. It matters very much, Ivy has been a constant companion, particularly to my wife. In addition, we have lost 4 dogs in the last 6 years to various illnesses so it is a sort of 'here we go again' moment.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Our dogs have all been rescue dogs and it is our intention to protect them from pain or distress. It hurts when we feel we cannot do this.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: There is no one to blame for this, she has had the best of care since we had her and it is just one of those things.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We have a measure of control in that, if there is any treatment required, we can decide whether to go ahead or not. For instance, if the vet suggested surgery, we would have the option to go ahead with the operation, look for non-invasive treatment such as drugs or, keep her comfortable until such time as we have to let her go.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Most of this was unexpected, we thought the lump was going to be an issue. It wasn't so that was good news however we hadn't even considered a heart problem so that was totally out of the blue.

situation: I was having a conversation with a friend about their dog's health. They mentioned that their dog was not doing well health-wise and feared that the dog might pass away soon. The dog is 15 years old now, so she is quite elderly, but I have known her since she was a puppy. Initially, I felt shocked when my friend shared this news, as we often assume good health will persist unless something significant occurs. I tried to be strong, reassuring, and supportive for my friend, who was clearly distraught. I also felt deeply saddened, both for myself and, perhaps more so, for my friend. I wanted to express my sadness to show empathy and support for my friend, but I also wanted to conceal it to appear strong in their presence. I felt sorrow for the dog as well, but I also recognized that she had lived a long and happy life. I felt really conflicted about whether to continue discussing it with my friend or to change the subject to try and lift their spirits and distract them. However, we kept returning to the topic of the dog. Once I returned home and was alone, I was very upset and cried. The dog sadly died the next day.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last Thursday when my friend and I were out for a walk. It mattered a lot to me and really affected me emotionally because I have known the dog for many years and I could sense the pain my friend was in.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it was sad and shocking news, but to be able to talk to my friend, about the dog and other things, felt quite cathartic and I think it helped us both.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think both my friend and I were both responsible for it because we have a genuine emotional link between us, and these kind of events bring those emotions out and show it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I had a sense of control as I did most of the talking and was asking most of the questions. I felt like I could be silent if I wanted to and so had the control in the situation, but I did not feel that was a negative, it was just the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The situation started with something very shocking and unexpected, but as we spoke and the situation played out I think it did meet my expectations, although these expectations were not conscious.

situation: I needed a doctor's appointment because I was experiencing severe leg pain. I used the econsult service and received a reply saying I would have to wait four weeks for a 'routine' appointment, even though I had already disclosed that the pain was so bad it was significantly affecting my sleep and day-to-day activities. I asked to be referred for further diagnostic tests, but the situation left me feeling very, very angry. I was particularly cross because illegal immigrants get 24/7 access to medical services, yet I cannot, despite having paid my National Insurance for over 45 years.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday. It matters a lot to me because I'm in pain.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It has prolonged my pain.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The government.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not in control at all. I didn't have a choice as to whether I accepted the situation or not.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No they did not go as expected. I was surprised they said I could only go in the queue for a 'routine' appointment.

situation: I was on a video call with my 24-year-old son, and we started reminiscing about a pancake shop we used to visit when he was a kid. It was a nice trip down memory lane, but it also made me sad thinking about the times I wasn't there with him. His mum and I split up when he was 6, so I missed a lot of his youth. Initially, I just wanted to enjoy the shared memories with my son, but later it struck me how much time was lost. I felt happy at first because I always enjoy our conversations, but then I felt sad. I always make sure to take time to check in on my son, ensuring he's okay mentally and physically by listening to him and asking open questions. Dad mode is hard to switch off!

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday evening, as we try to schedule a call every other Sunday. I think the fact that we both want the call shows how important it is to us and our relationship.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I'm not sure hurt or help is quite the right term, but I do get a lot of enjoyment from our chats as we talk about all sorts of things. It's always great to talk to him so I guess you could call it beneficial.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think both of us get something positive from the call, so I suppose we're both responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Definitely during the call but I was surprised how sad I felt afterwards as I've described earlier.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I guess it took me by surprise when he mentioned the pancake house, I think he realises how much time we missed not being together as he grew up.

situation: I lost my dog earlier this week. His name was Carlo and he was 10 years old. I'm feeling sad because he'd been with me constantly as I work from home. I didn't need any comforting since he'd been sick for a while, so it was expected. As a dog owner all my life, I've learned how to deal with these setbacks. It was important to me that he wasn't in any pain and that he was comfortable.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot because I work remotely, so Carlo was my constant companion. It's tough to lose a pet like that.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because he died. There are no positives that come out of a loss of a close companion - human or pet.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: He had contracted a liver complaint and we were dealing with that condition. His death was not sudden or a surprise.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I was in control as I had a vet who was caring for Carlo. We did what we could.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things progressed totally as expected as we knew his prior condition.

situation: My cousin recently lost her dog, who passed away after 13 years. I tried to console my cousin, but it was hard because it reminded me of my own losses, like when I lost my childhood pet and my grandfather. As I sat with her, memories of those times flooded back, making me feel more emotional and sad than before. I wanted to share my experiences to connect with her and show empathy, but I was cautious not to overshadow her grief with my own. Just making her feel better was my priority in that moment, so I focused on listening and offering comfort.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because it mattered a lot to her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I guess it helped me to process some of my own grief, as the loss of my grandfather, but hurt me because I guess I really wasn't prepared to have another conversation like that.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Like who was at fault? I don't think anyone was, really.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Somewhat. I just felt as if I was second guessing myself more than I cared to. I didn't want to sound or come across as dismissive or insensitive.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes. Neither of us really left the conversation feeling 100% better. It was just nice to have someone to vent to I think.

situation: About a week ago, I became very frustrated when I thought I had deleted a personal document and that it was gone forever. I needed the document in order to get a Real ID, so losing it made me feel hopeless, angry, and depressed. I was really anxious and upset for a couple of days until I remembered that I had backed the document up. Thankfully, I had.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me. Without a Real ID, I couldn't get access to certain things, like getting a passport.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt upset.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt most responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control of the situation because I felt helpless.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I did not expect to remember that I had created a backup of the document.

situation: A situation that made me emotional was when the anniversary of my niece's death passed recently. I really needed a hug from my family, but we live in different states, so that wasn't possible. It left me feeling like life still has to continue and I have to be strong and raise my kids.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last year, but the anniversary of it was last Thursday. It mattered to me because it was a significant emotional moment related to my niece's death.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation both helped and hurt me. It helped me heal, but it also hurt because she is no longer here.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Can't answer that, too personal.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of my emotions for the most part.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected. I prayed and watched videos of her and her kids.

situation: I had a horrible migraine all through last week that really scared me. I finally got a chance to see my GP, and they told me it was just stress and dehydration and asked that I drank more water. I just needed the migraine gone and I just wanted to feel better. I felt both emotionally and physically drained. I started envying everybody else living a migraine-free life. I could not go to the office all week, and it just made me have to do everything from last week, this week.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it mattered a lot to me because I could not function as normal.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because the migraine meant I couldn't do anything else, and I was functioning at 20 percent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: According to the doctor, it was dehydration and stress.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control because I could not function properly.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things didn't go as expected until I met the doctor.

situation: I was admitted into the hospital for a week with multiple medical issues. During that time, I was trying to get rest and treatment, but the whole experience left me feeling drained. Support from my partner was really important to me throughout the situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 weeks ago and it mattered greatly to me because my life was literally on the line.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by diagnosing my problems and working on a plan to rebuild my health.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My grandmother and partner, who made me go to the ER, and my care team at the hospital were most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control because it was up to me to actually go.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting any of it.

situation: A cat keeps sitting under our gazebo in the garden, and my wife has become quite fond of it. The other day, I let our dog out into the garden because it had been raining all day, and she hadn't been for a walk. The dog saw the cat and chased it out, and my wife got mad at me for letting the dog out. I tried to explain that I didn't know the cat was out there and it's not our cat, but she still got mad at me, spoiling our weekend evening. I was feeling angry because I didn't see this as my fault. I have no control over a cat that I don't own. I was disappointed that we had the weekend spoiled over this issue.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last weekend on Saturday. It mattered to me because it spoiled our downtime from work.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt my feelings by my reasoning not being understood. I felt it was clear this was not deliberate action.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My wife
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I felt like I was taking the blame for something out of my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Once an argument has started it went how I knew it would, by us not talking for a day.

situation: I had to cut off a friendship that I had for years because my friend became so self-damaging as a drug addict, and it started affecting our friendship greatly. It's more about him; he needs to want to change, but it's very clear he doesn't want to do anything anymore for himself and constantly asks for money. It's sad because we've known each other for years, and I literally have seen him over time turn into this bum. I just have these good memories of him, and then I see the way he is now. It's crazy.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a few months ago in January. It mattered to me because I've known him for years and have seen him change over time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I have not felt much of a difference except this daily text of him asking me to hang out and see if I can bring him cigarettes and beer.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I have no clue that is his problem to figure out.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Of course not. It's his life. His decisions only affected me because he was using our friendship to find his highs or constantly asking for help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, at the end of the day after cutting off the friendship I have had more peace. Realizing just how much stress he was causing was surprising.

situation: I was shocked to receive the largest utility bill ever. The notification came via email, and having been literally snowed in for two weeks with wind chills reaching around fourteen degrees below zero, I knew it wasn’t going to be good news. But to actually see it — well, let’s just say it was a good thing I was sitting down. I wanted to find out whether others in my area were experiencing similar shock. The situation left me worrying about my finances. Could I actually pay the entire bill at once? Would it be possible to make partial payments until the whole amount was paid off? It’s always most important to me to 'keep calm and carry on' whenever possible. I know I did my best to trickle water and adjust the thermostat as low as possible to avoid possible pipes bursting and to bundle up, wearing layers, covering up with blankets and all those sorts of things. At least I know I did my best. I can accept the reality of the situation. On to the next thing!

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: For days the meteorologists had been warning us about extreme weather on the way. It turns out they knew what they were talking about. I did everything I knew to do to protect my household. I stocked up on food, some of which I knew wouldn’t spoil. I saved water. I bought batteries for flashlights. I made sure devices were charged. I prayed we wouldn’t have power outages (and we didn’t!). I grieved for communities nearby who had it so much worse — no power for weeks, downed trees, all kinds of unimaginable issues. Actually, I was so lucky. Life happens. It could have been so much worse. I am blessed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation reminded me that change is inevitable — it’s the only thing that’s constant. If we don’t stay alert to possibilities and be prepared to roll with the punches, we’re in trouble. We need to take things as they come as much as possible and save for a rainy (or in this case, snowy/sleety/icy) day, and keep the faith that this too shall pass. Yes, my purse might not be quite as full as I had expected, but I’m ok. I have enough to cover my expenses, thankfully. And when I look at the bigger picture, I’m grateful. I have my health, I have loved ones. Life is good.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The weather is nothing I can control. It’s an act of God. It’s up to me to try to be prepared for what might happen.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes. I did my best. I can’t know about external circumstances, but I have learned, and continue to learn some valuable lessons by experiencing life.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The weather here had never been so extreme and had never lasted so long.

situation: I missed the deadline to submit an important project at work, and my boss sent a follow-up email asking about it. I felt a rush of panic when I saw the email. I had to explain that I needed more time to complete the project to the best of my ability, but I had underestimated how much time the final details would take. When I realized I missed the deadline, I wanted to avoid disappointing my boss and needed a way to fix my mistakes without damaging his trust in me. The situation left me feeling anxious and ashamed, and I was worried that I had permanently damaged my boss's confidence in my reliability. Being seen as dependable is very important to my identity at work, and the fear of being viewed as unreliable influenced my immediate panic and my urge to quickly justify the delay.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal to me in that moment. My sense of competence and self-worth felt directly tied to delivering that project on time. Failing to meet the deadline made me feel like I had failed at being the person I want to be at work. It happened about a month ago.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me by shaking my confidence and making me doubt my abilities. However, it also helped me realize I need to improve how I estimate time for future projects.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that I was mostly responsible for the situation since I mismanaged my time. However, I also think the project's scope was larger than initially anticipated.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control once I realized the deadline was approaching and I wasn't ready. The more I tried to rush, the more the details seemed to slip through my fingers.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I had planned to finish with time to spare, but the final phase required more revisions and testing than I had accounted for.

situation: It was the fourth anniversary of my dad's death, and I was just trying to survive the day at work. I wanted some acknowledgement and grace from others, but I didn't want to bring it up directly to anyone. Honestly, I struggle to identify how I feel, but it's somewhere between sad and hopeless. I also thought about how sad it is that my dad doesn't get to see how far I've come, meet my partner, or ever meet his grandchildren.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last Thursday. It mattered to me because it reminds me how much time has passed since I lost my parent, and the weight of that. It was a really sad thing to happen.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as it reminded me how much I’ve suffered over the past four years.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I don't attribute responsibility or blame to anyone or anything for how I felt or how the day went.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel like I was in control of my emotions and the situation. I cried and had tears running down my face on the tube. I think grief hits you in different ways, and it’s important to just feel it as it comes.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I was in the office and things were 'normal'. But I guess just a heavy weight over the course of the day.

situation: One of my adult children has been facing health challenges, and their endoscopy took place last week. It was an incredibly stressful and tense period for us. I focused on providing them with emotional support and strength because they tend to experience anxiety and could have had a panic attack. Before the procedure, I felt anxious and under significant pressure to ensure my child could handle it, and I took proactive steps to prevent any panic attacks from occurring. Maintaining my own well-being and resilience was also crucial during this time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week, and it mattered significantly to me because my child could finally get the test they had been waiting for since last November.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation was emotionally exhausting for me, but it didn't hurt me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No person was responsible for the situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control as much as I could be.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went better than expected. The unexpected part was that the appointment was brought forward with only 3 hours notice to the morning, which meant less anxiety build-up.

situation: After completing a challenging project that had me feeling overwhelmed, my friends surprised me with a weekend getaway. I was thrilled by the unexpected treat and felt incredibly thankful for their thoughtfulness. It was a wonderful reminder of the strong support and appreciation they have for me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in January, and it was really important to me because I needed it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me unwind.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My family was most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control because I could decide not to go.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected.

situation: On Tuesday, it was me and my wife's anniversary, and it turned out to be anything but positive. The car battery died, her work was overworking her, and I couldn't get anything done at my job. I even bought a jump starter, but it didn't work. My wife came home crying, and I was overstimulated. We ended up spending almost $100 on Ubers and food. I was distraught. We weren't really trying to achieve anything specific; it was just that day was horrific in terms of how it was treating us. We wanted to go out for dinner, but it was an utter disaster from the get-go since we couldn't even drive. We felt like the world was against us the whole time. My wife even said, if we get this car running, we shouldn't drive because at this rate, we might die in a car crash. That's how bad it was. Nothing was important except that at 2:00am, I was finally able to jumpstart the car. But after an entire day of headaches and pain, there was nothing to be positive about.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened primarily at home, but with my wife hers was at work and at home. It mattered because it was supposed to be a nice day, but it was just completely toxic and full of negativity through no fault of our own.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt because it really did feel like nothing was going right for us. It didn't help us remotely and it just made us feel like we should just resign ourselves for the day.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Everything was external. Nothing we did or could have done would have changed the outcome of a single thing. That's probably why we were so frustrated because anything in our control, we can handle. Anything outside we can't and everything was outside.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Absolutely zero control from work to the car to us not going out, etc.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything was unexpected.

situation: My son moved out, and I just got very upset. I wanted him to stay, but I tried to hide how upset I was. The whole situation left me feeling very sad and emotionally drained. Above all, I just want my son to be happy and safe.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I love my son and we all enjoy each other's company. Not only will I miss him, but I will also miss the fun times we have.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation didn't help or hurt me; it is something that has to happen. He is an adult, and the time would always come for him to move out.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was myself and my husband who were most responsible, as we are emigrating and my son does not want to come with us.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt both in control and not in control. I was in control because it is my husband and my choice to move, but out of control because my son chose not to come with us.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as I expected. We all had a good cry and cuddles.

situation: I told a colleague about what had happened during a previous work call when a client advised that his wife had died. While I held it together with the clients, telling my colleague made me emotional. I was just telling my colleague because they knew the client too, and we were both so upset for him. I felt much better after talking to my colleague about it. It was a relief to talk about it with someone. I was just glad the client was okay at that time. I checked he had friends or family around who could help him organize things.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened one day in work last week. It mattered a lot to me because he's a great client and I enjoy chatting to him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation upset me, but only in that I was upset for the client and how they would cope.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The news of the death was responsible for all of this, but no one was personally responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I lost control by letting it upset me and then causing my colleague to be upset.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The news was not what I was expecting and I wouldn't have expected to become so upset with other clients.

situation: I received an award and recognition at work, which made me feel really special. I was trying to improve the process of how we do some activities at work and make them easier for the employees. This recognition made me feel good about myself and happy that I could help out my coworkers and the company. It was important to me that the company recognized my efforts and didn't overlook them.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the past week and it mattered a lot to me because I felt like I was able to help out the company and my coworkers.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me become more reliable as an employee and more trustworthy as an employee.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think my supervisor was most responsible for all of this and recognizing what I did.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt I was in control and able to explain everything that was needed.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything did go as expected and I feel wonderful about the entire process.

situation: My sister got a promotion at work, and I was just praying and hoping it would work out for her—and it did. I was elated; I couldn't contain my joy. The promotion was a big deal, and the competition was high, so I was so excited that she got the promotion. Another reason that made me happy is that I got a profit from a stock that I bought. It brings hope. With everything happening in today's world, little good news like this offers some sort of hope to keep going.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Both events happened last week. For my sister, I was happy that she's happy and has gotten what she works hard for. For me, I am equally happy that I made the right decision in choosing the stock. It ignites my ability when it comes to decision making.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It actually helped me a lot to keep going and to trust my instinct.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My intuition and my research ability.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes. I felt like I made the right call and waited for the result, and the result came in positive.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it did.

situation: Scenario: I went to a party with my spouse, and he ended up dancing with someone who has been a concern in our relationship. Initially, this affected me negatively because he did not seem to understand my feelings. I wanted him to acknowledge that his actions impacted me and to empathize with my perspective, but I felt my emotions were overlooked. I did not feel appreciated in the relationship. However, upon reflection, I realized that true happiness comes from within, and I have decided to focus on my own happiness. I am feeling better now and am committed to nurturing my own well-being.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot because I had just stepped out to use the toilet when the whole incident occurred. It made me question my spouse's commitment to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt betrayed by my spouse, and disappointed in the fact that he didn't admit his wrongs.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that the lack of accountability is the main issue.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like at the time when I felt very emotional, I was not in control of my feelings, but after a few days, I regained control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because I never got an apology, but I decided to move on and keep my mind off things by doing something positive for myself, and so I signed up for a gym membership.

situation: At the time, I really needed listening ears and someone to tell me it would be okay soon. I was looking for reassurance that I’m not alone. The situation left me feeling like I had to figure it out myself, and I kind of did. But what was important to me was the clarity that came with it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered so much because it was really about me trying to figure out my next steps.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped a great deal, instead of sulking, I decided to find a solution by myself, I stopped waiting around.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I would say the stage I’m in right now is mostly responsible for it and then myself, my past decisions which mostly didn’t turn out well.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt like I was in control, I felt like I could finally do what I set my mind to.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, things went as expected.

situation: I am dealing with a challenging situation involving my partner's financial responsibilities. I had given my partner money to look after, but it was spent without my knowledge. My partner also told me that certain debts had been paid off, yet we received bailiff letters, indicating otherwise. I'm trying to keep a roof over our heads and wanted to ensure that the money I gave to my partner was used responsibly and that our debts were managed properly. This situation has left me feeling anxious, and I'm using substances like alcohol and vaping weed almost every day to cope with these feelings. I've expressed that if this situation happens again, I will move back home.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in October last year, and it was the fourth time it occurred. This situation matters to me because it has been a recurring issue, affecting my trust and causing constant worry about money over the last 18 months.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by affecting my trust and making me feel vilified. I've been constantly worried about money for the last 18 months. Additionally, I feel like I never do enough for their daughter, and this situation contributed to my decision to split from my fiancée for a month a week before the wedding due to a dog sitting booking conflict.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel my fiancée was most responsible for all of this.
