appraisal_reasoning.control: I initially thought I was in control. However, my perception changed when I went to the showroom to pick up a car, unaware that the money had been spent.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I was left in the middle of a town near Burnley that I didn't know, with no money to get back home via public transport.

situation: Sometimes when I'm alone, I find myself getting emotional. In those moments, I really need comfort. Being by myself can leave me feeling sad and lonely.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on a Saturday night when I was sitting at home feeling lonely. It mattered to me because I felt very alone.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I felt very alone.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt like I was responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control of the situation because I made myself switch emotions to happier ones.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as I expected during this time; my emotions turned happy.

situation: I had recently connected with an ex-colleague who was looking for an English tutor. We set up a Zoom meeting, but she wasn't able to attend, and since then, she hasn't responded to any of my emails. I'm not quite sure what's going on. I was trying to help her improve her English and simply needed a response to the corrected work I sent her after she inquired via email. I just feel confused because I have no idea why there haven't been any responses to my emails, especially since her previous emails were polite and deferential. Really, I just wanted acknowledgment that she had received my proofreading of her writing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It was significant because about 5 years ago I had informally worked with her in school and she had expressed an interest in being tutored by me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was a disappointment because I was also going to experiment with the Zoom teaching because I have always been more comfortable with all forms of in-person teaching.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: In a way, I feel I was because after a few emails with no response, I was uncomfortable moving forward and I can certainly work on using Zoom without that specific student.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I did not because when we first met about 6 years ago there was a similar false start that involved in-person instruction.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was only disappointed because there was no closure on the situation and I feel it is very awkward to send another email because I believe that responsibility should fall on her.

situation: I recently got into a bad argument with my boyfriend. There was lots of yelling and accusing, and eventually it ended with me and the baby leaving. During the argument, I was trying to be seen, but I still feel unheard and unseen. It's just really stressful.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 days ago. It matters a lot to me because I put good things in but I'm sick of being treated badly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurts me because I feel like it will be just like all the other times; he does good for a few days then goes back to being selfish.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like he's responsible for his actions and I'm responsible for allowing things to get like this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I did not feel in control during the argument. He gets upset and says the meanest things and I just shut down.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I told him what I wanted but I can't take being talked to the way he does.

situation: I ran out of food to eat during the week while I was working, and I ended up having to eat cheese and crackers. I really wanted to have a meal with some pasta and meat in it, or at least something with protein and substance, but there was nothing available. This left me feeling hungry, frustrated, and dissatisfied. I was at work, so I didn't want to be cranky.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened during the week, particularly Wednesday. It mattered to me because everyone else in the household ate all of the food and we hadn't gone grocery shopping yet.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me hungry and a bit stressed due to hunger.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The lack of food was responsible. And the lack of time and finances for me to go and buy groceries.
appraisal_reasoning.control: After the situation and after I went grocery shopping, I felt in control because I could eat and had options to choose from.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes. They went as I expected because I was able to satisfy my hunger and need for food.

situation: We came home from an outing and found that my dog had a bloody runny stool in the house, which is really unlike her. I was nervous and scared, and I felt sad that she was sick. I wanted to make her feel better and assure it was not something serious. It was important to me to make sure she was OK.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because I love my dog.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I would say neither - it was not helpful or hurtful - it was just a situation that happened.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt it was likely that she ate some yucky food or got into something outside that upset her stomach.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I couldn't pinpoint exactly what caused it nor could she tell me because she's a dog.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected. She ate less the next few days and slept more, but then fully recovered after the bug passed.

situation: I had a long assignment that was due two days ago, and I ended up spending a few nights trying to complete it on time. I was really focused on making sure it was up to a presentable standard, but I needed more time to do it well. The whole situation left me feeling crushed and heavy because of the deadline pressure, and I was also feeling dazed and under the weather from staying up each night. It was really important to me to ensure I did well on it and maintained a high standard.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It started 2 weeks ago and was due 2 days ago. It mattered a lot as it was a 2-week long important project that needed to be done well for the company.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as I didn't have enough time and led to sleepless nights.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The company for putting such tight deadlines or not reducing workload in other aspects.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, as it felt like I was just working and working.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected but it took a lot from me.

situation: My son has just turned 17, and on Sunday, I took him out in the car to practice driving for the first time. It was a poignant moment for me because it's a big marker of the end of his childhood. I needed to focus and be clear on teaching him what he needed to know to learn to drive. However, the situation left me feeling quite disappointed in myself as I didn't handle it well. I found teaching him more difficult than I imagined it would be. What I had expected to be a positive experience for us both ended up being quite stressful. I need to learn from this and be clearer and less stressed the next time that I take him out.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on Sunday morning. I wanted to do a good job and for the experience to be positive because it was such an important moment in both of our lives.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped us to build a bond. We connected by spending time together and sharing a milestone moment.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was most responsible because I was the teacher in that moment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control because I ultimately stopped the experience when it turned out badly.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, it was stressful and I needed to think the steps through more carefully.

situation: My son came to me and told me that he wants to move out. I have to move now because I can’t afford the place without his income, which is embarrassing for me to admit. I understand he’s 20 but almost 21. We just needed a little bit more time to put a little bit of money together so we can move, but it came out of nowhere. I felt a little bit hurt and upset because we found out that he doesn’t even care if he sleeps on someone’s couch; he just wants to move. That kind of hurt our feelings. Just having more time with my son.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It matters to me a great deal, but I didn’t let him know that.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It just hurt my feelings. I mean, I understand he wants to move out with his girlfriend. I get it, but it still hurts my feelings because it just could’ve gave us more time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: His girlfriend.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I mean, yeah we both talked back-and-forth. I mean he doesn’t know how much it hurt my feelings and I wasn’t control of the conversation it just it’s very hard to explain when it comes to your children.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The whole situation was unexpected. I mean, we thought it was. We were gonna have a couple more months so it was definitely out of left field.

situation: I had to make a decision that I knew was necessary, even though I didn't want to take it. I was trying to stick to my boundaries, which was really important to me. After making the decision, I felt empty temporarily, but I know it was for the best.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened 2 weeks ago and mattered a lot to me because it involved 6 years worth of friendship.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me know I was strong enough to hold myself, but it hurt me because I was going to have to leave my bestie.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt they were obviously responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control when I finally called it out.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because I anticipated an involvement from a polo guy but got none.

situation: About two weeks ago, my ex-boyfriend and I broke up. He was the one who brought it up first, and we both agreed it was better to part ways since our life plans are very different. Despite the breakup, we're still friends and living together in the same apartment. During and after the breakup, I needed comfort and wanted someone I could talk to without worrying about being judged or having my feelings invalidated. The whole situation left me feeling devastated, and I'm still trying to figure out how to recover from it. Self-introspection has been really important to me, so I started journaling to help process my feelings.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The breakup mattered a lot to me because I lost a partner who cared about me more than anyone else did. He was someone who helped me learn boundaries because I've never understood that concept until recently.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me emotionally, especially since the timing wasn't good as I'm still jobless. But it also helped me realize that I have personal issues that need to be resolved.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think it was the both of us. We were too attached to each other to want to let go, so he censored himself and his worldview just to keep the relationship.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I don't think I was in control because I lost him. If I was in control, I wouldn't have let him go.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected. It was something that's been sitting in the back of our minds for a few months already.

situation: The situation I chose was the end-of-year party that took place a few days ago. There had been unwarranted rancor between two lovers recently, which was very ugly and uninteresting. It was caused by unwarranted or unconfirmed rumors spread by a friend of the lady, who had a crush on her lover. The whole truth came out through a recorded confession, and the woman got to know the truth. Fortunately, the man still loves her and came back to profess his love for her at the party. She accepted his apologies with a lovely kiss and a big hug. All I wanted in this situation was for the two lovebirds to reconcile and move ahead with their beautiful love story. Witnessing their reconciliation made me think about the fact that I am still unmarried and wish to be in love like this one day too. What stood out for me is the prevalence of truth.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago and it mattered to me a lot because the man involved is my close friend and I know the whole truth from way back.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me a lot and did not hurt me in any way. I believe true love still exists and I hope I will find mine one day.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I do not want to apportion blames here, all I want to reinforce is that when we have access to information, we should try to find out the truth.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I never felt in control at all but, I just prayed and hoped for the best result to come out and it did.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected because I knew both of them have been true to each other from way back and I can actually vouch for my friend too.

situation: My best friend's mother is old and it looks like she will be dying soon, and my friend was very upset about it. I was trying to comfort my friend while also feeling emotional myself because my parents died a few years ago. The situation left me feeling sad. It's important to me to be there for her, but I'm unable to go be with her because she's pretty far away and I don't have transportation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered greatly to me because I feel bad that I can't be there to help her through this time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it made me feel like I failed my friend, that I'm not a good friend.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am responsible because it's mostly my fault that I currently don't have transportation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't feel in control because I can't do much at this point to get the transportation needed to go see her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I guess things went as expected. She realizes that I don't have transportation at this point. I'm sure she still feels sad that I can't be there though.

situation: My daughter left for college, and it's a few hours away from home. It was hard on my wife, but she's coping with the change. I know she's going to be okay because we raised her well. I just hate that her college is so far away. Besides her being okay, I want my wife to understand that it's important for our daughter to grow and spread her wings. I'm proud of her and a bit worried, as any parent should be. It's just going to take some getting used to, but time fixes everything.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: She left for college a few weeks ago and it meant a lot to me to see her make it to this part in her life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did a bit of both, I felt I have did well as a father and at the same time I feel like I'm losing a bit of myself.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody was really responsible, it's life and these changes are apart of it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did as much as I could, I feel like I have to support my wife more than anything, she had a stronger relationship with her than I did.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I just wish I could have anticipated how hard it was going to be on my wife to see her daughter leaving the nest.

situation: A friend I hadn't spoken to in years called me, but I didn't answer. This stirred up a lot of complex emotions in me. I felt a strong need for closure when my friend reached out to me after all this time. I was very upset. She got married about six years ago, and the communication wasn't like it used to be. They moved away, but we were still on good terms. Then her birthday came up, I wished her a good one, and later found out she was in town at the time. I expressed my feelings about it, and she shared her reasons, which I tried to understand. I decided to respect her choice of interaction, so since then communication faded. One time she said she would like to talk with me later, I was hopeful, but it never happened. For reference, she now has a 5-year-old child that I know of through other friends. When she called, I felt uncertain about how to respond; she feels distant to me right now, and it brought back those challenging memories.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened about three days ago, and it mattered because before we had issues, we had been friends for about ten years.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt because it brought to surface a lot of negative feelings that I had buried so deep that I had forgotten they even existed.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Honestly, I think I could have gone on just fine with my life without her reaching out to me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: At the end of the day, it was up to me to choose how to react, so I feel I was in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What was expected was a deep heartfelt apology, I didn't get that, so I guess things didn't go how I expected.

situation: My husband and I were out with friends last weekend, and he started talking about a purse I bought during our Christmas visit to my brother in Wisconsin. The purse was from Scotland, bought at an Irish shop, and it was special to me because it reflects my heritage. It cost $72, which is the most I've ever spent on a purse before. He brought it up and pointed out that it is made with wool, and the two friends we were with are vegan, which made me feel put on the spot and judged. I was very uncomfortable about it but didn't say anything to him. I knew that the purse wasn't made from vegan-friendly materials, so I had no intention of putting a spotlight on it at all. I'm on a tight budget, so I don't spend often on unnecessary items for myself like that, making it a special purchase. I didn't feel good that he started talking about my finances with other people or that he felt the need to call attention to the fact that it was not vegan-friendly. My intention is to have my needs respected, so I would like him to not talk about my spending, investing, saving, or income with anyone else. It made me feel disrespected and exposed. What stands out is that I have asked my husband numerous times in the past not to discuss anything regarding my finances with other people, and he keeps disregarding it.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last weekend, and it mattered to me because I felt put on the spot and judged. I started thinking about it more the next day while my husband was at work, and I began feeling very angry about it. It feels almost pointless to say anything because he keeps disregarding my requests to keep my finances private.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because there is information that I consider personal. I am very self-conscious about my lower income, and although I budget tightly, I occasionally treat myself to small things and I don't want to feel judged for that. I also want to respect other people's beliefs and preferences, so I don't want to rub it in someone's face that I have a purse that may be constructed from wool or leather if that person is vegan. It seems disrespectful to them to bring it up.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel my husband is 100% responsible for it because he brought it up when there was no need to. No one asked about the purse. No one asked about my purchases. He decided to bring it up out of the blue and I have no idea why.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control because I've talked to him about this before and he has obviously ignored my feelings. And I don't always want to make a scene in front of other people because I feel like I'm constantly getting angry at him in front of others and it makes me look like the nag.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Overall, the day trip was actually quite nice. It was that moment that made me feel sour.

situation: When I got to be a Dad, I was trying to be there for my family and those who needed me the most. This experience left me feeling proud and happy. It was also important to me how my friends came to support me during this time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because it was a memorable day and a first for me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience helped me as my status in society was a bit stronger as a father.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible for my family and my closest people.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control partially, but the truth is that I didn't know what to do at such a moment.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things didn't go as expected due to the baby arriving late, so plans were changed.

situation: I had to go on some errands, and my last stop was a grocery store. Everything went fine and I drove home, which was about a half-hour drive. Once I got home, I put away the groceries and sat down to relax for a few minutes. It was then I realized I hadn't checked my phone in a long time, and I didn't even remember seeing it shortly after I left my house. So I had to go find it. Fortunately, it was at the grocery store. Almost two hours were wasted and all the gas, I was pretty upset for sure. I was really worried at first that I might not find it. Then I felt both relieved and mad when I found it. Losing all my info on that phone was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: A lot. When I realized at home that I had lost it I was pretty concerned. Info and money could be lost.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Cost me time and money and angry.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I didn't know where or if I could find it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I eventually found it.

situation: I have broken up with my long-term partner of 12 years. I was trying to get them to come over or meet somewhere to talk about things because we lacked communication. This whole situation left me feeling very low and depressed, as well as very anxious. I didn't know why they just gave up on us.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot as I felt left aside.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It really hurt me. I didn't leave the house for a few days and couldn't stop crying.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was on both of us.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Not at all. He started to call the shots and let me down a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not really as he let me down a lot and didn't show or call.

situation: I was having counselling about a sensitive matter in my life, and it led to an overcome of sadness. I was trying to work through the situation with help from the counsellor and wanted to feel less sad; however, it only made me feel worse. After I talked through my feelings, it did eventually make me feel better, but it made me feel deflated and tired. It was important to me that I worked through my feelings and that I was listened to in that situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because of how it made me feel and that I wanted to work through it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was a mixture of both. Talking about your feelings both helps me and hurts me at different times but I know talking about my feelings will eventually make me feel better. Talking through issues helps me work through existing problems that I have. The more you confront your issues the better chance you have of solving them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was the most responsible person for this because I'm the one who takes charge of my own problems.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control of the overall situation because it was my decision to go to counselling and to make myself better.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They went as best as they could and while it did make me feel sad, I was able to talk through my problems and get to the root of the problem.

situation: I was thinking about the end of my life, which gives me anxiety and makes me dread being old and dying. I was just worrying and going through it in my head, considering the process of getting older, slower, experiencing more pain, and then dying. This left me feeling a bit of anxiety and dread.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week. It's not that important to me now since it's far away.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation didn't really help me; I guess it just made me worry.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel just me is responsible for it since I tend to worry a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't really feel in control because it's hard to stop anxiety and worrying.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went pretty much as expected.

situation: I spoke to my friend the night before, and the next day, I got a call telling me he died in an accident. I needed comfort, but I didn't know how to feel; I was dead inside. I felt really sad and just wished I could have said goodbye.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last week, and it was a very close friend so it mattered a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help me. Imagine losing a close friend abruptly. Well, I am better now but his memory still makes me sad.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one, that's why it was so bad. I wish I could blame someone.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was not in control. I just felt I couldn't control how I feel.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I mean I am better now, so as expected.

situation: This was when my sister got engaged to her long-distance friend. I really wanted her to be happy getting married to her friend and not feel like she was marrying a stranger. I felt emotional about the whole thing because I've been encouraging her and advising her to stay hopeful. She had been feeling like she was getting old and worried about not being able to get married, so this engagement was a big change for her.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me because she is older than I am and I felt bad that she wasn't settled yet.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me because she is happy so I am happy too for her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt the spouse was responsible for taking a long time to make up his mind to settle down and get married.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I wasn't in control because I wasn't in the mind of her spouse.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected, she accepted the proposal and other wedding arrangements will be made as follows.

situation: My sister is undergoing cancer treatment, but she doesn't want anyone knowing the details. I get emotional because I feel shut out and unable to help. I really needed her to contact me and share a little of her feelings about the situation. I felt upset, and when I talked about it to one of my friends, I started crying. I want the best for my sister. I want to be able to support her at this difficult time, but I am being prevented from doing this by her actions.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened four days ago. It matters a lot to me because my sister and I used to be close. It is sad that she is shutting out those who are closest to her at this time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me, because my sister and I used to be close. Her illness has changed this.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The cancer has been the cause of this divide. Neither I nor my sister are coping well with her diagnosis.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I was not in control. I wanted to be there to support my sister through a tough time and I am being stopped from doing this.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No things did not go as expected. I had hoped she would welcome my support, but that is not the case.

situation: Yesterday, I had to put my dog down. My family has had this dog for about a decade, so it was really tough. I'm just looking to share this to hopefully feel some relief from the sadness. Right now, I feel very empty, and I miss our dog very much.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened yesterday. It mattered a lot.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Putting my dog down hurt me because I lost a family member.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My dog's kidneys were failing. She was suffering. There wasn’t much we could do anymore.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I didn’t really have a choice. We had to put her down because she was suffering.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected.

situation: I read a poem at a burial, representing my daughter at her Grandad's funeral. I was reading to a group of relatives, and I felt sad but pleased that I had done it. It was important to me to get through the reading without crying.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me very much as it was a very sad occasion and I wanted to do a good job.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to say goodbye. It didn't hurt, but it was a very sad occasion.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt most responsible to my daughter.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control, but only just as it was a difficult poem to read in difficult circumstances.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as I hoped and perhaps better than expected.

situation: Buying my first car was a situation that made me really emotional. I had always planned on getting the perfect car that suited my needs and met my budget requirements, so I kept going back and forth between two models. In the end, I chose just one. I wanted a car that was reliable and would be cheap in the long run. I didn't mind paying more upfront as long as it was economical over time. The emotions I felt were like I had climbed Mount Fuji. It was as though I had finally reached one of my goals, and a substantial one at that, having to buy something like this. I felt a sense of pride but also generosity—pride in the sense that I can accomplish adult things on my own, and generosity because I can share the car with my mom and dad whenever they need a ride. What really influenced my decision was saving time by not having to worry about repairs on my old car. I felt excited about being able to spend more of my precious time with friends and family, which is very important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about 3 months ago and I still feel the effects of it to this day. It mattered to me a lot because I can spend my time on other valuable things. You see I use a lot of time commuting to work or perhaps cooking and cleaning but sometimes I would use it on maintaining the upkeep of a car which takes time. So now with a new car almost guaranteed less time needed to make repairs I can finally share it with things that matter most in life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me a lot in that I can help others rather than myself that way I'm not seen as selfish or so self-centered if that makes sense. I always want to make sure those around me feel good and not have to worry so much in day-to-day life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My parents. Plain and simple, they helped me get to where I'm at and also helped me achieve what I needed to be able to purchase the car.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes I did feel in control because I was able to manage finances and my emotions.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes things did go as expected but there were a few failures along the way such as repairs for the house or having to step out of that goal in order to keep promises for others.

situation: I recently made a big transition from trading options in the stock market to trading futures. Just about two days ago, I blew my account. My goal is to switch to day trading full-time, and I switched to futures because they're supposed to be better and it's what prop firms would want me trading. After this happened, I felt very defeated. I had put so much time and effort into getting better, and all it took was me breaking my own rules for a second to lose over half of my account. I keep telling myself it's all part of the process. I know this, but it doesn't hurt any less for sure.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in the morning when a position I had didn't close as expected, resulting in a loss. It mattered greatly to me because I have been working very hard to become consistent, and this setback knocked me back significantly.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me financially and damaged my ego. I hope it helps me say no in the future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am 100% responsible for what happened.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I lost control the second I started panicking. Even though I made the money back for a moment, the panic carried over and disrupted my system, causing me to make a bad decision.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Nothing went the way I wanted, but I hope that the loss will help me in the future.

situation: I paid off a large debt that had been a struggle for me for a long time. It felt so good and was such a relief. It's improved my overall mood since paying it off. I wanted to pay off the debt so that it wasn't hanging over me anymore or stressing me out each month, and so that I could start saving for our next family vacation. Now, I'm feeling happy, excited, and relieved. What's really important to me is that I did it myself, and it made me proud.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot. It was high on my to-do and priority list. It had been weighing on me for a while.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by making me less stressed and more financially stable.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I worked hard to work extra hours, do more side jobs, and save the money.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It did, I was able to pay it off on the timeline I had set for myself.

situation: I have a family member who has become so obsessed with far-left politics that it's impossible to talk to her anymore. She's constantly commenting on any other family member's social media posts like she's on a crusade. She's even taken to preaching to her grandchildren. It wouldn't bother me much, but her facts are 100 percent wrong and easily provable. I've given up on trying to address the misinformation because it's impossible with someone who pretends not to know things or that certain facts didn't happen. I'm trying to let it go, but I'm very frustrated, especially with the influence she might have on her grandchildren. How do you deal with someone so blatantly partisan that they threaten to excommunicate family members who disagree with them?

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last summer when she banned me from her house and told my wife to leave me because of my 'political extremism'. It mattered to me because it lasted until she needed to borrow my truck.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation did neither help nor hurt me, as other family members just rolled their eyes at her.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I believe she was most responsible, as I would never ban someone from my home for their political views.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt sort of in control. At that point, I decided engaging with her was not worth the time or effort anyways.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I did not believe she was so out of control that she would threaten to excommunicate family for not agreeing with her.

situation: It was my sister's funeral, and I was trying to understand why she died. I felt empty, like there was a pit in my stomach. My mum is in hospital and couldn't go to her funeral, which made everything even harder to process.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Monday, and it was important that everything was right.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because she should still be here, and I shouldn't have had to be doing this.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I blame her partner for this, not phoning for an ambulance sooner.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, and that's the worst thing. I felt helpless.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The funeral went as expected but still hurt all the same.

situation: I had a really important doctor's appointment where I needed to make a case to stay on a medication they wanted to withdraw. I was anxious because I had written out a long speech, hoping the doctor would understand how much better this medication makes my life. My husband came with me for moral support, which was really important to me. The doctor was very kind and understanding, and I felt very relieved when they agreed that I could stay on the medication, at least for now.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago. It mattered a lot to me because I had to wait several weeks for the appointment and became more and more anxious and stressed about it beforehand.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me by alleviating the vast majority of the stress. Things may change again in the future, but I am trying not to worry about that right now.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The doctors had been told by the NHS to withdraw the medication for the majority of patients.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn’t feel in control at all as the outcome was not my decision either way.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn’t sure what to expect but things certainly turned out well.

situation: I received a phone call advising that a family member has died. I was overwhelmed with many emotions and just needed those around me to acknowledge the situation and give me space to grieve. I felt a mix of emotions, ranging from sadness to happiness. It was important for me to know what was going to happen next, like when the funeral would be.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a lot to me because the family member and I were very close. It was sudden, and the family member was healthy and very active in life.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I would not see the family member alive ever again, and I would not be able to talk to them.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible; sometimes things happen unexpectedly.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was in shock at first, and then once the shock subsided, I regained control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, it all went as expected. I was informed by family members about the funeral date and time. The funeral was pleasant and a nice reflection of the family member's life and all the good they did in the community.

situation: I was feeling really stressed about money and the cost of living because everything is becoming more expensive. I was trying to figure out how much money I had left for the month for groceries and anything else, and it turned out to be much less than I expected. I really wanted the money to go further, but the situation left me feeling stressed and frustrated.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered because it has a big impact on me and my family life. It makes everything more stressful for everyone.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It frustrates me that I have to be very careful with money, limit days out and treats, and struggle to pay for things that enhance life.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just the rising cost in everything, everything has become much more expensive.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No not all. Because I cannot control how much things cost.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, I expected the budget for the month to go further.

situation: My daughter got accepted to study for A levels, which was a big moment for us. We went to an interview at the college where she had to explain the qualifications she had gained to be accepted. I really wanted her to gain the best professional opportunities she can and be successful. This whole experience left me with a feeling of great pride and accomplishment. It's important to me that my daughter has a better career than I ever had.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When she got accepted, it mattered quite a lot because her main aim is to go to university eventually.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped the morale of the family. However, there were definitely difficulties at the beginning as my daughter wasn't motivated enough.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like outside influences towards my daughter were the main culprits.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was totally not in control of the situation and I could have done better.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things didn't go as expected as I had hoped, but I was pleasantly surprised by the outcome.

situation: My nephew dressed up for World Book Day, and it was very cute and emotional. I wanted to capture this moment, so I took a picture. Seeing him grow up and attend his first book day event felt positively emotional. He seemed very happy, which made me happy too.
