appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Unfortunately, yes I expected to be upset emotionally or be reminded of something unfortunate like my unemployment because of the situation.

situation: The release of the Epstein files hit me hard, stirring up extremely negative emotions. It started with horror and quickly turned into disbelief as I realized I had been taken in. I found myself grappling with radical uncertainty about what to believe, and I was astonished that conspiracy theorists might be more correct than anyone had given them credit for. There was a complete decentralization in my thoughts and emotions, making it difficult to process everything in the usual way. I felt disbelief and couldn't quite name the feeling that this might have been an orchestrated, intended effect. Fear for the future, both immediate and long-term, crept in. I'm trying to figure out how the world actually works differently from what I've always assumed or been led to believe. While I don't need anything right now, reassurance would be nice. I feel like I need a plan for when WWIII breaks out and Los Angeles is razed to the ground. I imagine setting fire to the Santa Monica Mountains could cause easy chaos and destruction, even after the rain. Maybe the events of the last few years have been experiments. The situation hasn't left me, and I'm still feeling horror, disbelief, radical uncertainty, astonishment, decentralization, difficulty in processing thought and emotion, disbelief, and fear for the future.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This is ongoing and matters a great deal to me. The situation hasn't left me, and I'm still feeling horror, disbelief, radical uncertainty, astonishment, decentralization, difficulty in processing thought and emotion, disbelief, and fear for the future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It's helping in that it's forced me to sharpen my thoughts and prepare myself for upheaval. It is hurting in the sense that uncertainty will always gnaw at you if not kept under control, and this is a hard one to keep under control. It also simply causes me emotional and existential pain to be told that humanity is very much worse than I imagined, and class-structured in a much more malevolent way than anyone thought.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Who even knows? Frankly, at this point I wouldn't rule out aliens, although on the surface it looks a great deal as though this has all been whipped up by Israel.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I'm not 100% in control because of the emotional overload and existential crisis, and that it seems to have been an intended effect that this should be so.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Evidently things went very much not as I expected. That should be clear from everything I have already expressed.

situation: My neighbor, who was also a very good friend, passed away unexpectedly. I really needed him this past weekend to help with some chores around the house. His absence left me feeling a sense of loss and somewhat numb. He was always there for me, helping out and keeping me motivated. Mainly, it was the friendship that was important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me a lot, not only losing a friend, but more like a brother.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt knowing he's no longer present, but I take everything I learned from him, moving forward. His positive energy to all he taught me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the positive relationship we had, learning from each other. So I would say the both of us.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I always felt in control around him. We had each other's backs.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things were always good between us, whatever we had planned went as expected.

situation: My long-term girlfriend of three years broke up with me. I really wanted to try and save our relationship, but she wasn't interested in that. I just wanted her back and to have the life we had together again. I desperately needed to talk to someone about it. The breakup left me feeling cold and empty. The support I got from friends and family in the days after was very important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The breakup happened about a week or two ago, and it mattered a lot to me because I really loved this girl.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me greatly as she said she had just fallen out of love with me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt mixed emotions; angry with her for breaking up with me but sadness to do with myself as I struggled to understand why she felt the way she did.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I definitely felt like I was not in control because she broke up with me out of the blue.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It was very unexpected for her to do this; I felt like there were little to no signs of this.

situation: My adult child lied to me, and all I wanted was honesty from them. The situation left me feeling so hurt and absolutely drained emotionally. I was tearful and anxious, struggling to process what had happened.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered greatly to me because I've always tried to instill honesty in our family, and lies make me nervous.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me deeply, making me feel very low and rejected.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible for allowing myself to feel this way and also held my adult child accountable for not trusting me.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control at all because I had zero control over his lies.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because he wouldn't talk to me.

situation: The loss of my mother to cancer happened shortly after the birth of my first child. Initially, I needed to be on my own for a period of time and avoid people, but then slowly I opened up and was able to talk about it. The situation left me feeling empty and lost. The support of my family, who were also dealing with the grief, was important to me. Having my newborn daughter provided a great sense of focus during this difficult time.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened around 5 years ago and it mattered as she was the one person who I could always turn to in an hour of need and was a great champion for and of me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me as the loss left a huge void in my life; however, I know she is watching down on me and it spurs me on to achieve things in my life such as my career.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: It was a lifetime of smoking which ultimately led to the cancer which led to her death.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't really feel like I was in control at all as cancer has no barriers and is a terminal disease.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: The treatment was unsuccessful sadly.

situation: My wife and I were traveling overseas and we got into a disagreement at a pub about ordering food. We had plenty of food in the Airbnb we had, but she wanted to eat out. I told her we don't have enough time in this town to finish the food we had at the Airbnb. We went out for a beer, and I thought we were going to return to our room to eat dinner. Then she wanted to eat out. I was exasperated and told her to order something, but by then it was too upsetting and I went outside the pub. It was a bad evening after that. I wanted her to realize that we had purchased too much food already and we needed to eat that food first. She didn't agree. But she also doesn't like to waste food, so I told her we should eat what we have first. I also thought we just went out for a beer, not to eat out. I was upset and didn't really understand why she couldn't grasp my point about the food we had.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered enough for me to remind her we had enough food already. I was upset that what we had agreed to had changed, as we were just going to go out for a beer, but then she wanted food.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt because she wasn't listening to my perspective. I don't like being put in the middle of something that didn't have to happen in the first place. If she had mentioned wanting to eat at the bar beforehand, I would have agreed not to buy more food before going out.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I thought she was responsible because she wasn't listening to what I was saying.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because she wasn't listening to the logic I was presenting to her. So it was out of my control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: What was unexpected was how she changed the evening with her wants for food. I just wanted a quick beer and then to go back to the room. I was tired.

situation: I've been really frustrated lately because I've been looking for a new job. I've spent a lot of time on applications, but I've barely gotten any replies. What I really want is a job where I feel more fulfilled than I do at my current job. This whole situation has left me feeling frustrated and discouraged. It's important to me to find a job that offers some level of financial stability.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It's been ongoing for several weeks but really came to a head last week after I checked and had no responses on my job searching site. It mattered a great deal because I was hoping to find a new job before spring.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me because it set my plans for the year back a bit. It is also a bit of an ego blow because I am more than qualified for the jobs I applied to.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel like the job market is most responsible. Employers are uncertain how the economy is going so they lost jobs but are afraid to fill them.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I have some level of control based on how many applications I put in but that some of it is out of my hands.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things have not. That's been the entirety of our conversation. I expected at least one response from an employer.

situation: Scenario: My vehicle broke down, and I feel like it's mainly his fault. I had to beg for a ride or to use his vehicle, even though I had already given him a set of my keys. I needed to go pick up some medicine, and the whole situation left me feeling very upset. It feels like I'm always giving in my relationship, and he's always taking. I allowed him to use my vehicle whenever he wanted, but now I'm stuck without a way to get around. I decided to take action and get my vehicle fixed, so I can regain my independence and not have to rely on him for transportation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week, and it mattered a lot to me because it involved picking up medicine that I take daily.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me realize what kind of person I'm dealing with. It hurt me because I know he's never going to change.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel he is most responsible for all of this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel in control because I had no other way to go.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected because he would not take me.

situation: My sister-in-law, who has MS, visited me for the first time in 6 months. She has developed some paralysis on her right side and is finding walking very difficult. I found this emotionally upsetting. I wanted to offer positive support to her, but I felt rather helpless. It was important to me to show her how life could still be good despite the challenges she is facing.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This happened in the last few days. It has had a huge impact on my brother as my sister-in-law is 16 years younger than him.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I wanted to offer practical ways to support them and I didn't know how. I realised how lucky I am to be healthy but a little bit hopeless about the future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Circumstances in general.
appraisal_reasoning.control: For a lot of time yes but not really emotionally because there is no real answer.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I wasn't expecting to see how tough life was for them but was grateful that they enjoyed my company.

situation: My younger sister was upset and needed support because she felt unwell and didn't know what help she needed. It happened last Saturday evening. We contacted the doctors for advice, and they suggested she visit the clinic for a check-up. I was trying to ensure she received the appropriate care and support. I felt concerned but also relieved. It was important to me that my sister got the treatment she needed. At the clinic, she was diagnosed with a bacterial infection and was hospitalised to receive intravenous antibiotics. She is now feeling better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened early hours of Friday morning when I got a call from my sister, who lives on their own and had no support. It mattered to me because I felt concerned and relieved, and it was important that my sister got the treatment she needed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me emotionally as my sister looked poorly and weak, and I felt unable to help.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt responsible for my sister.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt sort of in control as I asked for medical help, but I could not personally fix it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went worse than I expected as my sister was hospitalised and needed treatment.

situation: I was recently baptized, and it was a really emotional experience for me. I wanted to make an outward proclamation that I've turned my life over to Jesus Christ, who died for my sins on the cross. I also wanted to make my son proud of me. Believe it or not, I was really tired afterward. Being up there was emotional, and I felt vulnerable. But it was great because my whole family came to support me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Sunday and it meant very much to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me in just getting a little bit more confidence in myself and that I'm on the right track and I'm on the right road.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Into recovery 6 months ago and had been a chronic relapser and I don't want to do that anymore. I repeatedly let myself down and my family down.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I am in some sort of control because my life is not chaotic and foolish selfishness and depression.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything went as I expected and we went over to friend's house from church and had a nice brunch.

situation: My daughter was rude to me, speaking to me like I was a child and listing all my negative attributes. I just wanted her to listen to me. The situation left me feeling angry, upset, and hurt. I felt small and like I was the problem.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It didn't matter when I said what I said. It was just conversation. She made it something more.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Help? There was no help. She hurt me by being hurtful and blunt.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Her obviously. I was just making conversation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I wasn't in control after she spoke to me like that. I stopped talking because I was upset and overwhelmed and I didn't want to cry in front of her.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Her outburst was unexpected.

situation: I was reassigned to a different position at work, and honestly, I was devastated. I really wanted to keep doing what I was doing because I enjoyed the position so much. It was making a huge impact, and now, with this reassignment, I'm also facing a large pay cut.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened a couple weeks ago. It mattered a ton.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me financially and also hurt my career.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Our superintendent.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No. I had no choice or voice.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was blindsided.

situation: This situation happened at work not long ago in the past week. My manager gave me a task to complete within a specific time frame, but I couldn't finish it on time. This made my manager angry, and they started saying discouraging words to me, which made me feel absolutely bad. I needed more time because the task was a bit complicated. It was important to me that my supervisor could resonate with my situation and understand my vulnerability.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it really did matter to me because it was a task I was given to complete to obtain some reward but was rather unfortunate I could not finish on time.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me when my manager got angry at me by saying discouraging words to me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I was expecting my manager to give me enough time and he didn't so I think the fault is from him.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No I didn't feel that way. Because my manager was the one who gave the task and provided the time I was supposed to finish. I think he was in control.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes things didn't go as expected because I didn't finish with the task on time.

situation: I felt like my experience with another doctor was disregarded, simply because they were in the same field. I needed her to understand why I did not want to see this other doctor. The situation left me feeling misunderstood and not heard. It's important to me because these types of dismissals can impact decisions to seek medical care or not.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered a great deal to me. I needed my doctor to understand that I needed this secondary doctor to focus on my condition and not who she believed I was.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The experience hurt me by making me feel afraid to discuss problems with my doctor in regard to getting the right healthcare.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am not sure who was most responsible. I know the other doctor was more interested in my character or life than my medical needs. But I also know if my regular doctor had been supportive instead of dismissive, that would have helped me to find the right care.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel that I was in control; I felt trapped. First, I was encouraged to speak openly, and once I did, I felt reprimanded for it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had no concrete expectations. I felt I was taking a risk, but I was encouraged to speak openly.

situation: I was in a cafe trying to enjoy some peace when someone nearby started blasting their phone loudly. I confronted them because I wanted them to shut up and remind them to use earphones like a normal person. When they refused to listen, I felt really aggravated. In my frustration, I even threatened to break their phone.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when I was trying to study and enjoy some quiet. It mattered to me because I did not want to hear inane garbage blasted from a speaker, which seemed to purposely piss people off.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by disrupting my peace and study time. However, it helped me realize that I need to be more creative in how I encounter people, suggesting or asking instead of demanding.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt that some people are naturally clueless and rude, possibly due to being raised in countries without basic decorum.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control because I chose to engage with the ridiculous behavior.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did not go as I expected. I figured they’d put headphones on, but I don’t believe they did.

situation: I was due to get root canal treatment and I didn't sleep well the night before because I don't like going to the dentist. I had made an appointment for first thing in the morning as I wanted to get it over and done with quickly. I made sure not to sleep in, got up earlier than normal to get ready, and as I was on my way to the appointment, I got a message informing me that it had been cancelled due to unforeseen circumstances. I just needed to get it over and done with since I've been having intermittent problems with this tooth, and at my check-up, the dentist said it needed more attention. She would only really know the extent of the issue once she started working on it. The cancellation left me feeling disappointed, annoyed, and slightly angry. Now, I'll have to go through the whole process of waiting and attending the new appointment, which isn't until three weeks from now, and hope that I don't have any problems in the interim.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and it mattered to me because I have needed to get this done for a while. I wasn't able to get a suitable appointment for various reasons, so now it is delayed even more.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me by disrupting my availability and causing unnecessary anxiety, which I will have to go through again leading up to my next appointment. It hasn't helped because I know I have an issue causing pain and swelling intermittently.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I am probably more to blame as I have a fear of the dentist due to terrible experiences as a child. The dentist was unwell, which is unavoidable, so it wasn't their fault.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt both in control and not in control. As an adult, I could rationalize the situation as foreseeable and normal, which I shouldn't have been so worked up about. However, I was worked up about it and hadn't slept well the night before.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things didn't go as expected. My scheduled appointment for root canal treatment was unexpectedly cancelled on the morning of my appointment when I was on my way to it, disrupting my day and plans.

situation: Last week, my supervisor, who's the operation manager, was following me around all week, trying really hard to catch any mistake I made. There was even one occasion where they ridiculed me. I just wanted to do my best and get through the day without getting into any beef. By the end of the week, I felt exhausted. The whole situation left me feeling demeaned at some point and made me realize the real workplace politics that could be easily avoided with better communication.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened last week and went through to Friday. It mattered to me because I felt targeted or isolated.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me in many ways, but I felt more demeaned. I felt like my contribution to the company was meaningless, and personally, it exhausted me each day.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My supervisor was most responsible for all of this. My supervisor single-handedly orchestrated all these.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was only in control of my work, but the moment I was done, I felt my supervisor had control and dictated everything.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. I tried to avoid her, and the good thing was the supervision ended at the end of the week. Overall, my performance was great.

situation: I'm out of work and struggling to get my wife to understand the importance of frugality and avoiding foolish spending. Until I find another source of income, I really want to focus on spending only on absolute necessities. This whole situation leaves me feeling not good at all—I'm frustrated and really concerned about having no money.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 3 months ago. My car broke down that I use for work. I have no other transportation. It won't be fixed until we have many warm days in a row. I have not had income from my job since then.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: No money to buy groceries. I need to go to the dentist for a root canal but can't get there.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one. it just happened.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I'm not in control of mechanical break downs.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I had no expectations. I am surprised this has lasted this long.

situation: Scenario: It was a Friday evening, and I was busy in the kitchen making dinner when my son came home with a small gift box. At first, I was curious, but then he told me the gift was for me and that he had bought it to show his appreciation. His words made me emotional, and I smiled with joy. I felt loved, appreciated, and like a happy mom.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened on a random Friday. It mattered to me that my son thought of me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It gave me the strength to keep going as a mom.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My son, of course.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, they went smoothly.

situation: A few days ago, I was overwhelmed by the hurt and betrayal from two friends of mine, which happened about two years ago. I thought I was past it, but the pain resurfaced unexpectedly. Seeing one of these people triggered the emotions, and I found myself back at the point of not understanding how they could do that and how I am supposed to be okay with it. Although I am okay today, I am aware that I have not fully healed and the pain might come back again. I wasn't trying to do anything specific when the feelings resurfaced. I saw one of the people who hurt me, recalled why they are not my friends anymore, and everything came back. I wanted someone to acknowledge my pain and feel my hurt, even without an apology. I wanted someone to know that I'm still hurt by their actions. The situation left me feeling messy. I was shocked because I thought I had moved on. I was worried about never forgetting the pain and questioned if I would ever get past it. I felt vulnerable for about two days and kept wondering if seeking validation was wrong. For a long time, I avoided thinking about the situation, but I felt like life handed me this pain to deal with because I cannot escape it—avoid, yes; escape, no. One of the people who hurt me was given a new environment, which felt like they were given a chance to start over while I was left with the pieces of what was done, unable to run away.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about two years ago, and it mattered to me a lot because it shaped how I see people around me. I realized you don't have to be a bad person for people to be bad to you, and that truly, the heart of people is really wicked. They were two of my closest friends, and they destroyed every good memory of them dating back to when we were on campus.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation allowed me to get in touch with reality. I was always too trusting and naive because I believed that as long as I am good to people, they will be good to me. The reality is far from that, and I was forced to take that as a hard pill.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I will say my two friends were equally responsible. They knew what they did, they knew it was out of spite, and still did it.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I think I had some control. Two years ago, this would have destroyed my mood for the whole week. I would have been crying and a little depressed. This time, I was able to deal with it gracefully.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Not as expected because I thought I was past this. The fact that I can still feel bitter and pain is unexpected.

situation: I was able to submit a project to the organization, and after presenting it, it was approved and funded. It was a great relief. I wanted to work hard, and my efforts finally bore fruit. I felt satisfied, happy, and accomplished. It was also a relief to be able to finish the job. This project was a stepping stone that may help me in the future with career growth.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me as I was able to display my talent and ability to the management as well as impact the company growth.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me have more self-confidence. Trust in my ability and work even harder to achieve my career goals.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself, I worked for long nights drafting proposals and creativity which boosted the project.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, because all the authority was put on me to deliver quality results.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Everything was smooth and went as expected. I was able to deliver on schedule.

situation: I was listening to an upbeat song that I used to sing and dance to when I was a little girl. It reminded me of when I used to do that a lot, entertaining my dad, who enjoyed watching me pretend to dance like a teenager. My dad has passed on and this memory gave me a warm feeling of nostalgia. I was listening to music as a way to chill out and relax after two weeks straight of mostly focusing on doing work-related tasks. This situation improved my mood and even made me a little happy. Remembering those cherished moments spent with my dad at that stage in my life is always important for me to hold onto.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: I was a child who loved music from as long as I can remember, and my dad encouraged me by purchasing a kiddie record player and some records that were popular at the time. So, it mattered a great deal to me that my dad supported my love of music.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation helped me to gain a deeper appreciation of different styles of music and different sounds that could be made by musicians playing instruments, and singers doing different things with their voices. I had already started to learn how to play the piano.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My dad was definitely responsible for investing his hard earned money into music lessons, the record player and records. My godmother also supported my music appreciation back then.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was very much in control. I was given the freedom to choose what records I listened to when I stayed with my dad. And dad knew that I loved watching shows that featured musical artists and young people dancing, and we often watched those shows together.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: For a while, things went as expected. However, several years later, when my dad got married, and I started living with him and my stepmother, my music lessons abruptly stopped, which wasn't what I wanted. My stepmother was responsible for this interruption.

situation: Our kid got accepted into their dream college, and we've been waiting for this moment since they were born 18 years ago. We were just incredibly happy to have reached this milestone in our lives, so we celebrated by going out for dinner. We felt very proud of our kid and extremely happy that we've made it this far. It was important to us that our kid handled the application process all by themselves, which showed us their maturity, independence, capability, and strength.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a week ago in the evening while I was cooking in the kitchen. It mattered a lot to me because it was a moment we had been waiting for since our kid was born 18 years ago. Hearing the news made me feel incredibly happy, and I instantly stopped cooking to celebrate with our kid.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped acknowledge that our effort in the last 18 years raising a kid has paid off.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: We all, my partner, my kid, and myself, were responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control for most of the time. During difficult times, we learned how to get over them.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went mostly as I expected. Of course, it's more about our kid going their way than my way.

situation: I very sadly had to put my old horse to sleep after a few months of struggling with veterinary problems. He was 21, and I bred him and owned him all his life. He had Cushing's disease, which was first diagnosed in 2023. He had been on medication but repeatedly suffered from bouts of laminitis. I tried desperately to save him, but in the end, there was nothing more we could do. I wanted to make sure that I’d done everything I could for him and that I wouldn’t regret any decisions I made about his treatment. I just felt terribly sad and frustrated that I couldn’t save him. I didn’t want other people to think that I hadn’t tried hard enough.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened in January and it mattered so much to me as he was the first horse that I’d bred.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It was a sad decision that I had to make but one that I have had to make before. Now that he’s gone I am confident that it was the right decision at the right time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was particularly responsible; it is just the luck of the draw.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt in control of the situation, yes, but not in control of the disease.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went more or less as I expected, although I was hoping against hope that he may be able to comfortably live a bit longer.

situation: There was a family disagreement about the need to house our parent. I felt like it was a priority and an important task, but my siblings didn't see it that way. I struggled to understand why everything seemed to fall on me to initiate or solve. I wanted all of us, including myself, to join efforts and either purchase or construct a house together. The situation left me feeling abandoned and like I was being taken advantage of. There wasn't anything else important to me in this situation, just a lot of frustration.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened 5 days ago. It matters a lot that the family unites to lessen burdens on each other.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It is now a financial burden to me as I am still in the process of buying a house.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My parent is pressuring this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I am not fully in control of this. I hate disappointing my parent.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No. I expected not to be pressured to do this fast.

situation: I was FaceTiming with my eight-year-old granddaughter, and she was enthusiastically describing her weekend to me. I laughed out loud and told her, 'I love you so much!' She is my pure joy. I just wanted to catch up with what she's been doing. She was so exuberant with me that it became a special moment between us. I felt full of love and joy and oh so proud. It represents the kind of moments we enjoy when we're together, whether it's in-person or FaceTiming.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: These times matter the most to me as I am retired, live alone with my dog, and look forward to these times with my four grandchildren.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It made me feel happy, joyful, and loving so it definitely helped me.

situation: I recently had a negative experience when I shared a photo of my deck and landscape renovations with my mother. I really like the changes, but my mother responded via text that it looked barren and was a waste of money. I live in the high desert, so the landscaping is for fireproofing and water management. I wanted to remove part of the deck to add space for new water catchment barrels because I'm on a private well and need the water for my flower and vegetable garden. I also wanted to plant waterwise plants around the deck to conserve water but maximize color in the summer. Her response made me feel a little depressed for a while, and then I questioned why I bother to share photos with her at all. It made me think that I shouldn't share things that are meaningful to me because her response is always negative.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: At the time it happened, her negativity really impacted my mood. I wanted to share something positive with her that I really liked, but her attitude made me rethink the work and money that I had put into the project.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think it impacted me negatively in the short term. It reminded me of past events where she was always negative, like my decision to purchase a house in a rural area.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think I was most responsible for how it unfolded because I sent the photo even though I knew that she would respond negatively.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was totally in control of the situation because I could have chosen not to send it.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: In the moment I was excited and wanted to share the project completion with her. So it was unexpected. But I should have thought about past events a little more.

situation: Last week, a close friend I hadn’t spoken to in a while reached out during a difficult time. We ended up talking for hours, reconnecting and supporting each other. In that moment, I really wanted to reconnect and offer support to my friend, and I needed reassurance that our friendship was still strong and that we could be there for each other. The whole situation left me feeling warm, relieved, and grateful. I felt a renewed sense of closeness with my friend, along with happiness and comfort knowing we could support each other again. It was also important for me to feel heard and understood, and to let my friend know they weren’t alone. Strengthening trust and mutual support mattered a lot to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered greatly because it reaffirmed my friendship, showed mutual support, and strengthened trust. I felt relief, gratitude, and closeness, realizing how important care and understanding are in relationships.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation mostly helped me. It strengthened my friendship, boosted my emotional well-being, and reminded me of the value of support and trust. It didn’t really hurt me, though it stirred vulnerability.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my friend was most responsible for this, because their decision to reach out during a difficult time made the reconnection and emotional support possible. Their openness created the space for trust and closeness to grow.
appraisal_reasoning.control: During the situation, I felt somewhat in control. I could choose how much to listen, how to respond, and how to offer support, which allowed me to guide the conversation while still being emotionally present.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things mostly went better than I expected. I anticipated a brief conversation, but unexpectedly we talked for hours, reconnected deeply, and shared meaningful support, which strengthened our friendship more than I had imagined.

situation: I had a highly emotional conversation with my husband about our taxes. I thought we would be getting a refund that we could use to pay down some credit card debt, but he informed me that he still owed money on his taxes from last year, so we would not be getting a full refund. I wanted to confirm that we were making a joint decision about how best to use our joint refund to pay down some of our joint debt. I was angry because I felt like he had intentionally hidden his personal debt from last year from me, and frustrated that we would not be using our joint refund for our joint debt but instead on his personal debt. He did apologize and tell me he was embarrassed about his inability to manage his own finances, which made it hard for him to talk to me about it, and that helped my feelings of anger.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a great deal. I was very upset and frustrated, which doesn't happen that often with my husband and I as we have a good relationship with a lot of trust.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt excluded from decisions that would impact us both and angry that something so important would be hidden from me. It made me wonder if there were other things he wasn't being honest about.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think we haven't had a lot of experience talking about finances, and given that I make a lot more money than him, I think there were feelings of insecurity and embarrassment.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control as I was leading the discussion, asking for information, and taking the lead on figuring out next steps.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They didn't start off or end as expected as the whole situation was a surprise! I do feel like we ended on a strong note and have a plan moving forward.

situation: My football team scored a goal, and I was thrilled because I really wanted my team to win the game. The feeling was incredible—I was elated and excited. What made it even more special was sharing the experience with my family.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened yesterday afternoon at about 3.30 pm. It mattered a great deal as how my team does is something I think about for most of the year.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me by giving my team a better chance to climb the table and potentially get promoted.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The player Callum O'hare as he scored the goal.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, the situation is beyond my control and down to the team and manager.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected a win so that was good, but there is always doubt in sport.

situation: I was reflecting on my time with my fiance as an exercise to write my vows for our upcoming wedding, and I began crying tears of happiness. I wanted to isolate some important, romantic moments in time from our 8 years together. The whole experience left me feeling happy and glad to have met my partner. It was important for me to be able to structure the memories and what she means to me in my vows, reflecting those memories.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Our proposal is a great example of our relationship. We were on holiday and I had a surprise event planned to propose at, but my partner wanted to be lazy and go back to the hotel. It ended up being a spur of the moment proposal instead which we loved.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It didn't help or hurt me, it had me laugh.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Just the way we are together and individually. We mesh well.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, because ultimately I didn't want to give away the surprise!
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No absolutely not. I ended up proposing 2 days later, almost at random, because the moment was perfect.

situation: My wife and I are planning to buy a flat in London this year. We've already viewed several flats and have placed a few offers on some of them. The task of deciding the amount and figuring out how to write the offers has led to some arguments between us. We were trying to decide on the money amount for the offers and needed to write an email template to send out to agents. It's a really stressful situation because you don't know whether you're asking the right amount, and it creates arguments between me and my wife, so it's important for us to hear what both parties, my wife and I, have to say; this is teamwork.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event did matter to me very much. This is because we were deciding on a really important decision, which was purchasing a flat.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: In a way it helped us because we could continue with the process of buying a flat, but at the same time it hurt us both because we did argue several times.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I wouldn't put the blame on any of us. It was more about the stressful situation.
appraisal_reasoning.control: We were in control in terms of the monetary amount and email template to send out. However, we were not in control to decide whether our offer was going to be accepted.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: We are still in the process as we have not had any offers accepted yet, but we are currently in the negotiation process.

situation: I was taking a study on Prolific, trying to raise some money to pay my electric bill before it becomes past due. During the study, I hit a question that I found really disturbing. It asked me to describe a situation where I had power over someone, using at least five sentences with details about what happened and how I felt. As I was contemplating the question and trying to think of a situation to use, I started feeling more and more agitated and disturbed. Eventually, I decided to stop the study and return it, canceling it. In the cancellation, I included the reason that I found the first question about power disturbing. The study only paid $0.40, and I didn't think it was worth causing myself distress, which I believe would have greatly escalated if I'd continued. Even though I experienced some residual disturbances from the time I spent contemplating the study's question about power, I felt relief and some good feelings about myself for choosing to call and hold a boundary. I valued my well-being more than money.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event mattered to me because I have abuse and trauma-related issues and have been working on my personal recovery for many years. Thinking about these things is triggering to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because I set and held a boundary. It also pointed out an area that needs attention, as thinking about situations where I had power over another was disturbing to me and likely trauma adjacent.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: These are my issues. The villains in my backstory had a part in my reaction, but the survey writer had no reason to expect their question would be disturbing to some people. I find myself primarily responsible for this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I felt in control during the situation. I've taken over 1000 surveys on Prolific, and one point is present in almost all of the consent and disclosure forms: the test taker has the right to stop the test at any time without penalty, other than possibly not getting paid for the time spent so far.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected. I return around 1 of every 8 surveys I start on Prolific.

situation: I was feeling really emotional when I heard about the 92,000 job losses in the United States, and no new jobs being created. I'm currently unemployed, and all I want is a job so I can work. This situation has left me worried about my future. I'm also concerned about why companies aren't hiring and why it seems necessary to go through 3-4 interviews before even getting an offer.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened when the last jobs report showed the destruction of the job market in the United States. It mattered to me because I'm currently unemployed and worried about my future.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I want a job.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Nobody but us Americans can help get things right.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control because of how I put action into doing my best to find a job.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: How we lost 92,000 jobs is unexpected.

situation: I went golfing with my partner and nephew. I was trying to give my nephew a good experience because he just had a birthday. He has a tough life at home, and I like to help him have happy experiences. It was a great day. My nephew used to have a lot of mental health problems, but he has become a lot better these days, and I'm very proud of him. I gave him his birthday gifts, which he seemed to like. Then we took him shopping for some new clothes at a store he'd never been to, and he really had fun.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered a lot to me because my dad came too, and he was in a really good mood for once. He's been sick for a long time but seemed to be feeling better.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped me to give me peace of mind that my family is doing okay right now and my nephew has a shot at a happy future.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: My nephew for the work he has put in to get better and start to become who he really wants to be.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I feel like I was in control because I planned the day out.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things didn't go as expected. I thought they would go poorly, which has happened before when I met up with my family, but they went very well. I was surprised that my dad was in a good mood.

situation: A few years ago, I had a knee injury, and recently, I decided to try swimming for the first time since then. I was optimistic that exercising would benefit my knee, but I quickly realized that swimming isn't manageable for me anymore. This experience left me feeling like this injury might be something I'll be dealing with indefinitely. It also prompted me to reflect on the increasing importance of health as we grow older.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: When the event happened it mattered a lot, I think about it throughout the day now, even though some time has passed.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation mostly hurt me because I associate it with a negative feeling.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: The injury was my own doing so I am responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I think I was the only one that could avoid the injury because it was overuse.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I was surprised by the injury, I would have avoided the cause if I knew it was going to happen.

situation: My partner of four years and I broke up about three and a half months ago. Our birthdays are really close to each other, so we always had joint celebrations. This year, we couldn't be together, which was a huge bummer. He sent me a short video of his family singing happy birthday and him blowing out the candles on the cake they made to celebrate. I was happy to have friendly and open communication with him, but the video made me feel really sad, catching me a little off guard. I was trying to keep the lines of communication open with my ex-partner. We agreed to be friends and to see if our relationship rekindles sometime in the future. I needed that check-in with him because I really miss him. I was happy that he shared the video with me and I smiled while I watched. So I was happy but with an underlying twinge of sadness. By the time the video ended, I realized just how sad it made me. I could feel myself getting more and more sad, but it didn't last the whole day. I just recently started an SSRI and haven't been as melancholy as usual, which is one reason why I was so surprised by this deep sadness. Hearing his mom's voice as she was recording the video kind of struck me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened about three and a half months after my partner and I broke up. It mattered a lot to me, but it didn't affect me all day. It felt like progress because I was able to accept what I felt, and there wasn't much to do about it.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think that it helped me a little. It was somewhat welcomed because I was getting worried that my medication was causing emotional monotone. I felt my heart sink as the video continued, but there is not much to do in this situation any longer.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel that I was responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: It kind of felt 50/50. I have control over my phone and whether or not to act on those feelings, but the video did just kind of pop up on my phone.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Honestly, I can't pinpoint what I was expecting. I guess maybe I was not expecting anything. I know that when we speak to or see one another, it is affecting both of us.

situation: A few years ago, I had my gallbladder removed, which has led to some tummy issues. The other night, I ate greasy pizza way too fast, and it hit me hard—I really needed to poop. My 18-month-old daughter was sitting on the bed with me. After an accident last year, I can't walk very well, but I decided to get up and head to the bathroom. We live in a camper, so the toilet is maybe 2 feet from our bed. As I was pulling my pants down and getting onto the toilet, my daughter scooted over and grabbed a tube of sour spray candy. I didn't notice because I was focused on not going to the bathroom in my pants. I also didn't see her walk over to the edge of the bed, trying to hand it to me, and then she flipped off head first onto the floor. Luckily, she was okay—she didn't cry, scream, moan, groan, grunt, or anything like that. I was trying to go to the bathroom and poop without anyone to grab my daughter from the bed, thinking she would be safe. I felt like I made a poor choice, but she's probably not going to do that again. I know I need to eat greasy foods less often, and I should get up to go to the bathroom a little bit more promptly instead of assuming it's just a fart. Next time, I should carry my daughter with me if I have to.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: At the time it mattered a whole lot on several levels. First of all, I am a 32-year-old woman; I should not be almost pooping my pants. Second of all, I should have noticed that the candy was sitting on the bed, knowing it's her favorite and she would want it. Third, never leave your child unattended on a bed; I know this rule, this is not my first baby.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It definitely hurt me because I know better on all three of these situations that I can buy them into one with pure dumb luck.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I should have been in control, but I definitely lost control when I almost lost control of my bowels.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: They went out I should have expected them to go, but at that moment I was not expecting her to move that fast.

situation: Recently, we welcomed a new kitten into our home, and it has been an incredibly uplifting experience for us. We were looking to adopt a companion for our current cat, hoping to find a perfect match for our family. The new kitten was quite timid at the shelter, and we weren't sure if he would open up, but he has blossomed beautifully. I'm thrilled about this new addition, though a bit concerned because our existing cat seems quite unsettled by it. Understanding how cats behave, I'm optimistic she will eventually form a bond with him. She's a bit grouchy about the new kitten, which is challenging, but I'm confident she will come around.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: We adopted him on Saturday so 2 days ago, it’s very fresh. It mattered a lot because a cat is a big life change, they can live for over 20 years so it was important that it went well.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It’s helped make our lives better, more joyful, fun, but also it has me worried about our other cat, I’m hoping it doesn’t take her too long to come around.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Me, I wanted the cat.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did feel like I was in control because it was ultimately up to me to pick the right cat, and introduce them well.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went exactly as expected.

situation: Scenario: Last week, one of my friends was relocating to another state after getting a job transfer. I watched her finally leave after packing up her previous house. Although I wished she could stay behind, I understood it was necessary for her work. Seeing her go was bittersweet, but I felt optimistic about the new opportunities ahead. Our children had grown so fond of each other; they never left each other's side, even at school. They were very close, but we promised to keep in touch and arrange visits so they could continue their friendship.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It happened last weekend, and the event mattered a lot because it involved one of my friends.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I felt sad and faint-hearted. I did feel like going out to the picnic in the evening after my friend left.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself, I tried to lift my spirit up so I can cope with work.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, I was in control because I was finally able to concentrate with work and house chores.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, everything went as I expected.

situation: I was attending a training session when a doctor started talking about a shameful situation he experienced while delivering a baby, where the mother had a birth injury. This immediately brought me back to a similar situation during the birth of my son, and all the stress associated with it. Hearing the doctor's perspective made me rethink the injury I had. I hadn't planned on revisiting those memories that day; I just wanted to attend the training. But instead, I found myself needing some introspection and time to process everything. The whole experience left me really sad, and it triggered some physical stress responses.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened during a training. It mattered because it brought back memories that I do not usually think about.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It helped because it made me remember how lucky I am but it was hurtful because I hadn’t planned on thinking about those things that day.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: No one was responsible. The doctor was talking about his personal experience which he is entitled to speak of and it happened to trigger my own thoughts.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I only feel a slight lack of control because I do not usually experience emotions that bring me back to a stressful time.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No- this was wholly unexpected. I usually have some thoughtful moments during training that help me to explore my own actions in professional and personal situations but I had not experienced this kind of traumatic response before.

situation: In the past week, I found out that one of my long-time friends, whom I've known for about 34 years, is seeing a doctor for congestive heart disease and might be more frequently out of contact because of it. We talked online, but he did not want to disclose too many details. I tried to encourage my friend by letting him know that I had been through something similar. I wanted him to know that it's not only survivable but that he'd eventually recover and be living his life as normal again. Just to let him know that things will get better. The situation left me feeling melancholy and sad. I've known him for many years, and we have shared some good times together. He also lives several hundred miles away, so I can't really see him in person that often.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Because he was my friend, of course it was important. I shouldn't have to explain that part.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It's helped in making me take stock of my own life since a similar incident happened to me. I was able to move on despite the trauma of the medical condition, especially after treatment, both short term and long term, was received.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Most responsible for what happened was the passage of time and our bodies getting older. Medical complications are bound to happen no matter what.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No one is really in control in circumstances like that. You try to lead a healthy life, but mistakes and lapses always happen, and even if you do everything right things will still go wrong and break down eventually.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I don't know how things are going to go, anticipated or not. It's only been a week, and we only talked the one time, so it's an ongoing, developing situation. But as far as things stand now, I guess things went mostly as I anticipated.

situation: My friend had to cancel a skiing trip that I was going to join them on because they had to fly out to see their dying grandmother. I wanted to be able to help my friend, but I felt helpless. It made me feel like I wish I knew what to do. It was important to me to be a good friend.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened to me last Wednesday. It mattered quite a bit to me because this friend is the girlfriend of my childhood friend, and I want her to feel included in our friend group and like I care about her.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It did not necessarily help or hurt me, but I felt sad that there wasn't more I could do.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt most responsible for not knowing what to best do.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I did not feel like I was in control, because this was not a personal issue, and I live far away so there was nothing I could directly do to help.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things went as expected, in that I did not think of anything specific to do to help.

situation: This weekend, I stopped by a woman's house to buy something secondhand, and they had two small girls around my daughter's age. My daughter instantly connected with them, and it was amazing to watch her follow the other girls and want to play with them. She sat down at their little table and played with toys for the few minutes that we were there. It made me so happy that she wasn't scared or nervous around other kids her age. I hoped she would have fun, and seeing her so comfortable and engaged made me feel excited and eager to try and find opportunities for her to interact with more kids her age. For context, I have a two-year-old daughter and I do not know anyone with children in her age range, so she has never had a chance to interact with any other children before. Just that she had a positive experience with other kids her age.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened this weekend. It mattered a lot to me because the only other time she has ever been around another kid her age, she was scared of them and cried when they came near, so this was a good improvement.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation helped me because it was a positive improvement for my daughter. It was important because she wasn't scared or nervous around other kids her age, unlike the previous time.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Everyone involved was equally responsible.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't feel in control at all. It was all up to my daughter and the other two girls if they got along, and I'm glad they did.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I definitely did not expect her to have such a good time with two other children she had just met.

situation: Someone on Facebook was offering free cuttings from their plant, and I decided to go and get some. I wanted these cuttings so I could root them and add them to my collection of plants. I felt ecstatic about the whole experience! It was really important to me because I thought it was very kind of this woman to share. She could have sold this type of cuttings for a lot of money, but instead, she gave them away.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened earlier today. It mattered a lot to me because I love plants but can't afford to buy any.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This experience helped me grow my planty collection without spending money, it also helped me get out of the house and take a break from work.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I think the lady who was giving the cuttings away was most responsible for it. She posted on Facebook giving them away.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I feel like I had control on whether or not to pick it up, and when to pick it up. I didn't have control over what cuttings I got or when she was available, or if she would give them to me at all, so I feel it was a mix of both.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things didn't go as expected, I was pleasantly surprised, we pulled up and she walked out with the cuttings ready and everything, we were in and out in just a few seconds. I thought it was going to be more tedious like us having to find the house and go knock on her door and wait and have small talk.

situation: Scenario: I was trying to leave for work when I realized my car was missing for the second time in six months. All I wanted was to have my car back, preferably in one piece. The situation left me feeling hopeless and stressed.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened overnight into Monday morning. It mattered to me because my car is my way of making money as a DoorDash driver.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I couldn't make money.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt living in a more run-down neighborhood caused this.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No, I was not in control because I could only put in a police report and wait.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: No, things did not go as I expected. I expected to get it back in one piece, and when I did get it back, it was kinda damaged.

situation: The other day, I sent an email to a few of my managers asking for more hours. I thought it was a really good email and I laid out a few points about how I could use this extra time. That was Tuesday, and I haven't heard anything back. I was trying to get more hours at work because otherwise, I will have to look for another job. I'm upset and kind of feel rejected or overlooked. The situation left me feeling dejected. The fact that I feel overlooked and ignored is important to me.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened on Tuesday, and it matters so much to me because I like my job and it stresses me out thinking about looking for a new one.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because I have always felt quite respected at the company, but this made me feel overlooked and not respected.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I feel the managers and directors who haven't responded are responsible, as well as the disorganization of the company.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I do not feel in control because I have done all I can, and the ball is in their court.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I expected a response quite quickly, so the lack of a quick response was unexpected.

situation: Me and my boyfriend are living long distance now, which is a recent change for us. He was very upset about it, and that made me feel upset too. I wanted to comfort him and reassure him, but it feels tricky because it was my choice to go long distance. I don't feel guilty about the decision and don't want to apologize, but I wanted to be empathetic. I also wanted to cheer him up again and for him to be positive, as I worry for him. The whole situation left me feeling a bit overwhelmed and a bit tired.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: We had had a bit of a disagreement about a message he sent me where he implied he felt punished (I had partly left due to some of his behavior) and I confronted him on that and said it wasn't an acceptable thing to say. Then today we had a call and we were talking and he suddenly got very upset. It matters a lot to me; he is in a geographically isolated place at the moment and is a bit lonely, and has struggled previously with mental health, so reassuring him and making him feel more positive was important to me.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: I think it was helpful that I confronted him about what he had said and set a boundary that it wasn't acceptable, that made me feel more empowered. I was hurt by what he had originally implied, but I think ultimately we did handle the conflict pretty well, and we talked it through on the phone and although he was upset it was a productive and long conversation.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: While I do feel a little responsible for the wider circumstances that I am currently working abroad and that is something I have chosen to do, however, he was the person who originally started last night's disagreement.
appraisal_reasoning.control: Yes, reasonably I felt in control. I did feel a bit overwhelmed, and some other factors like money etc. were not really in my control but I felt I had control over what I could control if that makes sense.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Yes, I think so. I am getting better at holding boundaries.

situation: My car recently had an oil leak, and when we took it to the garage, they told us it was quite severe and undriveable until fixed. Unfortunately, that particular garage couldn't do the repair. Luckily, the car is now fixed, and the cost wasn't as bad as we thought. Given the age of the car, we're considering upgrading to a new one. We were trying to find a way to get the car fixed as quickly as possible while figuring out how much money we had available to either fix the car or replace it if necessary. The whole situation left me feeling very overwhelmed. It's important for us to have two suitable vehicles to make functioning a bit easier.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot because it has an impact on my daily life.

situation: I was quilting by myself when I started feeling nervous because my blood sugar was low, and I didn't recognize it right away. I realized I needed to eat something to feel better. After I ate, my blood sugar increased, and I felt better.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: Last evening. It mattered a lot due to my health. My daughter called on the phone to tell me my blood sugar was low.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: Since I treated my low blood sugar it helped.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Myself
appraisal_reasoning.control: I didn't count my carbs right at dinner.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went as expected.

situation: My parents were making fun of me for not having a job. They kept seeing other people my age in jobs and started putting me on blast. I tried to deescalate the situation, but they just continued and continued. I needed to be comforted. The situation left me heartbroken and hopeless. I felt like a disappointment. The next day, my parents continued making fun of me again.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened some months ago, and it mattered a lot to me because I felt sad and like I was nothing.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation hurt me because it felt like I was a disappointment and it felt like I wasted all the opportunities my parents gave me.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt I was most responsible; I did it to myself.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was half in control. I knew I needed a job, but nobody was accepting me.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things are still bad, but I have side gigs now.

situation: I recently sat down to dedicate some time to completing two important tasks for my older daughter. I needed to finish her registration for kindergarten next year and finalize plans for her 5th birthday party, which is coming up in two weeks. As I worked through these tasks, I started feeling nostalgic and began looking through old photos and videos from her birth, infancy, and toddler stages. It made me really emotional because time has flown by so quickly, and now she's about to head off to a big elementary school all on her own. I was feeling anxious about how fast time is passing, and I'm a bit afraid that before I know it, she'll be an adult facing the world on her own. While I was excited for her getting older and entering a new stage in her life, I also felt afraid of the new challenges she would soon be facing. It was a moment filled with mixed emotions—happiness, sadness, and anxiety. It was really important to me to cover all the details for her birthday so she could see and feel how special she is.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: This event happened last Monday morning. It mattered greatly to me because I have been extremely busy lately, and this was a brief moment where I actually sat and reflected on how far I've come as a mother, and how far my child has come developmentally.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: This situation didn't necessarily hurt me, but it has left me feeling more anxious the past week as I continue to get closer to her birthday and her eventual venture into elementary school. It helped me realize I maybe need to slow down and enjoy things as they are now before they change.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: Not particularly. This was an authentic moment that came about on its own due to normal everyday tasks/obligations that needed to be met.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I felt like I was in control of completing the tasks at hand, but I didn't fully feel control of the emotions that arose around these tasks.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: I did not expect to feel afraid or anxious. I was initially very excited to not only complete these items from my to-do list, but I was actually initially excited for both her birthday and her starting school. The feelings of worry and fear were new.

situation: I had to drive home in bad weather. It was late at night, and the roads were very slippery, which made it stressful. I needed to get home from work, but the conditions left me feeling worried that I wouldn't make it home safely. My safety was my top priority, and nothing else really mattered in that situation.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: The event happened a few days ago. It mattered a lot to me because not getting home safely has very serious consequences. Best case scenario, I have to repair some damage to my vehicle; worst case scenario, I die.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: The situation neither helped nor hurt me due to the outcome being favorable, as I got home safely.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I felt my employer was most responsible for all of this for not cancelling work or doing anything to mitigate potential damage to employees' lives, property, and safety.
appraisal_reasoning.control: I was in control in the sense that I operated the vehicle.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: Things did go as I expected. I got home safely, and I had to drive slowly to do it.

situation: Recently, my girlfriend has been a lot more negative towards me, with name calling and threatening me. She wanted me to send her money this weekend, and I refused because I was tired of the way I was being treated. She blew up at me and once again threatened me and told me to never contact her again. I just didn't want to keep giving her money if she was gonna continue to treat me like shit. The whole situation left me feeling pissed off. I just wished she would treat me like a person and not a punching bag.

appraisal_reasoning.relevance: It mattered to me a lot because I miss the way we used to be.
appraisal_reasoning.congruence: It hurt me a lot because she refuses to acknowledge that she treats me differently. She specifically said she doesn't care, and that she wouldn't have to talk to me like that if I just did what she wants.
appraisal_reasoning.accountability: I really don't know.
appraisal_reasoning.control: No because she always says things to try to get me to do what she wants.
appraisal_reasoning.certainty: It went the way I expected, but not in the good way.
